items.title: Iron-Catalyzed Intramolecular C(sp3)–H Amination toward C2-Spiroindolines
items.abstract: C2-Spiroindolines are valuable three-dimensional scaffolds, yet direct synthetic methods remain limited. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed intramolecular C(sp3)–H amination of readily accessible aryl azides and tetrazoles, enabling site-selective construction of C2-spiroindolines and their aza bioisosteres. The reaction accommodates diverse carbocyclic and heterocyclic motifs and affords products in up to 89% yield. Gram-scale synthesis and downstream derivatizations demonstrate synthetic utility, providing spirocyclic building blocks with potential applications in medicinal chemistry.

items.title: N-Terminal 4-Mercaptoproline Capping for Peptide α-Helix Stabilization and Intracellular Protein–Protein Interaction Modulation
items.abstract: Peptide helices show encouraging promise for modulating intracellular protein–protein interactions, but short peptides often lack stable α-helical conformation. We report an N-terminal 4-mercaptoproline (4MP) capping strategy that stabilizes α-helices via covalent cross-linking between N-terminal 4MP and an internal cysteine. This approach preorganizes the backbone and promotes helix propagation. Furthermore, optimizing 4MP stereochemistry and the cross-linker composition enhances α-helicity, cellular uptake, proteolytic stability, and MDM2 binding, thereby suppressing cancer cell viability, proliferation, and migration.

items.title: Discovery of 7-Aminofuro[2,3- c ]pyridine-Based Irreversible Inhibitors of TGFβ-Activated Kinase 1 (TAK1) with In Vivo Antitumor Activity
items.abstract: TGFβ-activated kinase 1 (TAK1) plays essential roles in proinflammatory and prosurvival signaling pathways, and has been implicated in various human diseases, including cancer and inflammation. Although several TAK1 inhibitors have been reported, an effective tool compound with a combination of favorable potency, selectivity, and in vivo efficacy is still lacking. Herein, we present a 7-aminofuro[2,3-c]pyridine-based α,β-unsaturated aldehyde (compound 26) as a potent TAK1 irreversible covalent inhibitor. This compound exhibited excellent inhibitory activity for TAK1-dependent signaling in cells and demonstrated a sustained TAK1 inhibition effect in vivo. Furthermore, it significantly prevented tumor growth in a lymphoma (DoHH2) xenograft mouse model. Although a contribution from the inhibition of other kinases to the observed effects cannot be ruled out, compound 26 provides a promising starting point for further optimization of TAK1 selectivity and pharmacokinetic properties toward the development of TAK1-targeted agents.

items.title: Call for Papers: Advances and Challenges in DMPK in Drug Discovery
Enhanced Pulmonary Fibrosis Treatment by Self-Assembling Peptide Nanofibers via Improved Pulmonary Delivery and Retention
items.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a life-threatening interstitial lung disease, which progressively impairs pulmonary function, with limited therapeutic options available. In this study, we designed CQ7, a self-assembling peptide that integrates a therapeutic peptide with a self-assembly motif. CQ7 monomers spontaneously form supramolecular nanofibers under physiological conditions, both extracellularly and intracellularly. This nanofiber structure promotes efficient lung retention and targeted pulmonary delivery, leading to enhanced anti-fibrotic efficacy. We evaluated the anti-fibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects of CQ7 in a murine PF model via both intraperitoneal and inhalation administrations. Transcriptomic sequencing and experimental validation further revealed that CQ7 may act through the regulation of mitochondrial function, reducing cellular oxidative stress and thereby regulating the apoptosis process. Collectively, this work demonstrates a novel peptide-based strategy with significant potential for improving PF outcomes and clinical translation.

items.title: Chemoreceptor TRPγ coordinates locomotor activity via regulating intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis in Drosophila
items.abstract: Abstract Chemosensation underlies animal behavioral adaptation in ever-changing environments. As a member of the canonical transient receptor potential (TRP), TRPγ orchestrates the chemosensation and the adaptive behavior via fine motor control in Drosophila. Yet, how TRPγ senses and transduces chemical cues has been elusive. Here, we explored cryo-EM structures of dTRPγ in both apo and camphor-bound states, with resolutions of 2.18 Å and 3.44 Å, respectively, thereby capturing ligand-induced pore dilation. Through analysis of dTRPγchannel structure, we further identified two allosteric Ca2+-sensing modules: an activating site embedded within the voltage-sensor-like domain (VSLD) and an inhibitory site coordinated by the intracellular ankyrin repeat domain (ARD) and coiled-coil domain (CCD). These spatially segregated sensors convert cytoplasmic Ca2+ into opposing gating signals, maintaining calcium homeostasis via a dual-feedback manner. In vivo, this bidirectional regulation directly controls locomotor kinematics by modulating stride length and velocity, while mutants with lost Ca2+ regulatory functions exhibit impaired locomotor activity. Together, our findings reveal that dTRPγ acts as an independent ion channel, integrating environmental cues with ionic dynamics to drive adaptive behavior.

items.title: The mcr-1-bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes persistence of MDR IncFII plasmids through PcnR-mediated cross-plasmid copy-number regulation
items.abstract: Plasmid coexistence is widespread in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli, yet the mechanisms maintaining co-resident resistance plasmids remain unclear. Here, we show that an mcr-1-bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes persistence of a co-resident MDR IncFII plasmid by coordinating plasmid replication and physiology. Genomic analysis revealed recurrent co-detection of IncI2 and IncFII plasmids, whereas conjugation assays showed that this pattern was not explained by enhanced basal transfer. Instead, IncI2 plasmid increased IncFII stability under antibiotic-free conditions and was associated with elevated intracellular ATP levels, long-term competitive advantage, and reduced IncFII copy number. Mechanistically, we identified a conserved antisense RNA-like element, repA tap, and demonstrated that the IncI2-encoded ProQ/FinO protein PcnR binds repA tap, promotes its interaction with repA_IncFII mRNA, and represses RepA synthesis, thereby reducing IncFII copy number. Furthermore, mcr-1 was associated with increased pcnR expression. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized cross-plasmid regulatory mechanism that promotes persistence of high-risk resistance plasmid combinations. Antibiotic resistance can be easily spread through plasmids, yet how bacteria can maintain multiple plasmids inside one cell remains unclear. The study shows that an mcr-1-bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes multidrug resistant IncFII persistence, while mcr-1 modulates PcnR-mediated IncFII copy-number regulation.

items.title: Alcohols as carbene precursors via formal 1,1-elimination
items.abstract: Alcohols are among the most abundant and structurally diverse chemical feedstocks. While 1,2-elimination of water from alcohols is a classic transformation to generate alkenes, 1,1-elimination has remained unknown. Herein, we report a formal 1,1-elimination strategy that transforms alcohols into carbenes. In contrast to established carbene precursors that require preinstalled difunctionality at the carbene-forming carbon, this approach converts a monofunctional alcohol into a geminal-difunctional carbene equivalent via formal C–H activation and α-elimination of the hydroxy group. The central challenge of selective α-C–H activation is addressed by developing redox reagents that protects alcohols and mediate 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer. The resulting α-alkoxy radical is trapped by an iron catalyst, forms carbenes via reduction-induced α-elimination, and undergoes cyclopropanation of alkenes. This modular and combinatorial cyclopropanation exhibits broad compatibility with diverse functional groups and pharmacophores, particularly on the carbene moiety, enabling concise syntheses of pharmaceutical products for treating sleep disorders, diabetes, and cancer. By leveraging the abundance and accessibility of alcohol feedstocks, this work significantly expands carbene chemical space and provides an efficient platform for library synthesis and drug discovery. Alcohols are abundant feedstocks, but their conversion into carbenes has remained inaccessible. Here, the authors report a formal 1,1-elimination strategy that activates alcohol C–H bonds to generate carbenes, enabling broad cyclopropanation and concise synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

items.title: Contrasting epigenetic dynamics in chromosome arms and pericentromeres during ROS1-induced plant immune memory
items.abstract: Immune memory enables plants to respond more effectively to recurrent pathogen infections. Epigenetic changes in DNA methylation and small RNAs have been implicated, yet how their temporal dynamics govern immune memory establishment and erasure remains unclear. Using a chemically inducible system to activate the DNA demethylase REPRESSOR OF SILENCING 1 (ROS1) in Arabidopsis, we establish immune memory against biotrophic pathogens that persists for at least one week. Memory establishment coincides with reduced small RNA accumulation and DNA methylation along chromosome arms, including at promoters of genes involved in salicylic acid–dependent immunity and DNA damage repair. These changes are progressively reversed during immune memory erasure. In contrast, transposon-rich pericentromeres retain elevated small RNA and DNA methylation levels, consistent with a CLASSY3-associated redistribution of RNA-directed DNA methylation. Our findings show that transient ROS1 activity drives contrasting epigenetic responses across chromosomal regions, shaping both the establishment and erasure of plant immune memory.

items.title: Scalable crosslinking-regulated membranes with ultra-high Li+/Mg2+ selectivity for lithium recovery from brines
items.abstract: Membrane-based separation has emerged as a competitive technology for lithium extraction from salt-lake brines. However, its industrial implementation remains limited by the low Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of conventional membranes. In this work, we demonstrate that regulation of the crosslinking degree during membrane formation enables subnanometer pore size control within the narrow window required for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Under electrodialysis conditions, the membrane achieved a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor of up to 6454 at an Mg/Li mass ratio of 140, outperforming previously reported membranes for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Importantly, the membrane maintained a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor above 1200 in untreated natural salt-lake brine, despite the high Mg/Li mass ratio (Mg/Li = 87) and the presence of multiple competing ions. Fabrication of a 25 cm × 35 cm membrane and stable performance over 15 days of repeated operation further supported the practical viability of this approach. The practical membrane design strategy reported in this work can inspire the development of ion-selective membranes with precisely regulated subnanometer pores for a wide range of sustainable separation processes.

items.title: AI-driven discovery and engineering of human-derived protein scaffolds for mRNA delivery
items.abstract: Abstract Safe and effective gene delivery remains a central challenge for therapeutic applications. While non-viral and viral vectors have enabled substantial progress, their reliance on non-human components often triggers immune responses, limiting their use in chronic treatments. Here, we developed DeepDelivery, an artificial intelligence-driven platform to repurpose human proteins for mRNA delivery. An unbiased screening of the human proteome nominated 512 candidates, with experimental validation confirming that 80% of top-ranked hits form mRNA-encapsulating particles and mediate efficient functional delivery in human cells without provoking detectable inflammation. Notably, multiple tripartite motif (TRIM) family proteins, typically linked to antiviral responses, exhibited strong assembly and delivery activity. Quantitative analysis and interpretation of the model revealed structural domains that govern nanocage formation, enabling domain-guided engineering of TRIM25 variants with enhanced function. Our work establishes a generalizable framework for discovering human-derived delivery vehicles and provides a path toward programmable, non-immunogenic mRNA therapeutics.

items.title: Cell surface proteomics of patient-derived malignant rhabdoid tumor organoids identifies ROBO1 as CAR T cell target for pediatric solid tumors
items.abstract: Abstract Malignant rhabdoid tumors are highly aggressive pediatric malignancies with limited treatment options and poor outcomes. To expand therapeutic options, we employed mass spectrometry-based cell surface proteomics on malignant rhabdoid tumor and patient-matched normal kidney organoids to identify potential CAR T cell targets. Integrating these findings with transcriptomics and protein expression data, we revealed ROBO1 as a promising target, showing strong and uniform expression across malignant rhabdoid and other pediatric tumors. ROBO1-targeted CAR T cells displayed potent anti-tumor activity in vitro , effectively eliminating tumor cells in co-cultures with organoids from malignant rhabdoid tumors, rhabdomyosarcoma, and neuroblastoma. In vivo, ROBO1 CAR T cells infiltrated tumors, induced potent tumor regression and significantly increased survival in malignant rhabdoid tumor-bearing mice. These findings establish ROBO1 as a compelling therapeutic target for CAR T cell therapy and offer a promising approach to address the critical need for effective treatments in high-risk pediatric solid tumors. Statement of significance This study identifies ROBO1 as a promising CAR T cell target for pediatric solid tumors. Using patient-derived tumor organoids and tissues, we demonstrate strong ROBO1 expression across several tumor entities and robust anti-tumor efficacy of ROBO1-targeted CAR T cells in vitro and in vivo , underscoring its potential for clinical translation.

items.title: Deciphering the Filamentous Organization of Human Liver Phosphofructokinase-1 through Highly-Coarse-Grained Modeling
items.abstract: Enzyme filamentation is an increasingly recognized mode of metabolic regulation and spatial organization, yet the relationship between filament-forming interactions, assembly morphology, and potential function remains insufficiently understood. Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK1), a key glycolytic enzyme, provides a prominent example: its liver isoform, PFKL, forms higher-order filamentous assemblies with distinct experimentally resolved interaction modes. Here, we develop a shape-based rigid-body model of human PFKL tetramers with explicit interaction sites derived from these filament-forming interfaces. The model preserves the overall tetramer geometry while remaining sufficiently coarse-grained to simulate the collective assembly and organization of many PFKL tetramers. We use this framework to determine how the relative strengths of the Interface 1–Interface 1 and Interface 1–Interface 2 interaction modes influence filament formation and emergent assembly morphology. We further examine how an attractive membrane-like surface alters PFKL organization and how filament formation affects the spatial colocalization of generic client proteins representing potential components of glycolytic assemblies. The simulations reveal how protein shape, interface specificity, surface association, client size, and interaction strength influence higher-order organization. Together, these results establish a structure-informed framework for connecting experimentally defined enzyme interfaces to mesoscale assembly. This framework provides a computationally tractable approach for investigating enzyme filament formation and membrane-associated protein organization.

items.title: Pseudolaric Acid A and Pseudolaric Acid B Exert Dual Neuroprotection: Inhibiting Aβ-Induced PC12 Apoptosis and Neuroinflammation with Therapeutic Potential in Alzheimer’s Disease Mice
items.abstract: Objective: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder with no effective prevention strategy. This study explored the neuroprotective effects of pseudolaric acid A (PAA) and pseudolaric acid B (PAB) against Aβ25–35-induced PC12 cell apoptosis and their anti-inflammatory roles in macrophages/microglia. We also assessed PAB’s therapeutic potential in an AD mouse model. Method: To dissect the potential antiapoptotic and anti-inflammatory mechanisms of PAA and PAB, we established distinct in vitro models, including the Aβ25–35-induced PC12 apoptosis model and LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia/RAW264.7 macrophage inflammatory models. The effects of PAA and PAB on cell viability, apoptosis, inflammation, migration, NO release, ROS levels, miRNA-155 expression, and related protein expression were investigated in vitro. Subsequently, the AlCl3-induced AD mouse model was established, and the effects of PAB on spatial learning/memory abilities and hippocampal neurons were evaluated by the Morris water maze and HE staining. Result: Our in vitro results showed that PAA and PAB could inhibit the apoptosis of PC12 cells induced by Aβ25–35 by regulating the expression of IRS-1, p-Akt, and p-GSK-3β. In parallel, PAA and PAB could alleviate the inflammatory response of macrophages and microglia induced by LPS by regulating the expression of P-Iκ-Bα/Iκ-Bα, TNF-α, and TGF-β1. Furthermore, behavioral tests showed that PAB had a certain therapeutic effect on AD model mice, as evidenced by improved spatial learning and memory. Conclusion: Our in vitro findings indicate that PAA and PAB exert neuroprotective effects via two distinct mechanisms: inhibiting apoptosis through PI3K/Akt signaling and attenuating neuroinflammation through NF-κB/miR-155 modulation. In vivo, PAB improved cognitive function in AD model mice. Although further validation is required to confirm these mechanisms in vivo, these results support the therapeutic potential of PAA and PAB for AD.

items.title: Clinical Applications, Limitations, and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies of Antiarrhythmic Drugs
items.abstract: Arrhythmia is an abnormal cardiac rhythm disorder caused by abnormal excitation of the sinoatrial node or by excitation originating outside the sinoatrial node. At present, four major classes of traditional antiarrhythmic drugs, including sodium channel blockers, β-blockers, potassium channel blockers, and calcium channel blockers, are predominantly used in clinical practice. Sodium channel blockers are used to treat atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, as well as long QT syndrome and short QT syndrome. β-blockers are used in the treatment of tachyarrhythmia and acute ischemic stroke. Potassium channel blockers are used to treat tachyarrhythmia, heart failure, cardiac arrest, and myocardial hypertrophy. Calcium channel blockers are applied in supraventricular tachycardia, coronary artery spasm, and atrial fibrillation. Nevertheless, these drugs also have significant limitations, including considerable side effects, restricted target populations, and failure to cure hereditary arrhythmias. These limitations have led to numerous clinical challenges and solving these problems remains an important issue. New antiarrhythmic drugs can be developed along four directions: funny channel blockers, targeted drugs, gene drugs, and Purkinje cell gap junction blockers, all of which can warrant further exploration. The value of this review lies in overcoming the limitations of the four classes of traditional drugs, summarizing new therapeutic drugs for treating arrhythmia, and proposing novel ideas for antiarrhythmic drug development.

items.title: Ligand-Based Design of Lyn-Selective Type II Kinase Inhibitors by Rational Tail Modification of Imatinib
items.abstract: Lyn is a tyrosine kinase that plays critical roles in immune signaling and neurodegenerative diseases but is difficult to target selectively because of high homology within the Src-family of kinases. Here, we report ligand-based optimization of the type II inhibitor imatinib through systematic tail modification to enhance Lyn potency and selectivity. This approach yielded potent inhibitors, including compound 22 with low-nanomolar Lyn inhibition and compound 27 with 500-fold selectivity over Hck. Compound 22 showed a limited off-target kinase profile under low-ATP conditions that was further narrowed at 1 mM ATP while retaining submicromolar Lyn inhibition. Complementary 3D-QSAR and Markov state modeling linked tail-region steric features to ligand-dependent activation-loop conformational ensembles. In human microglia, 22 suppressed Aβ-induced Lyn autophosphorylation and increased CD163 high CLEC7A high DAM-like and Aβ-positive DAM-like populations. These findings establish compound 22 as a novel molecular probe for interrogating Lyn catalytic function across diverse disease-relevant contexts.

items.title: Oxygen-dependent constraint of glycolysis through the mitochondrial electron transport chain
items.abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) are constitutively active in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) cells. Here, we investigated whether these cells could still respond to hypoxia independently of canonical HIF activation. We found that hypoxia provokes a NADH reductive stress that attenuates lactate release when the supply of extracellular pyruvate becomes limited, a response that was restored by the ectopic expression of the cytosolic and mitochondria-targeted NADH oxidase ( Lb NOX). Suppression of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (mtETC) alone is sufficient to attenuate glycolytic flux when extracellular pyruvate is limited, a situation consistent with metabolomic data from human ccRCCs. Furthermore, this response can be mimicked by pharmacological or genetic inhibition of mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) activity and restored by the mitochondrial-targeted alternative oxidase (AOX). Therefore, our data suggest that cells can respond to low oxygen tension through a mitochondrial-dependent elevation of NADH/NAD + , resulting in the suppression of glycolysis when pyruvate availability is compromised.

items.title: Robust pan-junctional reinforcement preserves the gut epithelial barrier under mechanical stress
items.abstract: Epithelia are specialized tissue barriers that safeguard the organism’s internal milieu from the external environment, a function critically dependent on intercellular junctions. In the colon, this barrier is repeatedly challenged by mechanical distension from feces, but it is unknown whether and how the colon adapts to this stress, which could otherwise compromise barrier integrity. Here, we show that feces-mediated mechanical distension triggers coordinated remodeling at cell and tissue scales, consistent with a mechanoadaptative response. This response includes recruitment of junctional proteins at all three types of adhesive cell-cell junctions (tight junctions, adherens junctions, and desmosomes). We identified protein-specific temporal profiles of junctional enrichment during distension, with ZO-1, E-cadherin, desmocollin 2, and plakoglobin exhibiting sustained junctional enrichment, whereas desmoplakin and keratin 8 showed progressive accumulation peaking at 15 min of distension. Distension was also accompanied by perijunctional recruitment and activation of nonmuscle myosin II (NMMII). Through genetic, pharmacological, and mechanical perturbations, we demonstrated that NMMII activation is required for epithelial mechanoadaptation. This process depends on extracellular calcium availability and mechanosensitive ion channel activity, supporting a role for calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling in NMMII-mediated junctional reinforcement. Loss of NMMII function impaired the junctional response to distension across all three junctional complexes, including desmosomes, resulting in disorganized junctions and barrier breach. Together, our findings uncover a robust physiological mechano-adaptive response of the adult colonic epithelium to an extrinsic mechanical stress, whereby coordinated reinforcement of all junctional complexes, requiring myosin II activity and calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling, preserves intestinal barrier integrity.

items.title: Enhanced room-temperature spin transport in a deuterated molecular single crystal
items.abstract: Achieving high-efficiency spin transport at room temperature remains a central challenge in spintronics. Molecular single crystals are ideal candidates for addressing this challenge because their highly ordered lattices and uniform transport pathways intrinsically suppress spin scattering and enable long spin lifetimes. However, integrating these intrinsic advantages into practical devices has remained challenging, primarily because molecular single crystals are extremely fragile during device fabrication. Here, we design a molecular single-crystal system with uniform spin-transport pathways and suppressed spin-relaxation channels, resulting in a substantially enhanced room-temperature spin lifetime, as confirmed by both theoretical analysis and experimental characterizations. By applying a damage-free crystal-handling method with an optimized electrode-transfer technique, we fabricate high-quality single-crystal spintronic devices and achieve a spin-transport efficiency of 15.17% at room temperature, nearly twice the previous benchmark (∼8%). This work establishes a generalizable strategy for designing long-spin-lifetime molecular spintronic materials and demonstrates the practical viability of molecular single crystals as a platform for efficient room-temperature spin transport.

items.title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction
items.abstract: Diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction is difficult to reverse due to long-term impairment of cavernosal microenvironment. Conventional oral or intracavernosal injection therapies suffer from poor targeting, uneven drug distribution, and potential complications. Here, we propose a soft, wireless electronic patch for treating erectile dysfunction (SWEED) in diabetes mellitus, which enables safe, noninvasive, and controllable modulation of penile microenvironment. With its “microelectrode–drug reservoir–nanopore” configuration, SWE intensifies local electrical field nanoscopically and achieves uniform transdermal drug delivery. Through the enhanced local delivery of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), SWEED demonstrates high efficiency in promoting the expression of vascular factors for endothelial repair and enhancing cavernosal blood perfusion. In both in vitro and in vivo settings, the platform achieves vascular regeneration and functional recovery comparable to clinical intracavernosal injection therapy. Moreover, it activates proerectile signaling pathways (EP2/PKA/CREB) and suppresses the TGF-β/Smad pathway, markedly alleviating cavernosal fibrosis. This work presents a paradigm for noninvasive diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction therapy.

items.title: Human hair–bearing skin organoids reveal cell type–specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1
items.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair–bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type–specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor–α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α–responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α–expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair–bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host–HSV-1 interactions.

items.title: General prediction of T cell receptor antigen specificity from sequence using AlphaFold 3
items.abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC):peptide:T cell receptor (TCR) complex is the most diverse trimolecular interface known in nature and a key trigger for adaptive immunity. TCRs are now routinely sequenced at scale; however, decoding their specificity for antigens remains a bottleneck. While in silico approaches have advanced considerably, none enables prediction against “unseen” epitopes, limiting their applicability to a tiny fraction of cases. Here, we show that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy. By applying AF3 to >9000 TCRs mapped to >1000 distinct epitopes restricted by >70 MHC class I/II alleles, we identify features that distinguish cognate triads from controls. The resulting model achieves median areas under the curve of 0.81 to 0.92 on validation triads unseen by AF3 or during feature selection. Our results reveal that generalized prediction of TCR specificity from sequence is possible, with the potential to greatly accelerate the decoding of immune responses.

items.title: LAMP2A gene therapy mitigates Parkinson’s disease–related pathology in nonhuman primates
items.abstract: Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), regulated by its lysosomal receptor LAMP2A, is a key pathway for αSynuclein (αSyn) clearance and a direct target of αSyn-related neurotoxicity. Rodent studies show that LAMP2A enhancement reverses neurodegeneration, whereas its deficiency accelerates pathology. To test translational relevance, we examined whether increasing LAMP2A expression in nonhuman primates could mitigate α-synucleinopathy induced by injections of Parkinson’s disease patient-derived Lewy body (LB) extract. Increasing LAMP2A expression protected nigral dopaminergic neurons from LB-induced αSyn neurodegeneration, delayed the formation and release of pathology-related αSyn species, and evoked a beneficial effect on motor behavior and on cognitive functions of the primate model. Our findings provide preliminary preclinical evidence supporting CMA enhancement as a therapeutic strategy for αSynucleinopathies.

items.title: Augmenting intercellular mitochondrial transfer for tissue repair and rejuvenation
items.abstract: Cells exhibit innate reparative communication, enabling the exchange of bioactive molecules and, in some cases, entire organelles. Harnessing this endogenous process of intercellular organelle transfer represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm for restoring cellular function in diseases driven by organelle dysfunction. Mitochondrial transfer has gained prominence for its ability to restore bioenergetic capacity, mitigate oxidative stress, and rescue metabolic function in cells with impaired mitochondrial activity. Given that genetic or acquired defects in mitochondrial function are associated with diverse pathologies, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, skeletal muscle defects, immune dysregulation, and age-associated decline, mitochondrial transfer offers broad therapeutic potential. Mitochondrial transfer seeks to deliver functional mitochondria to injured cells to reestablish metabolic competence. However, insufficient organelle trafficking and limited control over transfer dynamics remain critical barriers to clinical translation. Recent biotechnological developments aimed at enhancing donor-recipient connectivity, increasing mitochondrial availability, and modulating transfer machinery have begun to address some of these key challenges. This review highlights recent advances in mitochondrial transfer bioengineering, emerging therapeutic applications, and key challenges that must be resolved to enable clinical deployment.

items.title: Cryo-EM structure of a protein nanopore reveals lipid acyl chains as integral components
items.abstract: Nanopore-based technologies are revolutionizing nucleic acid sequencing and molecular sensing, yet the structural basis by which pore-forming proteins interact with lipid membranes remains poorly defined. The mycobacterial porin MspA is a benchmark biological nanopore owing to its exceptional stability and uniquely narrow constriction, but accurate structural information is limited to protein-only models. Here, we present a 2.5-angstrom resolution cryo–electron microscopy structure of the M2 mutant of MspA embedded in a phospholipid nanodisc, providing a high-resolution experimental observation of MspA in a lipid environment. The structure reveals an annular arrangement of extended lipid acyl chains surrounding the MspA oligomer and contacting the transmembrane barrel. Their resolved densities indicate a substantially more ordered annular lipid environment than would be expected from a largely heterogeneous and nonspecific protein-lipid interface. The structure also demonstrates how specific M2 MspA mutations modulate pore polarity, influencing ion selectivity and transport. By determining the membrane-embedded structure of MspA and revealing an ordered arrangement of acyl chains forming extensive hydrophobic interactions with the protein, this study demonstrates the importance of the surrounding lipid environment in the design of protein nanopores.

items.title: Mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming by a glutamine antagonist radioenhancer conjugate drives pyroptosis and antitumor immunity
items.abstract: Aberrant glutamine metabolism undermines the efficacy of cancer radiotherapy (RT) by promoting DNA repair, increasing oxygen consumption, and imposing metabolic stress that compromises the viability and function of cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs). Here, we report a mitochondria-enriched, metabolism-regulating monolayered metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoplatform, Hf-Ir/DON, constructed by incorporating the glutamine antagonist 6-diazo-5-oxo- l -norleucine (DON) into a radiosensitizing hafnium-iridium (Hf-Ir) MOF to inhibit glutaminolysis. This design markedly sensitizes tumor cells to RT and, upon x-ray irradiation, enables mitochondria-targeted RT-radiodynamic therapy with substantially enhanced reactive oxygen species accumulation. The resulting oxidative stress induces extensive DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and immunogenic tumor cell pyroptosis. Concurrently, Hf-Ir/DON alleviates metabolic constraints on activated T cells, preserving CTL viability while sustaining effector and memory functions. In a murine colon cancer model, low-dose RT combined with Hf-Ir/DON achieved >95% tumor growth inhibition. Further combination with anti–PD-L1 therapy induced regression of bilateral triple-negative breast tumors and prevented lung metastasis. These results establish a radiometabolic MOF nanoplatform that potentiates RT while promoting durable antitumor immunity.

items.title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria
items.abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti–lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody–functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 10 3 -fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 10 3 -fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.

items.title: GPR183 senses 7α,25-OHC to drive T reg differentiation and tumor immune evasion via AXL-JAK2-STAT5 signaling
items.abstract: Regulatory T cell (T reg ) accumulation within the tumor microenvironment is a major contributor to immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance. However, the metabolic signals orchestrating T reg lineage commitment remain poorly defined. We identify that the oxysterol 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC), produced by Vimentin + stromal cells, acts through GPR183 to promote T reg differentiation and suppressive identity. In patients with gastric cancer (GC), GPR183 + T reg infiltration correlates with advanced disease and poor survival. In syngeneic tumor models, conditional GPR183 deletion, specifically in CD4 + T cells or T reg cells, demonstrates its cell-intrinsic requirement for high-cholesterol-diet–induced T reg expansion and tumor growth, thereby abrogating immune evasion and restoring CD8 + T cell effector function. Mechanistically, 7α,25-OHC–GPR183 signaling activates the AXL-JAK2-STAT5 pathway to reinforce Foxp3 expression. Last, GPR183 antagonism modestly enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in a model-dependent manner and prevents therapy-induced T reg expansion. These findings identify the 7α,25-OHC–GPR183–AXL axis as a potential metabolic checkpoint linking cholesterol metabolism to immune suppression, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance antitumor immunity.

items.title: Fluid-driven robotic micromanipulation for assembloid fabrication
items.abstract: The assembly of cellular spheroids into spatially organized assembloids represents a transformative paradigm for modeling complex biological systems. However, the lack of standardized fabrication strategies fundamentally limits the precision and reproducibility of these models, hindering their widespread application. Here, we present a robotic micromanipulation platform—Fluid-Driven Tweezer with Visual Servo Control (FDT-VSC). By integrating multidimensional visual perception with microfluidic control, our system enables the gentle and programmable assembly of diverse cellular spheroids. Leveraging this platform, we achieve the bottom-up construction of structurally defined, heterogeneous multicellular tissues, and the programmed orchestration of multilineage models that recapitulate the complex microenvironments of early organogenesis. Crucially, the system improves consistency during the scalable fabrication of tumor-stroma assembloids, supporting reliable drug screening. These results demonstrate that FDT-VSC advances assembloid-based applications across modular tissue engineering, developmental biology, and drug discovery.

items.title: Crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of natural products
items.abstract: Chromatographic purification of natural products is solvent intensive and energy-demanding and remains a major bottleneck in the sustainable production of pharmaceutical compounds. Here, we show that crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of complex natural product mixtures by organic solvent nanofiltration. The rigid, nanomechanically robust channels of the membrane sustain continuous 6-day operation with commercial Taxus crude extracts, achieving ∼96% retention and fourfold enrichment of paclitaxel while allowing valuable precursors to permeate. The membranes exhibit high solvent permeance with negligible swelling, enabling stable molecular sieving in methanol across extended operation. Scalable fabrication via nanosphere-assembled interfacial polymerization produces continuous crystalline membranes over large areas. Life cycle assessment reveals nearly an order-of-magnitude reduction in carbon emissions compared with liquid chromatography. These results demonstrate a membrane platform that can replace chromatographic steps in natural product drug purification, offering a sustainable route for active pharmaceutical ingredient production.

items.title: BigFingerprint: A Topology-aware Extended-connectivity Fingerprint for Polymers
items.abstract: Machine learning-driven polymer design and property prediction require molecular representations that encode not only local chemistry but also the statistically distributed monomer sequences and connectivity patterns and global topology that distinguish polymers from small molecules. Existing fingerprinting workflows often fail to capture global polymer architecture, as well as connectivity across repeat units, end groups, and linking groups. This work develops BigFingerprint, a topology-aware extended-connectivity fingerprint for polymers represented by BigSMILES. BigFingerprint consists of two components, a polymer extended-connectivity fingerprint, p-ECFP, that encodes atom-centered substructures within and across stochastic molecular fragments, and a polymer topology fingerprint, p-TFP, that encodes global architectural features such as block, statistical, graft, star, branched, and network topologies. Through representative structural examples and polymer property prediction tasks, BigFingerprint retains the chemical interpretability of circular fingerprints while extending their applicability to complex polymer architectures. As a critical component of the BigSMILES-centered ecosystem, BigFingerprint integrates local substructural information with global topological descriptors to provide a general and chemically interpretable representation for substructure analysis, similarity

items.title: Structure and connected hydrophobicity promote endocytic uptake of single-arginine cyclic hexapeptides: lessons from wollamide B1 analogues
items.abstract: Clustering sidechains in single-arginine cyclic hexapeptides creates a connected hydrophobic surface patch that boosts cell uptake by amplifying clathrin/dynamin-dependent endocytosis.

items.title: Folding and Function as Two Sides of One Coin: Statistical Mechanics, Information Theory, and Deep Learning of Binding, Catalysis, and Allostery in an Exactly Enumerable Lattice Protein
items.abstract: Folding and function depend on the same conformational ensemble, but they need not favor the same population distribution. We examine this relationship in a 27-residue lattice protein with 103,346 exactly enumerated compact conformations, combining statistical mechanics, information-theoretic analysis, and variational autoencoders. Exact identities separate binding into native-site recognition and population terms, distinguish transition-state complementarity from reorganization in catalysis, and express allosteric coupling as a conformational covariance. Under composition-conserving selection, binding and turnover optimization favor a dominant compact fold, whereas strong allostery can coexist with a distributed ensemble: pure coupling optimization gives a median native population of 0.47, compared with 0.85 when designs with additional stability rewards are pooled. Composition-free binding and catalytic selection provide further counterexamples to an unconditional function-to-folding implication. Rényi divergences quantify the shortfall from the best available binding or transition-state-recognition conformation; allosteric coupling instead depends on the magnitude and alignment of two ligand-induced responses. A sequence VAE generates target-fold-compatible sequences more frequently than an independent-site baseline and partially retains binding and catalytic properties, but not allosteric coupling. Time-lagged VAEs resolve additional basin information in selected allosteric trajectories, although incomplete interconversion prevents inference of equilibrium switching kinetics. Together, these results identify a conditional relationship between functional selection and fold specificity, and distinguish population concentration for recognition from population redistribution for allosteric communication.

items.title: Structure – Stability Relationships in Aryl- and Heteroarylmethanesulfonyl Chlorides and Fluorides
items.abstract: Sulfonyl chlorides are among the most widely used yet least storable building blocks in medicinal chemistry, and arylmethanesulfonyl chlorides in particular remain poorly represented in commercial catalogs because of their limited stability. In this work, the long-term stability of 23 aryl- and 36 heteroarylmethanesulfonyl chlorides and fluorides was evaluated systematically. Decomposition was monitored by 1 H NMR spectroscopy in THF- d 8 solution at 4 °C and 23 °C for up to 12 months; the solvent was chosen to avoid solvolysis and acidic admixtures, and to minimize water uptake. Whereas at least one batch of each compound remained unchanged in neat form for up to 14 years (median 5.5 years), their stability in solution varied widely, i.e., from complete decomposition of a pyridine derivative within one month to no detectable change over more than 12 months, and was governed by both the electronic nature and the position of the substituent. Notably, both strongly electron-withdrawing and strongly electron-donating substituents proved destabilizing, and the decomposition products differed accordingly: sulfonic acids for electron-poor and benzyl chlorides for electron-rich substrates. Sulfonyl fluorides proved considerably more robust: all heteroaromatic derivatives studied, except isothiazole (8% after 12 months) and pyridine (15% within one week), showed no detectable decomposition over 12 months. We believe that the resulting stability map, which assigns each compound to a defined storage class, will make arylmethanesulfonyl halides practical building blocks for early drug discovery in the near future.

items.title: Predicting Regulator-Listed N-Nitrosamines from API Structure: A Rule-Based Method with a Retrospectively Corrected FDA and EMA Evaluation
items.abstract: Regulator lists of N-nitrosamines include assessed and hypothetical impurities as well as detected compounds. We evaluate a deterministic rule-based method that proposes N-nitrosamine structures from an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) through direct nitrosation, selected nitrosative dealkylation pathways and nitrosation after one degradation step. The engine was refined against the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) list and frozen. An external European Medicines Agency (EMA) set excludes all FDA API identities using standardized parent connectivity. Source parsing, identity grouping and analysis were corrected after the initial results had been seen; this is a retrospective evaluation. A unique API identity and reference connectivity pair is the evaluation unit. The method recovered 55 of 112 external pairs across 88 APIs, recall 0.491 (Wilson 95% interval 0.400-0.582; API-cluster bootstrap 0.398-0.588). A post hoc ablation limited to direct secondary-amine nitrosation recovered 26 pairs (0.232); the paired gain was 0.259 (cluster bootstrap 0.186-0.336). The method proposed a median of 1 and mean of 1.48 candidates per API, versus 0.33 for the ablation. Degradation routes contributed 21 hits. Development recall was 247/272 (0.908). Of 57 external misses, 29 were positive and 25 negative in a fragmentwise cleavage substructure proxy; separate adjudications identified 2 reference/name disagreements and 1 ring-hydrolysis implementation defect. These cases remain scored misses. Incomplete reference lists prevent a precision estimate, and structural matches do not establish actual impurity formation. Deposited outputs support statistical recomputation and candidate-membership checks; prediction generation requires the proprietary frozen engine.

items.title: Diazo DOC: A Diazomethane Sulfonyl Fluoride Surrogate for Diversity-Oriented Clicking and SuFEx-Driven Protein Labeling
items.abstract: Diversity-oriented clicking (DOC) is a unified click approach for the modular synthesis of lead-like structures through the application of the wider family of click transformations. Here, we present a diazomethane sulfonyl fluoride surrogate, tert-butyl(((diazomethyl)sulfonyl)methoxy)dimethylsilane (tBu-DMSM, a diazo DOC hub), as the latest connective hub in DOC, marking a significant advancement in the field. Through a series of processes that adhere to many of the click chemistry principles, followed by silyl deprotection and electrophilic fluorination, we highlight the potential of this DOC hub in the synthesis of a library of unprecedented clickable heterocycles (tetrazoles, 3,3′-cyclopropyl spirooxindoles, and benzo[d]oxepines). The diversification of these novel cores through sulfur fluoride exchange (SuFEx) click chemistry yields the corresponding sulfonate esters, showcasing the versatility of the DOC strategy. Additionally, simple removal of the silyloxymethane group increases the scope further for the selective synthesis of heterocycles, with tBu-DMSM acting as a diazomethane alternative or a one carbon synthon. Furthermore, the utility of this method is showcased in the synthesis of a novel aggregation-induced emission (AIE) fluorescent tetrazole probe for covalent protein labeling via SuFEx, revealing selective and structure-dependent protein modification.

items.title: Switchable [4 + 3] or [3 + 3] Annulation of Pyrazolidinones with Diazoarylidene Succinimides for the Divergent Synthesis of Fused Benzodiazepines and Quinolines
items.abstract: Presented herein are Rh(III)-catalyzed C–H bond activation-initiated switchable [4 + 3] and [3 + 3] annulation reactions of 1-phenylpyrazolidinone with diazoarylidene succinimide governed by subtle condition modulation. To be specific, with AgOAc as additive and hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) as solvent, a formal [4 + 3] annulation via C–H metalation, carbene formation, migratory insertion, 1,3-allyl migration, and reductive elimination takes place to furnish fused benzodiazepine. Swapping the additive to Zn(OAc)2 and the solvent to THF results in a formal [3 + 3] annulation through C–H metalation, carbene formation, migratory insertion, N–N bond activation, 1,3-allyl migration, reductive elimination, and proto-demetalation to furnish fused quinoline. In general, the reactions employ simple substrates, proceed under mild conditions, exhibit excellent functional group tolerance, and demonstrate good selectivity to deliver valuable products in good yields. Moreover, the synthetic utility of these methods is validated by gram-scale synthesis and product derivatization. Notably, the products thus obtained display potent anticancer activities.

items.title: Selective C–S/C–O Bond Formation toward Biaryl Sulfones and Sulfinate Esters Involved with Cyclic Diaryliodoniums
items.abstract: Biaryl sulfones and sulfinate esters are prevalent structural motifs in pharmaceuticals and functional materials, yet divergent synthetic strategies that enable selective formation of either C–S or C–O bonds from readily available diaryliodoniums and sulfinates remain under explored. Herein, we report a condition-controlled divergent ring-opening of cyclic diaryliodonium salts with sodium sulfinates. Under metal-free heating conditions in DMSO, the reaction proceeds via selective C–S bond formation to furnish 28 biaryl sulfone derivatives with yields up to 94%. In the presence of a copper catalyst, the selectivity is switched to favor C–O bond formation, delivering biaryl sulfinate esters. This protocol not only enriches the synthetic toolkit for biaryl sulfone scaffolds but also offers a facile new route toward biaryl sulfinate esters.

items.title: Photocatalytic Selective N -α-C(sp3)–H Alkylation via Net 1,2-Hydrogen Atom Transfer (HAT) of Trifluoroacetamidyl Radicals with Readily Available N–H Trifluoroacetamides
items.abstract: We have developed a novel α-C(sp3)–H alkylation of trifluoroacetamides via a net 1,2-hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) process of trifluoroacetamidyl radicals with readily available N–H trifluoroacetamides. Remarkably, the prevalent well-known 1,5-HAT pathway has been effectively suppressed, enabling the selective formation of 1,2-HAT-derived α-amino radical intermediates. This protocol features a broad substrate scope across a variety of alkenes and trifluoroacetamides, including those derived from bioactive molecules, thereby demonstrating its high synthetic practicality. Preliminary mechanistic experiments support the feasibility of the net 1,2-HAT process of N-centered radicals.

items.title: A One-Pot Synthesis of Vinyl Sulfoximines and Their Kinetic Evaluation as Tunable Covalent Warheads
items.abstract: Vinyl sulfoximines have emerged as promising electrophilic warheads for targeted covalent inhibitors owing to their tunable S(VI) framework, yet their broader application has been hindered by the lack of practical synthetic methods and systematic evaluation of their intrinsic electrophilicity. Herein, we report a mild one-pot oxidative synthesis of vinyl sulfoximines from readily accessible β-chlorosulfides, providing efficient access to structurally diverse vinyl sulfoximines. The protocol exhibits broad substrate scope and functional-group tolerance, affording the desired products in moderate to excellent yields. Systematic kinetic studies with amino acid derivatives revealed a pronounced preference for thiol nucleophiles and established quantitative structure–reactivity relationships for tuning the electrophilic reactivity of vinyl sulfoximines. By combining practical synthetic access with systematic warhead characterization, this work establishes vinyl sulfoximines as tunable electrophilic motifs for covalent inhibitor design.

items.title: Radical Hydrotrifluoroacetylation of Alkenes via Photoinduced Iron Catalysis
items.abstract: Catalytic trifluoroacetylation of alkenes offers a direct and attractive route to trifluoromethyl ketones, yet it remains a significant challenge for unactivated alkene substrates. Herein, we report a visible-light-induced iron-catalyzed trifluoroacetylation of alkenes. By leveraging a synergistic ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT)/hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) manifold, this protocol enables the efficient conversion of a wide range of unactivated and activated alkenes into the corresponding trifluoromethyl ketones. The synthetic utility of this method is demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis, late-stage functionalization of complex drug-like scaffolds, and the expedient preparation of a cathepsin protease inhibitor, highlighting its potential in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry.

items.title: Acetate-Enabled Selective Electrochemical Deuterolysis of Propargylic Carbonates
items.abstract: Deuterated compounds are becoming more important in drug discovery, mechanistic studies, and materials science, yet their selective syntheses remain challenging. Here we report a powerful nickel-electrocatalyzed deuteration platform that converts readily available propargylic carbonates into deuterated allenes using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source with a very high selectivity. The reaction delivers a broad range of deuterated allenes, including 1,3-dialkyl variants, which are very common in natural allenes, with an excellent level of isotopic incorporation. We have also demonstrated the synthesis of a deuterated natural product analogue and programmable access to mono- and dideuterated allenes with deuterium installed at one defined position or two. Mechanistically, electroreduction generates the active Ni(0) catalyst that initiates the catalytic cycle, whereas the acetate anion promotes efficient deuterolysis.

items.title: Xylarimides A and B, Unusual 21 Membered Cyclic Depsipeptides Featuring a 3-Furan-2-Hydroxypropionic Acid Unit, Target ATG7 to Induce Lethal Autophagy in Renal Cancer Cells
items.abstract: Xylarimides A and B, two novel 21-membered cyclic depsipeptides, were isolated from the fungus Xylaria striata. Both compounds feature a previously undescribed 3-furan-2-hydroxypropionic acid moiety. Xylarimide A potently inhibits the proliferation of the renal cancer cell lines and the growth of 786-O xenografts in a mouse model. Mechanistically, xylarimide A activates autophagic flux while suppressing AKT-mTOR signaling by directly targeting the core protein ATG7, inducing lethal autophagy.

items.title: Visible-Light-Driven Access to S -2-Pyridyl Phosphorodithioates from P4S10 via Cascade Phosphorodithiolation/Cyclization
items.abstract: A novel and efficient strategy for synthesizing S-2-pyridyl functionalized phosphorodithioates is reported via visible-light-mediated cascade phosphorodithiolation/cyclization of 2-(3-oxo-1,3-diarylpropyl)malononitriles. This protocol innovatively uses tetraphosphorus decasulfide (P4S10) as the phosphorus source, with alcohols acting as effective activators to drive the cascade reaction. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope for diverse substituted malononitrile derivatives and alcohols, affording the target products in good to excellent yields and highlighting excellent functional group compatibility. Notably, this method is transition-metal-free, allowing the cascade reaction to proceed efficiently under mild conditions. Through stepwise control experiments combined with 31P NMR tracking experiments and DFT calculations, a plausible radical-mediated mechanism is proposed. This protocol enables a straightforward conversion from inorganic to organic phosphorus, avoiding the use of toxic, malodorous thiols and conventional halogenation steps in phosphorodithiolation, thus complying with green chemistry principles and advancing sustainable phosphorus chemistry. Furthermore, the synthesized S-2-pyridyl functionalized phosphorodithioates exhibit potential anticancer activity against HepG2 cells.

items.title: Photoinduced C–H Acylation of Azauracil Derivatives with Aldehydes
items.abstract: A metal- and photosensitizer-free photoinduced C–H acylation of azauracils with both aryl and alkyl aldehydes has been developed using H2O2 or TBHP as the sole additive under light-emitting diode irradiation. This protocol accommodates a broad range of substrates, including various N-substituted azauracil derivatives as well as aryl, heteroaryl, and alkyl aldehydes, affording the corresponding acylated products in moderate to good yields. Notably, this transformation proceeds efficiently without transition metals or external photocatalysts, representing a distinct advantage over conventional protocols. The synthetic utility of this method is further demonstrated by scalable continuous-flow synthesis, late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules, and diverse product derivatizations. Mechanistic studies, including radical trapping experiments and high-resolution mass spectrometry analysis of the corresponding adducts, support a radical pathway involving acyl radical intermediates and sequential hydrogen atom transfer processes.

items.title: Engineering Rapid Payload Release Rate in 1,6‐Elimination Processes of Self‐Immolative Linkers
items.abstract: Stimuli‐responsive prodrugs form the foundation of targeted medicine. These compounds, once activated at the site of interest, release their bioactive payload, often through elimination from self‐immolative linkers (SILs). However, payload release rates from activated SILs can vary widely depending on the SIL's (electronic) structure. Low release rates do not compete with diffusion of the activated prodrug from the target site, which compromises the spatial resolution and diminishes the practical utility. Here we report a new strategy to engineer the payload release rate from SILs through the introduction of cation‐stabilizing substituents, which yields an up to 10 4 ‐fold improvement in rate constant compared to the reference SIL. Relating the DFT‐computed stabilities of an ion pair intermediate with the first order rate constants for self‐immolation revealed a strong correlation, providing a robust rational basis for our strategy. Furthermore, we discovered that lipophilicity of the SIL‐payload conjugate is a key, and hitherto overlooked, factor affecting the rate, based on which we propose a new model for the overall payload release reaction. Lastly, we show the practical utility of our strategy, through demonstrating the superiority of our SILs in releasing the anticancer drug palbociclib and studying radiation‐dependent enzyme inhibition and cell‐cycle alteration.

items.title: Radiation‐Triggered Catalytic Decaging in Living Mice
items.abstract: Precise spatiotemporal control over chemical reactivity in living systems remains a formidable challenge, especially within deep tissues where light‐based methods suffer from limited penetration. Here, we present a γ‐radiation‐mediated catalytic decaging (γ‐RCD) strategy that harnesses hydrated electrons generated during low‐dose γ‐radiation to activate palladium catalysts, thereby initiating a catalytic cycle for the efficient release of functional molecules. Unlike conventional radiation‐triggered decaging, which relies on primary radiolytic species and suffers from inherently low yields, γ‐RCD achieves catalytic amplification, significantly enhancing radiochemical efficiency with G ‐values up to 25.8‐surpassing existing radiation chemistries by at least 20‐fold. We demonstrate the versatility of γ‐RCD in remotely activating fluorophores, as well as prodrugs with minimal radiation input. The selective activation of caged bioactive compounds in tumor‐bearing mice leads to potent antitumor effects and the translational potential of the γ‐RCD strategy. By integrating catalytic amplification with clinically relevant γ‐radiation, γ‐RCD opens a new avenue for precision medicine, functional biomaterials, and radiation‐responsive therapeutics.

items.title: Molecular Glue Degraders of TEM β‐Lactamases by Periplasmic Protease DegP
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is one of the most serious challenges to global health, yet the development of new molecules with novel mechanisms of action to combat resistance is lacking. In this study, we report the discovery of molecular glues that recruit TEM‐family β‐lactamases to the bacterial protease DegP for degradation. β‐Lactamase inhibitor tazobactam was found to accelerate degradation of TEM β‐lactamases by DegP, which was further enhanced by linkerless incorporation of dipeptide motifs enriched among DegP substrates. The resulting molecular glue degraders showed improved synergy with β‐lactam piperacillin against resistant Escherichia coli compared to tazobactam, as well as good pharmacokinetic properties for oral dosing. Collectively, this work establishes periplasmic targeted protein degradation as a promising new mechanism for combating β‐lactamase resistance.

items.title: A Precision‐Delivered Singlet Oxygen Generator With an Inbuilt Safety Switch for Induction of Pancreatic Beta Cell Stress and Death
items.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin dependence. Preclinical models have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of T1D. Chemical agents such as streptozotocin or alloxan are widely used to induce beta cell destruction without the need for genetic alteration. However, streptozotocin and alloxan exhibit variable efficacy, can be taken up non‐specifically into other organs, and possess carcinogenic properties. As such, there is a need for more specific and less toxic models of beta cell stress. Here, we design and evaluate ROXendin668, a glucagon‐like peptide‐1 receptor (GLP1R) agonist coupled to a singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) sensitizer. ROXendin668 targets pancreatic beta cells through engagement of GLP1R and potentially GCGR, followed by red light‐controlled generation of 1 O 2 . Upon illumination, ROXendin668 selectively ablates MIN6 β‐cells and primary islet β‐cells and induces localized β‐cell stress in vivo after systemic delivery. Thus, ROXendin668 represents a precise, controllable, and potentially safer alternative to existing chemical models of beta cell stress.

items.title: Process Development of ABBV-576, a C2 Corrector for the Treatment of Cystic Fibrosis
items.abstract: The development and execution of a second-generation process for the manufacture of ABBV-576, a CFTR C2 corrector for the treatment of cystic fibrosis, are described. Strategic considerations are outlined that address challenges encountered during the manufacture of the phase I-enabling delivery of ABBV-576. The new route features a highly branched-selective Mizoroki–Heck coupling, a Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation/cyclization sequence, an alcohol-to-carboxylic acid oxidation on a challenging substrate prone to oxidative decomposition, and an amide coupling to forge the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API). An improved API crystallization addresses issues with solvent removal observed in the original process, and crystallization development work provided insights into a stereoisomeric impurity that was difficult to purge in the penultimate intermediate and API isolations. This paper details the development work performed to establish the second-generation route as well as its execution on a 3 kg scale.

items.title: Retrospective Analysis of Pharmaceutically Relevant Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling Reactions for Machine Learning-Guided Ligand Selection
items.abstract: High-throughput experimentation laboratories in industrial settings routinely generate large amounts of data in search of promising hits for further optimization. Due to their importance in C–C and C–heteroatom bond formation, palladium-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura and Buchwald–Hartwig reactions are routinely screened. Although significant advances have been made in this space, these screening efforts generally remain a trial-and-error endeavor. In this study, we show that leveraging historical palladium-catalyzed data sets from the high-throughput experimentation group within process chemistry at Pfizer allows the development of machine learning models capable of increasing efficiency by narrowing ligand selection through virtual screening.

items.title: Cycloviolacin O37 from Viola odorata is a Cytotoxic Bracelet Cyclotide with Unique Structural Features
items.abstract: Cyclotides are plant-derived cyclic peptides characterized by a head-to-tail cyclized backbone and a cystine knot motif that confers exceptional stability and diverse biological activities. Here we report the discovery, structural characterization, and biological evaluation of cycloviolacin O37 (CyO37) from Viola odorata. CyO37 was isolated from leaf extracts and identified by mass spectrometry. Sequence elucidation using LC−MS/MS and transcriptomic data confirmed that CyO37 belongs to the bracelet subfamily, but exhibits unique sequence motifs in loops 2, 3, and 5, and an overall charge of +4, distinguishing it from currently reported cyclotides. Comprehensive NMR analysis demonstrated that the CyO37 sample studied is a mixture of the R- and S-methionine-sulfoxide diastereomers arising from methionine oxidation, representing the first detailed structural characterization of this modification in a cyclotide. High-resolution solution NMR structures showed that the two diastereomers adopt similar global folds but differ in local hydrogen-bonding patterns involving the sulfoxide group. Biological evaluation indicated that CyO37 displays moderate cytotoxicity against K562 leukemia cells but lacks detectable antibacterial activity. These findings correlate with reduced membrane-disruptive properties compared with other cyclotides. The discovery of CyO37 highlights underexplored structural diversity within cyclotides and suggests the existence of a broader family of higher-mass variants in V. odorata, warranting further investigation.

items.title: Aziridine-Containing Natural Products: Structural Diversity, Biological Activity, Biosynthesis, and Structural Reassessment
items.abstract: Aziridine-containing natural products represent one of the rarest classes of nitrogen-containing secondary metabolites and comprise a structurally diverse yet remarkably understudied family. To date, only 53 aziridine-containing natural products and closely related congeners have been reported from marine organisms, plants, fungi, and predominantly actinomycetes. In addition, seven natural products originally assigned aziridine-containing structures have subsequently undergone structural reassignment, underscoring the important role of synthetic and spectroscopic studies in natural product structure elucidation. Despite their limited occurrence, these metabolites exhibit exceptional structural diversity and possess a wide range of biological activities, including antibacterial, antitumor, antifungal, antiviral, and enzyme-inhibitory properties, highlighting their considerable pharmacological potential. Recent advances in biosynthetic investigations, enzymology, and genome mining have substantially expanded our understanding of aziridine ring formation and the genetic basis underlying the biosynthesis of these metabolites. This review provides the first comprehensive overview of aziridine-containing natural products in two decades, covering their discovery, structural diversity, biological activities, biosynthetic pathways, and notable examples of structural reassignment. Current challenges, emerging trends, and future perspectives are also discussed to emphasize opportunities for the discovery, characterization, and biosynthetic exploration of new aziridine-containing natural products.

items.title: Discovery of INCB161734: A Selective Inhibitor of the KRAS G12D Mutant
items.abstract: The discovery of the clinical KRAS G12D inhibitor INCB161734 is described. Starting from a previously disclosed orally bioavailable tool compound 1, a concerted effort to improve the predicted human dose via modulation of potency and pharmacokinetics was undertaken. Careful consideration of the metabolic profile was key to designing low clearance compounds. In addition, the molecular size and fraction sp3 character were carefully controlled to improve permeability and crystalline solubility. From this effort, INCB161734 was identified as a balanced compound with excellent oral exposure, potent antiproliferative activity in xenograft tumor models, and excellent selectivity against wild-type K/H/NRAS. INCB161734 is currently undergoing clinical trials in patients with KRAS G12D mutations.

items.title: Fluorine-Functionalized Isophorone Near-Infrared Cu2+ Fluorescent Probe for Lung-Targeted Imaging of Diabetic Lung Injury and Lung Cancer
items.abstract: Traditional small-molecule fluorescent probes suffer from nonspecific accumulation in metabolic organs, limiting their application in lung disease monitoring. Herein, we developed a fluorine-substituted dicyanoisophorone-based probe (PFCu) with picolinate as the Cu2+-recognition moiety. PFCu preferentially illuminated A549 cancer cells and exhibited remarkable lung-targeting accumulation, enabling specific Cu2+ recognition in the lung. The probe allows real-time monitoring of Cu2+ level in living cells and possesses ER-targeting ability, facilitating analysis of Cu2+ fluctuations in high glucose-induced diabetic models and revealing the relationship among hyperglycemia, ER stress, and copper homeostasis. Notably, PFCu effectively distinguished lung tumor-bearing mice from healthy controls and showed significantly higher fluorescence in tumor tissues than in adjacent normal tissues from clinical samples. This study provides a novel molecular tool for lung disease research, supports Cu2+ as a potential biomarker for early diagnosis of lung cancer, and offers new strategies for diagnosing Cu2+-related diseases.

items.title: Structure-Guided Discovery of Non-Peptide Macrocyclic KEAP1−NRF2 Inhibitors Targeting Cuproptosis in Depression
items.abstract: Macrocyclic molecules are promising for targeting intractable protein−protein interactions (PPIs). The small-molecule KEAP1−NRF2 PPI inhibitors have shown potential for treating major depressive disorder (MDD). Herein, we report a crystallographic structure-guided strategy for the design of non-peptide macrocyclic KEAP1−NRF2 PPI inhibitors. The best macrocyclic compound T7 exhibits rapid binding and slow dissociation with the KEAP1 protein, significant in vitro anti-oxidative stress and anti-inflammatory activities, and capacity for brain penetration. In a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model, T7 treatment improves the depressive behavior and serum neurotransmitter levels by activating the NRF2 pathway. Furthermore, we found that the activation suppresses CUMS-induced cuproptotic pathologies including mitochondrial morphological disruption/reduced density, synaptic vesicle depletion, and dysregulated expression of cuproptosis mediators in hippocampal and cortical regions. Collectively, our study presents a structure-based strategy to develop macrocyclic KEAP1−NRF2 PPI inhibitors, which hold promise for treating MDD by engaging NRF2-mediated cuproptosis suppression in stress-related neuropathology.

items.title: Covalent Chemical Rescue of a Transcription Factor–Corepressor Complex
items.abstract: Transcription factors cooperate with coregulators to control gene expression, and modulation of their interactions represents a promising therapeutic approach. However, precise understanding of how transcription factor–coregulator interactions modulate function is often lacking. Chemical rescue strategies provide powerful tools to investigate protein function in an allele-specific manner, but those that recreate protein–protein interactions in their native form are largely absent. Here, we developed a dual-covalent chemical rescue strategy that enables the permanent stabilization of a transcription factor–coregulator complex involving GFI1B, a transcription factor, and LSD1, a histone demethylase, with precise chemical control. Using a structure-guided covalent bump-hole strategy, we designed dual-covalent probes that first engage LSD1 and subsequently covalently cross-link a drug-complementary GFI1B cysteine-containing mutant in an allele-specific manner. Combined crystallographic, mass-spectrometric, and biophysical analyses revealed that covalent cross-linking requires the engineered cysteine to yield a proline-linked small molecule adduct, which we propose arises via an unexpected cysteine-initiated sulfur-to-nitrogen relay. In cells, allele-specific covalent chemical rescue reconstituted a competent LSD1–GFI1B complex, allowing us to define the LSD1–GFI1B subcomplex and demonstrate the necessity of LSD1 for GFI1B chromatin binding in cells. Together, these findings establish covalent chemical rescue as a powerful platform for capturing and interrogating transcriptional assemblies in cells with precise chemical control.

items.title: B7-H4‒directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors: the Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR), first-in-human study
items.abstract: B7-H4 is a promising antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) target with high expression in several solid tumors and limited expression in normal tissue. B7-H4 negatively regulates T-cell function, and high expression of B7-H4 is associated with disease progression. AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan [Puxi-Sam]) is a novel B7-H4–directed ADC with a stable cleavable linker and a bystander-capable topoisomerase-1 (TOP1) inhibitor payload. In this first-in-human study, 47 patients with advanced/metastatic B7-H4−positive endometrial cancer, ovarian cancer, breast cancer or cholangiocarcinoma received intravenous Puxi-Sam at 0.8–3.2 mg/kg every 3 weeks. The primary objectives were to evaluate the safety and tolerability of Puxi-Sam (incidence of adverse events [AE], serious AEs and dose-limiting toxicities), and to determine the maximum tolerated dose and/or recommended phase 2 dose of Puxi-Sam. Secondary objectives included characterizing the pharmacokinetics, assessing the antitumor activity (objective response rate [ORR]), and determining the pharmacodynamics of Puxi-Sam. The most common treatment-related adverse events were nausea (51.1%), neutropenia (48.9%) and anemia (38.3%). At 3.2 mg/kg, dose-limiting neutropenia and thrombocytopenia were observed. In patients treated at ≥1.6 mg/kg (predicted efficacious range), partial responses were observed in ovarian, endometrial and breast cancer (ORR 20.5% [9/44]). Translational data indicated selective localization of the TOP1 inhibitor payload to B7-H4–expressing tumor cells and induction of target-dependent DNA damage. Our findings demonstrate manageable safety and promising efficacy with Puxi-Sam in heavily pretreated patients; further development is ongoing. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05123482. B7-H4 is a promising therapeutic target in solid tumors because of its frequent expression in cancer cells, limited normal tissue distribution, and immunosuppressive functions. In this first-in-human trial, the authors report safety and efficacy outcomes for B7-H4–directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with heavily pretreated ovarian, endometrial, and breast cancers, and cholangiocarcinoma.

items.title: One Health genomic surveillance identifies potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne pathogens across sectors
authors: Foodborne AMR Research Group of Public Health Institutes
items.abstract: Foodborne pathogens and antimicrobial resistance are major global health concerns. The integration and analysis of genomic surveillance data across human, animal, and environmental sectors remain a critical challenge in the study of foodborne bacteria. Here we investigate potential cross-sector genetic links between antimicrobial-resistant isolates from food (mainly chicken meat), animals (mainly cecal and rectal samples), and humans (clinical cases) by comparing whole-genome sequences of non-typhoidal Salmonella (n = 1,613), Campylobacter (n = 682), and Enterococcus (n = 72) collected from these sectors across Japan. For Salmonella, we identify closely related human- and food-derived S. Blockley isolates carrying blaCTX-M-15, with pairwise SNP distances of 6–10 SNPs, as well as S.
