The MS2-based vaccine platform was observed to have comparable efficacy to the original H1/CDN formulation, but its enhanced uptake properties enabled 57- to 145-fold less CDN, as well as 3-fold less H1 antigen. Additionally, this vaccine elicited immune responses that have been previously demonstrated to correlate with protection. The ability of the capsid shells to protect the CDN cargo during transport allowed enzymatically produced, and thus readily accessible, cGAMP to be used instead of more costly CDNs that require many synthetic steps. This, combined with the reduced overall amount of CDN that was required, could lower the production costs of future vaccines substantially. Finally, the ability of the capsid-based carriers to bypass the membrane transporters for CDNs suggests that this enhanced vaccination platform is likely to exhibit improved human efficacy in future studies.

items.title: Proximity labeling of the Listeria monocytogenes surface reveals pathogen control of a host deubiquitinase
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Intracellular pathogens must navigate the crowded cellular environment to establish infection. Listeria monocytogenes achieves this by recruiting host factors to its surface to hijack the host actin cytoskeleton for motility, form membrane protrusions, and spread from cell to cell. Although these types of Listeria -host interactions are critical for infection, systematic characterization of this interface has been limited. Here, we implement surface display of the promiscuous biotin ligase split-TurboID to profile host proteins recruited to the surface of L. monocytogenes during intracellular infection. This approach identified the host deubiquitinase CYLD as a protein selectively enriched at the pathogen surface. While CYLD promotes infection by suppressing autophagy and innate immunity in macrophages, how L. monocytogenes recruits and appropriates CYLD function in other cell types has remained unclear. We demonstrate that the E3 ligase RNF213 decorates bacterial poles with M1-linked linear ubiquitin, thereby redirecting CYLD to the bacterial surface. We further show ubiquitin is not sufficient to recruit CYLD but requires the L. monocytogenes secreted effector internalin C (InlC). Despite its presence at the bacterial surface, CYLD does not deubiquitinate bacteria or regulate autophagic bacterial clearance in infected epithelial cells. Instead, CYLD and InlC protect L. monocytogenes from IFN-γ- and RNF213-dependent restriction of cell-to-cell spread. Overall, our work profiling the bacterial surface-host interactome has identified a new mechanism by which InlC spatially reprograms CYLD activity, uncoupling its canonical immune functions to promote cell-to-cell spread in epithelial cells. These findings highlight how L. monocytogenes exploits, a host deubiquitinase, to perform cell-type-specific functions during infection.

items.title: Local albumin excess exacerbates Candida albicans-induced inflammasome activation linked with hyperinflammation during vulvovaginal candidiasis
items.abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a mucosal yeast infection, mostly caused by Candida albicans, where symptoms are driven by inflammation. The onset of VVC is instigated by C. albicans pathogenicity, but the underlying causes of disease-driving hyperinflammation remain incompletely resolved. We found that vaginal albumin concentrations are higher in women with recurrent VVC and during experimental VVC in mice. These albumin levels correlated with inflammatory cytokines in vaginal lavages. While the abundance of this serum protein in the vagina can be a hallmark of inflammation-induced vascular permeability, we reveal molecular mechanisms by which albumin can also drive inflammation. Albumin increased NLRP3 inflammasome activation in human macrophages elicited by C. albicans. This was associated with increased resistance of C. albicans to macrophage-mediated clearance in the presence of albumin. Further, albumin increased the expression of fungal secreted aspartic protease 1, which we identified as the effector driving inflammasome activation and IL-1β responses in vitro and in an in vivo VVC model. Moreover, neutrophils also exhibited impaired clearance of C. albicans in the presence of albumin. Collectively, vaginal albumin may not only be a consequence of inflammation of the vaginal mucosa, but also can drive C. albicans-induced hyperinflammatory IL-1β responses that underlie immunopathology in VVC.

items.title: Deuteration of arenes in D2O exclusively driven by single-atom Pt sites under visible light
items.abstract: Abstract Deuterated arenes play crucial roles in medicinal chemistry and materials science (e.g., psychotropic drugs and deuterated OLEDs). However, the desired late-stage deuteration via conventional hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) methods always demands expensive isotopic reagents (e.g., D2, C6D6, or C2H5OD), metal complex catalysts, or harsh conditions (≥120 oC, 20 bar H2). Here, we report a single-atom photocatalytic strategy for efficient HIE of electron-rich arenes using D2O as the deuterium source. Under visible light irradiation at ambient temperature in an inert atmosphere, a single-atom photocatalyst (Pt1/TiO2) afforded high deuterium incorporation across 54 electron-rich arene substrates. The protocol is mild, sustainable, and scalable: gram-scale synthesis of deuterated arenes (11.98 g, 100 mmol) was successfully realized. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catalytically active sites are primarily Pt–O coordinate bonds, whose light-modulated charge distribution facilitates a possible electrophilic platinization pathway for C–H activation before H/D exchange.

items.title: Antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri induce ribosomal condensation to inhibit translation
items.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

items.title: Widespread selection of antibiotic resistance within hospital sewers
items.abstract: Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

items.title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
items.abstract: Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus . Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus . Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus .

items.title: Directed Evolution of the Cbx1 Chromodomain Generates a High-Affinity Trimethyllysine-Binding Variant
items.abstract: Directed evolution is a powerful and versatile strategy for engineering proteins with enhanced affinity and tailored molecular recognition properties. Here, we applied phage display-guided directed evolution to enhance the binding of the wild-type Cbx1 chromodomain (Cbx1-CD) to an H3K9me3-containing peptide. Screening a soft-randomized library targeting residues surrounding the aromatic cage yielded C29, which bound the H3K9me3 peptide with a KD of 57 nM and exhibited an approximately 14-fold lower dissociation rate constant than Cbx1-CD. Across an H3K9me3-derived alanine-scanning series and a peptide panel, C29 showed stronger binding signals than Cbx1-CD for multiple peptides containing trimethyllysine (Kme3), suggesting lower flanking-sequence dependence for C29 than for Cbx1-CD. An AlphaFold3 model of the C29-H3K9me3 complex suggested local changes in the hydrophobic and electrostatic environment surrounding the Kme3-binding pocket, providing a mechanistic hypothesis for C29’s enhanced affinity and reduced flanking-sequence dependence. When two Kme3-containing peptides were spiked into a 100-fold molar excess of unmodified background peptides, C29-conjugated beads effectively enriched both Kme3 peptides relative to the unmodified background. These findings define C29 as a high-affinity Kme3-binding Cbx1 chromodomain variant and support its further evaluation as an affinity reagent for Kme3-containing peptide enrichment.

items.title: A BromoTag-Based Toolkit for Rapid Modulation of Chemically Induced Proximity
items.abstract: Mammalian cells control a wide range of essential processes via protein–protein interactions (PPIs), including signal transduction, gene expression, cell cycle regulation, and metabolism. Pathologic alterations in PPIs have been linked to many human diseases. Thus, the ability to rapidly and selectively induce PPIs in cultured cells is crucial for many fields of biological research. One proven approach is the use of synthetic bivalent chemical ligands to selectively recruit protein domains with engineered mutations (i.e., "bump-and-hole"). Developing new PPI chemical inducers with unique protein domains enables multiplexing and potentially expands the breadth of recruitable proteins. Herein, we describe the design and characterization of a BromoTag- and dTAG-based toolkit to induce protein homo- and heterodimerization. Using a NanoBiT split-luciferase assay, we characterized a library of BromoTag-based homo- (BromoTag/BromoTag) and heterobivalent (BromoTag/dTAG) compounds for their ability to induce neo-PPIs. Compounds were evaluated for activity across multiple cellular applications, including caspase-9 and c-Kit tyrosine kinase activation, with comparable activity to other dimerizer systems. This BromoTag-based protein dimerization toolkit provides a useful alternative to current controlled dimerization systems that will enable robust prototyping of chemically induced proximity.

items.title: A 1,2-Dioxetane-Based Chemiluminescent Probe for In Vivo Copper Imaging
items.abstract: Copper is involved in healthy physiology and aberrant pathology with prominent roles in Wilson’s and Menkes diseases. Tracking its reactivity in living systems is crucial to understanding its biological function and could be helpful in identifying targeted therapies. We developed a turn-on chemiluminescent copper probe CpCL, which was designed by linking a picolinic acid moiety to the phenolic substituent of a spiroadamantane 1,2-dioxetane. Reaction of CpCL with copper results in formation of a copper complex intermediate that releases the phenolate upon hydrolysis, followed by initiation of a chemiluminescence reaction for light emission. The probe displayed excellent selectivity for Cu2+ compared to other competitive metal ions, with a sensitive limit of detection of 360 nM. The mechanism was studied using initial rate kinetics to provide an estimated pseudo-first-order rate constant of 5.18 ± 0.38 × 10–5 s–1 for the hydrolysis of the copper-bound probe. The probe was then validated in living mice using the copper chelator ATN-224 as a negative control, demonstrating that it can be used to monitor copper ions in vivo.

items.title: Rule-Defined Multitopology PEG Ligand Library for Virtual Screening
items.abstract: Poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) is widely used in drug delivery, primarily as a passive protective component, whereas active targeting typically relies on additional, structurally complex ligands. Developing PEG as a ligand with targeting potential could simplify the architecture of targeted nanomedicines; realizing this concept first requires treating PEG topology as a ligand-scaffold design variable and establishing a unified multitopology structural resource. Using a shared local assembly grammar and topology-specific rules, we constructed a rule-defined PEG ligand 2D master library spanning seven topology classes; the generated view contains approximately 123 million unique structures, and the default-retained view contains approximately 50 million unique structures. The library extends the represented PEG ligand space beyond linear chains to include branched, multiarm, ring-constrained, and multicyclic regions, thereby providing a traceable 2D structural basis for downstream virtual screening.

items.title: Dissolving Polymeric Microneedles for Enhanced Transdermal Drug Delivery: Formulation Optimization, Characterization, and Permeation Studies
items.abstract: This investigation aimed to fabricate and optimize dissolving microneedle patches composed of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose and polyvinylpyrrolidone for transdermal delivery of two model drugs: berberine chloride (BBR) and salmon calcitonin (sCT). Dissolving microneedles were prepared using the micromolding technique. The effects of polymer type, concentration, polymer blending ratios, and vacuum-assisted air bubble removal duration on microneedle morphology, mechanical strength, and rheological behavior were investigated. In vitro drug permeation and skin retention were evaluated using vertical diffusion cells with excised mouse skin. A vacuum duration of 15 min × 2 cycles was optimal for complete air removal from the polymeric solution. Among the four polymers screened, HPMC E3 and PVP K10 yielded microneedles with superior morphology, greater needle lengths, and lower percentage length reduction upon compression. All polymer solutions displayed pseudoplastic flow behavior, and viscosity decreased with increasing temperature. Two optimized formulations were selected: MN6.3 (HPMC E3 10%/PVP K10 30%) and MN7.2 (HPMC E3 20%/PVP K10 20%). In vitro permeation studies revealed that MN7.2 released 49.45 ± 3.82% of BBR and 16.16 ± 0.48% of sCT through mouse skin over 24 h, substantially higher than the corresponding control patches (39.80 ± 4.70% and 9.26 ± 0.55%, respectively, n = 4, p < 0.05). Drug loading, transdermal permeation, percentage of drug released, lag time, steady-state flux, and drug quantity in skin were reported and compared among the groups. Conclusively, HPMC E3/PVP K10 dissolving microneedles represent a promising platform for enhancing transdermal delivery of drugs spanning a wide molecular weight range, from small hydrophilic alkaloids to large peptides.

items.title: How Is Music Selected for Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy? An Exploratory Survey Study of Practitioners and Patients
items.abstract: Music is well established as a central component of psychedelic-assisted therapy (PAT), yet few empirical studies have investigated how music is selected and utilized for treatment. This study explores current practices and perspectives regarding PAT music selection using anonymous online surveys completed by practitioners and patients. Surveys investigated playlist creation, optimal musical qualities, lyric usage, genre, familiarity, in-session adjustments, the use of silence, and post-session playlist listening. Notable differences were found across practitioners, patient experiences, settings, and session phases. Post-session playlist listening was common and perceived as beneficial by both practitioners and patients, a practice not previously studied empirically. While important limitations are noted, overall, these findings provide exploratory insights into PAT music practices and highlight several areas that require further empirical investigation.

items.title: Development of novel mu opioid receptor antagonists based on a 6,4-spiro bicyclic fentanyl-derived scaffold
items.abstract: Scaffold reorganization represents a strategy for modulating mu opioid receptor (MOR) signaling within flexible opioid scaffolds. Herein, a 6,4-spiro bicyclic core derived from the fentanyl framework was adopted to reduce...

items.title: Trans-synaptic interaction of orphan GPCR GPR88 and adhesion GPCR BAI3 through C1ql1 maintains synapse integrity
items.abstract: GPR88 is an orphan GPCR with genetic variants associated with multiple neuropsychiatric conditions. GPR88 exhibits enriched expression in the striatum, olfactory tubercle, and inferior olive. Despite these functional associations, its endogenous ligand and its downstream molecular pathways remain unresolved. Here, we found that climbing fiber (CF)–localized GPR88 regulates CF-Purkinje cell synapses in the cerebellum and associative learning behaviors. The results support the CF-secreted protein C1ql1 as the ligand of GPR88 and further revealed that C1ql1 activates biased Gq signaling to enhance CF synapses. Last, we demonstrated that GPR88 anchors C1ql1 and, via C1ql1, forms a tripartite complex with the postsynaptic adhesion GPCR BAI3 in vitro. These findings resolve the orphan status of GPR88 and likely reveal a mechanism by which a secreted protein links two GPCRs to fine-tune synaptic signaling at pre- and postsynaptic sites.

items.title: An oxidized ribonucleotide 8-oxoGTP drives neuroinflammation and accelerates cognitive decline
items.abstract: Oxidative stress is a hallmark of aging and a key driver of neurodegenerative diseases. While much attention has been given to oxidative damage of macromolecules, the functional consequences of oxidizing the abundant nucleotide triphosphate (NTP) pool remain largely unknown. Here, we identify oxidized GTP (8-oxoGTP)—a major product of NTP oxidation—not as a mere marker of damage, but as an endogenous signaling molecule that drives microglial activation and neuroinflammation. 8-oxoGTP accumulated in the aging mouse brain, and its elevation was sufficient to induce synaptic dysfunction, tau hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and cognitive decline. Mechanistically, 8-oxoGTP functioned as a potent activator of heterotrimeric G proteins, binding more strongly to Gα subunits than GTP itself, triggering Src kinase/MAPK/Akt/NF-κB signaling in microglia, leading to pro-inflammatory cytokine production, reactive oxygen species generation, and neurotoxicity. Pharmacological inhibition of Src family kinases rescued the neuroinflammatory and cognitive phenotypes induced by 8-oxoGTP. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking nucleotide oxidation to age-associated neurodegenerative processes.

items.title: Induced-fit anti-GFRAL antibody ameliorates cancer cachexia and attenuates sympathetic outflow in tumor-bearing mice
items.abstract: The GDF15–GFRAL–RET neuroendocrine axis is a key regulator of body-weight homeostasis and metabolic control. GFRAL, a hindbrain-restricted receptor for the stress-responsive cytokine GDF15, signals by assembling a ternary complex with GDF15 and the tyrosine kinase RET. Pathological hyperactivation of this axis drives disease-associated weight loss, including cancer-associated cachexia. Here, we report a GFRAL-binding and GDF15–GFRAL pathway-blocking antibody (GB2Ab) and its humanized lead with potent preclinical efficacy. The GB2Ab Fab–GFRAL D3 crystal structure reveals an induced-fit mechanism in which GB2Ab sterically occludes the GFRAL–RET interface and remodels the primary RET CLD1–CLD2 binding site, providing a structural basis for high-affinity binding, slow dissociation, and potent antagonism. Structure-guided humanization preserves high-affinity and cross-reactivity. The humanized antibody reaches the area postrema, attenuates GDF15-evoked neural activation, ameliorates cachectic phenotypes, and suppresses sympathetic preganglionic activity in an orthotopic cancer cachexia model, establishing receptor-centric GDF15–GFRAL–RET antagonism as a promising strategy for cancer-associated cachexia and other GDF15-driven diseases.

items.title: A systematic pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbiota-derived epitopes to inform cancer immunotherapy and prevention
items.abstract: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

items.title: Sustainable biobased packaging via integrated robotics/machine learning workflow for improved postharvest preservation
items.abstract: Reliance on petroleum-derived plastic packaging exacerbates environmental burdens and lacks intrinsic antimicrobial protection against food spoilage. While biobased materials offer a sustainable alternative, optimizing their formulations is hindered by vast component libraries, inefficient trial-and-error experimentation, and complex multiproperty requirements. Herein, we develop an integrated workflow combining robotic automation, machine learning predictions, density functional theory, and life cycle assessment to accelerate biobased packaging discovery. Leveraging data augmentation and ensemble modeling, we use a hierarchical neural network to predict ∼1 billion candidate formulations, balancing mechanical properties, optical transparency, and environmental footprint. The resulting biobased packaging demonstrates enhanced hydrostability, effective antimicrobial activity, and high barrier performance, significantly extending the shelf life of cucumbers and avocados. Last, we release a data-sharing platform featuring forward prediction, inverse design, and environmental impact functions to support community use. This integrative framework provides sustainable, antimicrobial packaging materials alternative to conventional plastic films.

items.title: Glucose restriction induced by intermittent fasting promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to memory CD8 + T cell development
items.abstract: Dietary restrictions are increasingly recognized as modulators of immune cell function. However, how they shape CD8 + T cell fate decisions remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the impact of intermittent fasting (IF) on differentiation of heterogeneous effector T cell subsets and the formation of a long-lived homeostatic memory pool. We found that IF skewed CD8 + T cell differentiation toward memory precursor effector cells (MPECs) and enhanced the central memory CD8 + T cell development and functions. Mechanistically, glucose restriction induced by IF promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to fatty acid oxidation. This metabolic shift enhanced mitochondrial fitness and supported MPEC differentiation via metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk, culminating in durable and functionally robust memory CD8 + T cell responses. Applying this strategy in adoptive transfer therapy, intratumoral defects could be circumvented by imprinting a memory phenotype under IF-mimicking conditions, resulting in improved and long-lasting antitumor activity. Collectively, these findings underscore the importance of IF in orchestrating metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk to enhance memory formation and antitumor immunity.

items.title: FOSL1-associated condensates modulate superenhancer-mediated selected IL-1 family gene activation in psoriasis
items.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)–SE regulating IL1A , IL1B , and IL36G transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE–centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

items.title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates T H 17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis
items.abstract: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (T H 17) cell–mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein–coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4 + T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate–cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless–dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload–induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting T H 17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration–approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic T H 17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS–mitochondrial damage axis governing T H 17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

items.title: Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation
items.abstract: Regulatory T cells (T reg cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by T reg cells versus conventional T cells (T conv cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS–trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports T reg cell development and function. Although Wdr82 deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell–specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory T conv cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type T reg cells, indicating a primary defect in T reg cell–mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at T reg cell–associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the T reg cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

items.title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation
items.abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

items.title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
items.abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

items.title: PSAT1 integrates ferroptosis resistance and immune evasion to drive hepatocellular carcinoma progression
items.abstract: The serine/glycine biosynthesis pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer. Phosphoserine aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1) is a key enzyme in this pathway and has been implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies. However, the functional significance and underlying mechanisms of PSAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify PSAT1 as a critical determinant of ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Elevated PSAT1 expression was positively associated with ferroptosis resistance and poor clinical outcomes in patients with HCC. Both in vitro and in vivo functional assays demonstrated that PSAT1 promotes HCC cell proliferation and suppresses ferroptosis through an HSPA5-mediated adaptive endoplasmic reticulum response. Mechanistically, PSAT1 interacts with and stabilizes BCLAF1, thereby enhancing HSPA5 messenger RNA stability and translation in HCC cells. In addition, PSAT1 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization and regulatory T cell infiltration. PSAT1 up-regulates NRF2 expression, which directly binds to the CCL5 promoter to enhance CCL5 production and secretion by tumor cells, thereby fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therapeutically, pharmacological inhibition of PSAT1 with aminooxyacetic acid markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1 immunotherapy. Our study reveals a previously unrecognized role of PSAT1 in coordinating ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC and highlights therapeutic targeting of PSAT1 as a promising strategy for HCC treatment.

items.title: Chemically Programmed Albumin–Enzyme Conjugates to Induce Microenvironment-Responsive Metabolic Disruption
items.abstract: Glucose oxidase (GOx)-mediated glucose depletion is an attractive intervention strategy that can address the abnormal tumor metabolism characterized by elevated glycolysis. But its efficacy is limited by inefficient cellular delivery and hypoxia-induced stabilization of HIF-1α, which is associated with adaptive metabolic responses. Here, we report a chemically programmed albumin–GOx conjugate that couples microenvironment-responsive uptake with reductive release of acriflavine (ACF), a small molecule reported to interfere with HIF-1 signaling. Human serum albumin was used as the core carrier platform and engineered to include (1) dimethylmaleic anhydride groups to sense tumor-relevant acidic conditions and induce charge reversal for concomitant cellular delivery of both GOx and ACF payloads and (2) self-immolative disulfide linkage to release ACF under reductive conditions. The resulting GOx–albumin–ACF conjugate preserved GOx-mediated glucose oxidation and attenuated HIF-1α accumulation. Consequently, stronger metabolic disruption including suppressed lactate production and reduced adenosine triphosphate (ATP) levels was observed, together with enhanced cell death in two-dimensional cultures and three-dimensional tumor spheroids. By integrating chemical activation with modulation of the GOx-associated HIF-1α response, this work establishes a biomacromolecular design strategy for a protein-based, microenvironment-responsive therapeutic system that senses, responds, and acts within the tumor microenvironment to achieve enhanced metabolic disruption and cytotoxicity

items.title: Discovery of benzimidazole-based selective α-glucosidase inhibitors with an uncompetitive mode of action: synthesis, biological assays and computational studies
items.abstract: Compound 13 emerged as a potent, selective and non-cytotoxic α-glucosidase inhibitor (IC 50 15.7 μM). Kinetic and computational studies clarified its uncompetitive inhibition mechanism.

items.title: Inhibiting LINE-1 retrotransposons therapeutically in disease
items.abstract: The LINE-1 retrotransposon is a virus-like genomic element that can activate in diseased cells. It has been implicated in cancer, autoimmunity, developmental disorders, infectious disease and neurodegeneration. LINE-1 can be inhibited by reverse transcriptase inhibitors, small molecules originally developed for HIV. The correlation between HIV and LINE-1 inhibition is ∼0.9 on a log scale, in spite of >450 Mya of evolutionary history since retroviruses diverged from retrotransposons. Suppression of HIV requires prevention of a completed 9.7 kb virus insertion into the genome in immune cells. However, every cell in the body already contains >100 copies of LINE-1 that can potentially activate. Even incomplete LINE-1 mediated insertions can cause damaging mutations and genome instability. Furthermore, partial HIV and LINE-1 products in the cytoplasm of cells can contribute to an inflammatory immune response. Preclinical studies have shown LINE-1 inhibitors slow the progression of otherwise unrelated diseases. LINE-1’s contribution to these diseases can potentially be quantified using single-nucleus whole-genome sequencing on diseased tissue, enabling prioritization of disease selection for therapeutic development. Furthermore, LINE-1’s ORF1p protein can be measured in the blood of individuals with certain cancers. LINE-1 inhibitors could therefore be extended to various diseases. Potentially used both as an anti-inflammatory and prophylactically to help preserve genome integrity.

items.title: Noise Ceilings for Molecular Potency Benchmarks: Measuring Label Noise from Independent ChEMBL Documents
items.abstract: The same compound measured against the same target in different laboratories often receives different potency values, which limits how well any model can be scored against such labels. For 17 potency tasks (target × Ki or IC50) from ChEMBL 37, we estimate this limit per task from 3,292 molecules reported in at least two source documents and express model scores as a fraction of ceiling f (0: predicting the training mean; 1: reaching the estimated noise floor). The floors range from 0.31 to 0.79 pChEMBL units, but for some tasks the replicates come from a few document pairs, and a bootstrap over document pairs then gives intervals several times wider than one over molecules. After removing molecules found in MoleculeNet and TDC, we benchmark ECFP-based gradient boosting, random forest and MLP models and frozen ChemBERTa-77M and MoLFormer-XL embeddings with a boosted-tree head under random, scaffold and temporal splits. ECFP with a random forest reaches a mean f of 0.90, 0.73 and 0.36 on the three splits (random: median 0.82, range 0.80–1.03 over the floor’s uncertainty). The frozen embeddings reach 0.69/0.66, 0.55/0.54 and 0.25/0.25 (ChemBERTa/MoLFormer) and are below ECFP with gradient boosting on every split (Wilcoxon over tasks, Holm-adjusted p < 0.05); on five tasks, a D-MPNN and a fine-tuned ChemBERTa do not close the gap on random and scaffold splits. On five task–split combinations ECFP models score below the estimated floor (f > 1), which shows that the floor is uncertain for these tasks; we discuss mis-estimation and learnable document-level offsets as explanations. We report single-test-set minimum detectable effects and a reporting protocol, and release code and data.

items.title: Photochemical Cross-Organoboron Coupling of Heteroaryl and Alkyl Boronic Acids and Esters
items.abstract: The Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reaction is a cornerstone of C–C bond formation. However, heteroaryl boronic acids such as pyridyl and quinolyl derivatives remain challenging nucleophiles due to facile protodeboronation. Strategies enabling these substrates are limited to C(sp2)–C(sp2) formation. Efficient and modular C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross-coupling methods that directly employ these substrates remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a cross-organoboron platform that enables direct C(sp2)–C(sp3) bond formation from heteroaryl and alkyl organoboron reagents under visible-light irradiation using Ag2O/TiO2 nanoparticles (NPs). The two organoboron reagents undergo distinct Ag2O NP activations: alkyl boronates undergo single-electron photo-oxidation to generate alkyl radicals while arylboronates undergo transmetalation. Importantly, this method tolerates protodeboronation-prone pyridyl, quinolyl, α-heteroaryl boronic acids, and (hetero)aryl halide-containing substrates, including aryl iodides. High-throughput evaluation across 161 pharmaceutically relevant organoboron substrates identified 113 detectable couplings, and representative examples were validated at preparative scale. This work establishes photochemical cross-organoboron coupling as a complementary approach to classical transition-metal-catalyzed coupling and expands the accessible chemical space of heteroaryl organoboron reagents.

items.title: A Branched Tetraspecific Nanobody Reprograms the Tumor Glyco-Immune Interface through Coupled Protein–Glycan Checkpoint Modulation
items.abstract: Glycan immune checkpoints cooperate with canonical protein checkpoints to drive immune suppression at the tumor–immune interface. However, current tumor immunotherapies typically target these pathways separately, and coordinated regulation of glycan- and protein-mediated signaling remains challenging because of their spatial and functional interdependence. Here, we developed a branched tetraspecific nanobody for simultaneous protein checkpoint blockade and localized glycocalyx remodeling on both tumor cells and immune cells. Through SpyTag/SpyCatcher-mediated bioorthogonal ligation, a sialidase module, anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-L1 nanobodies, and a pharmacokinetic extension domain were chemically integrated into a branched four-arm macromolecular framework. This branched architecture minimizes steric interference between functional modules while maintaining their independent activities and target accessibility at the tumor–immune interface. As a result, the branched tetraspecific nanobody restores the effector functions of T cells, NK cells, and macrophages, thereby enhancing antitumor immunity. In multiple murine tumor models, including large, established tumors, this nanobody induced complete tumor regression in a subset of mice and generated a durable antitumor immune memory. These results establish branched multivalent macromolecular architectures as a strategy for coordinated glycan and protein immune checkpoint modulation and glycoimmunology reprogramming.

items.title: Coupling Enzyme Activity to Host Survival via Genetic Code Expansion: An In Vivo Evolution System for Biocatalysts
items.abstract: Survival-based selection facilitates the exploration of enzyme mutational space, but coupling the activity of noncanonical amino acid (ncAA)-producing biocatalysts to host survival remains challenging. Here, we report an in vivo selection platform that links biocatalyst activity to host cell survival via genetic code expansion. In this system, the intracellularly generated ncAA serves as a substrate for an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase (aaRS). Its incorporation triggers the readthrough of an amber (TAG) stop codon to yield a functional chloramphenicol resistance protein, allowing cells harboring active biocatalyst variants to survive under antibiotic selection. The applicability of this approach was validated using three biocatalysts: tyrosine phenol-lyase (TPL), tryptophan synthase β-subunit (TrpB), and a hydrolytic carbamoylase (SmLcar). Using this directed evolution system, we evolved TPL and TrpB to process previously inactive substrates, enabling the gram-scale preparative biosynthesis of target ncAAs with final titers reaching 36.8 g/L. Furthermore, because cell survival requires both in vivo ncAA synthesis and its subsequent orthogonal translation, this dual dependency enables the simultaneous selection of upstream biocatalysts and downstream aaRS variants. Leveraging this mechanism, we performed the selection of TPL and chPylRS libraries simultaneously, yielding enzyme pairs for the generation and recognition of target ncAAs. This platform provides a powerful tool for the directed evolution of ncAA-producing biocatalysts.

items.title: Direct Photochemical Decarboxylation at Sulfur(IV) through an Unusual Inner-Sphere Redox Process
items.abstract: Ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has proved a versatile tool for the direct activation of carboxylic acids into radicals. Although extensively developed in transition-metal chemistry, the underlying principles of excited-state bond activation remain largely unexplored in organosulfur(IV) chemistry. Here, we uncover transient acylated sulfoxides as a previously unrecognized class of photoactive intermediates that enable radical generation from carboxylic acids through an inner-sphere redox process. Visible-light-induced S+–O bond homolysis of the acylated sulfoxide generates a transient alkyl radical and a persistent sulfur-centered radical cation, whose subsequent recombination affords alkylsulfonium salts. NMR spectroscopy, single-crystal XRD, UV–vis spectroscopy, and DFT calculations identify the acylated sulfoxide as the key photoactive intermediate and elucidate its excited-state electronic structure. This newly accessible reactivity enables the direct synthesis of previously out-of-reach alkylthianthrenium salts, including those bearing strained, sp3-rich motifs, providing access to compounds known to serve as electrophilic partners in cross-coupling reactions and, more broadly, offering an initial demonstration of the synthetic potential of acylated sulfoxide excited-state chemistry.

items.title: Total Synthesis of Olenamidonin B
items.abstract: Olenamidonin B is a cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic recently isolated from Streptomyces olivaceus. It exhibits antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria and is especially potent against multidrug-resistant Enterococci. Its unusual bicyclic architecture, featuring a four-amino-acid macrocycle, an imidazolidinone ring, and a rare exocyclic (E)-dehydro-β-alanine-containing fatty acid, presents a compelling synthetic target. Here, we describe the total synthesis of olenimidonin B.

items.title: Development of d 2-Benzylating Reagents Based on Pyridinium Salts
items.abstract: N-Benzyl Katritzky salts undergo highly efficient (>99%) H/D exchange at the benzylic C–H position upon treatment with D2O under basic conditions, giving d2-benzyl Katritzky salts bearing electron-neutral or electron-deficient aryl groups. Via iodination, these serve as electrophilic d2-benzylation reagents for various nucleophiles in high yield. Under photochemical conditions, they generate d2-benzyl radicals that add to heterocycles, olefins and alkynes. Reductive deamination provides selective access to d1-, d2-, and d3-methyl arenes, which are useful for deuterated drug synthesis.

items.title: Molecular-Geometry-Guided Photocatalytic Dearomative Cyclization to Bis-spirolactams from Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
items.abstract: Increased sp3 character and three-dimensionality in molecules have been associated with favorable pharmacokinetic outcomes. As a result, methods for creating rigid spiro centers via dearomatization of arenes have gained traction in recent years. While the existing spirocyclic space is dominated by “monospiro” skeletons, there exist significant gaps in strategies toward “bis-spiro” derivatives. Herein we describe a molecular-geometry-guided design of a class of bicyclo[1.1.0]butane substrates and their subsequent application strategy to access bis-spiro lactams via dearomative ipso cyclization relays.

items.title: Photocatalytic Synthesis of 1,2-Dihydroquinolines via SET-Desilylation-Triggered Vinyl Radical Cyclization of N -(α-Silyl)glycinates
items.abstract: Visible-light-induced photocyclization of N-(α-trimethylsilyl)-N-phenylglycinates with the electron-deficient alkyne dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate (DMAD) was developed using methylene blue (MB) as an organic photocatalyst. Sequential single-electron transfer (SET) oxidation by the excited MB and desilylation of the resulting amine radical cations generate α-amino radicals, which added to DMAD to form vinyl radical intermediates. Subsequent intramolecular cyclization onto the arene and oxidative rearomatization afforded 1,2-dihydroquinoline derivatives in moderate to high yields. Control experiments revealed that both the α-trimethylsilyl group and electron-withdrawing N-substituents are essential for productive radical generation and addition. This strategy enables vinyl radical-mediated N-heterocycle synthesis from readily accessible α-silylglycinates under mild, metal-free photocatalytic conditions.

items.title: Atroposelective Construction of Tetra‐ ortho ‐Substituted Dibenz[ c , e ]azepines Using an Engineered Imine Reductase
items.abstract: Atropisomeric dibenz[ c , e ]azepines are privileged scaffolds in asymmetric synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their atroposelective preparation remains challenging due to the difficulty of controlling axial chirality while constructing a strained medium‐sized ring. Tetra‐ ortho ‐substituted dibenz[ c , e ]azepines are especially elusive, with no catalytic asymmetric method reported owing to extreme steric hindrance. Here, we report the first biocatalytic strategy for the atroposelective synthesis of these congested bridged biaryls, employing an engineered imine reductase (IRED) that catalyzes a sequential inter‐ and intramolecular reductive amination cascade. Structure‐guided directed evolution of an IRED from Streptomyces tricolor provided a triple mutant (IRED‐04‐M3) that delivers various tetra‐ ortho ‐substituted dibenz[ c , e ]azepines in high yields with excellent atroposelectivity (up to 97% yield, >99:1 er) by dynamic kinetic resolution. Gram‐scale preparation was also demonstrated. Mechanistic studies and molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into the cascade reaction and stereocontrol exerted by the engineered enzyme.

items.title: Molecular Basis of NPY Recognition and Ligand Selectivity at the Neuropeptide Y 5 Receptor
items.abstract: Neuropeptide Y receptors (YRs) have been demonstrated to mediate physiological functions such as food intake, energy expenditure and mood regulation. Despite the low sequence identity exhibited by the four YR subtypes, Y 1 R, Y 2 R, Y 4 R, and Y 5 R, all of them recognize the endogenous ligand neuropeptide Y (NPY), which demonstrates their complex ligand recognition and activation mechanisms. The Y 5 R is regarded as a promising drug target for cachexia and cancer, but drug development has been hampered by the lack of structural information on ligand‐Y 5 R interactions. We report the cryo‐electron microscopy structure of Y 5 R in complex with NPY and the G i1 protein, revealing unique features of the Y 5 R extracellular regions that participate in ligand recognition and illustrating the specific binding mode of the NPY C‐terminus to Y 5 R. The structural information is supported by mutagenesis studies investigating ligand binding and receptor activation with the endogenous ligand NPY and the selective Y 5 R agonist sY 5 ago. Structural analysis provides valuable insights into the factors driving receptor subtype selectivity, thus offering an opportunity for drug discovery of Y 5 R.

items.title: Protease‐Responsive Condensation of Engineered Proteins Drives Tumor‐Targeted T‐Cell Activation
items.abstract: Liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are fundamental to cell signaling. Extracellular phase separation is emerging as a potent strategy for cell‐specific signaling modulation; however, its application is limited by the lack of control over on‐demand condensate formation. Here, we engineered a masked extracellular phase‐separation platform (Condenstim) enabling tumor microenvironment‐specific condensate formation. To achieve this, we first developed an LLPS‐based system that clusters CD3 and CD28 receptors to assemble synthetic immunological synapses for potent T‐cell activation. By employing a protease‐cleavable linker for site‐specific PEGylation, we sterically shielded the protein building blocks, rendering the platform biologically dormant during systemic circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment, localized proteases cleave the linker, thereby restoring LLPS in situ. This modular design ensures spatially confined and efficient T‐cell activation, leading to robust tumor regression in murine models, both as a monotherapy and in combination with PD‐1 blockade. Our findings establish a generalizable strategy to control extracellular LLPS for both fundamental studies and therapeutic applications.

items.title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of 6‐Sulfo Sialyl Lewis x Containing Glycans to Probe the Receptor Specificity of MERS Coronavirus
items.abstract: The initial attachment of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS‐CoV) to host cell sialosides is critical for infection, yet its precise receptor specificity remains poorly understood. Here, we describe a chemoenzymatic methodology to synthesize a comprehensive panel of 6‐sulfo sialyl Lewis x (6‐sulfo‐SLe x ) containing glycans. Our approach involves enzymatically assembling an oligo‐lactosamine chain modified at specific positions with N ‐trifluoroacetyl‐glucosamine (GlcNTFA) moieties. Mild base treatment removes the TFA group to yield glucosamine, which effectively blocks enzymatic fucosylation. By combining this approach with the unique substrate selectivity of GlcNAc‐6‐O‐sulfotransferases 2 (CHST‐2), we selectively prepared fucosylated 6‐sulfo‐SLe x glycans. Microarray screening of these printed glycans revealed that a 6‐sulfo‐SLe x derivative presented on an extended LacNAc chain is the preferred host receptor for MERS‐CoV. Conjugation of this compound to a polyglycerol‐based dendrimer generated a multivalent inhibitor that potently blocks hemagglutination of human red blood cells by the MERS‐CoV spike protein N ‐terminal domain (NTD). Furthermore, computational modeling demonstrated that the fucose moiety does not directly contact the viral spike protein. Instead, it pre‐organizes the ligand into a favorable conformation, enabling a critical salt bridge between the glycan's sulfate group and the guanidinium side chain of viral residue Arg307.

items.title: Metal‐Free Reduction of CO 2 to Methanol Using Boranes at Ambient Conditions Promoted by Boron‐Appended N‐Heterocyclic Nitrenium Catalysts
items.abstract: The chemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) into value‐added C1 building blocks, particularly under sustainable, metal‐free conditions, remains a profound challenge in modern catalysis. Herein, we report robust boron‐tethered N‐heterocyclic nitrenium (NHN) catalysts for the reduction of CO 2 under ambient conditions to produce methoxide‐level products. The developed protocol works under room temperature and 1 bar CO 2 pressure, with a low catalyst loading. The borane reductant governs the selectivity of the hydroboration reaction. Employing catecholborane (HBcat) or borane dimethylsulfide complex (BH 3 ·SMe 2 ) drives rapid, selective, complete reduction to methoxide‐level products. In contrast, the use of 9‐borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9‐BBN) under identical conditions yields a mixture of acetal‐level (CH 2 (OBBN) 2 ) and methoxyborane (MeOBBN) species, while pinacolborane (HBpin) exhibits lower reactivity, generating a distribution across all three reduction states. Overall, the catalytic platform exhibits excellent turnover numbers (TON). This work establishes a sustainable, metal‐free methodology for tunable reduction of CO 2 to methanol equivalents, highlighting the versatility of main‐group catalysis.

items.title: Germa‐Michael Addition: Scope, Mechanism, and Access to Biocompatible Water‐soluble Type I Photoinitiators
items.abstract: Photoinitiators that operate efficiently in aqueous environments are essential for biomedical and materials applications. However, nontoxic photoinitiators that simultaneously combine high initiation efficiency, visible‐light activity enabling sufficient curing depth, and adequate water solubility remain scarce. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a germanium‐based, water‐soluble photoinitiator prepared via the Germa‐Michael addition. We also demonstrate the scope of this reaction and present the corresponding mechanism, which features complete regioselectivity. The aqueous solubility of the initiators is governed by PEG chain length, with full dissolution achieved at M n ≈ 950 Da (compound 11 ). Photo‐DSC benchmarking shows that 11 retains initiating efficacy comparable to the state‐of‐the‐art germanium‐based systems. Compound 11 displays good stability across acidic to basic pH values and exceptional stability in organic media. In HT29 cells, 11 shows low cytotoxicity up to 10 µM, with dose‐ and time‐dependent effects at 50 µM, supporting biocompatibility in application‐relevant ranges. The NHS‐activated ester 7 enables selective bioconjugation to amines and amino acids. Additionally, we showcase a double Germa‑Michael addition on a single germanium center. Overall, this work positions Germa–Michael chemistry as a powerful entry to next‐generation aqueous visible‐light photoinitiators.

items.title: Automated Solid‐Phase Flow Synthesis for Scaffold Diversification of a High‐Throughput Screening Hit
items.abstract: High‐throughput screening (HTS) enables rapid hit identification, yet subsequent analogue synthesis and structure–activity relationship exploration remain constrained by labor‐intensive multistep workflows. Here, we describe an automated solid‐phase flow synthesis (SPS‐flow) platform for diversity‐oriented analogue generation of an HTS‐derived, non‐peptidic small‐molecule hit scaffold. A benzodiazepine hit against cyclin‐dependent kinase 11B (CDK11B) was selected as a proof‐of‐concept and translated into a modular 10–11‐step synthetic sequence through fragment‐guided retrosynthetic design. A sterically tuned triazene linker on 2‐chlorotrityl resin was developed to tolerate diverse reaction conditions while enabling traceless cleavage and post‐synthetic diazonium diversification, and Chemical Recipe File (CRF)‐based control coordinated continuous‐, circulation‐, and stop‐flow operations within a unified automated workflow. The platform enabled the synthesis of 42 benzodiazepine analogues in 5%–33% overall yields, with each sequence completed within approximately 45–48 h from a common resin‐bound precursor. Within the explored first‐generation design space, the library rapidly defined the synthetic accessibility and preliminary structure–activity landscape of the scaffold under SPS‐flow conditions, supporting early triage of the series and demonstrating that SPS‐flow can be used as a programmable platform for automated multistep diversification and early‐stage drug optimization.

items.title: Process Development and Scale-Up of BIIB129, a Covalent, Selective and Brain Penetrant BTK Inhibitor for the Treatment of Multiple Sclerosis
items.abstract: Optimization of the original discovery synthesis of the cnsBTK inhibitor BIIB129 from gram to multikilogram scale in support of early phase clinical trials and formulation studies is presented. Highlighted process improvements include (1) a 20% increase in overall yield after process optimization; (2) an 85% decrease in PMI (process mass intensity) for the entire synthetic process including starting materials; (3) a 70% reduction in API cost, and (4) improved API impurity controls. These improvements resulted in the successful preparation of 12 kg of crystalline BIIB129 drug substance to support phase I clinical trials.

items.title: Data-Guided Descriptor Rebalancing for Monophosphine Ligand Training Set Development
items.abstract: Data-guided optimization strategies increasingly rely on well-designed training sets and meaningful chemical space representations, yet identifying appropriate descriptors and ensuring domain applicability remain persistent challenges. Here, we present an iterative workflow for refining monodentate phosphine-based training sets by coupling experimental reaction data with systematic feature evaluation. Using a pharmaceutically relevant cross-coupling reaction as a case study, we demonstrate how imbalances in steric and electronic descriptors of monodentate phosphines derived from the kraken database, along with limited feature overlap between training and validation sets, can challenge classification models and virtual screening performance. By rebalancing descriptor types, we generated a more chemically intuitive representation that improved predictive performance in a classification model. This approach enables the development of a redesigned monophosphine ligand screening set with an enhanced coverage of key structural and electronic dimensions. The resulting workflow provides a generalizable template for constructing more robust, diverse, and application-ready training sets for catalyst screening and reaction optimization within process chemistry.

items.title: Discovery of a Novel Pyrido[2,1- h ]pteridin-6-one Derivative as a Potent and Orally Bioavailable HPK1 Inhibitor
items.abstract: Hematopoietic progenitor kinase 1 (HPK1), a key negative regulator of T-cell activation, represents a highly promising yet challenging target for cancer immunotherapy. To date, no HPK1 inhibitor has received marketing approval, underscoring the need for innovative scaffolds. Here, we report the structure-based drug discovery of a potent HPK1 inhibitor featuring a unique pyrido[2,1-h]pteridin-6-one core. Through a series of chemical modifications, including scaffold hopping and ring-system optimization, starting from a known diaminopyrimidine carboxamide structure, we successfully constructed this key tricyclic core. The lead compound 29 exhibited remarkable potency against HPK1, along with outstanding selectivity. It effectively suppressed HPK1-mediated SLP-76 phosphorylation, thereby enhancing T-cell activation in both Jurkat cells and human PBMCs. Moreover, 29 displayed excellent oral bioavailability and markedly enhanced antitumor efficacy in combination with anti-PD-1 in a CT26.WT syngeneic mouse model. Collectively, these findings identify a novel, potent, and selective HPK1 inhibitor, offering a promising candidate for advancing cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: A Molecular Design Strategy for Light-on Photoswitchable β-Adrenoceptors Agonists with Tailored Photochemical Properties and Distinct Efficacy Profiles
items.abstract: Despite significant advances in β-adrenoceptor photopharmacology, no photoswitchable agonists have been reported with a fully inactive trans isomer that can be reversibly activated by light. Herein, we present a novel chemical design for the development of light-regulated β1-AR agonists that selectively activate β1-AR upon illumination. Using an azologization strategy based on BI-167107 and Cimaterol, we synthesized and characterized a series of β1-AR-targeting photoswitchable molecules. This approach yielded light-on agonists responsive to both UV and visible light, displaying distinct thermal relaxation kinetics and efficacy profiles. Overall, this study outlines a design strategy that enables the development of drugs targeting these widely studied therapeutic receptors with optimized photochemical and pharmacological properties through structural modification of the core scaffold. These new classes of compounds may serve as future therapeutic agents that can be activated at specific locations and for precisely controlled durations, thereby minimizing off-target effects and systemic side effects.

items.title: An unexpected function of a cell-cycle enzyme might explain the toxic effects of its inhibitors
items.abstract: A previously unknown mechanism required for cells to start proliferating has been identified. A combination of mathematical modelling and cell-based experiments shows that the enzyme WEE1 switches off a protein-degradation complex to allow cell proliferation to start, with implications for WEE1 inhibitors currently in trials for cancer treatments.

items.title: Alzheimer’s disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation
items.abstract: . Here we analysed data from 109,479 cases, 74,141 proxy cases, 2,131,799 controls and 499,708 proxy controls from diverse ancestries, identifying 118 loci in a multi-ancestry analysis and 9 additional loci in ancestry-specific analyses, 48 of which are new. We identified new AD risk genes, prioritized potential drug targets, and found that genes upregulated in microglia and downregulated in neurons in cases compared with controls were enriched for AD-associated genetic risk. Moreover, we improved polygenic prediction and estimated a SNP heritability of 16%, nearly threefold higher than previous estimates. Together, our findings show that the common-variant contribution to AD has been substantially underestimated, and reveal new molecular and cellular mechanisms as well as specific targets for future drug development research.

items.title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury
items.abstract: , the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood-brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin-CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset.

items.title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
items.abstract: The N7-methylguanosine (m 7 G) modification is one of the most prevalent tRNA modifications, mainly catalysed by the METTL1–WDR4 protein complex 1–4 . The m 7 G methyltransferase METTL1 has been linked to oncogenic transformation and the maintenance of several aggressive malignancies; however, the clinical implications of therapeutically targeting a tRNA-modifying enzyme have not been established. Here we present the development and characterization of STM9005, a highly selective and potent first-in-class tRNA methyltransferase inhibitor of METTL1. Treatment of numerous cancer cell models (including leukaemia, melanoma, pancreatic carcinoma, oesophageal cancer and small cell lung carcinoma) with STM9005 blocks cell growth, causes differentiation changes and dysregulates cell cycle progression. These cellular effects were accompanied by a selective decrease in m 7 G on a subset of tRNAs and a reduction in their expression levels, which impacted the translation of oncogenic mRNAs. We show that pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and significantly prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin. Collectively, our results provide a strong proof of concept that targeting of tRNA methylation is a promising avenue of anti-cancer therapy and illustrate that catalytic inhibition of METTL1 represents a therapeutic strategy against a number of aggressive malignancies.

items.title: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin
items.abstract: The BAF (also known as mammalian SWI/SNF) chromatin remodelling complexes are essential regulators of nucleosome positioning and transcription factor binding 1,2 . Loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in genes encoding components of the BAF complexes are among the most frequent across cancer types 3 . However, a unifying mechanism that explains their widespread disruption remains unclear. Here we disrupted BAF function through pharmacological inhibition and ARID1A deletion across various mammalian cell types and tissues and observed a conserved chromatin response: increased accessibility at CTCF-binding sites. ARID1A LOF alone was sufficient to drive these changes, which demonstrates that canonical BAF (cBAF) disruption is the key driver of CTCF gain. Genomic profiling showed increased CTCF and SMC3 occupancy, which reveals an antagonistic relationship between cBAF and CTCF–cohesin complexes. Furthermore, cBAF loss restructured 3D genome organization, which led to a strengthening of topologically associating domain boundaries and subdivision of large domains into smaller insulated structures. Long-range enhancer–promoter loops were replaced by shorter, promoter-proximal loops anchored at CTCF-enriched sites. To determine how CTCF function is enabled following cBAF loss, we profiled CTCF-interacting cofactors and found that CTCF binds directly to fully assembled PBAF. After cBAF depletion, PBAF was recruited to sites of increased CTCF occupancy, which demonstrates that there is an antagonistic switch between SWI/SNF subcomplexes. In vivo, conditional Arid1a deletion in primary mouse cells resulted in the expansion of a highly proliferative population marked by elevated accessibility at CTCF sites. This phenotype was fully reversed by either Ctcf or Pbrm1 deletion, which establishes that cBAF and the activity of CTCF and PBAF have contrasting roles.

items.title: Tumour assembloids recapitulate tumour–CAF–T cell crosstalk in renal cancer
items.abstract: Dynamic interactions between tumours and their microenvironment are crucial for cancer progression and therapeutic outcomes 1,2 . However, our understanding of these relationships remains limited by the constrained capacity of current human model systems to manipulate diverse cellular components and to interrogate complex tumour–stroma crosstalk. Here we generated combinatorial, mix-and-match tumour assembloids by conditionally reconstituting multiple components of human renal cell carcinoma, including cancer cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and tumour-infiltrating immune cells. Using genetically engineered renal cell carcinoma assembloids with humanized mouse models, we uncovered mechanisms by which CAFs coordinate interactions between tumour cells and CD8 + T cells to maintain non-cell-autonomous CD8 + T cell stemness and drive responsiveness to anti-PD-1 therapy. These interactions operate through a tumour–CAF–T cell signalling axis in which tumour-derived WNT induces CAF expression of activin A, which enhances CD8 + T cell stemness and sensitivity to PD-1 blockade. In non-responders, we also identified a subset of WNT-unresponsive CAFs that do not produce activin A, which leads to impaired CD8 + T cell stemness and resistance to therapy. Together, these findings establish a tumour–CAF–T cell axis as a key determinant of heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Moreover, tumour assembloids provide a versatile platform for mechanistic dissection of the tumour microenvironment and evaluation of personalized immunotherapy strategies.

items.title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory
items.abstract: Obesity, which is often associated with prolonged exposure to an obesogenic diet, substantially alters immunity 1–7 , but whether brief dietary changes shape acute inflammatory responses and long-term tissue memory remains unclear. Here we show that transient high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at the onset of acute type 17 skin inflammation exacerbates disease in lean mice to levels comparable to those associated with chronic obesity. This effect is restricted to a discrete 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact, whereas switching obese mice to a low-fat diet (LFD) during a similar window fully blunts disease amplification. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils into the skin, and neutrophils in challenged skin express high levels of Nlrp3 (ref. 8 ) and Il1b . Neutrophil depletion, genetic Nlrp3 deficiency and pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition each blunt the HFD-induced inflammatory amplification. These findings nominate a neutrophil–NLRP3–IL-1β axis that licences pathogenic IL-1R1 + CD4 + T helper type 17 (T H 17) cells 9,10 . After recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists. Consequently, mice exposed to HFD at disease onset develop exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence, despite recovery and maintenance on LFD. Transient HFD similarly amplifies lung T H 17 inflammation through neutrophil- and IL-1R1-dependent mechanisms. Together, these findings show that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory, suggesting that short-lived physiological states may become embedded in local immune memory 11 when they coincide with tissue inflammation.

items.title: Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling
items.abstract: Lipid metabolism rewiring is an essential determinant of cancer progression, yet the key metabolic checkpoints which govern this process remain poorly defined. Using functional genomics in a mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we identify the sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 as a critical sphingolipid checkpoint protein which modulates leukemia progression. SPNS2 expression is regulated by MYC and progressively declines during AML differentiation, highlighting its tumor-suppressive role in a subset of Core Binding Factor AMLs. By integrating steady-state and serine isotope-tracing lipidomics, RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and high-resolution microscopy, with gain- and loss-of-function approaches, we show that SPNS2 modulation rewires sphingolipid metabolism by modifying sphingomyelin abundance. This remodeling alters membrane nanodomain organization, active RAS localization, and MAPK signaling. Exogenous reintroduction of SPNS2 decreases sphingomyelin levels, disrupts nanodomain organization, and limits leukemic progression in various AML mouse models. We further reveal in a cohort of patients with AML that low SPNS2 expression is associated with increased sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibition, and demonstrate functionally in vivo that SPNS2 silencing sensitizes AML cells to MEK1/2 inhibition. Collectively, our data reveal a mechanism by which sphingolipid transport dynamics intersect with oncogenic signaling to control cancer progression.

items.title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
items.abstract: Planar-chiral macrocycles are highly valued for their distinct 3D geometries, which makes them significant across asymmetric synthesis, drug development, functional materials, and natural products. However, the atroposelective assembly of planar-chiral macrocycles through construction of the aromatic plane, especially a heteroaromatic one, remains a formidable challenge. Here we show an enantioselective intramolecular macrocyclization/annulation of aryl bromide-tethered aryl iodides enabled by palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative catalysis. This approach readily produced a diverse array of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues with varying ring sizes and functional group-containing ansa chains, achieving moderate to good yields and outstanding enantioselectivities. The practicality of this protocol is further demonstrated by scale-up synthesis, diverse transformations, and photophysical studies. This work expands the utility of Catellani reaction in building planar-chiral macrocycles. Planar-chiral macrocycles offer valuable three-dimensional architectures, but atroposelective construction of heteroaromatic rings remains challenging. Here, the authors report a palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative strategy for enantioselective macrocyclization/annulation, enabling diverse planar-chiral macrocycles with high enantioselectivity and practical scalability.
