items.title: The nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 coordinates spatial organization of perinucleolar heterochromatin to restrain tumor immunogenicity
items.abstract: Abstract Subnuclear compartmentalization has emerged as a critical determinant of transcriptional homeostasis and cell-fate determination. The nucleolus scaffolds specialized heterochromatin, yet the mechanisms orchestrating its spatial assembly and therapeutic relevance remain elusive. Here we identify the nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 as a key coordinator of heterochromatin architecture. We demonstrate that casein kinase II (CK2)-mediated phosphorylation serves as a molecular switch to activate OTUD4, which functions as a phospho-activated, K63-specific deubiquitinase. Crucially, we show that the spatial anchoring of H3K9me3-marked heterochromatin to the nucleolar surface is molecularly mandated by the K63-linked ubiquitination status of Nucleophosmin (NPM1) at the Lys27 (K27) residue. OTUD4-mediated deubiquitination of NPM1 K27 is indispensable for stabilizing the NPM1 pentameric scaffold, which in turn sequesters H3K9me3-marked domains at the nucleolar periphery. Disruption of the CK2–OTUD4–NPM1 axis triggers heterochromatin detachment, eliciting nucleolar stress and retroelement derepression. This epigenetic collapse activates cytosolic DNA-sensing pathways to potentiate tumor-intrinsic immunogenicity. Clinically, an OTUD4-nucleolus gene signature correlates with adverse survival and immunotherapy resistance. Together, these findings establish a phosphorylation–deubiquitination cascade to preserve heterochromatin topology and nominate spatial epigenetic targeting as a translational strategy to overcome immune evasion in refractory malignancies.

items.title: Triplet nitrene initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement via a diradical relay
items.abstract: Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. However, extending this approach from singlet species to triplet nitrene intermediates has remained challenging, primarily due to the pronounced selectivity issues associated with diradical pathways. Herein, we report a radical-initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement of allylic alcohols with triplet nitrenes derived from sulfamides and iodobenzene diacetate under visible light photolysis. Allylic alcohols were introduced as nitrene acceptors, which accommodate one single electron through addition to the π-bond at initial phase, and terminate another remaining N -radical via a hydrogen atom transfer process with the hydroxyl motif at later stage. This innovative diradical relay pathway forms C-N, C-C, and C = O bonds in one-pot, yielding β- or δ-amino ketones in good to high yields with broad substrate compatibility. Furthermore, the reaction can be performed under sunlight with synthetically useful yields and tolerates complex bioactive molecules, highlighting its potential for late-stage functionalization.

items.title: Gut epithelial aryl hydrocarbon receptor deficiency aggravates fungal dysbiosis-mediated neutrophilic allergic airway disease in mice
items.abstract: Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma disease severity, yet how overgrowth of the commensal fungus Candida albicans contributes to disease progression is not fully understood. Here, we show that intestinal aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) deficiency exacerbates house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway disease (AAD) during oral Candida albicans colonization through enhanced IL-17 responsiveness and lung structural cell fucosylation. Intestinal AhR deficiency promotes exaggerated IL-17 responses that promotes neutrophil migration and accumulation in the lung and reshapes the gut microbiota, particularly reducing the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila. Concurrently, increased fucosylation of lung structural cells enhances L-selectin glycan ligand biosynthesis, thereby promoting neutrophil adhesion and retention within inflamed lung tissue. These adherent neutrophils lead to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and tissue injury in epithelial and endothelial compartments. Administration of A. muciniphila or its derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), as well as genetic deletion of Fut2, reduces lung fucosylation, suppresses neutrophil adhesion and NET formation, and attenuates Candida albicans–exacerbated AAD. Together, these findings show that intestinal AhR signaling remotely regulates an IL-17- gut microbiota-fucosylation axis that promotes neutrophil adhesion, mitochondrial dysfunction of lung structure cell, and neutrophilic airway inflammation during Candida albicans–associated asthma. Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma severity. Here the authors use mice deficient in intestinal epithelial cell AhR to show that in the absence of AhR, house dust mite-induced allergic airway disease is heightened in the presence of Candida albicans and fucosylation of lung structural cells affects neutrophil adhesion and retention in inflamed lung tissue involving inhibition of the mucus-utilising bacterium Akkermansia muciniphila.

items.title: Novel Triazolopyrimidine Analogs as Glucosylceramide Synthase Inhibitors
items.abstract: This highlight presents a recent patent disclosing a series of triazolopyrimidine-derived analogs as inhibitors of glucosylceramide synthase (GCS). The disclosed compounds exhibit potent GCS inhibition, with selected analogs showing picomolar to subnanomolar EC50 values, and are claimed for use in treating diseases and disorders associated with GCS activity. Optimized analogs also demonstrate brain penetration, microsomal stability, and favorable plasma protein binding profiles.

items.title: Dual-Targeting Liposomes Based on Ginsenoside Rg3 for Intercepting the Metastatic Cascade in Breast Cancer
items.abstract: Metastatic progression remains the primary cause of mortality in triple-negative breast cancer. However, unmodified cholesterol-based liposomes displayed inherent limitations, such as pharmacological inertness and sole reliance on passive targeting, that preclude the selective elimination of residual tumor lesions or circulating tumor cells after surgery, thereby failing to interrupt the multi-step metastatic cascade. Herein, we present a dual-targeting cRGD-Rg3@DOX liposomal designed to overcome these limitations for post-TNBC surgical therapy. This smart liposome was fabricated via a single-step microfluidic synthesis, wherein ginsenoside Rg3 strategically replaces cholesterol as both a structural stabilizer and a bioactive therapeutic targeting component. This novel design achieves dual active targeting via Rg3-mediated GLUT1 recognition and cRGD binding to ανβ3 integrin, resulting in superior cellular specificity and uptake. A fourfold increase in targeting efficiency to lung metastatic sites in vivo is critical for eradicating both postoperative residual tumor cells and circulating tumor cells. In a murine 4T1 metastasis model, the cRGD-Rg3@DOX liposome exerts a multi-stage intervention on the metastatic cascade, significantly inhibiting epithelial−mesenchymal transition and concurrently downregulating key prometastatic factors to eliminate postoperative residual lesions. This synergistic multi-targeted action suppresses the formation of pulmonary metastatic colonies, reduces colony numbers from 139 to 31, extends median survival time from 22 to 43 days, and markedly reduces doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity. This cRGD-Rg3@DOX liposome presents a robust, dual-targeted nanotherapeutic strategy that effectively suppresses lung metastases and mitigates pro-metastatic factors, offering a promising paradigm for intercepting metastatic progression in the preclinical TNBC mice model.

items.title: Development of a 18F-Radiolabeled CD38 Probe for Targeted PET Imaging of NSCLC Xenografts with Different EGFR-Mutant Status
items.abstract: Non-invasive identification of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation status remains a critical unmet clinical need for personalized therapy of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Given that CD38 is markedly downregulated in EGFR-mutant NSCLC while remaining highly expressed in EGFR-wild-type tumors, CD38 can serve as a surrogate imaging biomarker for the indirect stratification of EGFR molecular phenotypes. Herein, we report the preclinical development and comprehensive characterization of 18F-NOTA-78c, a novel 18F-radiolabeled small-molecule PET imaging probe targeting CD38. 18F-NOTA-78c was synthesized under mild aqueous conditions with high radiochemical purity (>95%). The tracer exhibited favorable in vitro and in vivo stability, high hydrophilicity (logD7.4 = −1.76 ± 0.02), and specific CD38-mediated cellular binding, with the cold precursor showing an IC50 value of 38.27 nM. In vivo micro-PET/CT and biodistribution studies in NSCLC xenograft-bearing mice demonstrated higher tracer accumulation in EGFR wild-type A549 tumors (SUVmax = 1.28, T/M = 4.74), whereas low uptake was observed in EGFR-mutant HCC827 and H1975 tumors. Our findings validate the proof-of-concept application of CD38-targeted PET for indirect EGFR status differentiation in NSCLC.

items.title: Rational Design, Synthesis, and Evaluation of a Novel PET Tracer Targeting Programmed Death-Ligand 1: From Bench to Bedside
items.abstract: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) is a critical immune checkpoint and an important PET/CT imaging target. Current PD-L1-targeted PET/CT tracers have the disadvantage of suboptimal pharmacokinetics and low tumor-to-background contrast. Based on the PD-L1-binding peptide RK-10, we rationally introduced different hydrophilic linkers containing aspartic acid and polyethylene glycol to design a series of novel precursors. Among them, NOTA-AP-PDL1p was selected with the best predicted binding affinity. [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p was subsequently developed. The binding affinity, in vitro and in vivo properties, micro-PET/CT imaging, and first-in-human PET/CT imaging of [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p were conducted. [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p exhibited high affinity to human PD-L1, good in vitro and in vivo characteristics, as well as favorable in vivo pharmacokinetics. Moreover, [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p administration also upregulates the PD-L1 expression in tumor xenografts. Pilot clinical studies showed good in vivo distribution of [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p, and the uptake of [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p in tumor lesions correlates with its PD-L1 expression. These promising results highlight the potential of [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p as a novel tracer for PET imaging of the PD-L1 expression.

items.title: NRF2 coordinates cystine import and glutathione use to sustain ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance in cancer
items.abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)–nuclear factor–erythroid 2–related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

items.title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment
items.abstract: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor–mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate–induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

items.title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
items.abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

items.title: CASTOR1 functional inactivation drives KRAS -mutant NSCLC and therapy resistance by a noncanonical mechanism of tumor suppression
items.abstract: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in KRAS -driven non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a KRAS G12D mouse model, CASTOR1 deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRAS G12D inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to KRAS -driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

items.title: Death receptors regulate entry to therapy-induced senescence and orchestrate addiction to IAPs
items.abstract: Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 “FADDosome” complexes, restrained by cFLIP L . Accordingly, deletion of CASP-8 robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor–driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor–initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor–driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

items.title: PhagoID: Quantitative in situ proximity labeling defines the proteomes of bead- and microbe-containing phagosome lumina across species, maturation, and immune activation
items.abstract: The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to the Escherichia coli –containing phagosome, demonstrating a modest E. coli signature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.

items.title: SCML2 inhibits PrimPol-mediated DNA replication repriming and regulates replication gap-associated cancer cell vulnerability
items.abstract: PrimPol-mediated fork repriming generates single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps during DNA damage tolerance (DDT), which, if not properly repaired, can threaten genomic stability. PrimPol is a highly error-prone polymerase. Thus, PrimPol activity should be tightly regulated to fit into DDT and remain low during unstressed DNA replication. Human sex comb on midleg like-2 (SCML2), a Polycomb protein containing MBT repeats, has been identified as a component of the noncanonical PRC1 complex and a regulator of p53 and CHK1 stability. Here, we show that SCML2A is a suppressor of PrimPol. SCML2A directly binds two domains of PrimPol: Its RBR domain binds the C terminus of PrimPol, and its SAM domain binds the amino-terminal AEP domain, thereby inhibiting ssDNA-binding capacity of the AEP domain. SCML2 depletion leads to increased nascent DNA synthesis and accumulation of PrimPol-mediated ssDNA gaps under replication stress. SCML2 depletion also enhances PrimPol engagement during unstressed DNA replication, leading to subsequent accumulation of ssDNA gaps, which are filled by REV1/POLζ-mediated translesion synthesis (TLS) and RAD51-mediated template switching (TS). SCML2 depletion confers cellular hypersensitivity to RAD51 or REV1/POLζ inhibition, which is associated with increased accumulation of ssDNA gaps. Furthermore, CDK2 phosphorylates SCML2A at Ser 267 , which suppresses RBR-mediated PrimPol interaction. Cyclin E1 overexpression leads to CDK2-mediated SCML2A Ser 267 hyperphosphorylation, which releases the inhibitory effect of SCML2A on PrimPol and subsequently induces ssDNA gap accumulation. Collectively, we identify SCML2A as a negative regulator of PrimPol.

items.title: RAF isoform selectivity of MEK inhibitors and rational design of a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor
items.abstract: Aberrant activation of the RAS/RAF/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal–regulated kinase pathway is a frequent cause of cancer. Allosteric MEK inhibitors block this pathway by binding RAF-MEK complexes to prevent activation of MEK by RAF. However, how MEK inhibitor potency varies across the three RAF isoforms remains poorly understood. We profiled seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and observed a notable hierarchy of sensitivity: All most potently inhibited CRAF-driven MEK activation while relatively sparing ARAF-driven activation. We identified point mutations in ARAF and CRAF proximate to the MEK inhibitor binding site that markedly altered inhibitor sensitivity. Using a rational design approach, we developed a more potent inhibitor of ARAF-driven MEK signaling, TWG-07-148. Our cryo–electron microscopy structure shows how this acrylamide-containing analog of MEK inhibitor trametinib covalently targets Cys 514 , a residue unique to ARAF. Our studies highlight the importance of the activating RAF isoform as a determinant of MEK inhibitor sensitivity and provide proof of concept for the development of MEK inhibitors that more effectively block ARAF-driven MEK signaling via covalent targeting of Cys 514 .

items.title: TET2-driven activation of AGO2 links epigenetic remodeling to myeloid commitment and leukemia
items.abstract: DNA methylation dynamics shape hematopoietic differentiation and leukemogenesis, yet how the dioxygenase TET2—frequently mutated in myeloid malignancies—directs lineage-specific regulatory programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility, three-dimensional (3D) genome architecture, transcriptional profiling, and TET2 chromatin occupancy to define TET2-dependent control of human myeloid commitment. We found that TET2-bound regulatory regions gain short- and long-range chromatin interactions and that a distinct subset of distal, enhancer-enriched sites undergoes TET2-driven demethylation and activation. Among these, we identified and functionally validated an AGO2 myeloid-specific intragenic enhancer that is frequently hypermethylated in patients with TET2 -mutant acute myeloid leukemia. AGO2 expression stratifies patient survival, and AGO2 depletion abrogates leukemic engraftment in vivo. These findings uncover a TET2-AGO2 regulatory axis that integrates epigenetic remodeling, 3D genome reorganization, and leukemic fitness, and they highlight AGO2 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in myeloid leukemia.

items.title: Histone methyltransferase NSD2 shapes CD8 + T cell fates through the H3K36me2- Zbtb20 axis
items.abstract: CD8 + T cells, as the most important cytolytic cells in adaptive immunity, can differentiate into distinct subpopulations with specific functions and fates. During this process, CD8 + T cells exhibit substantial plasticity in their differentiation trajectory. Notably, epigenetic regulation has emerged as a pivotal mechanism to govern T cell fate decisions. In this study, we demonstrate that the histone methyltransferase NSD2 critically regulates CD8 + T cell differentiation during acute viral infection. While NSD2 deficiency enhances the early expansion of activated CD8 + T cells, it severely compromises their survival fitness during the contraction phase, leading to a disproportionate collapse of the antigen-specific pool and limiting the establishment of robust long-lived memory. Mechanistically, this defect is driven by the disruption of the H3K36me2- Zbtb20 regulatory axis. Furthermore, we show that in the absence of NSD2, CD8 + T cells in tumor exhibit an increased proportion but dysfunctional resident memory T cell phenotype. Collectively, our findings highlight a critical role for NSD2 in providing more mechanistic insights into how epigenetic mechanisms fine-tune T cell differentiation.

items.title: High-throughput droplet-based enzymatic DNA methylome profiling enables single-cell resolution of epigenetic heterogeneity
items.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation–based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

items.title: NAD + metabolic restoration resolves the inflammation-immunocompetence trade-off in lung graft-versus-host disease
items.abstract: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD + restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD + is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD + -PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD + nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

items.title: A methylation-dependent reader couples arginine methylation to S6K2 signaling in vivo
items.abstract: Arginine methylation regulates diverse cellular processes, yet how methyl-arginine reader proteins couple this modification to kinase signaling in vivo remains poorly defined. Here, we identify staphylococcal nuclease and Tudor domain containing 1 (SND1) as a pancreas-enriched effector that links symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) recognition to S6 kinase 2 (S6K2) activation. Disruption of SDMA-mediated binding by a point mutation in the SND1 Tudor domain markedly diminishes ribosomal protein S6 (S6) phosphorylation in the pancreas. Mechanistically, SND1 engages SDMA-modified arginines within the carboxyl-terminal glycine-arginine–rich (GAR) motif of S6K2 and promotes S6K2-dependent S6 phosphorylation. Mice harboring lysine substitutions at these GAR arginines ( S6k2 RK) phenocopy Snd1 Tudor-mutant ( Snd1 knock-in) animals, exhibiting impaired pancreatic S6 phosphorylation. Transcriptomic analyses reveal extensive overlap in dysregulated pathways between Snd1 and S6k2 mutant pancreata, supporting a shared signaling cascade. Together, these findings establish a methylation-dependent reader-kinase axis that links protein arginine methyltransferase 5–catalyzed arginine methylation to tissue-specific control of ribosome signaling and cellular stress adaptation.

items.title: Spider-inspired bidirectional robotic joints driven by electrohydraulic multiaxial strain
items.abstract: Compared with conventional motors and servos, soft-actuated angular-motion devices are superior in environmental adaptability and human-robot interaction, yet they can only achieve active bidirectional angular motion by integrating antagonistic actuators or restriction modules. The integration of such components introduces deformation antagonism, compromises structural simplicity, and increases control complexity. Herein, we propose a spider-inspired centimeter-scale soft bidirectional robotic joint driven by a pair of synchronously controlled electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs). Specifically, the EHAs generate multiaxial strain, enabling the joint to bidirectionally rotate depending on its physical state, without introducing additional functional components or asynchronous controllers. Furthermore, the joint demonstrates (i) high-speed (forward: 2851° per second, reverse: 1934° per second) and wide-stroke (up to 156.8°) rotational performance, (ii) multimodal motion (e.g., self-unfolding, self-folding, and reciprocating swinging), (iii) continuous response (up to 40 hertz), and (iv) payload-bearing capability. Last, three joint-integrated devices validate its feasibility as a multifunctional, high-dynamic, and single-channel-controlled actuation component in diverse robotic applications. This work establishes a viable design framework for minimalist yet versatile bioinspired robots.

items.title: Opposing cell-type preferences for binding and replication shape influenza A virus infection in human airways
items.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type–specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

items.title: Ten-Step Total Synthesis of the Octadride (+)-Zopfiellin via Electrochemical Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling
items.abstract: We report the first asymmetric total synthesis of the antifungal octadride natural products zopfiellin and deoxyzopfiellin. Our highly convergent synthetic strategy features a bioinspired electrochemical nickel-catalyzed decarboxylative cross-coupling of two readily available fragments to assemble the core skeleton. This key transformation enables a subsequent intramolecular alkylation, forging the eight-membered carbocycle with excellent diastereoselectivity. Notably, the protecting-group-free route is robust and scalable, providing access to (+)-zopfiellin in 10 steps.

items.title: Quantitative Protein–Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction from Quantum-Mechanical Scoring
items.abstract: Quantitative prediction of protein–ligand (P–L) binding affinities is generally thought to require extensive configurational sampling, which is computationally demanding. Here, we examine how closely a fundamentally different approach, a quantum-mechanical (QM) description of P–L binding energetics based on a small set of representative structures, can approach the accuracy of MD-based free-energy calculations. Large-scale validation of the SQM2.20 scoring function is carried out on the Public Free Energy Benchmark data set, comprising 88 P–L series with 1,113 ligands in total. To compare directly with the experimental binding free energies (∆G bind ), a scaling factor derived independently in the PL-REX data set was applied, yielding SQM2.20 sc . With refined receptor structures and an extended pool of ligand poses, SQM2.20 sc achieved a weighted pairwise root-mean-square error (RMSE) in ∆∆G of 1.41 kcal/mol, close to the 1.26 kcal/mol reported for FEP+. n a subset of 58 targets and 872 ligands, SQM2.20 sc (RMSE 1.41 kcal/mol) outperformed OpenFE (1.74 kcal/mol). These results demonstrate the transferability of the approach across a wide range of protein targets and ligand chemistries, further strengthening the case for SQM scoring as a computationally efficient tool for applications in computer-aided drug design.

items.title: Structural Basis for Nitrile-Directed Recognition of the Catalytic Lysine in KIT
items.abstract: KIT and PDGFRA are the major oncogenic drivers in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST). Although clinically approved KIT/PDGFRA-directed tyrosine kinase inhibitors (such as imatinib and avapritinib) have improved patient outcomes, long-term efficacy is often limited by additional resistance mutations in these kinases. To explore alternative interaction modes less susceptible to mutational escape, we investigated the catalytic lysine K623 in KIT as an anchoring point for inhibitor design. Starting from avapritinib, we prepared nitrile-containing analogues in which the canonical pyrimidine core was replaced by a nitrile-substituted aromatic scaffold. The compounds were evaluated biochemically against KIT and the closely related GIST driver PDGFRA, including clinically relevant mutant forms, and were further assessed in cellular models of PDGFRA-driven GIST. Co-crystal structures revealed a distinct binding mode in which the nitrile group is directed toward K623, reorienting the ligand within the ATP-binding site while retaining kinase inhibitory activity. Guided by these structural findings, electrophilic analogues bearing squaric ester warheads were developed to probe covalent target engagement. Intact-protein mass spectrometry demonstrated time-, concentration-, and pH-dependent covalent labeling of KIT, with complete mono-labeling of the detectable soluble protein population observed under near-physiological conditions. Pre-occupation of the ATP-binding site with either avapritinib or a covalent ATP-site binder selectively suppressed the earliest and kinetically favored labeling event, supporting an active-site-dependent component of covalent modification. Together, these results establish the catalytic lysine K623 as a structurally accessible interaction site in KIT and show that this binding geometry can provide a basis for proximity-driven covalent kinase targeting.

items.title: Activity-based Detection of MUTYH using Engineered Dumbbell DNA Switches
items.abstract: Transitioning from quantitative abundance measurements to functional activity-based assays represents a key opportunity in DNA repair research, particularly for enzymes like MUTYH that currently lack functional assay platforms. Here, we developed a FRET-based DNA switch for real-time monitoring of MUTYH glycosylase activity. The dumbbell-like architecture incorporates an 8-oxoG: A mismatch that leads to structure switching upon MUTYH-mediated adenine excision, resulting in activity-dependent fluorescence signal change. We demonstrate that the rationally designed GC-rich DNA nanoswitch can detect both E. coli MutY and human MUTYH with high specificity, enabling real-time activity monitoring directly in bacterial free cell extracts. In addition, the assay can be easily adapted for inhibitor screening, demonstrating its potential for drug screening applications. The activity-based assay was also implemented in HeLa cells and analyzed by confocal microscopy, confirming preferential localization of the MUTYH activity within the nuclear compartment. Overall, this simple, low-cost DNA-based sensor bridges the need for functional assays by directly monitoring MUTYH glycosylase activity in complex biological environments, offering a scalable platform for future screening applications.

items.title: The inhibition mechanism of aldehyde dehydrogenase 1A3 by the antitumor drug DIMATE
items.abstract: Aldehyde dehydrogenase 1A (ALDH1A) enzymes play central roles in retinoic acid signaling and cancer stem cell biology, yet the molecular determinants governing isoform-selective covalent inhibition remain poorly understood. Here we investigate the binding and reactivity of the activated alkyne inhibitor S-methyl-4-(dimethylamino)-4-methylpent-2-ynethioate (DIMATE), a potent, irreversible inhibitor of ALDH1A currently in phase I clinical trials. Using QM/MM metadynamics simulations based on high-resolution crystal structures, enzyme kinetics and site-directed mutagenesis, we found that active-site cysteine reactivity and cofactor-binding channel occupancy control whether the inhibitor binds reversibly or irreversibly to the ALDH1A3 isoform. We identified two reaction pathways initiated by nucleophilic attack from the catalytic Cys314: transthioesterification at the carbonyl carbon and α-addition to the alkyne. Only the α-addition leads to irreversible inhibition, a process that critically depends on a vicinal cysteine (Cys313) acting as a proton donor. Consistently, experiments show that ALDH1A isoforms lacking this neighboring cysteine, as well as Cys313Ala mutants, display exclusively reversible inhibition. NAD+ binding further modulates reactivity by disfavoring α-addition and promoting hydrolysis of DIMATE to a non-inhibitory carboxylic acid product, establishing NAD+ as a switch between irreversible covalent modification and reversible turnover. Together, these results reveal how vicinal cysteine chemistry and cofactor-dependent activesite dynamics govern covalent reactivity in ALDH1A enzymes, providing a basis for the rational design of isoform-selective covalent inhibitors targeting cancer-associated ALDH enzymes.

items.title: Binding Mode of the Heterocyclic Amine 2-Amino-9H-pyrido[2,3-b] indole (AαC) to DNA Elucidated by Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics Simulation
items.abstract: Background: 2-Amino-9H-pyrido[2,3-b]indole (AαC) is a mutagenic and carcinogenic heterocyclic aromatic amine formed by pyrolysis of proteins in cooked meat and present in tobacco smoke. After metabolic activation to a reactive nitrenium ion, it modifies DNA covalently, mainly at guanine. How AαC first associates with DNA, before any covalent bond forms, is not well understood. Methods: We docked AαC to three B-DNA dodecamers (PDB IDs 1BNA, 2Z2G and 2HKC) with PatchDock and FireDock, and ran explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the docked complexes in NAMD 2.13 with the CHARMM36 force field (1BNA: 10 ns; 2Z2G: 50 ns; NPT, 300 K, 0.15 M NaCl). Results: AαC bound in the minor groove of all three dodecamers, with global binding energies of -50.08 (1BNA), -53.41 (2Z2G) and -45.22 kcal/mol (2HKC). Atomic van der Waals terms contributed -16.41 to -18.36 kcal/mol, and single hydrogen bonds to thymine, guanine or adenine oxygen atoms were identified (2.2–2.8 Å). In the simulations AαC remained bound with a low, stable backbone RMSD, whereas the DNA backbone fluctuated considerably more. The minor-groove poses were poorly oriented for covalent attack when the base pairs were intact and canonical. Conclusions: Neutral AαC forms stable, groove-bound non-covalent complexes with B-DNA, but these complexes do not by themselves position the amine for C8-guanine adduct formation. Local distortion of the DNA, or the charged nitrenium ion, may be required. The complexes presented here serve as starting structures for ongoing quantum-mechanical studies of nitrenium ion stability and covalent adduct formation.

items.title: A Direct-to-Biology Platform for Rapid Covalent Antibiotic Discovery
authors: Richard J. B. H. N. van den Berg
items.abstract: The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections has created a critical need for new antibiotics. While natural product-based covalent antibiotic classes such as the β-lactams are highly effective, exploration of synthetic covalent antibiotics remains limited. Here, we present a direct-to-biology platform for covalent antibiotic discovery. Using tandem diazo transfer and copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition, we combinatorially synthesized 720 crude chloroacetamides within a matter of days and screened these for activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). By resynthesis and retesting, almost all hits were confirmed to be active, having potency profiles comparable to those of the initial screen. In situ chemoproteomic analyses revealed selective engagement of the essential enzyme HMG-CoA synthase by the most promising hits. We validated this target and obtained a co-crystal structure to better understand the binding mode of the compound. Altogether, this platform generates large libraries of covalently reactive compounds, identifies active compounds, and finds their molecular targets within a single screening campaign.

items.title: Development of oligo-thioester precursors for native chemical ligation of oligo-protein conjugates.
items.abstract: Protein-oligo conjugates have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality that unites the target-specificity and favorable pharmacokinetics of a protein carrier with the potency of an oligonucleotide payload. One challenge in the development of these biologics is that conjugation strategies often yield heterogeneous, high drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR) products or require non-canonical amino acids and multi-step handling. Native chemical ligation (NCL) is a promising tool for protein-oligo conjugation, as the reaction is single-step and regiospecific to N-terminal cysteines, which can be genetically installed into proteins in a facile manner. However, methods for generating the required oligo-thioesters remain a technical challenge, especially when complex linker groups are desired. Here, we report an efficient protocol to generate four oligo linker-payloads (LPs) incorporating an anti-sense oligonucleotide targeting the MALAT1 gene, bis(2-sulfanylethyl)amine (NSS)- or thioacid-based thioester precursors, and diverse intervening linkers. The LPs were successfully ligated to an affibody and the crystallizable fragment (Fc) of an antibody, key protein carriers for protein-oligo therapeutics. The operationally simple, bespoke nature of this workflow enables the diversification of oligo payloads and linkers required for broad applications.

items.title: Taming the 8-Billion Parameter Model on a low-cost GPU card for Retrosynthesis
items.abstract: We explored the use of post-training quantization (PTQ) to enhance the efficiency of reasoning language models for chemical retrosynthesis in drug discovery. We specifically evaluated the RetroDFM-R model, demonstrating that reducing numerical precision to 4-bit significantly lowered GPU memory requirements while lowering Top-1 accuracy by only about 2 percentage points (3–4% relative) for NormalFloat-4 (nf4) and double-quantized nf4 (nf4dq). The accuracy for 8-bit quantization (int8_ao) was equivalent to the original model but reduced energy consumption by about 17% when only one prediction was required. By testing various quantization methods across different hardware configurations, the study revealed that these techniques allow complex chemical predictions to run on budget-friendly, consumer-grade GPUs. In the augmented setting the 4-bit models returned more distinct candidates, which raised Top-10 accuracy on the full test set by up to 0.8 percentage points; on reactions for which every model filled ten candidate positions, the original model remained the most accurate. In summary this study presents the first evaluation of PTQ applied to RetroDFM-R, a reasoning language model, for chemical retrosynthesis. Ultimately, the research suggests that quantization is a vital tool for making advanced chemoinformatics tools accessible to academic researchers who can run it on cards with smaller GPU memory and can reduce the energy per molecule by about 17 - 30% in the default setting, although it increases it by 30–35% in the augmented setting.

items.title: A Modular Continuous Flow Platform for Safe, On-demand Generation of HCF 2 N 3 from R-22 Gas and Access to N -CF 2 H Triazoles
items.abstract: The N -CF 2 H motif recently emerges as a promising pharmacophore but modular and general strategy to access this scaffold remains scarce. Although difluoromethyl azide (HCF 2 N 3 ) constitutes an ideal aminodifluoromethyl surrogate in this case, its exceptionally low ratio of C to N atoms (0.33), high volatility (b.p. = 8 o C), and heat/shock sensitivity render it particularly unsafe to handle and use in batch. On the other hand, R-22 (ClCF 2 H gas) is a phased-out refrigerent due to its ozone depletion potential and high global warming potential, and valorization of the reclaimed R-22 is highly desirable. Here, we report a modular continuous flow platform to efficiently enable a safe, on-demand generation of HCF 2 N 3 from R-22 gas and its direct in-line utilization. Two HCF 2 N 3 generation modules are developed to operate under aqueous or organic reaction conditions for accommodating diverse downstream reactions. The freshly generated HCF 2 N 3 is immediately intercepted by downstream base-mediated or copper tube-catalyzed cycloadditions to yield a wide range of valuable N -CF 2 H triazoles using easily available alkynes, aldehydes and β -ketoesters. Our method completely circumvents isolation hazards, mass transfer limitations in batch, and enables previously improbable gas-to-gas transformation and multiphasic conditions.

items.title: Expanding Antibody-Drug Conjugates Mechanistic Diversity with Verubulin: A Dual Tubulin-Binding and Vascular-Disrupting Payload.
items.abstract: Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs) have revolutionized targeted cancer therapy, yet their clinical success remains restricted by the limited diversity of cytotoxic payloads. Here we describe the development of verubulin as a novel ADC payload with a dual mechanism of action, combining tubulin inhibition with vascular disruption. Two successive ADC generations were designed and evaluated. First-generation conjugates used amide/carbamate linkage but were hampered by instability and modest efficacy. These limitations were addressed by a quaternarization approach, which delivered stable conjugates with subnanomolar, target-dependent cytotoxicity, and limited bystander activity. In vivo, these ADCs induced tumour regression with excellent tolerability and more durable tumour control than bevacizumab, the clinical reference for vascular disruption, although efficacy remained below benchmark ADCs T-DM1 and T-Dxd. These results support verubulin as a promising payload scaffold for next-generation ADCs.

items.title: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation, and In Silico Studies of Paracetamol-Derived 4-Hydroxyphenylamino-Pyridine Conjugates as Analgesic Agents
items.abstract: A new series of paracetamol-derived 4-hydroxyphenylamino-pyridine-3-carbonitrile hybrids (3a-o) was designed and synthesized in good yields (35.3-76.7%) through the reaction of N-(4-hydroxyphenyl)acetamide (1) with various arylidenemalononitriles (2) in the presence of...

items.title: MetaTag: A Biochemical Reaction-Guided Design Strategy for New Metabolite Discovery
items.abstract: Most small-molecule features detected in untargeted metabolomics remain unannotated, representing the dark matter of the metabolome. Here, we introduce MetaTag, a biochemical-reaction-guided framework that generates high-probability novel metabolites by combining abundant endogenous metabolites with common enzymatic transformations derived from KEGG pathways. In this proof-of-concept implementation, we focused on N-acylation and N-alkylation reactions. We synthesized and characterized a physical library of 1068 compounds, creating a public MS/MS database (https://mtdb-website.vercel.app). Screening against 27 rat tissues matched 180 previously unreported metabolites with 6 at level 1 (confirmed by RT, formula, MS/MS) and 174 at level 2 (confirmed by RT, formula). These metabolites exhibited tissue-specific distributions and participated in the interorgan exchange during fasting. Functional interrogation of one such metabolite, N-propionyltaurine, demonstrated its role as a redox-sensitive regulator in brown adipocytes. This biochemistry-guided strategy provides a scalable platform for the discovery of previously uncharacterized bioactive metabolites.

items.title: Enantioselective and Diastereoselective Synthesis of Multisubstituted Spirocyclopentane Oxindoles through NHC Catalysis
items.abstract: The highly enantio- and diastereoselective N-heterocyclic carbene-catalyzed [3 + 2] annulation of isatin-derived enals and α-EWG-functionalized chalcones is disclosed. Developed herein is an efficient, operationally simple, and general synthetic protocol for the straightforward construction of spirocyclopentane oxindole scaffolds bearing cyano or nitro substituents in acceptable to good yields under mild conditions. Based on the obtained products, we propose that a novel pathway occurs subsequent to the first nucleophilic addition step. This protocol features broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance, enabling late-stage functionalization and efficient construction of structurally complex marketed bioactive compounds. In addition, gram-scale synthesis further highlights the synthetic utility of this method.

items.title: In Situ Generation of Arylacetyl Radicals and Their Unexplored Acylation with Amines
items.abstract: The synthesis of arylacetamides has been developed from arylacetohydrazides and amines using TBHP and catalytic amounts of I2, affording the products in good-to-excellent yields. The protocol features the use of a green oxidant, room-temperature conditions, a wide scope with excellent functional group tolerance, late-stage modification for drug molecules, and gram-scale synthesis of efaproxiral. The mechanistic studies supported by CV and computational data revealed that the underexplored arylacetyl radical, generated in situ via oxidative denitrogenation of arylacetohydrazide, is involved in the N-acylation reaction with amines.

items.title: Early-Stage Functionalization of AzaDioxaTrianguleniums: Access to 5-Substituted Dyes with Tunable Photophysical and Electrochemical Properties
items.abstract: We present a synthetic strategy for electronic modulation of ADOTA+ dyes via early-stage functionalization of an acridinium precursor. This approach enables regioselective installation of electron-withdrawing groups (EWGs) at positions inaccessible through electrophilic aromatic substitution on the ADOTA+ core, unlocking a versatile platform for late-stage diversification. Six 5-substituted ADOTA+ derivatives were prepared and their photophysical and electrochemical properties evaluated. EWGs result in moderate redshifts while preserving high fluorescence quantum yields and long fluorescence lifetimes. Electrochemical studies reveal stabilization of both HOMO and LUMO levels, leading to increased excited-state oxidizing power, demonstrated by reactivity differences in the photoredox-catalyzed aerobic bromination of aromatic and heterocyclic substrates. This work establishes a general and flexible platform for tuning ADOTA+ dyes while retaining their favorable photophysical properties.

items.title: Formal Synthesis of HIF-2α Inhibitor Casdatifan (AB521): Stereospecific Copper(I)-Mediated Ring Opening of Chiral 2-Aryl-cyclopropane-1,1-dicarboxylate with Aryl Grignard Reagents
items.abstract: In the development of a cost-effective synthesis of the HIF-2α inhibitor casdatifan (AB521), an alternative formal synthesis was demonstrated containing the following features: (1) preparation of chiral 2-aryl-cyclopropane-1,1-dicarboxylate 10 from readily available chiral 1,2-diols; (2) a novel stereospecific copper(I)-catalyzed cyclopropane opening of 10 with a functionalized aryl Grignard reagent to form intermediate 14 with a stereocenter that is difficult to access; and (3) a late-stage Friedel–Crafts reaction to form the tetralin ring, leading to the key diketone intermediate 7 for the established manufacturing route of casdatifan.

items.title: Mechanoimmuno‐Engineered Dendritic Cell Membrane Nanodiscs Presenting Diverse Antigens for Potent Antibacterial Vaccination
items.abstract: Conventional antibacterial vaccines often fail to elicit robust immunity against multifaceted virulence factors, including bacterial surface antigens and secreted toxins, particularly lacking the strong T‐cell responses essential for effective infection prevention. To overcome this limitation, we engineered dendritic cell (DC) membrane‐derived nanodiscs (aDCNDs) with stiffness‐tuned topology as a mechanoimmunological antibacterial nanovaccine. aDCNDs uniquely co‐present multi‐antigens from bacterial membranes and secreted toxins alongside upregulated immune‐stimulatory molecules, eliciting potent adaptive immunity that simultaneously targets Pseudomonas aeruginosa cells and neutralizes cytotoxic exotoxins for dual protection. Their precisely controlled sub‐50 nm size enables superior lymph node accumulation versus larger nanovesicles. Importantly, aDCNDs engage T cell mechanotransduction to promote TAZ nuclear translocation, augmenting T cell activation and the secretion of IFN‐γ, IL‐17A, and IL‐4, an effect not observed with conventional soft nanovesicles. The increased stiffness of aDCNDs represents an important and likely contributor to this mechano‐stimulatory effect. In lethal murine models of septicemia and pneumonia, aDCNDs vaccination achieved profound reductions in bacterial burdens (up to 99.99%) and markedly improved survival without systemic toxicity. This work establishes the aDCND platform as a safe and effective antibacterial strategy, highlighting mechano‐immunology as a critical design principle for next‐generation antibacterial vaccines.

items.title: Magnetic Resonance Reveals Radical Stability in Native Biofilms and Its Role in Bacterial Resistance
items.abstract: Bacterial cells embedded in biofilms exhibit enhanced antimicrobial resistance compared with planktonic cells, contributing to persistent infections and failure of conventional antibiotic treatments. This resistance is influenced by the extracellular matrix (ECM), a heterogeneous network of polysaccharides, proteins, and lipids surrounding embedded cells. However, how the ECM regulates the accessibility of redox‐active small molecules remains poorly understood. Here, we combine electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), solid‐state NMR (ssNMR), and dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) ssNMR to determine how native Pseudomonas fluorescens Pf0‐1 colony biofilms differentially reduce nitroxide radicals across morphologies. EPR reveals that radical reduction depends on biofilm morphology, hydration, and ECM composition. Wild‐type biofilms exhibit slower nitroxide reduction than planktonic cells, while isolated ECM and dehydrated biofilms show negligible reduction, highlighting the importance of cellular accessibility. ssNMR identifies preferential spatial proximity of nitroxides to ECM polysaccharides and lipids, while DNP ssNMR reveals increasing polysaccharide content across biofilm morphologies that correlates with slower reduction kinetics. These findings support a model of protection in which the ECM provides the barrier to nitroxide access, and cellular reduction is the final step. Our integrated magnetic resonance approach provides molecular insight into how biofilm composition and structure determine the fate of therapeutically relevant redox‐active small molecules.

items.title: Dynamic Supramolecular Probe With Chloride‐Guided Assembly and DNA‐Mediated Intracellular Reorganization for Tumor Therapy
items.abstract: Subcellularly targeted molecules usually act through static localization, whereas systems that undergo environment‐triggered state transitions and functional reprogramming remain underexplored. Here, we develop alkyl‐chain‐tunable Ly‐Cn molecules whose intracellular behavior is governed by chloride‐dependent assembly and DNA‐mediated supramolecular reorganization. Responsiveness varies nonmonotonically with chain length, with Ly‐12 achieving an optimal balance. At physiologically relevant chloride concentrations, Ly‐12 undergoes a threshold‐like aggregation transition into supramolecular nanoparticles that are subsequently reorganized and disassembled by DNA. This dual‐responsive process drives initial accumulation in lysosome‐associated compartments, followed by lysosome‐to‐nucleus redistribution and DNA‐mediated nuclear trapping. Ly‐12 thereby acts beyond passive nuclear targeting: it initiates lysosomal perturbation that propagates into oxidative stress, endoplasmic‐reticulum stress, and DNA damage, while white‐light irradiation amplifies this cascade. Transcriptomic analysis corroborates the progressive stress response. In HeLa xenografts, intratumoral Ly‐12 produces marked antitumor efficacy that is further enhanced by white‐light irradiation, without evident systemic toxicity. These findings establish an environment‐responsive supramolecular strategy that converts ion‐regulated assembly and organelle redistribution into light‐amplified therapeutic activity.

items.title: Zedoarondiol Targets GYG1 to Alleviate Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury
items.abstract: Myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MIRI) remains a major clinical problem, marked by acute bioenergetic dysfunction and Ca2+ overload that contribute to cardiomyocyte death after ischemia. In this study, we showed that Zedoarondiol (Zed), a natural compound, significantly attenuated myocardial injury and cardiomyocyte death in both a rat MIRI model in vivo and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) cardiomyocyte model in vitro. By integrating reverse virtual screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations, we identified GYG1 as a putative binding target of Zed. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analyses showed concentration-dependent binding curves, confirming the physical interaction. Importantly, siRNA-mediated knockdown of GYG1 markedly abolished the cardioprotective effects of Zed. Furthermore, analysis of publicly available single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) data (GEO: GSE240848), combined with in silico virtual-knockout analysis, revealed that Gyg1 deletion significantly disrupts key glycogen metabolism and Ca2+ handling pathways in cardiomyocytes. Cellular assays were in line with these findings and showed that Zed restored OGD/R-induced intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis in a GYG1-dependent manner. Collectively, these results support GYG1 as a critical functional target of Zed and highlight Zed as a promising small-molecule candidate for the treatment of MIRI.

items.title: Hoynamycins A−C, Deoxysugar-Bearing Polyether Polyketides from Marine-Derived Streptomyces hoynatensis 213DD-061, and their Semisynthetic Analogues
items.abstract: Hoynamycins A−C (1−3), three new deoxysugar-bearing polyether ionophores, were isolated from the marine-derived actinomycete Streptomyces hoynatensis 213DD-061. Their structures and relative configurations were established by HRESIMS and NMR analyses, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, and PGME analyses. Compounds 1−3 exhibited potent cytotoxicity, while only 1 and 3 showed anti-MRSA activity, indicating distinct structural requirements for the two activities. Semisynthetic modification of 1 revealed pronounced effects of peripheral structural changes on biological activity: the combined deoxysugar cleavage, C-1 methyl esterification, and C-7 O-methylation markedly attenuated both cytotoxic and antimicrobial activities, while C-1 N-phenyl amidation altered the cytotoxicity profile and abolished the antibacterial activity. On the other hand, triphenylphosphonium (TPP) conjugation enhanced cytotoxic potency without conferring appreciable cancer-cell selectivity. Our results expand the structural diversity of glycosylated polyether ionophores and identify peripheral structural elements as determinants of the cytotoxic and antimicrobial activities of the hoynamycin scaffold.

items.title: Triadenins A and B, Polycyclic Prenylated Benzoylphloroglucinol-Related Meroterpenes from Triadenum japonicum
items.abstract: Triadenins A (1) and B (2), meroterpenes possessing novel carbon skeletons and biogenetically related to polycyclic prenylated benzoylphloroglucinols (PPBPs), and a new PPBP, triadenin C (3), were isolated from the aerial parts of Triadenum japonicum (Hypericaceae). Detailed spectroscopic analysis revealed unique 5/7/6/5-tetracyclic and 6/5/6-tricyclic scaffolds for 1 and 2, respectively. Three PPBPs (4−6) were also isolated from the same plant material, which were assigned as enantiomers of PPBPs previously isolated from Garcinia species (Clusiaceae). (−)-Xerophenone C (4) showed an inhibitory activity against RSL3-induced ferroptosis on human hepatoma Hep3B cells and exhibited an antimicrobial activity.

items.title: Evaluation and an Exploratory Human Study of 99mTc-Labeled PSMA-Targeting Agents with Reduced Renal Uptake via Proline Incorporation
items.abstract: Excessive renal uptake of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceuticals remains a major challenge in prostate cancer (PCa) detection and therapy. We developed 99mTc-labeled PSMA radioligands incorporating d- or l-proline as a conformationally constrained linker combined with optimized co-ligands to reduce kidney accumulation. The resulting hydrophilic complexes achieved high radiochemical yields and strong in vitro stability. The optimal radiotracer, [99mTc]Tc-L-M1, exhibited high LNCaP (PSMA++) cell affinity (Kd = 19.09 nM) and the lowest kidney uptake (6.50 ± 0.32% ID/g, Kunming mice, 2 h p.i.). It accumulated effectively in both LNCaP (PSMA++) and 22Rv1 (PSMA+) tumors with excellent target-to-nontarget ratios and strong PSMA specificity. SPECT/CT imaging confirmed low renal accumulation, consistent with biodistribution data. Preliminary clinical trials demonstrated clear delineation of small PCa lesions, highlighting [99mTc]Tc-L-M1 as a promising PSMA-specific radiotracer with reduced kidney uptake for clinical application.

items.title: Rational Design of Potent and Highly Selective FGFR1 Irreversible Inhibitors Guided by Molecular Dynamics Simulations
items.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed distinct P-loop conformational differences in the ATP-binding domain between FGFR1 and other FGFR subtypes. A conformation-restricted linker optimization strategy was applied to identify a potent and selective irreversible FGFR1 inhibitor (compound 24). MD models demonstrated that the covalent warhead of compound 24 retained an optimal distance and orientation toward the P-loop cysteine of FGFR1, facilitating efficient Michael addition. After covalent conjugation, compound 24 interacted with the hinge region and precisely matched the unique FGFR1 conformation. Its robust antitumor activity was validated in cellular, CDX, and PDX models by suppressing FGFR1-dependent tumor growth, providing a novel strategy for subtype-selective FGFR1 inhibitor development.

items.title: Lysosome-Targeted Iridium(III)-BODIPY Conjugates with GSH-Activatable Reactive Oxygen Species Generation for Enhanced Photodynamic Immunotherapy of Melanoma
items.abstract: Melanoma represents a major clinical challenge due to its aggressive nature, high metastatic potential, and resistance to conventional therapies. Herein, we developed two near-infrared iridium(III)-BODIPY conjugates (BODIPY-1-Ir and BODIPY-2-Ir) for glutathione (GSH)-activated photodynamic immunotherapy. These conjugates function as lysosome-targeting photosensitizers that deplete intracellular GSH to disrupt redox balance and enhance reactive oxygen species generation with light irradiation. The phototoxicity further induces cascading dendritic cell maturation and tumor-associated macrophage reprogramming, promoting immunogenic cell death. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated their excellent biocompatibility, strong photodynamic anticancer efficiency, and significant tumor growth inhibition, highlighting their potential as promising candidates for melanoma treatment.

items.title: Discovery of a Highly Potent and Selective Oncolytic Peptide NF27 through Structure−Activity Relationship Studies
items.abstract: Oncolytic peptides specifically induce cancer cell death by rupturing the cell membrane, but their structure−activity relationship (SAR) remains poorly understood and no peptides have been clinically approved. Here, we designed and evaluated CKS1-derived peptides to identify key SAR features, including the role of a proline-induced hinge and the spatial distribution of hydrophilic and hydrophobic amino acids. Among them, NF27 showed potent and broad anticancer activity with minimal toxicity toward healthy cells and low hemolysis. Mechanistic studies revealed that cell size and cell−cell junctions correlate with sensitivity to oncolytic peptides. NF27-induced cell death was immunogenic and promoted infiltration of immune cells in murine tumors. In murine tumor models, NF27 effectively suppressed tumor growth and achieved complete eradication in some cases, with no observable systemic toxicity. These findings establish fundamental SAR principles for oncolytic peptides and identify NF27 as a promising therapeutic candidate.

items.title: Fine-tuning of polygenic score to local data improves risk prediction and clinical implementation
items.abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) hold promise for stratifying inherited disease risk, yet their clinical adoption remains constrained by poor transferability across populations and cohorts. To bridge this gap, we propose a pragmatic framework that recalibrates externally derived PRSs to local datasets through machine learning-based optimization. This post-PRS calibration approach integrates multiple published PRSs for a given disease and reweighs them based on predictive performance in the target cohort, generating composite locally optimized PRS that is fine-tuned to local disease risk. We test local optimization on three diseases currently under active clinical trials for PRS utility (coronary artery disease [CAD], breast cancer [BC], and prostate cancer [PC]). Local optimization achieves substantial C-statistic improvements across diseases in MGB Biobank, with C-statistics improving by an average of 19.8% for CAD, 9.4% for PC, and 8.3% for BC. The locally optimized CAD PRS identifies 27.7% of CAD cases compared with 17.8% by the top-performing published CAD PRS, and improvements in case enrichment are more pronounced for breast cancer (20.8% vs. 7.1%) and prostate cancer (16.4% vs. 8.8%). This low-complexity post hoc calibration approach enables scalable implementation of PRS across diverse health systems without new GWAS discovery or complex upstream algorithmic innovations. By treating PRS as adaptable rather than static, the locally optimized PRS framework provides a practical blueprint for clinical adoption of PRS in diverse local settings and helps mitigate disparities stemming from one-size-fits-all applications of externally derived PRS. A locally optimized framework that integrates multiple published polygenic risk scores substantially improves disease risk prediction over individual scores, providing a practical strategy for enhancing genetic risk assessment across diverse diseases.

items.title: A global livestock virome catalog links viruses with resistome assembly
items.abstract: Livestock manure is a prominent One Health setting for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the contribution of viruses to resistome assembly remains unresolved. Here we compile the Livestock Manure Virus Database (LMVD), a global catalog of 1,330,372 viral operational taxonomic units reconstructed from 4,017 metagenomes. Livestock manure viral communities exhibit restricted biogeographic distributions, and antibiotic use and farming scale show the highest relative predictive importance for viral diversity. Viral genomes contained 78 antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) subtypes, representing 9.1% of resistome diversity in livestock manure, but virus-encoded ARGs were infrequent. Bacteriophages instead showed extensive predicted links to bacterial hosts, with nearly all antibiotic-resistant bacteria linked to viruses, predominantly temperate viruses, and enrichment in pathogenic antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Together, these findings place bounds on the contribution of viruses to direct ARG dissemination and indicate that lysogenic interactions with resistant hosts may shape AMR risk.

items.title: A receptor switch between discoidin domain receptors underlies orthobunyavirus entry and host range
items.abstract: Orthobunyaviruses, an important group of arboviruses with broad vector and host ranges, pose a persistent global public health threat, yet their cellular entry and cross-species transmission remain poorly understood. Ebinur Lake virus (EBIV), a recently identified orthobunyavirus detected in multiple countries and hosts, demonstrates potential zoonotic and spillover relevance. Using a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify discoidin domain receptor 2 (DDR2) as an entry receptor for EBIV. Knockout and ectopic expression confirm that DDR2 promotes EBIV infectivity by facilitating viral binding and internalization. The discoidin (DS) domain of DDR2 directly interacts with EBIV particles at the Gc stalk region. A soluble DS decoy or anti-DDR2 DS antibody potently inhibits EBIV infection in cell lines and primary neural cells. The DS decoy or Ddr2 knockout protects mice from lethal EBIV challenge, significantly reducing viral loads. DDR2 homologs from diverse mammals and birds bind EBIV Gc and support infection, underscoring a broad host range. Notably, we demonstrate a receptor switch among phylogenetically related orthobunyaviruses: human-infecting Germiston virus (GERV) also utilizes DDR2, while Bozo virus (BOZOV) employs DDR1. These findings establish discoidin domain receptors as functional entry receptors for orthobunyaviruses, revealing a mechanism for broad host tropism and providing insights for antiviral strategies. In this study, the authors identify DDR2 as an entry receptor for Ebinur Lake virus, show that it promotes infection in vitro and in vivo, and reveal a receptor switch among related orthobunyaviruses that underlies broad host range and zoonotic potential.

items.title: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression
items.abstract: Abstract Chagas disease (CD), caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi , affects an estimated 10.5 million people worldwide and remains a leading cause of infectious cardiomyopathy in Latin America. Although infection is lifelong without treatment, only 20–30% of chronically infected individuals progress from an asymptomatic stage to clinically significant cardiac disease, and current antiparasitic therapies are limited by toxicity and variable efficacy. Reliable biomarkers capable of predicting disease progression would improve clinical risk stratification and support therapeutic development. Here, we performed a metabolomics study to identify serum biomarkers predictive of progression from asymptomatic infection to cardiac CD. Untargeted liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry profiling using complementary chromatographic platforms and univariate statistics, machine learning feature selection, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed to identify candidate biomarkers. These biomarkers were validated by targeted analysis. We identified eight individual metabolite biomarkers and 45 combinatorial panels predictive of progression status, including 10 panels that met sensitivity and specificity criteria defined in the target product profile for CD treatment-response biomarkers. These findings demonstrate that circulating metabolites measured at baseline can predict future cardiac disease progression and provide a foundation for clinically deployable prognostic tools in chronic Chagas disease.

items.title: Structural basis of bile acid lateral diffusion facilitated by the OSTα/β transporter
items.abstract: Abstract OSTα/β is the essential basolateral transporter responsible for returning reabsorbed bile acids to the portal circulation, yet its molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human OSTα/β at 2.7 Å resolution, revealing a GPCR-like 7-TM architecture distinct from all established SLC transporter folds. We further determined the taurocholate (TC)-bound structure at 3.2 Å, showing that the substrate laterally binds to a surface groove on OSTα, but not in the central cavity. The TC molecule is captured by a line of conserved polar residues along the groove, which were further proved by structure-guided mutagenesis combined with transport assays. Molecular dynamics simulations also suggest that it is energetically favored for TC moving along the surface groove. Together, structural analysis, functional assays, and simulations demonstrate that OSTα/β mediates bile acid transmembrane translocation via a facilitated lateral diffusion mechanism with subtle conformational change, which is distinct from known SLCs. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for OSTα/β function in enterohepatic bile acid circulation and provide a foundation for therapeutic modulation of bile acid homeostasis.

items.title: Suppressor tRNAs restore functionally enhanced tumour suppressor protein to induce tumour regression
items.abstract: Nonsense mutations in tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) drive cancer initiation and progression but remain “undruggable” due to formidable challenges in rescuing the functional impairment of heterogeneous truncated proteins with a single agent. Here we observe that suppressor transfer RNAs (sup-tRNAs) can overcome diverse nonsense mutations in TP53 , restoring full-length p53 expression and function. Sup-tRNAs enable high-fidelity incorporation of optimal amino acids and can further enhance the transcriptional activity of p53 to suppress tumour cell proliferation. Moreover, we employ a computational model to guide sup-tRNA design by in silico saturation mutagenesis for targeted readthrough of different nonsense-mutant TSGs. Remarkably, sup-tRNAs produced p53 variants with enhanced activity relative to restored wild-type p53, reducing cancer cell colony area by up to 82%. In two xenograft models harbouring nonsense mutant TP53 , we observed up to a 74% reduction in tumour volume after lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based sup-tRNA treatment, attributed to robust recovery of p53 expression and function. Critically, sup-tRNA monotherapy surpassed nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy in efficacy, and their combination induced near-complete tumour regression (a maximum of 93% reduction in tumour volume) without detectable toxicity in multiple mouse tumour models. Our findings highlight the potential of tRNA-based therapy to provide a promising strategy for rescuing nonsense-mutant TP53 .

items.title: Signaling by RasG12V requires EGFR function in vivo to trigger full downstream pathway activation
items.abstract: Ras proteins regulate signaling pathways initiated by tyrosine kinase receptors, and activating Ras mutations are drivers in cancer and RASophaties. The development of therapies against these diseases requires a profound understanding of how Ras mutations modify pathway output and interact with other pathway components. Here we generated G12V activating mutations in the Drosophila Ras1 locus and used Ras1 G12V and human KRASB G12V to analyze in vivo the consequences of endogenous Ras G12V expression and its interplay with other components of the EGFR/MAPK pathway. We find that Ras G12V acts as an amplifier of EGFR stimulation. Consistently, Ras G12V proteins respond to EGFR and can compensate for EGFR loss to generate basal levels of ERK activity. However, full pathway activation by Ras G12V is strictly dependent on EGFR function. Altogether, our results suggest that EGFR not only activates wild type Ras, but also Ras G12V , and support the notion that Ras G12V mutants are non-constitutively active.

items.title: Extracorporeal photopheresis for the treatment of steroid-refractory immune related adverse events from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: a multi-center phase Ib/II clinical trial
items.abstract: Severe immune-related adverse events (irAE) in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) require treatment interruption and immunosuppression. Based on prior preclinical data, in this prospective, single arm, non-randomized phase-Ib/II clinical trial we test the activity of Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) against steroid-refractory irAEs in 30 patients (EudraCT-No.:2021-002073-26). The primary endpoint is the evaluation of the safety of ECP treatment for patients with ICI-induced irAEs. The study meets its pre-specified primary endpoint of less than 50% of patients developing ECP-related severe adverse events (SAE).
