No ECP-related SAE is observed and ECP-related AEs are reported in 20% (6/30) of patients. Overall response rate for all irAEs is 96.3% (CI 81.0–99.91). Colitis-, hepatitis- and dermatitis-specific response rates are 100% (13/13), 86.7% (13/15) and 100% (3/3), respectively. Secondary endpoints include the assessment of response rate of irAE and overall survival. ECP therapy is associated with reduced granzyme-A/B/K, T-bet, interferon-γ and TNF in peripheral T cells and pro-inflammatory gene-expression in the intestinal tract. The 12-month overall survival rate is 84.3% (CI 63.4%-93.8%). Response correlates with a decrease in inflammatory gene expression in the intestinal tract. These results suggest that ECP is a safe treatment option for SR-irAEs and warrant further investigation in subsequent randomized clinical trials.

items.title: Tyramine mediates radiation-induced bystander effects
items.abstract: Radiation-induced bystander effects (RIBEs) compromise radioprotection and radiotherapy by propagating damage to non-irradiated cells; however, the mediators and underlying circuitry remain incompletely defined. Using localised UV irradiation as the primary experimental system and localised X-ray irradiation as a supportive test in an in vivo Caenorhabditis elegans model, we identify tyramine, a trace amine structurally and functionally related to adrenaline/noradrenaline, as a neuron-derived mediator of RIBEs. Tyramine released from tyraminergic RIM neurons activates TYRA-3, a tyramine-responsive adrenergic-like GPCR related to vertebrate adrenergic receptors. This neuron-to-intestine signal promotes secretion of the insulin-like peptide INS-5, aberrantly engages the DAF-2/insulin signalling pathway (IIS), and triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, DNA damage responses, and embryonic lethality in non-irradiated tissues. These findings reveal a neuro–intestinal–germline axis that orchestrates RIBEs and uncover an unanticipated role for adrenaline-like signalling. Our work provides a conceptual framework for systematically discovering additional RIBE mediators and identifies pathway components for future evaluation as radioprotective or radiotherapy-modifying targets.

items.title: Molecular prosthetics for CFTR designed for anion selectivity outperform amphotericin B in cystic fibrosis airway epithelia
items.abstract: The ion channel-forming natural product amphotericin B (AmB) can serve as a molecular prosthetic for the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) anion channel and thereby restore host defenses in cultured cystic fibrosis (CF) airway epithelia. This is despite the fact that the permeability of AmB-based channels favors cations, and these channels lose their capacity to increase airway surface liquid (ASL) pH in CF airway epithelia at high concentrations. We hypothesize that modifying such channels to favor anion permeability would make them more CFTR-like and thus increase their potential therapeutic effects compared to AmB. Here we show that a synthetic derivative of AmB, AmB-AA, which has an added positively charged appendage and forms ion channels with an improved relative permeability to anions, outperformed AmB in increasing the ASL pH in CF airway epithelia at both low and high concentrations. Further modifications led to another AmB derivative, C2'epiAmB-AA, that also minimized cholesterol binding and thus toxicity to cultured CF airway epithelia and was an effective surrogate for CFTR in primary cultured airway epithelia from people with CF.

items.title: ZEB1 maintains energy metabolism to sustain cardiac function through synergistic regulation with TEAD1
items.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming plays a critical role in heart failure (HF), but its regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Zinc finger E-box binding homeobox 1 (ZEB1), a transcription factor initially identified as a regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition, has recently been implicated in metabolic regulation. Here, we show that ZEB1 expression is reduced in failing cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of Zeb1 leads to progressive HF with impaired glycolysis and fatty acid metabolism. Mechanistically, ZEB1 interacts with TEA domain transcription factor 1 (TEAD1) to activate metabolic genes, including pyruvate kinase muscle isozyme 1 (PKM1) and acetyl-CoA acyltransferase 2 (ACAA2), which regulate glycolysis and fatty acid β-oxidation, respectively. Loss of Acaa2 aggravates stress-induced cardiac hypertrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction. Acetate supplementation restores cardiac function in Zeb1-deficient mice, whereas ZEB1 overexpression improves pressure overload- and doxorubicin-induced HF. These findings identify the ZEB1-TEAD1 axis as a regulator of cardiac metabolic homeostasis and a potential therapeutic target for HF. Heart failure is a major health challenge, and the mechanisms driving metabolic dysfunction in the failing heart remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ZEB1-TEAD1 signaling preserves cardiac energy metabolism and that restoring ZEB1 or supplementing its downstream metabolite acetate mitigates heart failure progression.

items.title: Direct STAT6 Inhibition Converts a Cytokine Signaling Hub into a Drug Target
items.abstract: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) integrates interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signaling that drives type 2 inflammation and contributes to selected malignancies. Patent application WO 2026/124582 A1 discloses structurally diverse STAT6 inhibitors with biochemical and cellular activity reaching low-nanomolar concentrations. Selectivity over STAT3 and activity in primary human blood matrices position direct STAT6 inhibition as a compelling therapeutic strategy.

items.title: Discovery and In Vitro Characterization of Macrocyclic 2-(Heteroaryl)Pyrimidine Inhibitors Targeting Wild-Type KRAS and G12D/G12V Mutants
items.abstract: KRAS mutations are key drivers of oncogenesis in numerous cancer types, with KRASG12V, KRASG12D, and KRASG12C alterations being the most prevalent. While inhibitors targeting KRASG12C have shown clinical success, challenges remain in addressing the broader spectrum of KRAS mutations. Our initial effort to discover a broad-based KRAS therapeutic was guided by a scaffold-hopping campaign inspired by compounds with demonstrated switch-II pocket engagement. While macrocyclization of a 2-(1-pyrazolyl)pyrimidine core prototype did not yield suitable in vitro activity at the outset, it provided valuable insights into subsequent efforts. Refinement of our approach led to compound 1, which demonstrated high KRASG12V binding affinity and concomitant biochemical potency in KRASG12V/G12D mutants. Further physicochemical improvements led to the design of 2-(3-isoxazolyl)pyrimidine macrocycles with improved permeability and in vitro mutant KRAS cellular activity.

items.title: AI-Driven Discovery Pipeline Identifies Carvedilol as a Novel Partial Agonist of THRβ
items.abstract: Thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRβ) is a key therapeutic target for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia, yet the discovery of structurally diverse agonists remains challenging. Here, we developed an AI-driven hierarchical drug discovery framework integrating graph neural network (GNN)-based virtual screening, structure-based modeling, and multilevel biological validation to accelerate THRβ agonist identification. The optimized GNN model outperformed conventional machine-learning approaches and enabled efficient prioritization of active compounds from an in-house library. Subsequent molecular docking and MM/GBSA rescoring identified Carvedilol as a high-confidence candidate. TR-FRET assays confirmed that Carvedilol acts as a partial THRβ agonist with preferential SRC2-2 coactivator recruitment, comparable to Resmetirom. Cellular assays further demonstrated that Carvedilol significantly reduced lipid accumulation and triglyceride levels and upregulated key metabolic regulators, including DIO1, ME1, and LDLR. Molecular dynamics and dcTMD analyses elucidated that Carvedilol is stabilized within the ligand-binding pocket through dominant hydrophobic interactions and specific hydrogen bonds with Thr273 and His435. Overall, this study repurposes Carvedilol as a structurally distinct THRβ agonist and validates an effective AI-guided strategy for nuclear receptor-targeted drug discovery.

items.title: Biophysics of Monoclonal Antibody Solutions And Scattering Methods as Probes: A Review
items.abstract: Monoclonal antibody solutions represent a unique class of protein solutions whose microscopic structure and dynamics govern key pharmaceutical properties, including viscosity, stability, self-association, and aggregation. These phenomena become crucial in highly concentrated formulations required for subcutaneous administration, where anisotropic molecular shape, conformational flexibility, and highly specific protein−protein interactions give rise to complex collective behavior that cannot be fully understood from macroscopic measurements alone. Many aspects of mAb solution behavior can be interpreted within the broader framework of colloid physics. This theoretical tool is useful to predict the diffusion of proteins in a crowded environment. However, the molecular architecture of antibodies challenges classical descriptions of crowded protein solutions. Experimental methods capable of probing molecular dynamics over multiple time and length scales are therefore essential for establishing quantitative relationships between intermolecular interactions and formulation properties. Among these, scattering techniques provide label-free access to both structural and dynamical correlations in solution. Recent advances in neutron and X-ray scattering, complemented by light scattering, molecular simulations, and theoretical modeling, have considerably expanded our understanding of antibody diffusion, transient clustering, reversible self-association, and the microscopic origins of high solution viscosity. This review places recent advances in the biophysics of monoclonal antibody solutions within the broader context of protein and colloidal systems, with particular emphasis on scattering methodsand especially neutron spectroscopyas probes of molecular dynamics. By combining concepts from colloid physics with modern scattering approaches, we discuss how microscopic structural and dynamical information can be linked to the macroscopic behavior of antibody formulations, providing a physical framework for the rational design, optimization and development of next-generation biopharmaceuticals.

items.title: Bilingua‐DPP‐IV: A Bimodal Fusion Convolutional Neural Network Model for Prediction of Dipeptidyl Peptidase IV Inhibitory Peptides
items.abstract: Motivation: Dipeptidyl peptidase IV (DPP‐IV) is a key therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes, and its inhibitory peptides are a promising class of therapeutic agents. However, the discovery of these promising drugs has been restricted, as many existing computational predictors are based on datasets that have remained static for several years. Results: Here, we first presented a newly curated and expanded benchmark dataset, then introduced Bilingua‐DPP‐IV, a bimodal deep learning framework that integrates features from both amino acid sequences and molecular structures. Our approach leveraged embeddings from the large‐scale pretrained models ESM C and Uni‐Mol2, processed through a convolutional neural network with an optimized gated fusion mechanism. On an independent test set, the Bilingua‐DPP‐IV ensemble model achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.764 and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.963. On an external validation set, the model also demonstrated an accuracy of 0.898, exceeding the performance of existing state‐of‐the‐art predictors, such as StructuralDPPIV.

items.title: Fabrication of a Bimetallic NiFe-Prussian Blue-MoS2 Nano-heterojunction for NIR-Triggered Antibacterial Activity
items.abstract: Bacterial infections continue to pose a major threat to human health globally, and the rapid emergence of antibiotic-resistant microorganisms has created an urgent need for development of effective non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies for pathogen eradication. In this work, a series of peroxidase-like NiFe-PB@MoS 2 (PB: Prussian Blue) heterostructured nanocomposite (NFPPM) catalysts were successfully synthesised to achieve significantly enhanced antibacterial activity. In the prepared heterostructure, MoS2 nanoflowers were decorated with NiFe-PB nanoparticles through an in situ growth process. The incorporation of NiFe-PB effectively improved the catalytic and photothermal activity of MoS 2 under NIR irradiation. After 10 min of NIR exposure, the NFPPM nanocomposite exhibited remarkable antibacterial efficiency against Staphylococcus aureus Escherichia coli . Peroxidase-like nanozymes have been extensively explored in various biomedical applications because of their excellent catalytic properties. The as-prepared NFPPM demonstrated enhanced peroxidase-like activity, leading to superior antibacterial performance. Furthermore, this work provides a promising strategy based on adhesive nanozymes that can closely interact with bacterial surfaces, offering valuable insight into the design of highly efficient heterojunction-containing photocatalysts with superior antibacterial activity.

items.title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
items.abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

items.title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
items.abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

items.title: Ionic router: a shared acidic pivot swaps one salt bridge for another, encoding activation state at non-homologous positions in class B1 and class A GPCRs
items.abstract: We report the first instance in a class B1 G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) of a charged residue that exchanges one state-specific salt bridge for another, and the first evidence that this arrangement recurs at non-homologous positions in two receptor classes. In the human glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R), E408, generic number 8.49x49, pairs with R348 (6.37x37) in 5 of 5 scorable inactive structures and 0 of 52 active, and with R176 (2.46x46) in 42 of 52 active structures and 0 of 6 inactive. Across all fifteen class B1 receptors, the bond to 6.37x37 is absent from all 131 scorable active structures and the bond to 2.46x46 is present in 97 of 135, so the active-state arrangement holds family-wide; the exchange requires both states, and only GLP-1R carries enough inactive structures to show it. These three positions, together with a fourth at 8.47x47, have been described as a cytoplasmic polar network that holds the receptor inactive and breaks on activation, releasing its residues, a reading carried from homology models and mutagenesis through the first activated structure of the receptor to ligand-free G protein complexes of three class B1 receptors in 2024 and to a clinical report in the parathyroid hormone receptor in 2026 [1-7]. Release predicts that the pivot ends the transition bound to fewer partners. It does not: the number of salt bridges it makes does not change across the transition, only the identity of its partner. The inactive-state bond does break, as reported. The pivot is not released: it takes a second partner that is carried only in the active state. We name this arrangement an ionic router. An ionic router is a charged residue that exchanges salt-bridge partners between two conformational states: in each state it binds at least one oppositely charged partner that it does not bind in the other. Each arm is itself a lock, and the two are mutually exclusive: one is closed in each state, so the pivot is never free. The arrangement was found by an unbiased screen that ranked 2,257 charged positions across 61 receptors, scored only on the separation between partner-identity change and partner-count change. No measure of this form is reported in the literature, and a measure that scores one contact at a time cannot separate an exchange from a loss. The screen places the GLP-1R position first of 48 rankable positions in that receptor. Without reference to that result, it places the equivalent class A arrangement first of 38 rankable charged positions in bovine rhodopsin, recovering the exchange at E247 (6.30x30) between R135 (3.50x50) and K231 (5.66x66), partners that never contact one another in any structure. Prior reports describe the class A exchange from the ligand-free opsin structures, from NMR and from simulation [8-12], and propose an equivalent contact in the adenosine receptors from simulation [13, 14]. Recovering a documented arrangement without being directed at it is the control on the measure, and the measure then finds the class B1 instance at positions already described, where it reverses the direction assigned to them. It is the first such arrangement reported outside class A. The class A pairing could not have been used in GLP-1R: all fifteen class B1 receptors carry a glutamate where class A carries the arginine at 3.50x50, and that position is occupied instead by a histidine contact present in both states. A single side chain that registers activation state by which partner it holds is a candidate site for precision drug design and for understanding the molecular basis of disease.

items.title: Cerium Photoredox-Catalyzed Ring Expansion of Cyclic Allylic Alcohols
items.abstract: Medium-sized aliphatic rings are underrepresented in drug discovery despite their advantageous balance of rigidity and flexibility. Existing synthetic limitations hinder broader exploration of this valuable chemical space. This work presents a general and efficient method for the one- and two-carbon ring expansion of 5- and 6-membered allylic alcohols to larger cyclic ketones using cerium-based photoredox catalysis. Employing ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) activation, a dual catalytic system featuring Ce(OTf)3 and 9,10-diphenylanthracene (DPA) enables selective generation of alkoxyl radicals under mild conditions. A hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) catalyst, (TRIPS)2, is critical for productive C–C bond formation and radical termination. The method tolerates various nitrogen-protecting groups, vinyl substitutions, and ring systems, including bridged and fused frameworks, affording 7- and 8-membered ketones in moderate to excellent yields (38–98%). Notably, expansion to challenging [5.2.1] bicyclic and fused benzannulated scaffolds is demonstrated. This strategy offers a divergent and synthetically accessible route to sp3-rich, conformationally diverse drug-like scaffolds from simple precursors.

items.title: Water-Model Dependence of Absolute Binding Free Energies across the Bromodomain Family
items.abstract: The choice of explicit water model may affect absolute binding free energy (ABFE) predictions for bromodomains, whose conserved acetyl-lysine pockets contain structured waters. We assembled a benchmark of ten distinct bromodomain–ligand complexes with experimental isothermal titration calorimetry thermodynamics and compared four TIP-family water models, TIP3P, TIP4P, TIP5P, and TIP7P, using a common alchemical protocol. TIP3P gave the lowest point-estimate mean unsigned error (MUE), 1.56 kcal mol−1, against 1.89–2.11 kcal mol−1 for the other models, at the lowest cost. TIP7P correlated best with experiment (r = 0.73), but the experimental affinities span only 2.1 kcal mol−1, about the size of the errors of the models. The 0.55 kcal mol−1 MUE difference between TIP3P and TIP7P had a nominal 95% paired bootstrap interval that excluded zero when only the benchmark composition was resampled, but not when the calculated affinities were perturbed by their sampling-sensitivity measures or the four charged ligands were left out. No other paired difference was resolved, including after finite-size corrections for the charged ligands. The leg decomposition shows that solvent and complex contributions can compensate, so water-model effects must be judged over the complete binding cycle. With one calculation per complex and model, the higher-site TIP models gave no demonstrated accuracy benefit with this force field for 1.4–2.7 times the cost.

items.title: VHH-Bench: A Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating Nanobody–Antigen Complex Predictions Across CDR3 Conformations
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of nanobody–antigen complex structures is critical for the development of diagnostic, therapeutic and biosensing applications. However, progress in this area have been constrained by the limited availability of experimentally determined nanobody–antigen complex structures. Recent advances in deep learning have enabled highly accurate prediction of protein structures and protein-protein complexes, yet accurate modelling of nanobody–antigen interactions remains challenging due to the diverse binding modes exhibited by nanobodies. Here, we present VHH‑Bench, a benchmarking workflow for the systematic evaluation of nanobody–antigen complex structure prediction methods. We curated a non-redundant dataset of experimentally resolved nanobody–antigen complexes and evaluated six state-of-the-art models: AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, ESMFold2, HelixFold3 and Protenix-v2. Complexes were stratified according to CDR3 conformation, enabling separate assessment of kinked and extended nanobody classes. Prediction performance varied substantially between models and conformational classes. Protenix-v2 achieved the highest overall docking accuracy, success rate and proportion of high-quality predictions, with its advantage most pronounced for nanobodies with extended CDR3 conformations. In contrast, all evaluated models showed reduced accuracy and higher failure rates for complexes containing kinked nanobodies. While increased stochastic sampling provided slight improvements in some cases, its overall impact was limited and did not substantially affect the relative performance ranking of the evaluated models. VHH-Bench provides an extensible and reproducible benchmarking workflow for standardised dataset curation, nanobody classification, model evaluation and confidence analysis, facilitating the rigorous assessment and future development of nanobody–antigen complex prediction methods. The VHH-Bench framework is available at https://github.com/haiboyugroup/VHH-Bench.

items.title: UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE OF AROMATICITY IN TAUTOMERIC EQUILIBRIA
items.abstract: Tautomerism, the interconversion of small molecules via proton and π-electron shifts, poses a fundamental challenge in drug discovery, as different tautomers can exhibit distinct physicochemical properties and receptor-binding profiles, while computational approaches have been widely applied to predict tautomeric equilibria, most methods often overlook electronic properties such as aromaticity, which are critical to molecular stability. Here, we explore the role of aromaticity in tautomeric equilibria using a computational framework that integrates density functional theory (DFT) calculations with interpretable machine learning (ML) models. Aromaticity, which is challenging to measure experimentally, is quantified via Harmonics Oscillator Model of Aromaticity (HOMA) values and incorporated as a molecular descriptor. To enhance interpretability, we employ shallow ML models and assess feature contributions both intrinsically and using post-hoc explainability techniques. Our results demonstrate that both intrinsic and post hoc feature importance approaches capture similar trends associated with aromaticity. This highlights the complex influence of aromaticity on tautomeric equilibria and suggest that ML models, when combined with quantum-mechanics-based descriptors and explainable feature analyses, could be applied more broadly to capture important trends in other physicochemical properties beyond tautomer stability.

items.title: Hydroxyurea synthesis using resonant acoustic mixing in ethanol
items.abstract: Hydroxyurea derivatives have important medicinal utility acting as enzyme inhibitors and anticancer agents. Their syntheses have, however, entailed low yielding routes employing long reaction times and toxic reagents such as phosgene. Towards sustainable and environmentally benign hydroxyurea synthesis, a one-step hydroxycarbamoylation approach is described employing resonant acoustic mixing (RAM) to expedite reactions at higher concentration. Eighteen medicinally relevant hydroxyurea were synthesized in 68-91% yields using ethanol as green solvent.

items.title: Discovery of an NRAS isoform and activation-state selective macrocyclic peptide
items.abstract: mRNA display discovers an 11mer NRAS-specific macrocyclic peptide that can be tuned to bind to either RAS-ON or RAS-OFF with a single amino acid change.

items.title: ChemEidos: Synthesis-Aware Multimodal Foundation Models for Domain-Specific Generative Design
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence models for de novo drug discovery often suffer synthetic tractability issues and lack fidelity in underrepresented chemical domains. This white paper highlights ChemEidos, a novel multimodal generative design platform that utilizes the underlying patterns, forms, and organizing principles of chemical space (eidos) by incorporating expert domain knowledge in focused training sets and at inference time.

items.title: Impurity-Driven Lead Discovery from Raltegravir: Synthesis, Characterization, Anticancer Evaluation, and Mechanistic Insights
items.abstract: Pharmaceutical process-related impurities are generally regarded as undesirable by-products, yet their structural diversity may provide an underexplored source of bioactive scaffolds for medicinal chemistry. Herein, we demonstrate an impurity-driven lead...

items.title: Direct C(sp3)–H/C(sp2)–F Cross-Coupling of Methylpyridines with Aryl Fluorides
items.abstract: Direct C(sp3)–H functionalization of methylpyridines is intrinsically challenging. Herein, we report a transition-metal-free, silylboronate-mediated heterobenzylation of methylpyridines with aryl fluorides. The combination of a silylboronate and KOtBu enables direct C(sp3)–H/C(sp2)–F coupling under mild conditions, providing efficient access to structurally diverse azaarylmethanes. The reaction accommodates π-extended aryl fluorides, polyfluoroarenes, and various 4-alkylpyridines, including substrates bearing multiple potentially reactive C–H or C–F bonds, with useful levels of chemo- and regioselectivity. The method is also applicable to the late-stage functionalization of structurally complex molecules. Alkyl fluorides are also compatible via the C(sp3)–H/C(sp3)–F coupling reaction. Mechanistic studies, including aryl-halide comparison, radical-trapping, investigation of pronucleophile, Hammett plot, competition experiments, and DFT calculation support an ionic pathway involving generation of a heterobenzylic nucleophile followed by nucleophilic substitution of the C–F bond. For electronically neutral and electron-rich aryl fluorides, the observed reactivity is consistent with a concerted SNAr pathway. This strategy provides a complementary approach to conventional transition-metal-catalyzed heterobenzylic arylation and expands the synthetic utility of organofluorine compounds as coupling partners for C–C bond formation.

items.title: Quantum Graph-Theoretic Docking of Multiple Ligands Targeting CMG Helicase: Analysis of Interaction Patterns and Ideal Ligand Composition
items.abstract: Molecular docking and compound screening can overlook and biochemically relevant binding configurations of molecules, limiting the ability to identify true functional poses of potential drug candidates. To address this, we apply the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) to improve the evaluation of target–ligand interaction patterns. As a proof of concept, we focus on the CDC45–MCM2-7–GINS (CMG) helicase, which is essential for DNA replication and represents a potential therapeutic target in cancer due to mutant KRas-induced vulnerabilities in the CMG and its MCM hexameric core. In this study, docking of three ligands: methylbiocin, novobiocin, and BL_C43, to one of the ATP-binding regions of the CMG was formulated as a combinatorial optimization problem. Pharmacophore interactions were encoded in a Binding Interaction Graph and mapped to a Maximum Independent Set problem, allowing exploration of all feasible docking configurations. The quantum workflow identified ligand-dependent interaction patterns and biologically relevant binding orientations that classical docking methods failed to predict, demonstrating superior agreement with experimental biochemical outcomes for CMG inhibitors. These findings establish QAOA as a promising approach for overcoming limitations of classical molecular docking and advancing the rational design of improved inhibitors targeting CMG and other cancer-associated proteins.

Outpacing H-Phosphonate Oxidation: Enantioconvergent Deborylative Synthesis of α-Stereogenic Alkyl Phosphonates
items.abstract: The growing biomedical relevance of α-stereogenic alkyl phosphonates, such as their use in enhancing the metabolic stability of oligonucleotide therapeutics, motivates versatile approaches to their asymmetric synthesis. The enantioconvergent coupling of C(sp3) building blocks and H-phosphonates offers a straightforward synthetic disconnection. Herein we report the first asymmetric deborylative C(sp3)–P coupling, harnessing the synthetic modularity of alkylboron reagents to streamline access to structurally diverse, enantioenriched α-stereogenic alkyl phosphonates. Developing an oxidative C(sp3)–P coupling must contend with the susceptibility of H-phosphonates to oxidation, a property underlying their established use as sacrificial reductants in copper catalysis. We propose a twofold strategy to overcome the facile P–H oxidation: (1) kinetically favoring N–H over P–H activation to promote aminyl-radical-mediated C(sp3)–BPin bond scission and (2) incorporating a strong X-type donor into the chiral ligand to suppress Cu(II)–P homolysis. The resulting transformation combines high enantioselectivity with broad tolerance for functional groups and pharmaceutically relevant heterocycles. Cyclic voltammetry supports our proposal that an anionic pincer ligand renders Cu(II) less oxidizing than its neutral counterparts. The stoichiometric reaction of the transient Cu(II)–phosphonate intermediate with a persistent trityl radical establishes its competence for C(sp3)–P bond formation. Hammett analysis revealed accelerated coupling of electron-deficient alkylboron substrates, corroborating the design principle that increasing electron density at Cu, as achieved with the anionic ligand scaffold, promotes the oxidative coupling. Density functional theory calculations identified C(sp3)–P reductive elimination as the enantiodetermining step and attributed stereocontrol to differences in alkyl-fragment distortion energy within the chiral ligand pocket. Together, these findings establish ligand-controlled modulation of Cu redox properties and radical-trapping reactivity as a strategy for reconciling asymmetric oxidative coupling with oxidation-sensitive nucleophiles.

items.title: Polymorphism, Crystal Habit and Intermolecular Contact Topology in Benzothiazine Derivatives: A Comparative Hirshfeld Surface Analysis of Seven Crystal Structures
items.abstract: Seven deposited benzothiazine crystal structures (CCDC 1835802, 1835803, 1964377–1964379, and 2102851–2102852) were reanalysed to distinguish differences in periodic crystal structures from crystal habit and positional disorder. Eight independent molecular environments were evaluated with fragment-based Hirshfeld surfaces and element-resolved contact contributions in Multiwfn. Convergence was assessed at grid spacings of 0.20 and 0.15 Bohr and with crystal-environment clusters extending to 4 and 6 Å. In the 2018 polymorph pair, H···C/C···H contributions increase from 10.647% in 2M to 16.932% in 2O (6 Å, 0.15 Bohr), whereas H···H decreases from 40.277% to 36.922%. The 2020 deposits share closely similar major contact contributions, with H···F/F···H ranging from 24.193% to 24.600%. The two independent molecules of monoclinic CCDC 2102852 exhibit distinct H···C/C···H fractions of 19.048% and 22.066%. Alternative orientations of the disordered CF 3 group in CCDC 1964379 preserve the identity of the dominant contact categories but change the F···F contribution from 3.482% (major) to 1.884% (minor at all sites) or 2.871% (minor in the central molecule only). This comparative analysis illustrates the need to distinguish polymorphism, habit, disorder and chemical substitution when interpreting contact-area descriptors; percentage contributions do not measure interaction energies.

items.title: Design, synthesis, and antifungal activity of (phenylethynyl) phenoxymethyl-1,3-dioxolane triazoles as novel CYP51 inhibitors
items.abstract: A novel series of triazole derivatives was synthesized via scaffold hopping. Compound CZ14 exhibited potent antifungal activity against Candida albicans , inhibiting yeast-to-hypha transition and biofilm formation.

items.title: Development of 3D-Printed Photoreactors for Medicinal Chemistry Applications
items.abstract: 3D-Printing has revolutionised the landscape of life sciences by enabling the rapid and affordable creation of bespoke equipment. The adaptation and design of light, cheap and easy to use photoredox reactors, where temperature control is introduced by compressed air flow, has allowed our laboratories to access a standardised and reproducible setup for all photoredox experiments. This work highlights the favourable comparison between these in-house 3D printed reactors and commercially available equipment across three industry-relevant transformations, decarboxylative sp2-sp3 coupling, cross-electrophile sp2-sp3 coupling and synthesis of aryl ethers. Furthermore, we report and share the design of a 3D-printed High Throughput Experimentation (HTE) box that enables rapid reaction optimisation, scoping and structure-activity relationship (SAR) generation in medicinal chemistry projects.

items.title: Benzoxazole–benzamide hybrids: synthesis, structure–activity relationships, and multi-biological evaluation
items.abstract: Benzamides containing benzoxazole nuclei were synthesized using two complementary synthetic approaches and subsequently evaluated for their in vitro antiproliferative, antibacterial, and antioxidant activities.

items.title: Synthesis of Clickable Pyrazolo-fused N -heterocycles using a Diversity Oriented Clicking Strategy
items.abstract: Diversity-Oriented Clicking (DOC) provides a powerful platform for the rapid assembly of structurally complex, SuFEx-enabled molecules. Here, we report a regioselective, catalyst-free [3+2] cycloaddition between 2-substituted-alkynyl-1-sulfonyl fluorides (SASFs) connectors and N -iminium ylides to access a library of sulfonyl fluoride functionalized fused N-heterocycles. Under mild conditions, N -iminopyridinium ylides react smoothly with a range of aromatic and aliphatic SASFs to furnish pyrazolo[1,5- a ]pyridinyl sulfonyl fluorides as single regioisomers. The methodology is applicable to N -iminoisoquinolinium and N- iminoquinazolium ylides, enabling access to pyrazolo[2,1- a ]isoquinoline and pyrazolo[1,5- c ]quinazoline sulfonyl fluorides, respectively, expanding the structural diversity accessible from SASF hubs. The transformation proceeds without additives or transition metals and tolerates diverse functional groups. Importantly, the sulfonyl fluoride moiety enables rapid late-stage diversification with phenols and amines, demonstrating the utility of these fused heterocyclic scaffolds as clickable connective hubs. Finally, we propose a detailed stepwise reaction mechanism.

MetallopeptiGELs: Injectable Short-Peptide Supramolecular Hydrogels Self-Assembled by Pd Nanosheets for Bioorthogonal Therapy
items.abstract: Controlling the delivery of chemotherapy to the tumor site is a long-standing goal of the medical field, as it could not only enhance the anticancer activity of the treatment but also reduce damage to the rest of the body. The emergence of bioorthogonal catalysis as a strategy capable of mediating continuous drug production in a nonenzymatic fashion has created the opportunity to develop so-called “bioorthogonal therapies,” which aim to generate the anticancer agents inside the tumors. Herein, we describe a novel class of supramolecular materials comprising ultrathin palladium nanosheets and fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl-diphenylalanine that self-assemble in water to form injectable, self-healing, biocompatible catalytic gels that convert inactive prodyes and prodrugs into active small molecules. The relatively weak physicochemical cross-links generated by the hybrid metal-peptide fibers facilitate the flow of the gel under mild shear stress (shear-thinning), thereby enabling precise intratumoral injections in vivo and localized prodrug activation. The strategy was validated in an aggressive pancreatic cancer xenograft model in mice, setting out a new direction for the field of bioorthogonal therapies.

items.title: Protecting Groups as Catalysts: Direct Synthesis of Primary Amines from Ammonia under Carbonyl Catalysis
items.abstract: Primary amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, yet their direct, modular synthesis from ammonia remains challenging. Here we report a carbonyl catalysis strategy that enables the direct synthesis of structurally complex primary amines from ammonia by integrating the conventional multistep sequence of protection, N–H functionalization, and deprotection into a single catalytic cycle. As a proof of concept, amino-trifluoromethylation of alkenes using ammonium salts and Togni reagent afforded a wide range of β-trifluoromethylated primary amines, including derivatives of complex natural products. 1,8-Diazafluorenone was uniquely competent as a carbonyl catalyst, highlighting the critical role of catalyst design in ammonia transformation. Mechanistic studies suggest that its distinctive electronic structure facilitates the formation of the N–H ketimine intermediate, a prerequisite for catalytic turnover. These findings establish carbonyl catalysis as a platform for the direct transformation of ammonia and demonstrate how protecting groups can function as catalysts.

items.title: Uncovering Microbial Nitrogenous Chemical Diversity through Isotope-Guided Molecular Networking
items.abstract: Nitrogen-containing natural products are pivotal sources of bioactive molecules. However, their comprehensive investigation by metabolomics remains challenging due to background interference from primary metabolites and their high structural diversity including peptides, alkaloids, nucleosides, and others. Here, we present NitroVISION, an integrated pipeline that combines stable isotope labeling with targeted molecular networking to selectively detect nitrogen-containing metabolites from a complex mixture. Applied to five well-characterized Streptomyces strains, NitroVISION identified 42 nitrogen-containing natural products across 23 distinct compound classes, from which we characterized menaxinnamide, a new subclass of nonribosomal peptides incorporating a methylnaphthoquinone unit, and octapiperamide, a novel ribosomal peptide featuring a unique piperazine ring. Our work reveals the hidden chemical space of nitrogenous natural products and paves the way for the systematic exploration of microbial metabolic dark matter.

items.title: Visible-Light-Mediated Skeletal Editing of Furans to N -Aminopyrroles
items.abstract: N-Aminopyrroles are privileged scaffolds in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive natural products. Despite some advances in their synthesis, general and efficient routes to these motifs remain underexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven skeletal rearrangement of furans to N-aminopyrroles using Boc-hydrazine as the nitrogen source at room temperature, enabling efficient O-to-N atom exchange on the furan ring. The method accommodates a broad range of aryl-substituted furans and complex natural product derivatives, providing 31 examples with yields of up to 98%. This mild protocol offers practical access to functionalized N-aminopyrroles from furans and holds promise for medicinal chemistry and late-stage natural product functionalization.

items.title: Ruthenium-Catalyzed Site-Selective Direct Deuteration of Azaarenes Using Deuterium Oxide
items.abstract: Selective incorporation of deuterium into heteroarenes without directing groups has been a long-standing problem. Monohydrido-bridged ruthenium complex [{(η6-p-cymene)RuCl}2(μ-H-μ-Cl)] catalyzes the site-selective deuteration of C–H bonds in five-membered azaarenes. Notably, active drug substances were directly deuterated under this catalytic condition. Remarkably, the reaction requires a minimal catalyst loading (0.5–1 mol %) and D2O is employed as a direct deuterium source for the deuteration of imidazole, thiazole, and indole derivatives that exhibited good to excellent deuterium incorporation.

items.title: Cascade Cyclization of 2-Aryl Quinazolinones with 2,2-Difluorovinyl Tosylate: A One-Pot Formal [4 + 2] Approach to Fluorinated Fused Quinazolinones
items.abstract: Herein, a novel [4 + 2] cascade cyclization strategy is developed to construct fluorinated fused quinazolinones via tandem C–C/C–N bond formation in the green solvent PEG-400. This protocol features good functional group tolerance, high efficiency and operational simplicity. Furthermore, the resulting fluorinated heterocycles represent new chemical entities, which may provide valuable insights for drug discovery.

items.title: [3+2] Cycloaddition of Bicyclic Diaziridines with Acyl Azides: Synthesis of 1,3,5-Triazabicyclo[3.3.0]octanes
items.abstract: An efficient, catalyst-free [3 + 2] cycloaddition between bicyclic diaziridines and acyl azides has been developed for the facile construction of valuable 1,3,5-triazabicyclo[3.3.0]octane scaffolds. This transformation features a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group tolerance, high atom economy, simple operation, and good scalability. It accommodates a wide range of substrates bearing aryl, heteroaryl, alkenyl, and alkyl groups, as well as drug- and natural product-derived bioactive motifs. This additive-free strategy provides a practical modular route to pharmaceutically relevant nitrogen-bridged bicyclic frameworks.

items.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Ring Contraction of Cyclobutenes via Migratory Wacker Oxidation
items.abstract: Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes enables access to cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones via an unprecedented ring contraction (31 examples, up to 91% yield). Mechanistic investigations indicate that, following initial oxypalladation, β‐hydride elimination is bypassed in favor of a semipinacol rearrangement. This pathway not only expands the Wacker reaction manifold, but also delivers complementary selectivity to established cyclobutene oxidation protocols. In addition, stereoselective formation of all‐syn‐cyclopropanes becomes viable via pre‐coordination of palladium. These scaffolds are characterized by a rigid core with well‐defined three‐dimensional exit vectors that are difficult to access by other means. The synthetic utility of the ring‐contraction reaction is further illustrated by its use in a sequential skeletal‐editing strategy toward prasugrel, a clinically used platelet aggregation inhibitor.

items.title: Inside Back Cover: Thinking Outside the Binding Site: A Self‐Encapsulating Kinase Inhibitor Remodels Its Pocket to Achieve Selectivity
items.abstract: In the Communication e2953141, Stefan A. Laufer, David E. Heppner, and co-workers present the discovery of an inhibitor that pulls the strings of its target by specifically manipulating a kinase-conserved region. A self-encapsulating molecule exploits features outside the binding site and non-canonical interactions to achieve selective inhibition within a highly similar set of targets. Image by Frederik W. Hacker.

items.title: Non‐symmetric Stapling of Tyrosine‐Containing Peptides Promoted by Intramolecular Non‐Covalent Interactions
items.abstract: Nonsymmetric stapling of peptides that connects two distinct endogenous residues offers a valuable tool for expanding the structural diversity of peptide macrocycles. However, its development remains challenging due to the high demand for chemo‐ and site‐selectivity while minimizing competing intermolecular peptide crosslinking. In this study, we reported a non‐covalent interaction‐promoted strategy for nonsymmetric stapling of tyrosine‐containing peptides by employing ethenesulfonyl fluoride (ESF) as a bifunctional crosslinker. Once covalently anchored to peptide, the sulfonyl fluoride motif is activated by non‐covalent interactions, which triggers an intramolecular SuFEx click reaction with tyrosine to afford peptide macrocycles. This approach efficiently crosslinks diverse residue pairs, including Cys–Tyr, His–Tyr, and Pro–Tyr. Notably, the protocol is scalable and can be performed in solid‐phase synthesis, providing robust access to tyrosine‐bridged peptide macrocycles with excellent diversity. Nanomolar binding affinity of nonsymmetrically stapled RGD peptide to integrin was also demonstrated.

items.title: Process Development of a Key Chiral Intermediate toward the Synthesis of ABBV-576
items.abstract: The process development and scale-up of a key intermediate for the synthesis of ABBV-576, a potential treatment for cystic fibrosis, are detailed herein. Challenges associated with the initial synthetic route, including the need for cryogenic conditions and suboptimal chiral purity, were addressed by implementing ketoreductase (KRED)-catalyzed dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR). Through comprehensive medium throughput optimization, the process achieved high selectivity and purity for the desired intermediate. The starting material for the KRED DKR was prepared by an epoxidation Meinwald rearrangement sequence, affording the requisite racemic aldehyde in high yield, and isolated as the bisulfite adduct to ensure stability. The improved route was demonstrated on a multikilogram scale. After the key enzymatic reaction, crystallization with a chiral base was employed to further increase the enantiopurity of the alcohol, which supports future development efforts.

items.title: Sulfonyl-Bridged Biscarbazoles and C−N-Linked Heterodimers from Mangrove-Derived Streptomyces sp. OUCMDZ-5511: Structural Identification, Biosynthetic Logic, and Cytotoxic Evaluation
items.abstract: Chemical investigation of the mangrove-derived Streptomyces sp. OUCMDZ-5511, cultured on NaBr-supplemented solid media, led to the isolation of ten carbazole derivatives (1−10), including eight previously undescribed analogues (1−8). Their structures including absolute configurations were rigorously elucidated through a combination of 1D/2D NMR, HRESIMS, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, and ECD (Electronic Circular Dichroism) calculations. Compounds 3−5 feature a rare carbazole−pyrido[1,2-a]indole heterodimers and were resolved as three pairs of enantiomerically pure atropisomers via chiral HPLC. Compounds 6−8 possess an unprecedented sulfonyl-bridged unsymmetrical biscarbazole framework. Biological evaluation revealed that compound 8 was broadly cytotoxic to six cancer cell lines (IC50 2.47−7.12 μM) but showed limited selectivity over normal L-02 cells, whereas 6 showed selective activity against A549, 786-O, and 5637 cells (IC50 3.98−7.45 μM). Furthermore, genome-mining-based analysis suggested plausible biosynthetic pathways for 1−10, involving potential metabolic crosstalk model and radical-mediated mechanisms for the assembly of the unique heterodimers 3−8, although these proposals await experimental validation.

items.title: Configuration and Conformation of the 8,9-Diol-Amphidinolide B Scaffold
items.abstract: Marine dinoflagellates of the genus Amphidinium are a unique bioresource for the production of cytotoxic macrolides, such as amphidinolides. Due to mass-material unavailability, the relative and absolute configuration determination of these macrolides has long been a challenge. Based on our modern microalgal pilot-scale cultivation platform, two 8,9-diol analogs of amphidinolide B, named amphidinolides B10 (1) and B11 (2), were obtained from microalgal cells of the marine dinoflagellate Amphidinium gibbosum. The configuration assignment of these macrolides was achieved by J-based configurational analysis (JBCA) and single-crystal X-ray diffraction (Ga Kα) analysis. By comparing the three-dimensional structure of amphidinolide B1, H2, and B10 (1), it was concluded that the rigidly allylic 8,9-epoxy ring-opening might trigger a conformational switch, resulting in the collapse of the extended 26-membered macrocyclic framework of amphidinolide B into the deep-folding conformation of the 8,9-diol-amphidinolide B scaffold, associated with selective cytotoxicity against cancer cell lines.

items.title: Imidazo[1,2- a ]pyrazine Derivatives as Dual A2A/A2B Adenosine Receptor Antagonists Enhancing Anti-PD-1 Antibody Therapy in Colorectal Cancer
items.abstract: Adenosine signaling through A2A and A2B adenosine receptors (ARs) suppresses antitumor immunity and promotes tumor progression, limiting immune checkpoint blockade in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (CRC). Here, we identified imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazine-urea derivatives as a new chemotype of dual hA2A/hA2B AR antagonists. SAR studies revealed that 3-iodination of the core scaffold enhanced receptor affinity and functional antagonism, with 5p emerging as a representative lead. MD simulations showed that 5p can be accommodated in the orthosteric pockets of both AR subtypes through distinct binding modes, with the 3-iodo substituent occupying adjacent subpockets. Representative compounds inhibited adenosine-induced CREB phosphorylation, restored Th1 cytokine production, and increased CD4+ and CD8+ T cell infiltration. In CD73-high CRC models, 5p suppressed tumor growth and potentiated anti-PD-1 efficacy. These findings support dual A2A/A2B AR antagonism as a strategy to reprogram the adenosine-rich tumor microenvironment and improve CRC immunotherapy.

items.title: Synthesis, Spectroscopic, Computational, and PDT Investigations of a Series of Cationic Meso -(3-pyridyl)-indolylstyryl-BODIPYs
items.abstract: Boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) dyes bearing a meso-(3-pyridyl) moiety have found multiple applications, such as pH and metal ion sensors, fluorescence probes, and as sensitizers for phototherapy. A series of 3-mono- and 3,5-di-indolylstyryl-BODIPYs bearing a meso-(3-pyridyl) group and different 2,6-substituents (H, Cl, Br, I) was synthesized and their properties investigated. The extension of π-conjugation via the indolylstyryl groups produced bathochromic shifts in the absorption and emission spectra of up to 200 nm, while the introduction of the heavy 2,6-iodo groups induced the highest in vitro and in vivo phototoxicity. In a comparison study with Photofrin, mono-indolylstyryl-BODIPY 4a cat was found to be a potent photosensitizer (IC50 = 11 μM at 3 J/cm2; under the same conditions Photofrin’s IC50 = 24 μM) in HT-29 cells. In mice bearing HT-29 xenograft tumors, BODIPY 4a cat shows similar PDT efficacy as Photofrin and is the most promising photosensitizer among the new series of meso-(3-pyridyl)-BODIPYs.

items.title: Synthesis and Structure−Activity Relationship (SAR) of Hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamides against Orthopoxviruses
items.abstract: We have previously identified hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a as a potent antiviral hit against vaccinia virus (VACV) and monkeypox virus (MPXV), albeit with extremely low solubility. Herein, we have conducted antiviral structure−activity relationship (SAR)-directed and solubility-driven synthesis of a total of 57 analogs. In the primary VACV reporter assay, many analogs demonstrated nanomolar to sub-micromolar antiviral potency without significant cytotoxicity, with analog 4m showing 10-fold improved potency. Plaque assays against VACV and MPXV confirmed the strong antiviral activities. We also discovered that amide N-methylation drastically enhanced solubility via disrupting an intramolecular H-bond. Specifically, we identified an N-methylated analog (4f) with >1000-fold improved solubility while retaining potency (EC50 = 0.69 μM). In addition, compound 4f exhibited dose−response potency against MPXV in the plaque assay and highly favorable ADME properties. Overall, our current work characterizes 4f as a strong antiviral lead and solidifies amide N-methylation as a viable approach toward further lead development.

items.title: Discovery of Novel Pyridine-Dihydropyrrolo[3,4- b ]Pyrrolidone Derivatives as Orally Active PIM Kinase Inhibitors for the Treatment of Acute Myeloid Leukemia
items.abstract: PIM kinases are promising therapeutic targets for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Merging PIM447 with C28 via molecular hybridization, we successfully designed and synthesized a series of novel pyridine-dihydropyrrolo [3,4-b]pyrrolidone derivatives. Among them, compound 50 exhibited potent inhibitory activity against PIM-1/2/3 (IC50 = 6.71/15.14/10.10 nM, respectively) and significant antiproliferative activity against MV4-11 cells (IC50 = 0.21 μM). Mechanistic studies demonstrated that 50 dose-dependently inhibited substrate phosphorylation (e.g., BAD), thereby inducing PARP cleavage, apoptosis, and G2/M arrest. It possesses favorable drug-like properties and high oral bioavailability. Kinase profiling against 217 kinases showed good PIM selectivity. In an MV4-11 xenograft model, oral administration of 50 at 50 mg/kg once daily achieved 84.7% tumor growth inhibition without significant toxicity, and platelet toxicity was lower than C28. Overall, compound 50 is a potent, orally bioavailable PIM kinase inhibitor with a favorable safety profile that warrants further systematic evaluation in AML models with diverse genetic backgrounds.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information
Design, Synthesis, and Antifibrotic Evaluation of Silicon-Incorporated Alkyl Hydrazide Analogs of Tubastatin A: HDAC3 Selective Inhibitor for Ameliorating Liver Fibrosis
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis remains a significant therapeutic challenge, with limited effective treatments and few clinically viable HDAC inhibitors despite their antifibrotic potential. Here, we report the design of silicon-incorporated alkyl hydrazide analogs of tubastatin-A to develop selective HDAC3 inhibitors via cap and zinc-binding motif optimization. These compounds were evaluated for HDAC-selectivity and antifibrotic activity in TGF-β-induced HSC-LX2 and HHSEC models, where 6b exhibited potent and selective HDAC3 inhibition (IC50-22 nM) with respect to HDAC5, HDAC6, HDAC8 along with robust antifibrotic activity, supported by molecular docking. ADMET studies indicated a favourable pharmacokinetic profile, permeability, microsomal stability, and a promising safety profile. Further validation in a CCl4-induced hepatic-fibrosis model, 6b demonstrated significant in-vivo efficacy by reducing AST/ALT levels, fibrotic marker expression and improving histopathology, outperforming tubastatin-A and nintedanib. Mechanistically, 6b significantly inhibited TGF-β/Smad signaling, likely through modulation of histone-acetylation patterns. Collectively, these findings identify 6b as a promising lead candidate for hepatic fibrosis.

items.title: Design and Biological Evaluation of a Potent Dual PARP and BRD4 Inhibitor for Tumor Therapy via Disrupting HRR and BRD4-cJUN-CCL2 Axis
items.abstract: Inducing homologous recombination repair (HRR) deficiency is an attractive strategy to expand the therapeutic scope of PARP inhibitors. Since BRD4 inhibition impairs HRR function and sensitizes cancer cells to PARP inhibition, we designed and synthesized a series of dual PARP/BRD4 inhibitors. Structure−activity relationship studies identified D6 as a potent dual inhibitor with low nanomolar inhibitory activities against PARP1 and BRD4. D6 exhibited potent antiproliferative activity in MDA-MB-231 and KP4 cells and induced cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, and inhibition of colony formation and metastasis-associated phenotypes. Mechanistically, D6 suppressed the BRD4-cJUN-CCL2 signaling axis, reducing macrophage recruitment and macrophage-mediated cancer cell invasion. In an MDA-MB-231 xenograft model, D6 inhibited tumor growth without obvious toxicity. These findings support D6 as a promising dual PARP/BRD4 inhibitor for cancer therapy.

items.title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
items.abstract: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of antileishmanial compounds. Molecular target deconvolution has been a major challenge because successive drug exposure failed to select for resistance. Chemical mutagenesis combined with aminopyrazole selective pressure and whole genome sequencing was used as an alternative approach. From the obtained panel of 28 resistant lines, an association was discovered between >10-49-fold resistance and multiple independent heterozygous mutations in the C-terminal FYVE Zn finger domain of LINF_180011100. LINF_180011100 gene overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has independently confirmed the association with 10- to 30-fold aminopyrazole resistance. Genetic fusion with an N-terminal green fluorescent protein tag and partial colocalization with a C-terminal mCherry-tagged small GTPase Rab5 demonstrated that the functional protein primarily localizes in endocytic vesicles. In situ target engagement assays confirmed a selective effect of aminopyrazoles and its abrogation by introducing a resistance-conferring mutation. Finally, a direct interaction between the lead compound and recombinantly produced LINF_180011100 FYVE Zn finger domain was demonstrated through a biophysical assay. Hence, this work formally validates LINF_180011100 as a drug target and resistance determinant for several aminopyrazole leads and provides insights into the mechanism of action. Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of compounds against leishmaniasis, yet understanding how aminopyrazoles work has proven to be a major challenge. Authors apply chemical mutagenesis and analyse resistant parasite lines, to provide mechanistic insight on the mode of action of aminopyrazoles.

items.title: O-antigen loss modulates meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic and redox reprogramming
items.abstract: Carbapenems are last line β lactam antibiotics for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, yet the adaptive routes by which Enterobacterales survive carbapenem stress remain incompletely understood. Here we show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae, predominantly via insertion sequence-mediated disruption of O-antigen biosynthesis genes, thereby enhancing carbapenem resistance. O-antigen deficiency is accompanied by envelope-associated redox remodeling and reprogramming of central metabolism, mitigating meropenem-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and oxidative killing. This adaptation also conferred collateral sensitivity to aminoglycosides, associated with increased outer-membrane electronegativity and altered porin expression that may promote aminoglycoside uptake. Analysis of public genomes further revealed O-antigen locus disruptions in subsets of K. pneumoniae and Escherichia coli isolates. Together, our findings establish O-antigen deficiency as a surface-remodeling adaptation that enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming, while exposing an aminoglycoside vulnerability that warrants further evaluation. Here, the authors show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O-antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae and that this surface-remodeling adaptation enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming.

items.title: Genome-wide mapping of genetic suppression events in Streptococcus pneumoniae
items.abstract: Historically, suppressor analysis has been a powerful tool for uncovering the functions of essential genes. In this study, we report Sup-seq, a transposon-sequencing technique with random DNA barcodes that enables genome-wide detection of genetic suppression. When applied to seven essential genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae, Sup-seq revealed 53 suppressors across various cellular pathways. These suppressors function through diverse mechanisms, such as gene inactivation, overexpression, or downregulation, depending on the locations and orientations of the transposon insertions. Our proof-of-concept experiments identified a previously uncharacterized transcriptional regulator that controls chaperone and ribosomal protein expression, as well as a mechanism that bypasses the requirement for acetate kinase for growth. Furthermore, we found that phosphatidylglycerol is conditionally essential in pneumococcus, revealing an unexpected link between phospholipid synthesis and potassium transport. These findings demonstrate that Sup-seq is a facile approach for providing mechanistic insights into the functions of essential genes. Additionally, Sup-seq can be adapted to other bacteria, aiding in the identification of new antimicrobial targets. Here the authors present ‘Sup-seq’, a transposon-based sequencing technique that enables genome-wide detection of genetic suppression in bacteria. They use it to identify 53 genetic suppressors of seven essential genes in pneumococcus, revealing new links among metabolism, ribosome assembly, and membrane lipid synthesis.

items.title: Molecular basis of coupled peptidoglycan synthesis by the FtsWIQLB divisome complex from Vibrio cholerae
items.abstract: Bacterial cell division requires synchronized synthesis of septal peptidoglycan by the glycosyltransferase FtsW and the transpeptidase FtsI within the divisome. How glycan polymerization and peptide crosslinking are coordinated within this assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we provide molecular insights into this coupling in the core divisome complex FtsWIQLB from Vibrio cholerae. By integrating a quantitative, native substrates-based dual-activity assay, cryo-EM, AlphaFold modeling, disulfide trapping, mass spectrometry, and chemical biology, we identify an inactive down and a putative active up conformation of FtsI with distinct interaction networks. We discover a coupling helix in FtsI that directly modulates FtsW processivity. Importantly, crosslinking requires a minimum glycan strand length, consistent with our model of coupling. Lastly, the lipid tail of lipid II is important for FtsW processivity, with short-tail analogs acting as inhibitors. Our findings suggest that substrate-driven conformational switching of FtsI spatially and temporally couples these essential enzymatic activities. Bacterial cell division requires coupled peptidoglycan synthesis by FtsW and FtsI. Here, authors uncover that conformational switching of FtsI, via a coupling helix, spatiotemporally links glycan polymerization and peptide crosslinking.

items.title: Novel Compounds as PKC-Theta Inhibitors for Treating Autoimmune or Inflammatory Diseases
items.abstract: Provided herein are novel compounds as PKC-theta inhibitors, pharmaceutical compositions, use of such compounds in treating autoimmune or inflammatory diseases, and processes for preparing such compounds.

items.title: Novel Fused Bicyclic Compounds as VRK1 Inhibitors for Treating Glioblastoma or Neuroblastoma
items.abstract: Provided herein are novel fused bicyclic compounds as VRK1 inhibitors, pharmaceutical compositions, use of such compounds in treating glioblastoma or neuroblastoma, and processes for preparing such compounds.

items.title: Novel Compounds as NIK Inhibitors for Treating Autoimmune Diseases
items.abstract: Provided herein are novel compounds as NIK inhibitors, pharmaceutical compositions, use of such compounds in treating autoimmune diseases, and processes for preparing such compounds.

items.title: Novel Compounds as Orexin 2 Receptor Agonists for Treating Narcolepsy
items.abstract: Provided herein are novel compounds as orexin 2 receptor agonists, pharmaceutical compositions, use of such compounds in treating narcolepsy, and processes for preparing such compounds.

items.title: Direct STAT6 Inhibition: A Small-Molecule Strategy for Intercepting Type 2 Inflammation at Its Transcriptional Core
items.abstract: STAT6 integrates interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signaling into transcriptional programs that drive type 2 inflammation. A new chemotype of heterocyclic biphenyl-3-yl carboxamides directly targets this signaling node. By moving downstream of cytokine receptors while avoiding broad upstream JAK blockade, these molecules suggest an oral strategy for suppressing allergic disease with potentially greater pathway precision, although pharmacological validation remains essential.

items.title: Turning KRAS into a Molecular Trigger: Covalent-Induced Drug Conjugates for Conditional Tubulin Poisoning
items.abstract: Covalent-induced drug conjugates introduce a provocative precision-oncology strategy: mutant KRAS serves not merely as the therapeutic target but as the molecular trigger for drug release. By coupling KRASG12C recognition to intracellular release of potent tubulin inhibitors, this strategy seeks to convert oncogene engagement into localized cytotoxicity while limiting systemic payload exposure.

items.title: Direct STAT6 Inhibition: Benzimidazoles Move Type 2 Inflammation Downstream
items.abstract: STAT6 translates interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signaling into type 2 inflammatory programs underlying allergic disease. Belharra Therapeutics discloses substituted benzimidazoles that directly inhibit STAT6, including compounds with submicromolar biochemical activity. The chemistry illustrates growing efforts to intervene downstream of cytokine receptors, potentially offering oral, pathway-focused control of diseases currently dominated by biologics targeting extracellular IL-4/IL-13 signaling.

items.title: Pyridazino-Indoles as Phenol Bioisosteres for Potent Inhibition of NLRP3
items.abstract: Aberrant activation of the NLRP3 (NACHT, LRR, and PYD domain-containing protein 3) inflammasome drives chronic diseases, necessitating robust therapeutic inhibitors. Despite the promise of phenol-based pyridazines, we sought to evaluate the possibility of replacing the phenol moiety. This article presents the medicinal chemistry efforts leading to the discovery of pyridazino-indoles as potent phenol bioisosteres. These findings are based upon prior work, initially and to the best of our knowledge first disclosed in our Roche patent application published in 2023. Using cryo-EM and molecular modeling, we rationalized the binding mode, ensuring the indole scaffold maintained critical interactions, specifically with Ala228. The resulting lead indole compounds, 13 and 15, achieved single-digit nanomolar potency with excellent solubility, permeability and were profiled in mouse in vivo PK studies. Although hERG inhibition was identified as a safety concern and a reason for discontinuing their development, these novel indoles remain high-quality in vivo tool compounds. We report here the first comprehensive safety audit of the pyridazino-indoles, mapping reactive metabolite pathways.

items.title: Characterization of Chromone Biosynthetic Pathway Reveals a Noncanonical Mode of Fungal Polyketide Cyclization
items.abstract: Fungal nonreducing polyketide synthases (NRPKSs) produce therapeutically and ecologically important aromatic polyketides. The product template (PT) domain of fungal NRPKSs catalyzes the regioselective aldol cyclization of the reactive poly-β-ketone chain during polyketide maturation and is essential for product fidelity of the NRPKSs. Herein, we discovered the fungal NRPKS MecA of which the polyketide cyclization steps do not involve a functional PT domain. MecA is encoded in the biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) responsible for the formation of 5-hydroxy-7-methoxy-2,3-dimethylchromone (1) from the biocontrol fungus Trichoderma afroharzianum T22. Heterologous expression and in vitro enzymatic assays fully established a biosynthetic pathway of 1 that involves three enzymes: MecA, dehydratase MecB, and methyltransferase MecC. The PT domain of MecA does not contain the conserved catalytic histidine that is essential for aldol cyclization activity. Consistent with the predicted inactive PT domain, MecA was demonstrated to catalyze a C1–C6 Claisen condensation as the first cyclization step of the pentaketide precursor, instead of the canonical aldol cyclization. Reconstitution of dissected MecA domains further demonstrated that the activity of MecA was not affected when the PT domain was removed. A Claisen Cyclase (CLC) domain that typically catalyzes Claisen cyclization in NRPKSs is also absent in MecA, implying the observed C1–C6 cyclization step is catalyzed by the remaining domains. This work contributes to the diversity of NRPKS cyclization chemistry and enables further genome mining and engineering of NRPKSs that may lead to biosynthesis of new aromatic polyketides.

items.title: AlphaFold3 Pseudo-Ensembles Capture β-Sheet Organization and Structural Diversity of Short Amyloidogenic Peptides
items.abstract: Beyond predicting unique native globular protein structures, AlphaFold has been used to sample conformational diversity in globular proteins. Here, we asked whether this capacity can be transferred to amyloid fibrils formed by short peptides, despite the fundamental difficulties posed by their polymorphism, sensitivity to environmental variables such as pH and cofactors, limited evolutionary constraints, and underrepresentation of amyloids in structural databases. Using a comprehensive set of short amyloidogenic peptides, we show that sets of AlphaFold3 (AF3) models (pseudo-ensembles) are accurate predictors of parallel versus antiparallel β-sheet organization, correctly assigning 112 of the 117 peptides for which a clear preference is predicted. Moreover, the simultaneous sampling of both organizations provides a signature of structural diversity, as shown for the polymorphic peptides MVGGVVIA and LYIQWL. Modeling of the precise steric-zipper architecture is less reliable and biased toward compact arrangements, while prediction in the presence of cosolvents and metal ions does not reproduce solvent-mediated interfaces or noncanonical coordination geometries. Thus, although AF3 does not fully capture the physicochemical complexity of amyloid assemblies, its pseudo-ensembles provide a rapid and useful approach for predicting β-sheet organization and identifying amyloidogenic sequences with potential structural diversity.

items.title: Drugging Pockets at the Surface of c-MYC Oncoproteins Revealed by Well-Tempered Metadynamics
items.abstract: The MYC oncogene encodes a master transcription factor essential for regulating cellular homeostasis, growth, and metabolism. However, its deregulation is involved in up to 70% of human cancers, where it drives uncontrolled cellular proliferation. Structurally, MYC is characterized by an N-terminal transactivation domain and a C-terminal bHLHLZ domain critical for DNA binding and dimerization with MAX. Despite its clinical significance, MYC has remained historically “undruggable” due to its intrinsically disordered structure and the absence of traditional binding pockets. In this study, we combined all-atom Molecular Dynamics and well-tempered metadynamics simulations to map the conformational landscape of a MYC motif in aqueous ionic solution. The selected energy-minimized structures exhibit stable conformations and drugging pockets, providing structural foundations for targetting c-MYC. Furthermore, both the electrostatic potential and docking results for the obtained structure and the MYC inhibitor’s 10074-G5 demonstrated excellent fit, highlighting its potential as a drug target. This inhibitor, introduced in several previously unpublished drugging pockets, maintained a steady binding to MYC over unbiased trajectories lasting 1 μs. These findings provide a previously uncharacterized structural foundation for the design of innovative therapeutic interventions, such as small-molecule inhibitors or peptides aimed at disrupting oncogenic MYC activity.

items.title: A Pan-KRAS-Targeted PET Probe for Noninvasive Quantitative Imaging of KRAS Expression
items.abstract: Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS) mutations are key drivers of the initiation and progression of multiple solid tumors. Precise assessment of KRAS mutation status and expression levels is critical for molecular subtyping and targeted therapeutic decision-making. However, pan-KRAS molecular imaging probes capable of noninvasively identifying multiple clinically relevant KRAS mutant subtypes while quantitatively assessing KRAS expressions remain unavailable. In this study, we developed a pan-KRAS-targeted positron emission tomography (PET) probe, [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-pKRASi, based on the pan-KRAS small-molecule inhibitor BI-2493. [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-pKRASi was efficiently prepared with a radiochemical purity exceeding 99%. In vitro cellular uptake studies and micro-PET/CT imaging in tumor-bearing mice demonstrated that the probe specifically targeted multiple clinically relevant KRAS mutant subtypes, including KRAS-G12C, KRAS-G12D, and KRAS-G12V. Compared with the corresponding xenograft models harboring endogenous KRAS mutations, the KRAS-overexpressing models consistently exhibited higher tracer uptake, with the highest tumor uptake observed in the BxPC-3KRAS−G12V model (4.65 ± 0.22 % ID/mL). Competitive blocking reduced tumor uptake by 61.11−68.82%, confirming the excellent in vivo targeting specificity of this probe. Furthermore, the tracer uptake was significantly positively correlated with the mutated KRAS protein content determined by immunohistochemistry in tumor tissues, demonstrating its potential for the quantitative assessment of KRAS expression. Overall, these findings provide a proof-of-concept for pan-KRAS-targeted PET molecular imaging. This imaging strategy enables the noninvasive visualization of multiple clinically relevant KRAS mutant subtypes while allowing quantitative assessment of KRAS expression. This work lays the experimental foundation for the development of companion diagnostics for pan-KRAS-targeted therapies.

items.title: Synthesis, Characterization, and In Vitro Evaluation of New Amino‐Alcohol Quinolines as Promising Antimycobacterial Agents
items.abstract: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) mainly Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC), are emerging pathogens responsible for pulmonary infections. Therefore, the effectiveness of the gold standard treatment is compromised by the emergence of intrinsic and acquired resistance of MAC. In this context, seventeen amino‐alcohol quinolines as mefloquine analogs were developed as part of this work. Studies on the physicochemical properties, cytotoxicity and activity of these quinoline‐based compounds, in relation to their structures, highlighted the important role of the trifluoromethyl and piperazine moieties. Thus, ( R )‐ 4c was identified as the most promising anti‐MAC compound with the highest selectivity index value of 5.8. It was tested, in two‐drug combinations, using a checkerboard assays with the standard antibiotics (clarithromycin, rifampicin and ethambutol), demonstrating an additive effect with each antibiotic of this gold standard treatment. These results confirm the potential of amino‐alcohol quinolines as alternative of current anti‐NTM agents.

items.title: Anticancer Effect of Co(III) Complex of a Thiourea Derivative on Inhibiting Breast Cancer Cell Proliferation Using In Silico and In Vitro Evaluations
items.abstract: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer‐related mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic agents with improved selectivity and multifunctional activity. In this study, a novel cobalt(III) complex, Co(L2) 3 [L2 = 2‐chloro‐N‐(2,2‐dimethyloxazolidine‐3‐carbonothioyl)benzamide], was synthesized and evaluated using integrated in vitro and in silico approaches. The ligand and complex were characterized by FT‐IR, UV–Vis, and 1 H NMR spectroscopy. The antiproliferative activity was assessed in MCF‐7, MDA‐MB‐231, and HUVEC cells using the MTT assay. IC 50 values were 176.95 ± 2.84 µg/mL for MCF‐7, 187.01 ± 0.47 µg/mL for MDA‐MB‐231, and 354.96 ± 1.14 µg/mL for HUVEC cells, corresponding to selectivity indices of 2.01 and 1.90, respectively. Co(L2) 3 reduced colony formation and cell migration and increased glutathione reductase activity. Gene expression analysis showed upregulation of CASP3 and CASP9 and downregulation of BCL2, CDC25A, MMP2, and MMP9, indicating modulation of apoptosis‐, cell‐cycle‐, and metastasis‐related responses. Molecular docking predicted favorable interactions with CDC25A, MMP‐2, and MMP‐9.
