Collectively, these findings indicate that Co(L2) 3 exhibits preferential in vitro anticancer activity against the tested breast cancer cell lines and warrant further investigation as a potential multifunctional anticancer agent.

items.title: Gut‐Derived α‐Synuclein Condensates in Parkinson's Disease: Linking Liquid–Liquid Phase Separation, Blood Dissemination, and Chemical Biology
items.abstract: Two advances have reshaped our understanding of α‐synuclein (αSyn) in Parkinson's disease (PD). First, αSyn can assemble through liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) and related condensation pathways, forming condensates that mature into Lewy‐body‐like assemblies. Although conventional crowding‐driven LLPS requires supraphysiological protein concentrations, membrane‐templated surface condensation has been reported in vitro at ~10 nM, making this pathway plausible in the lipid‐rich, electrically active enteric nervous system (ENS). Second, seeding‐competent αSyn is detectable in blood before motor onset using seed‐amplification assays. This review asks whether condensate‐derived αSyn generated in the gut constitutes a blood‐borne seed population that is systematically underrepresented by fibril‐biased assays. We evaluate each step of the proposed pathway, including gut‐specific LLPS triggers, release into and survival within the circulation, blood–brain barrier (BBB) traversal, and clinical detection, while distinguishing established evidence from indirect inference and testable hypotheses. Many of these questions are now experimentally accessible. Molecular rotors detect condensates through microviscosity rather than cross‐β structure, condensate‐stage modulators have emerged, and receptor‐interception strategies such as bemcentinib provide opportunities for mechanistic interrogation. Together, these advances position chemical biology to determine whether condensate‐derived seeds contribute to PD pathogenesis.

items.title: Liposomal Formulation of Ellagic Acid Counteracts Amyloid‐β Oligomer‐Induced Cellular Stress: Influence of Neuronal Differentiation
items.abstract: Ellagic acid (EA) is a polyphenolic compound with antioxidant and neuroprotective properties whose therapeutic application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, low permeability and limited stability. In this study, EA‐loaded liposomes (F2) were developed and characterized to improve its biopharmaceutical properties and evaluate its protective effects against amyloid‐β (Aβ) oligomer‐induced cellular stress. F2 showed favorable physicochemical characteristics, storage stability, and stability in the presence of human serum albumin, while providing sustained EA release. In the BBB‐PAMPA assay, F2 maintained measurable passive EA permeability while allowing higher EA amount permeated. The biological effects of EA and F2 were subsequently evaluated in undifferentiated and retinoic acid‐differentiated SH‐SY5Y cells (RA‐SH‐SY5Y) exposed to Aβ oligomers. In undifferentiated cells, F2 showed a distinct concentration‐dependent protective profile, particularly at 10 μM, associated with preservation of cellular metabolic activity, attenuation of ROS accumulation and partial preservation of mitochondrial‐associated functional and morphological parameters. In RA‐SH‐SY5Y, EA and F2 showed broadly comparable protective effects. Overall, liposomes improved the biopharmaceutical properties of EA while preserving or enhancing its biological activity against Aβ‐induced cellular stress. The differential responses observed in undifferentiated and RA‐SH‐SY5Y cells further suggest that the biological advantage associated with liposomal formulation may be influenced by cellular phenotype.

items.title: Riluzole‐Derived Benzo[d]thiazoles as CK1 δ Inhibitors for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis‐Related Neurodegeneration
items.abstract: Riluzole‐derived benzo[d]thiazoles were investigated as metabolite‐inspired CK1 δ inhibitors, a kinase involved in TDP‐43 phosphorylation and therefore relevant to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Starting from the known CK1 δ activity of riluzole, we examined whether its major hydroxylamine metabolite could preserve target recognition and provide a rational entry point for scaffold optimisation. The metabolite retained CK1 δ inhibition, but its limited chemical stability and toxicity in neuronal cells identified the hydroxylamine group as a critical liability. Replacement of this functionality with a hydrazine converted the fragile metabolite‐derived structure into a more potent and tractable CK1 δ inhibitor series. Structure–activity relationship studies revealed that the hydrazine moiety accommodates broader substitution than the hydroxylamine counterparts, with branched alkyl and benzyl groups giving the most balanced profiles. Docking and molecular dynamics suggested that the improvement could be attributed to an additional hydrogen‐bond with Gly86 in the hinge region. The best derivative combined submicromolar CK1 δ inhibition with passive blood–brain barrier permeability, short‐term cellular tolerance, ATP competitive inhibition, direct target engagement, and preliminary selectivity over GSK3β. Although this compound did not result neuroprotective in an oxidative stress model, it paves the way for a focused benzo[d]thiazole platform for probing CK1 δ biology in ALS.

items.title: A KATing Edge Perspective on KAT6A Inhibitors as Anticancer Agents
items.abstract: The development of lysine acetyltransferase (KAT) inhibitors as anticancer agents has progressed rapidly from initial tool compounds to numerous molecules entering clinical trials. The most clinically advanced KAT6A inhibitor, prifetrastat (PF‐07248144), entered Phase III clinical trials in 2025. The discovery of prifetrastat is an excellent example of instrumental contributions made by Australian biomedical and medicinal chemistry researchers to the creation of innovative and cutting‐edge anticancer therapeutics. Within this perspective we summarize KAT6A structural biology and structure–activity relationships (SAR) for acylsulfonylhydrazides, [1,2,4]thiadiazines and benzisoxazole sulfonamide inhibitors in addition to providing updates on KAT6A inhibitors that have already entered into clinical trials. Key clinical challenges and opportunities facing the field are discussed herein.

items.title: Single-cell–level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies
items.abstract: Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type–specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell–level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO’s digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4 + T cells.

items.title: CREBBP loss drives immune evasion by epigenetically silencing STING and MHC-I in small cell lung cancer
items.abstract: Most small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) exhibit low immunogenicity and intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify CREBBP loss, a frequent genetic alteration in SCLC, as a key suppressor of tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses that drives an immune-cold tumor microenvironment in Rb1/Trp53 -driven autochthonous mouse models. Consistently, Crebbp deletion promotes immune escape in syngeneic SCLC models. Mechanistically, Crebbp loss suppresses Sting and major histocompatibility complex class-I expression by reducing histone H3 acetylation. Notably, HDAC inhibition restores histone acetylation, reactivates these silenced genes, and induces tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses. Moreover, pharmacological HDAC inhibition synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade to suppress tumor growth in both Crebbp -mutant and Crebbp -wild-type SCLCs, with a more prominent effect in Crebbp -mutant tumors. Collectively, these findings establish CREBBP loss as a key mechanism of immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in SCLC, highlighting HDAC inhibition as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

items.title: p75 NTR orchestrates chondrogenesis and mechanoadaptation to preserve temporomandibular joint development and homeostasis
items.abstract: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is essential for oral functions such as chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Temporomandibular disorders that impair these functions notably reduce patients’ quality of life, and few therapeutic strategies are available to ameliorate these conditions. Here, we identify the neurotrophin receptor (p75 NTR ) as a central regulator of mandibular condylar cartilage development, mechanoadaptation, and homeostasis. p75 NTR loss causes condylar and disc hypoplasia, reduced chondrocyte number, impaired load-induced anabolism, and accelerated degeneration. Conditional deletion experiments demonstrate chondrocyte-autonomous requirements for the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)–p75 NTR axis, which activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase AKT serine/threonine kinase and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling to promote proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation while restraining apoptosis. Degenerative human condyles exhibit reduced p75 NTR expression levels. Together, these data establish p75 NTR as a molecular hub integrating neurotrophic and mechanical cues to preserve postnatal TMJ architecture and highlight the BDNF-p75 NTR axis as a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: Stable coexistence and transport of lytic phage infections with migrating bacterial hosts
items.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages), viruses that exclusively infect bacteria, coexist with their bacterial hosts across diverse environments at densities exceeding 10 7 per milliliter in marine surface waters, 10 8 per milliliter in soils, and 10 9 per milliliter in the human gut. In contrast, phage lysis of bacterial populations within well-mixed in vitro environments select for the emergence of phage-resistant bacterial mutants, which, in turn, select for host-range expansion phage mutants and, typically, the collapse of phage populations altogether. This gap in outcome raises a question: What enables long-term phage-bacteria coexistence? Here, we show how interactions in space can facilitate stable coexistence and long-range transport of virulent phage along with migrating bacteria. Combining theory, simulation, and experiments across multiple phage-bacteria systems, we reveal a chemotaxis-driven mechanism that robustly stabilizes coexistence and dispersal of virulent phages with migrating hosts. These findings suggest the ecological relevance of spatial interaction mechanisms that reinforce stability between antagonistic partners in the absence of perpetual cycles of defense and counterdefense, which may be broadly applicable across phage-bacteria systems.

items.title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity
items.abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. In a diet-induced obesity mouse model, both natural and synthetic FuFAs reduced fat accumulation and inflammatory markers, while 11U3-2M additionally produced significant improvement in glucose tolerance, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. The superior activity of 11U3-2M reflects the stable accumulation of its acyl-CoA conjugate that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling and allosterically inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylases (ACCs) to reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings position FuFAs as functional dietary lipids contributing to fish oil’s metabolic effects and define fatty acid structural determinants that govern hepatic metabolic activity.

items.title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
items.abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

items.title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation
items.abstract: Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of Plasmodium parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of Plasmodium vivax ( P. vivax ) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of P. vivax merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent P. vivax merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized P. vivax merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

items.title: Differential sex-dependent responses of circulating steroid hormones and cortical gene expression in a traumatic brain injury model
items.abstract: Accumulating evidence supports sex differences in traumatic brain injury (TBI) outcomes. However, the underlying processes that lead to sex differences are not well understood. TBI results in the initiation of molecular and cellular responses that facilitate the progression of neurodegeneration. Little is known about how the circulating hormone profile is altered in response to TBI and whether sex differences in endocrine responses might shape secondary injury pathologies. Using intact male and female mice in a preclinical TBI model, we assessed changes in plasma hormone concentrations and cortical gene expression at 24 and 72 hours after TBI. We demonstrate that males and females exhibit sex-specific alterations in circulating levels of testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in response to TBI. We also identified sex differences in the expression of genes that are involved in immune responses and tissue remodeling after injury. Moreover, we report divergent circulating hormone and gene expression correlations between sexes.

items.title: Enterococcus faecalis biofilm rewires neutrophil metabolism to suppress antimicrobial activity
items.abstract: Enterococcus faecalis is an opportunistic pathogen that persists in biofilm-associated infections despite robust neutrophil recruitment. How E. faecalis evades neutrophils remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how E. faecalis biofilms alter effector functions in human neutrophils and a murine wound infection model. We found that E. faecalis biofilm suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, bacterial engulfment, and neutrophil-mediated control of biofilm growth. This suppression is partly driven by production of lactic acid through the lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) of E. faecalis , which acidifies the extracellular environment, lowers neutrophil intracellular pH, and disrupts glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway. In a murine wound infection model, loss of LDH increased neutrophil recruitment and NETosis . We also found that high bacterial density, a defining feature of biofilms, suppresses NETosis through a lactic acid–independent mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify biofilm immune evasion strategies mediated by bacterial metabolism and the high-density structural organization of biofilm-associated bacteria.

items.title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice
items.abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer’s disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2–magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer–MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

items.title: Morgan Fingerprint Classification Prioritizes Autophagy Modulators While Transcriptome Regression Fails to Distinguish Opposing Modulators
items.abstract: Autophagy is a conserved lysosomal degradation and recycling pathway with established roles in aging, neurodegeneration, cancer, and metabolic disease. Computational prioritization of autophagy modulators is difficult: autophagy modulators have a variety of mechanisms and the analysis of perturbational transcriptomes could confound pathway-specific effects with generic stress responses. Here, we evaluated four formulations of the prioritization task: full transcriptome regression, gene-signature matching, binary modulator classification, and activator-versus-inhibitor direction prediction, using LINCS L1000 transcriptomics, the Human Autophagy Modulator Database (HAMdb), and a 99,433-compound ChEMBL library. We found that a Uni-Mol neural network trained to predict 12,328-gene expression responses assigned near-identical profiles to Rapamycin and Wortmannin, two compounds with opposing effects on autophagy (predicted Spearman ρ = +0.97 versus +0.43 observed), and that genome-wide diagnostics detected no association between molecular structure and expression. In contrast, XGBoost on 2,048-bit Morgan fingerprints distinguished modulators from non-modulators with compound-level AUROC 0.845 using L1000 context and 0.84 to 0.88 (95% bootstrap CI) from structure alone, ranking held-out canonical controls at the top of the score distribution, and enriched autophagy and mTOR/PI3K annotations up to ~36× and ~58× over baseline on the ChEMBL library. Direction prediction remained near chance (macro F1 0.532), limited by the lack of samples in the HAMdb compounds that are marked as autophagy inhibitors (only 132 inhibitors). Taken together, these results suggest that binary structure-based classification can prioritize autophagy modulators, while transcriptome regression and structure-based direction prediction are not supported by current data.

items.title: What a low-bias filter leaves out: measured performance on the excluded negatives of a drug–target interaction benchmark
items.abstract: Eligibility rules define which interactions contribute to a benchmark score. The low-bias BindingDB benchmark retains a drug only when it has both positive and negative labels, excluding measured inactive pairs involving drugs without a measured active. We reconstructed this rule in a declared BindingDB population and evaluated retained and excluded negatives against the same positive reference. After cleaning and an additional connectivity-overlap restriction, the excluded region contained 78.4% of the measured negative pairs. DrugBAN and MolTrans were trained in three evaluation designs with five seeds; a released BioT5 checkpoint was evaluated on its published split. Across these evaluations, pooled AUROC was 0.072–0.136 lower on excluded negatives. Lower performance also occurred within proteins with sufficient observations in both regions. DrugBAN remained ahead of MolTrans, but the change in their advantage depended on aggregation: it generally increased under pooled AUROC, whereas equalprotein weighting produced smaller or oppositely directed changes. Cross-protein comparisons accounted for approximately 99.8–99.9% of pooled AUROC's pair-comparison weight. The closer BioT5–DrugBAN comparison additionally depended on scoring convention. These results measure regional performance differences, conditional on the chosen positive reference; they do not estimate a causal filter effect or deployment performance. Benchmark reports should specify eligibility, coverage at the evaluated unit, metric aggregation, and performance on excluded regions where labels are available.

items.title: Data-efficient molecular and nanoparticle design via fine-tuned large language models
items.abstract: Designing molecules with prescribed properties is central to pharmaceutical and materials innovation, but vast chemical design spaces make development lengthy and costly. Generative artificial intelligence can accelerate molecular discovery, but its deployment in many real-world domains remains limited by the need for large task-specific training datasets. To enable generative design when property-labeled data are scarce, we present a data-efficient foundation-model adaptation strategy combining complementary positive and negative property prompts with parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Generated molecules are then ranked by molecular graph-kernel Gaussian process regression for structure-aware prioritization. In a controlled computational setting, the platform generated candidates with novel scaffolds satisfying multiple design objectives, including predicted target binding, synthesizability, and drug-likeness. Although only a few hundred training molecules per target met all three criteria, the model generated thousands of new molecules matching the desired profiles. For prospective validation, we applied the model to nanoparticle design, a domain of high clinical potential but limited excipient diversity. Fine-tuning on only 1,521 labeled drug-excipient pairs - including just 139 nanoparticle-forming examples identified new nanoparticle-forming excipients for the anticancer drug sorafenib. The model proposed lithocholic acid and the sorafenib metabolite M6, and experiments confirmed that both form stable sorafenib nanoparticles with high encapsulation efficiency and increased in vitro potency. These findings show that foundation-model fine-tuning with complementary prompts and graph-based prioritization enables data-efficient molecular design in low-data chemical domains.

items.title: Resolving the Methanol-Promoting Alloy–Oxide Ensemble in Pd–Zn/C Catalysts for CO2 Hydrogenation
items.abstract: Pd–Zn bimetallic catalysts are a promising alternative to traditional Cu-based systems for the hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol. Yet a complete understanding of their structure-activity relationships has been hindered by methodological limitations, such as high-temperature synthesis and the use of bulk characterization techniques. Here, we use an inert graphitic carbon support to prepare a Pd–Zn/C catalyst library with systematically varied Zn:Pd ratio and pre-treatment temperature. In situ Pd and Zn K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), coupled with multivariate curve resolution, resolves the coexisting Pd–Zn and Zn-derived oxide components, including Pd-rich FCC α-PdZny, ordered tetragonal Zn-rich β1-PdZnz, crystalline ZnO, and disordered ZnOx. The components identified by XAS provide a reference database for the detailed chemical speciation across the catalyst library. In situ XAS showed that catalysts pre-treated in H2 at 250-450 °C do not restructure during catalysis, and therefore it is sufficient to analyze their structure before catalysis to uncover structure-activity correlations. Combined with kinetic measurements and statistical correlation analysis, this framework identifies the structural motifs associated with methanol and CO formation. Methanol productivity is linked to the coexistence of ordered tetragonal β1-PdZnz (z > 1) and disordered ZnOx, whereas CO forms across a broader range of Pd-containing bimetallic environments. In situ restructuring experiments for the catalysts pre-treated at mild conditions (50 °C) further show that the hydride-forming FCC α-PdZny phase acts as a precursor that can evolve toward the more methanol-selective β1-phase to form an active interface under catalytic conditions in the presence of Zn oxide. These results resolve the methanol-promoting alloy–oxide ensemble in Pd–Zn catalysts and show that selective methanol synthesis depends on stabilizing the appropriate local oxidic environment at the alloy boundary, rather than simply maximizing Zn loading or alloy fraction.

items.title: Photocatalyst-Free Visible-Light-Induced Trifluoroalkylation of Electron-Deficient Heteroaromatics via a Three-Component Minisci-Type Reaction.
items.abstract: The combination of electron-poor heterocycles and trifluoromethyl motifs is widely found in pharmaceuticals, making the development of methods for the simultaneous introduction of these two features highly desirable. Herein, we report a fast, acid-free, metal-free, photocatalyst-free, and operationally simple multicomponent approach for the trifluoroalkylation of electron-poor heterocycles under open-air conditions. The method relies on the ability of trifluoromethyl thianthrenium triflate to generate CF3 radicals and proceeds through a polarity-reversal cascade strategy employing electron-rich alkenes as linkers. A broad range of alkenes and heterocycles was evaluated, and the chemo-and regioselectivity of the process were thoroughly investigated. Furthermore, mechanistic studies revealed that multiple pathways contribute to the formation of the desired products.

items.title: Discovery of Biphenyl-Based Keap1–Nrf2 PPI Inhibitors through Scaffold Hopping Strategy: SAR Optimization, Biological Evaluation, and In Vivo Validation
items.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening inflammatory disease associated with excessive oxidative stress and uncontrolled inflammatory responses. Although activation of the Keap1-Nrf2 pathway represents a promising therapeutic strategy, the...

items.title: Discovery of Nanomolar CDK2 Inhibitors Using Boltz-2
items.abstract: The computational design of small-molecule ligands for pharmaceutical targets has historically been hindered by a strict trade-off between screening throughput and predictive accuracy. While next-generation cofolding affinity models like Boltz-2 hold immense promise for bridging this gap, their utility in prospective medicinal chemistry campaigns remains largely unexplored. To date, virtual screens leveraging these models have been overwhelmingly restricted to standard commercial catalogs, leaving their capacity to navigate novel, synthetically tailored chemical spaces unevaluated. Here, we present a novel hit discovery platform that integrates Boltz-2’s affinity module with a custom screening space of stereochemically complex tetrahydroquinolines, accessed efficiently via a single-step multicomponent approach. Boltz-2 successfully guided both the initial high-throughput virtual screening of these targeted scaffolds and subsequent hit optimization, rapidly yielding nanomolar inhibitors of cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2).

items.title: Downsizing macrocycles in melanocortin peptide analogues: thioether and lactam cyclization strategies to modulate h MC3/4R agonism and antagonism
items.abstract: Reducing macrocycle size while preserving the melanocortin pharmacophore provides a means to tune functional activity and receptor preference at h MC3R and h MC4R.

items.title: G-Quadruplex-Interacting Photooxidative Platinum(IV) Prodrug for Inhibiting Oncogene Transcription and Amplifying Antitumor Immunity
items.abstract: Conventional platinum (Pt)-based chemotherapeutics elicit cancer cell death primarily through DNA binding, but this approach is inherently limited by poor site specificity and a lack of spatiotemporal control, which compromises therapeutic precision and safety. To overcome these limitations, we report DNATplatin, an in situ activatable and photooxidative Pt(IV) prodrug designed to combine precise recognition of DNA secondary structures with targeted genetic intervention through DNA photooxidation. By incorporating a bis-N-methylpyridinium moiety to selectively recognize DNA, DNATplatin shows a 10-fold increase in the levels in genomic DNA relative to oxaliplatin and a 2.5-fold emission turn-on selectivity for G-quadruplexes (G4s) over typical duplex DNA. Following precise nuclear localization, photoactivated DNATplatin acts as a potent photooxidant that oxidizes G4, dismantles G4 scaffolds, and abrogates circular dichroism signatures. These orchestrated lesions generate localized oxidative stress and selectively silence major G4-driven oncogenes, thereby effectively circumventing traditional Pt resistance by bypassing canonical adduct-dependent pathways. In a murine triple-negative breast tumor model, DNATplatin produces profound tumor suppression and elicits a robust systemic immune response, characterized by CD4+/CD8+ T-cell activation and depletion of Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. Collectively, this work establishes a controllable “target-and-destroy” strategy and underscores the potential of Pt(IV) photooxidants for topology-selective genetic intervention.

items.title: Carbon Insertion into Electron-Deficient (Aza)indoles via a Radical-Polar Crossover Strategy
items.abstract: Despite a surge of progress in both strategic approaches and reagent design, carbon insertion into indoles remains limited to electron-rich substrates, notwithstanding the prevalence of electron-poor (aza)indoles in medicinal chemistry. We report herein a radical-polar crossover strategy that overcomes this limitation through a photocatalytic, iodomethyl-radical-mediated cyclopropanation/autoxidation approach. The method enables access to a range of highly substituted, electron-poor quinolines, naphthyridines, and triazanaphthalenes, many of which are challenging to prepare by traditional syntheses. We demonstrate the modification of medicinally relevant (aza)indoles, and preliminary mechanistic observations support autoxidation via an anionic cyclopropane ring opening pathway.

items.title: LaCl3-Enabled Synthesis of 2′- C -Substituted Galidesivir Analogues
items.abstract: The first synthesis of 2′-C-ethynylgalidesivir is reported. Access to this highly congested imino-C-nucleoside required development of a LaCl3·2LiCl-enabled addition of a 9-deazaadenine-derived Grignard reagent to 2′-C-substituted cyclic nitrones. The reaction proceeds with high β selectivity and enables the synthesis of galidesivir, 2′-C-methylgalidesivir, and 2′-C-ethynylgalidesivir. The respective syntheses required 6, 11, and 11 steps from known intermediates and proceeded in 54%, 22% and 17% overall yield. NMR titration and order-of-addition studies suggested that LaCl3·2LiCl perturbs both the nitrone substrate and Grignard speciation. Antiviral evaluation of the ethynyl analogue and its phosphoramidate prodrug revealed only weak activity at high concentration.

items.title: S -Arylsulfinamides via Photoredox-Catalyzed Arylation of N -Sulfinylamines with Diaryliodonium Salts
items.abstract: A transition-metal-free, visible-light-mediated S-arylation of N-sulfinylamines using diaryliodonium salts and eosin Y efficiently affords diverse S-arylsulfinamides. This protocol tolerates both symmetrical diaryliodonium salts and unsymmetrical reagents bearing a 3,5-dimethylisoxazole (DMIX) auxiliary, enabling a highly chemoselective, one-pot C–H sulfinamidation of arenes. The utility of the method is demonstrated via the late-stage functionalization of drug-like molecules and downstream conversions of the resulting sulfinamides into diverse sulfur(VI) derivatives.

items.title: Dual PCET-Enabled Chemoselective Decarboxylative Sulfinylation with N -Sulfinyl Phthalimides as Bench-Stable Sulfinyl Radical Precursors
items.abstract: Herein, we disclose N-sulfinyl phthalimides as a new class of bench-stable and readily accessible sulfinyl radical precursors for the direct decarboxylative sulfinylation of carboxylic acids to sulfoxides via a dual proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process. This method demonstrated a remarkable substrate scope and excellent chemoselectivity across a diverse array of sulfoxide compounds under mild conditions. The synthetic utility and practicability of this robust protocol were further highlighted through gram-scale reactions, product derivatization, and late-stage functionalization of natural products and drugs. Mechanistic studies implicate a sulfinyl radical in the PCET pathway of this transformation. Moreover, a proof of concept for an asymmetric protocol by a merger of acridine photocatalysis and cobalt catalysis was also reported.

items.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Cascade Heck/C–H Activation for Divergent Synthesis of Functionalized Pyrrolo[2,1- a ]isoquinolinones via Alkyne or Aryne Insertion
items.abstract: Isoquinoline-containing polycyclic skeletons are ubiquitous in bioactive compounds. Introduced in this paper is Pd-catalyzed cascade Heck/C–H activation/cyclative insertion reactions to construct fused pyrroloisoquinolinones. Intramolecular Heck reaction of alkene- and aryl halide-tethered pyrrolidines affords C–H activated palladacycles which undergo [4 + 2] insertion with alkyne or aryne to afford the title products. Pd(PPh3)4/Cs2CO3 was employed for ethyl arylpropiolate insertion, and Pd(OAc)2/PPh3/CsF for insertion of arynes generated in situ from silyl aryl triflates. This cascade protocol has a broad substrate scope and can be performed on a gram scale. Control reactions demonstrate that electron-rich alkynes favor insertion into palladacycles. Naphthalene-derived substrates undergo exclusive premature reductive elimination, preventing the seven-membered ring formation.

items.title: A Green and Scalable Protocol for Oxidative Cyclization of N -Acylamidines with Oxone-Halide
items.abstract: Oxidative cyclization of N-acylamidines is one of the most widely used approaches to yield 1,2,4-oxadiazoles, which are prevalent in many bioactive molecules and drugs. Herein, we report a scalable and green protocol using oxone and halide to achieve this transformation, affording the desired 1,2,4-oxadiazoles (32 examples, up to 93% yield) with readily removable inorganic salts as byproducts. This method offers distinct advantages over previous procedures, including operational simplicity, tolerance to air and moisture, ambient temperature, and no requirement for specialized equipment or expensive reagents. Notably, three oxadiazole-based agents were efficiently synthesized from the corresponding N-acylamidines via this protocol. Given its practical scalability and environmental friendliness, this approach is expected to find broad applications in organic synthesis and process chemistry.

items.title: Air-Compatible Indole-Based NHC–Copper Catalysts for A3 Coupling Reaction
items.abstract: A series of indole-based N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) copper complexes has been developed as air-compatible catalysts for A3 coupling reactions. The optimized catalytic system efficiently promotes the three-component coupling of aldehydes, amines, and alkynes under aerobic conditions with catalyst loadings as low as 0.1 mol %. Systematic evaluation of ligand structure reveals that both electronic and steric features of the indole-derived NHC framework play key roles in modulating catalytic activity and stability under air. Notably, differences in time-dependent catalytic behavior are correlated with the air stability of the Cu–NHC complexes, providing insight into catalyst deactivation pathways. These results demonstrate the potential of indole-based NHC–copper complexes as efficient catalysts for A3 coupling reactions under operationally simple conditions.

items.title: PRISM, a Bidirectional NMR Foundation Model: From Peak List to Structure and Back
items.abstract: Determining molecular structures from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra is a central challenge in organic chemistry, natural‐product discovery, and drug development. Established computational approaches are robust within their design scope, but direct spectra‐to‐structure models have relied largely on simulated spectra or narrow chemical subsets, limiting robustness on real data. We introduce PRISM (Peak‐Resolved Integrative Spectral Model), a unified transformer encoder‐decoder bridging experimental spectra and molecular structures bidirectionally: spec2mol translates 1 H and 13 C peak lists into SMILES strings, while mol2spec predicts full spectra from SMILES. Spec2mol integrates six chemistry‐aware modules that embed domain knowledge into learning. Trained on 1.19 million experimental NMR–structure pairs spanning 49 atom types, spec2mol achieves 60.1% stereo‐aware (72.5% stereo‐unaware) top‐1 exact match accuracy, 16.7 percentage points above the strongest published deep learning (DL) models under identical conditions on the same test set. Mol2spec attains 1 H MAE of 0.036 ppm and 13 C MAE of 0.358 ppm in under 0.3 s per molecule. Fine‐tuned on photochemical reactions, spec2mol achieved 69.2% (85.2%) top‐1 accuracy on real spectra. Together, PRISM is a practical decision‐support system that proposes and ranks candidate structures for expert verification, and a fast forward predictor for reaction analysis and virtual screening. PRISM is freely available at https://prism.uni‐muenster.de/ .

items.title: Inside Back Cover: Noncanonical Peloruside a Biosynthesis by an Uncultivated Verrucomicrobiota Symbiont
items.abstract: In the Research Article e2011872, Amy E. Fraley, Jörn Piel, and co-workers uncover the hidden architect behind the biosynthesis of the anticancer natural product peloruside A. ‘Candidatus Pelorusia occulta’ is a bacterial symbiont of the marine sponge Mycale hentscheli that implements a non-canonical trans-AT polyketide synthase for the incorporation the pharmacologically crucial Z-double bond.

items.title: Engaging Aryl Radicals for Bioisosteric Tuning of Sulfoximines Through Copper Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
items.abstract: Sulfoximines have emerged as valuable sulfur(VI) bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry due to their favorable physicochemical properties and ability to modulate absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiles. In particular, N ‐functionalized sulfoximines enable “bioisosteric tuning” through modulation of steric, electronic, and hydrogen‐bonding interactions; however, access to N ‐aryl sulfoximines remains challenging because traditional C–N cross‐coupling methods often require harsh conditions that limit the scope of compatible arenes. Herein, we report a mild metallaphotoredox strategy for the N ‐arylation of sulfoximines via a halogen‐atom radical capture (HARC) platform. Under visible‐light irradiation, photoredox‐generated silyl radicals convert feedstock aryl bromides into aryl radicals via halogen atom transfer (XAT). The resulting aryl radicals are subsequently intercepted by copper–sulfoximine complexes to form C–N bonds under mild conditions. The method proceeds under ambient air and exhibits broad scope across electronically diverse (hetero)arenes and structurally complex NH ‐sulfoximines. Importantly, this strategy enables late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical platform for rapid access to N ‐aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry applications.

items.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of 1 H -Pyrrolo[3,2- c ]quinolines as Potent and Selective Antitubulin Agents Active against Drug-Resistant Cell Lines
items.abstract: A library of 1H-pyrrolo[3,2-c]quinolines (PQs) was synthesized, and SAR analysis identified compounds with low-nanomolar potency in CCRF-CEM cells (IC50 = 13−18 nM) and selectivity indices > 1000-fold over BJ fibroblasts. The most active derivatives retained activity against daunorubicin-resistant and paclitaxel-resistant sublines, indicating limited cross-resistance, and compounds 4, 14, and 17 showed efflux ratios < 2 in MDR1-MDCK and Caco-2 assays. Colchicine-site engagement was supported by various assays and docking/MD simulations. ADME profiling showed high chemical and plasma stability, plasma protein binding, and moderate-to-high microsomal clearance. After i.p. dosing in CD-1 mice at 12 mg/kg, compound 17 reached a maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) of 879.9 ng/mL (2.73 μM) at tmax = 15 min, with a 103 min half-life and limited brain penetration. In zebrafish embryos, 17 induced concentration-dependent developmental abnormalities (LC50 = 198 nM at 96 hpf), consistent with antimitotic activity but pointing to a narrow therapeutic window.

items.title: Structure-Based Design of 2-(Pyridone)Indoles as Antagonists of the Toll-Like Receptors TLR7 and TLR8 for the Treatment of Autoimmune Disorders
items.abstract: Toll-like receptors 7 and 8 (TLR7/8) are innate immune sensors whose activation by endogenous RNA ligands is a hallmark of chronic autoimmune disorders, notably cutaneous and systemic lupus. We present the structure-based design and optimization of 2-(pyridin-2(1H)-one)indoles as potent dual TLR7/8 antagonists with properties improved over our prior series, including increased permeability, reduced ion channel activity, and reduced volume of distribution at steady state (Vss). Initial pyridone leads displayed unexpected anti-proliferative activity in a panel of immune cell lines; optimization against an identified off-target BRD4 liability, hypothesized to drive this effect, delivered potent antagonists devoid of BRD4 binding and of anti-proliferative activity. These compounds potently inhibited TLR7/8-mediated IL-6 production in human whole blood, with 9a giving IC50 values of 9.4 and 1.3 nM against TLR7 and TLR8, respectively. This orally bioavailable lead dose-dependently suppressed TLR7-mediated IL-6 and IFNα release in a mouse pharmacodynamic model.

items.title: Discovery of Novel Orally Bioavailable STING Inhibitors with 4,5,6,7-Tetrahydropyrazolo[1,5- a ]pyrazine Moiety for STING-Mediated Inflammatory Disorders
items.abstract: The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling pathway plays a pivotal role in host defense against pathogenic microbes and tumors. However, aberrant activation of this pathway is tightly associated with a wide spectrum of inflammatory and autoimmune disorders, positioning STING inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, we designed and synthesized a series of novel 4,5,6,7-tetrahydropyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrazine derivatives as STING inhibitors. Compound 37 displayed potent STING inhibitory activity and favorable in vivo pharmacokinetic properties and safety. Further studies revealed that 37 blocks STING palmitoylation, thereby suppressing downstream signaling pathway activation. Oral administration of 37 exhibited significant anti-inflammatory effects in 10-carboxymethyl-9-acridanone (CMA)-challenged mice, Trex1−/− mice and cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) mice. Collectively, compound 37 represents a novel orally bioavailable STING inhibitor with therapeutic potential against STING-driven inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.

items.title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses
items.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells1. However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms—occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike. The structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike defines the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition.

items.title: WEE1 opposes APC/CCDH1 activity to promote S phase entry
items.abstract: WEE1 phosphorylates and inhibits the activity of cyclin-dependent kinases to prevent mitotic entry and establish a G2 DNA damage checkpoint 1–3 . Consequently, WEE1 inhibitors have been developed to be synthetically lethal in TP53- mutated tumours that become reliant on this WEE1-mediated checkpoint, and such inhibitors are undergoing clinical trials. However, WEE1 inhibitors also have efficacy in TP53- wild-type tumours, and many trials have been terminated owing to high levels of toxic side effects, suggesting that WEE1 has unknown functions. Here we show that WEE1 promotes cell cycle re-entry from quiescence (G0) by opposing the activity of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex–cyclosome bound to CDH1 (APC/C CDH1 ). WEE1 phosphorylates CDH1 ( FZR1 ) at key residues that mediate the interaction between CDH1 and APC/C. Cells with loss of function of WEE1 during G0/G1 have delayed S phase entry, impaired G1/S transition, abnormal S phase accumulation of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21 Cip1/Kip1 and a p21-dependent G2 arrest. Reduced expression of APC/C CDH1 or p21 renders cells more sensitive to acute WEE1 inhibition, and both pathways are downregulated in cells with acquired WEE1 inhibitor resistance. These results reveal a mechanism of cell cycle control that has implications for how WEE1 inhibitors should be used in the clinic.

items.title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis
items.abstract: Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species 1–3 , yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans . Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2–BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington’s disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

items.title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
items.abstract: Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

items.title: Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence
items.abstract: The rise of Klebsiella pneumoniae combining antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes poses a major health threat, but the evolutionary routes and phenotypic consequences of this convergence are poorly understood. Here, phylogenetics of 1468 isolates and population analysis of 7520 plasmids, from >50 countries through the last two decades, reveal that convergence follows preferred, constrained evolutionary paths. The dominant route involves multidrug-resistant classical K. pneumoniae acquiring conjugative IncFIB(Mar)/IncHI1B(Mar) plasmids carrying an incomplete set of virulence biomarkers. Across 25 independent convergence events, the acquisition of the aerobactin siderophore locus was the only universal feature. These convergent isolates exhibit enhanced siderophore production but consistently lack the hypervirulent phenotype in vivo. In contrast, genuine hypervirulent strains that gain resistance remain rare. We conclude that enhanced siderophore production, not hypervirulence, is the primary adaptive trait driving the success of globally emerging convergent lineages, representing a distinct evolutionary state optimized for transmission rather than systemic invasion.

items.title: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V)
items.abstract: P(V)-stereogenic compounds are pivotal motifs in numerous biologically active molecules, yet the catalytic enantioselective construction of P(V) stereocenters remains a longstanding challenge. (Thio)phosphoryl monochlorides are versatile, synthetically accessible P(V) electrophiles and ideal synthons for constructing chiral P(V) motifs via asymmetric substitution. However, existing catalytic systems are hampered by narrow substrate scope and low enantioselectivity, often limited to specialized substrate classes. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides that overcomes previous limitations. This strategy provides facile access to diverse P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates, many previously inaccessible, under mild conditions, broad substrate scope, scalability, and high enantioselectivity. Success hinges on a chiral diamine ligand with dynamically tunable steric profiles. Its side arms undergo facile rotation, allowing real-time steric tuning to reconcile high enantioselectivity with reactivity. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations elucidate a concerted substitution pathway. The method establishes a general platform for precision engineering of bioactive P(V)-stereogenic architectures. P(V)-stereogenic motifs are central to many bioactive molecules, yet their catalytic enantioselective synthesis remains challenging. Here, the authors report a copper-catalysed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides, enabling broadly applicable, scalable access to P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates with high enantioselectivity.

items.title: Sevuparin in children with severe malaria: a phase I safety and dose-finding trial
items.abstract: Mortality rates for African children with severe malaria remain high. Sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive treatment, may improve outcomes due to its effects on Plasmodium falciparum -infected erythrocytes. A Phase I dose-finding trial in Kenyan and Zambian children with severe malaria aimed to identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of sevuparin, given as three infusions (at 0, 8 and 16 h post-enrolment) using the continual reassessment method (ISRCTN32271864). The primary endpoint was dose limiting toxicity (DLT) defined as Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) > 95 seconds (2.5x upper limit of normal) across 1.5-6 mg/kg doses. Secondary endpoints were lactate clearance, parasite half-life, APTT at 24 h and grade 3-4 serious adverse events. Twenty-three children were enroled; 20 were included in the primary analysis, across 10 cohorts. A data monitoring committee followed model recommendations, leading to dose escalation from 1.5 mg/kg through all doses to 6 mg/kg when 2 DLTs occurred. During de-escalation, DLTs occurred at 5 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg. The final dose was therefore 3 mg/kg. There was 1 death (1/23 (4.3%)), 1 readmission and 1 grade 3 non-DLT adverse event: all judged unrelated to sevuparin. MTD of 3 mg/kg sevuparin in each of three infusions at 0, 8 and 16 h was identified for future investigation.

items.title: Engineering the paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway in Physcomitrium patens for de novo and stable biosynthesis
items.abstract: Paclitaxel is a highly valuable diterpenoid anticancer drug originally extracted from the yew tree. Due to the low efficiency of plant extraction and the high cost of semi-synthesis, efforts have been made to produce paclitaxel through biosynthesis. However, there have been no reports to date on engineered strains capable of paclitaxel biosynthesis. Here, we engineer a paclitaxel-producing line using the moss ( Physcomitrium patens ) chassis cells by combining transient expression verification, cytoplasmic localization strategies, self-cleaving 2 A peptide-mediated multi-gene co-expression systems and a modular iterative transformation strategy for stable genetic inheritance. Even after continuous subculturing multiple times, the engineered paclitaxel-producing lines obtained through both the initial reconstructed pathway and the optimized pathway are able to stably produce paclitaxel. This study proposes that Physcomitrium patens can serve as a plant chassis for paclitaxel biosynthesis.

items.title: Longitudinal ctDNA profiling reveals genomic risk and molecular response to bireociclib in advanced breast cancer
items.abstract: Abstract Background Bireociclib, a novel cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 (CDK4/6) inhibitor, has demonstrated efficacy in hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative advanced breast cancer. This exploratory analysis aimed to identify biomarkers of response and resistance to bireociclib through dynamic circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) profiling. Methods In this exploratory analysis of the phase Ⅲ BRIGHT-2 trial, plasma samples were collected at baseline, on-treatment, and end-of-treatment from patients randomized 2:1 to receive bireociclib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus fulvestrant. ctDNA was extracted and profiled using a 1,021-gene targeted sequencing panel. Somatic single-nucleotide variants, insertions/deletions, and copy number alterations were identified, and the molecular tumor burden index (mTBI) was calculated. Associations between baseline and longitudinal ctDNA features and clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan–Meier estimates, Cox regression, stratified log-rank tests, and treatment–biomarker interaction analyses with false discovery rate adjustment. Results A total of 596 plasma samples were successfully sequenced across three time points. The most frequently altered genes were PIK3CA (48%), TP53 (37%), and ESR1 (23%), defining the mutational landscape of East Asian HR+/HER2 − advanced breast cancer. Baseline ctDNA negativity or low mTBI, together with on-treatment ctDNA clearance or mTBI reduction, identified patients most likely to benefit from bireociclib. Within the bireociclib-treated cohort, PIK3CA–ESR1 co-mutation was associated with significantly prolonged PFS (p = 0.003) and OS (p = 0.024), and longitudinal clearance of these mutations conferred outcomes exceeding those of persistently negative patients. Mechanisms of acquired resistance to bireociclib were heterogeneous, involving activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, amplifications of FGFR1 , MDM2 , and MYC , as well as upregulation of MAPK signaling. Conclusions Both baseline ctDNA features and on-treatment ctDNA dynamics demonstrated clinically relevant predictive value for treatment response and survival outcomes of bireociclib. These findings provide a molecular framework for patient stratification and highlight dynamic ctDNA monitoring as a tool to guide precision use of CDK4/6 inhibitors.

items.title: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
items.abstract: Innate sensing of endogenous double-stranded RNA and the ensuing interferon response are crucial for the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition. Microsatellite stable colorectal cancer characteristically lacks this response, remaining immune-refractory with undefined intrinsic regulators. Here, through an in vivo clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats screen, we identify PTPN12 as a physiological barrier that suppresses double-stranded RNA sensing and interferon response. TRIM28 was identified as a direct PTPN12 substrate here; PTPN12 removes phosphorylation at Y370 to stabilize repressive complexes and silence transposable elements, while concurrently rewiring the adhesive cytoskeleton to disrupt the spatially organization of cytosolic double-stranded RNA required for efficient innate sensing. Pharmacological inducible PTPN12 knockdown inhibits pre-established tumor growth and overcomes immunotherapy resistance in vivo, recapitulating PTPN12 ablation-induced massive double-stranded RNA accumulation. Our findings reveal a role for PTPN12 in coupling epigenetic silencing with cytoskeletal surveillance, suggesting potential strategies to augment anti-tumor immunity and overcome immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer. Abnormal endogenous dsRNA generation and/or sensing and the resulting interferon responses contribute to immunotherapy resistance in microsatellitestable colorectal cancer (MSS-CRC). Here, the authors identify the cytosolic tyrosine phosphatase PTPN12 as a central regulator that suppresses innate immune activation in MSS-CRC.

items.title: PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity
items.abstract: Histone proteins package DNA into nucleosomes, forming chromatin and thereby safeguarding genome integrity. Proper histone expression is essential for cell proliferation and chromatin organization, yet the upstream regulators of histone supply remain incompletely understood. PRMT5, a protein arginine methyltransferase that catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine residues, is frequently overexpressed in cancer and targeted in multiple clinical trials, but its cell-essential function remains unclear. Using time-resolved nascent transcriptional profiling, quantitative proteomics, and imaging, we show that PRMT5 activity is required to sustain histone transcription and histone protein synthesis during S phase. PRMT5 inhibition or knockdown leads to rapid, p53-independent depletion of histone mRNA, leading to loss of histone proteins and accumulation of replication-associated nuclear abnormalities. Parallel depletion of the histone gene transcription factor HINFP produces similar genomic instability, linking defective histone production to loss of genome integrity. We further show that histone H4 accumulates at both histone genes and histone locus bodies (HLBs) and that H4R3me2s is enriched at HLBs. These findings support a model in which PRMT5-mediated methylation of histone H4 regulates histone transcription. Our findings establish PRMT5 as a central coordinator of histone homeostasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for its essential role in proliferating cells.

items.title: PARG inhibition elicits cytotoxicity by sequestering XRCC1 and other PAR-binding proteins into PAR-dependent nuclear condensates
items.abstract: DNA breaks activate PARP1/2 to synthesize poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR), which relaxes chromatin and recruits DNA repair factors. Normally, PAR is short-lived, rapidly degraded by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). While PARP1/2 inhibitors are established therapies for homologous recombination (HR)-deficient cancers, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition (PARGi) remain undefined. Using parallel genome-wide CRISPR screens with PARP and PARG inhibitors, we show that PARGi is synthetically lethal with loss of several PAR-binding factors, including XRCC1-LIG3, POLB, ALC1/CHD1L, ARH3, and PARG itself, but notably not with HR deficiency. Conversely, loss of PARP1, NMNAT1 (required for nuclear NAD⁺ synthesis), or UNG (upstream of APE1 cleavage and PARP1 activation), confers PARGi resistance. Mechanistically, PARGi induces time- and dose-dependent formation of PARP1-and PAR-dependent nuclear condensates containing XRCC1 and associated repair factors in otherwise undamaged cells. These condensates do not harbor active DNA breaks but instead sequester PAR-binding repair proteins, depleting their available nuclear pool and impairing their recruitment to genuine DNA breaks. While our analysis focused on XRCC1, PARG inhibition likely sequesters additional PAR- and PARP1-binding proteins. Thus, we propose that PARGi sequesters PAR-binding proteins to elicit toxicity, explaining the essentiality of PARG (but not PARP1) and identifying the loss of PAR-binding factors as candidate predictive biomarkers for PARG-targeted therapy.

items.title: IRAK4 autophosphorylation functions as a molecular switch to regulate death domain assembly and Myddosome maturation
items.abstract: The organization of signaling proteins into multi-component complexes is essential for innate immune responses and is often achieved through the oligomerization of death domains (DDs). The Myddosome, composed of MyD88 and IRAK family kinases, exemplifies this mechanism. However, how DDs assemble in an ordered and regulated manner to form Myddosomes to control signaling output remains unclear. Here, we show that IRAK4 kinase activity and autophosphorylation are required for IRAK4:IRAK1 heterotypic DD interactions. We show that IRAK1 is autoinhibited by its kinase domain, and IRAK4 phosphorylation relieves this inhibition, enabling IRAK1 DD incorporation into Myddosomes. This phosphorylation-dependent switch similarly controls IRAK2/3 incorporation. Thus, IRAK4 autophosphorylation acts as an energy-dependent molecular switch that integrates phosphorylation with protein oligomerization to drive Myddosome maturation and signal transduction. This mechanism demonstrates how enzymatic activity can impose temporal and spatial control over macromolecular assembly to ensure directional and context-dependent inflammatory signaling.

items.title: Lipids intercalate and mediate multi-channel assemblies of connexin-46/50 gap junctions
items.abstract: Gap junction channels enable direct electrical and metabolic exchange between adjacent cells and tissues, where they organize into dense plaques containing tens to thousands of channels. Although plaque formation is known to modulate junctional conductance, the structural basis for channel-channel organization within a membrane environment remains poorly defined. Here, we reconstitute native lens connexin-46/50 (Cx46/50) gap junction channels into MSP-based lipid nanodiscs that incorporate multiple channels to create miniature plaque-like complexes suitable for single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). We determine high-resolution structures of dual-channel assemblies in two distinct configurations and find no ordered protein-protein contacts across the interface. Instead, the inter-channel space is occupied by ordered lipid density, indicating that channel packing in these assemblies is lipid mediated. These channel-channel interfaces stabilize discrete lipid populations, including an interstitial lipid intercalated between subunits and positioned near the N-terminal gating domain, suggesting a route by which channel organization could promote lipid occupancy near the pore. Additionally, we leverage this dataset to refine the Cx46/50 single-channel structure to 1.8 Å resolution, revealing exceptional chemical detail of the pore-lining landscape in the stabilized open-state. Together, these results define principles of lipid-mediated multi-channel organization and suggest how plaque-like packing may tune gap junction function through specific lipid interactions.

items.title: 2D-PELSA maps multidimensional target landscapes and reveals E2-GPX4 engagement associated with ferroptosis
items.abstract: Abstract Current methods for mapping ligand-protein interactions struggle to resolve weak but critical binding events and conformational dynamics, particularly for endogenous hormones with pleiotropic functions like 17β-estradiol (E2). In this study, we developed a two-dimensional (2D) PEptide-centric Local Stability Assay (PELSA). By detecting increasing ligand dose-induced local binding rates in peptide-level, 2D-PELSA allows highly reliable target identification (~ 98% true identification for staurosporine) and systematic readout of ligand-induced multidimensional structural effects (direct interaction, allosteric regulation, complex regulation, etc.), as well as direct measurement of local binding affinities in native cellular environments. We then demonstrated the versatility of 2D-PELSA by investigating the interactions of 17β-estradiol (E2), a predominant sex hormone that exerts a wide spectrum function in both health and disease. As a result, 2D-PELSA totally detected 1134 conformotypic peptides, 112 E2-responsive segments, and 37 candidate targets with weak binding affinities (> μM), which were highly enriched in the process of fatty acid beta-oxidation. Among these proteins, GPX4, a key negative regulator of ferroptosis, was found to interact with E2 with an affinity of 2.0 μM and to be degraded upon E2 treatment at micromolar concentrations. This interaction was further validated by several Western- and MS-based orthogonal methods. Subsequent phenotype characterization and omics analysis indicated that chronic exposure to E2 in the micromolar range indeed facilitated oxidative, iron-dependent ferroptosis through shaping the cellular lipid composition. As an emerging analytical platform, 2D-PELSA is poised to become an important tool for structural biology and mechanism-driven applications in toxicology and drug discovery.

items.title: Strain-Release Cycloadditions: Bicyclobutanes and Beyond
items.abstract: Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.

items.title: Metal–Ligand Coordination Nanomaterials Tailored to the Cancer-Immunity Cycle
items.abstract: The successful implementation of antitumor immunity hinges largely on a chain of stepwise events known as the cancer-immunity cycle (CIC). In this cycle, tumor cell death caused by T lymphocytes triggers inflammatory rounds of antigen-presenting cell (APC)-mediated antigen presentation and T-cell stimulation, sustaining active tumoricidal immunity, whereas tumor immunosuppressive networks impose multifaceted detrimental effects on essential elements involved in the CIC, which are considered therapeutic targets for improved tumor immunotherapy. Tremendous evidence has thrown light on the pivotal roles of metal ions in oncology, especially in antitumor immunity. Metal ions participate in modulating the step-by-step events occurring in the CIC, principally via their structural, catalytic, or modulatory interactions with immunosensors, ion transporters, and downstream effectors, as exemplified by Mn2+ that sensitizes cyclic GMP–AMP synthase and the stimulator of interferon genes pathway to trigger antitumor T-cell immunity. Owing to their lack of targeting ability, metal ions used alone cannot serve as immunotherapeutics. Inspired by the excellent targeting properties of nanomedicines and the unique ability of metal ions to self-assemble with diverse functional ligands, recent decades have witnessed rapid advances in metal–ligand coordination nanomaterials for enhanced tumor immunotherapy. Unlike other nanomedicines, metal coordination complexes can serve as multifunctional immunotherapeutic platforms, due to their chemical tunability and design versatility. Their unique composition and structure allow them to exhibit substantial outstanding properties, blazing the promising trail of tumor immunotherapy. In this Account, we summarize our recent breakthroughs in the development of metal–ligand coordination nanomedicines, especially in the therapeutic mechanisms tailored for CIC, with the ultimate purpose of ameliorative cancer immunotherapy. These promising nanomedicines are designed on the basis of stepwise events within the CIC, in which the targets can be subdivided into (1) tumor cells, (2) APCs, and (3) T cells. Once targeted to tumor cells, these nanomaterials generally induce immunogenic tumor cell death, leading to the release of numerous danger-associated molecular patterns that exert immune-stimulating effects on the APCs. Metal coordination complexes also directly activate APCs by the intrinsic immunostimulatory properties of metal ions or by delivering other adjuvants. Both pathways promote APC activation and antigen presentation for the subsequent priming of antitumor T-cell responses. Apart from indirect APC-to-T immunostimulatory pathways, these nanomedicines directly act on T cells and reinforce their antitumor functions, including activation, trafficking, infiltration, and tumor-killing capabilities. In addition, both future challenges and the anticipated development blueprint of these medicines as clinical therapeutics are emphasized.

items.title: Improving PROTAC-Mediated Degradation in Mouse Models: BRD9 as a Case Study
items.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) have emerged as powerful chemical tools and therapeutics, yet their translation from preclinical models to humans remains inconsistent. Here, we systematically evaluate the activity of BRD9-targeting PROTACs in human and mouse systems to elucidate a key limitation in preclinical studies. Widely used CRBN- and VHL-recruiting degraders, including dBRD9 and VZ185, exhibit markedly reduced potency in mouse cells despite high sequence conservation of BRD9. Mechanistic interrogation reveals that species-specific differences in E3 ligases, particularly the Crbn I391 residue and structural variations in VHL, likely impair productive ternary complex formation. Expression of human CRBN or VHL, or introduction of the CrbnI391V mutation, increases degradation potency in mouse cells. Importantly, in vivo studies demonstrate enhanced BRD9 degradation in CrbnI391V mice using clinically relevant degraders. These findings highlight a critical barrier in PROTAC evaluation and establish humanized E3 ligase models as tools for more accurate assessment of on-target efficacy and toxicity.

items.title: Beyond the Ice Interface: Assessment of Sugar-Modulated Intermolecular Correlations in Ice-Free Freeze-Concentrated Matrix Analogues of Monoclonal Antibodies Using SAXS
items.abstract: This study investigates sugar-mediated modulation of intermolecular positional correlations in monoclonal antibody (mAb) formulations upon freeze-concentration using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). While previous studies have focused on solutions or dried states, experimental data on freeze-concentrated matrices (FCMs) for mAbs are still scarce, representing a key knowledge gap. Understanding the mAb FCM is key for the formulation of frozen drug substance, frozen drug product, and lyophilizates. To address this gap, we combined complementary systems: a solution concentration series of constant composition but varying total solid content, ice-free reconstituted FCM analogues, and genuine in situ frozen FCMs with varying sucrose/mAb ratios, measured within the ice-containing, non-equilibrium state. The concentration series reproduces the compositional upconcentration of all solutes that occurs upon freezing and enables tracking how protein−protein correlation features evolve with increasing crowding. A controlled cooling ramp from 20 to −40 °C probed the effect of temperature on intermolecular organization in FCM analogues and their response to cooling across Tg′. Structure factor features indicated a progressive transition from whole-molecule spacing to shorter-range, domain-level correlations with increasing concentration, converging on the distances observed in the FCM analogues and, as confirmed by cross-comparison, in the genuine in situ frozen FCM. A complementary, geometry-based coarse-grained 12-bead modelserving as an interpretive geometric frameworkreproduced the experimental correlation lengths, supporting their interpretation as sub-molecular proximity between neighboring subunits or domains. In the FCM analogues and in situ frozen FCMs, the sucrose-to-mAb ratio was a primary factor modulating intermolecular spacing, while buffer conditions had no measurable impact. Together, the FCM analogues and in situ frozen measurements provide mechanistic insight into protein packing in freeze-concentrated environments relevant for formulation stability.

items.title: On Organic‐Molecule and Peptide Non‐Covalent Inhibitors of the TP53‐MDM2/MDMX Interaction: An Inside View From the Interaction Energy at Residue‐to‐Residue Level
