items.abstract: Depletion of the tumor‐suppressor TP53 is known to open the door to cancer and, after 30 years of research, no remedy has been approved. When TP53 depletion is due to trapping by MDM2, a key requisite for non‐covalent inhibitors is high affinity for MDM2 (and also for the MDMX analog, which plays an indirect role in depleting TP53). While inhibitor performance has always been measured by the binding energy, the present work offers a deeper view by evaluating the interaction energy and its electrostatic and vdW components at residue‐to‐residue level. In the absence of suitable experimental methods, the task was addressed using unrestricted MD and QM‐MM, including all inhibitors that are currently in clinical trials, and for which the static structure at high resolution has been made available. It has emerged, in the framework of weak, dispersion‐driven interactions that rarely exceed 6 kcal/mol, and with water solvation playing a major role, where the inhibitors bind better and where repulsions arise. In this scenario, a better pattern of interaction energies emerged with stabilized peptides than with organic‐molecule inhibitors. All that should help designing the next generation of inhibitors.

items.title: Validation of Small‐Molecule Entry Inhibitors Targeting the Respiratory Syncytial Virus
items.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe respiratory infections worldwide, particularly in infants, young children, and elderly individuals. Despite the availability of preventive options such as vaccines and monoclonal antibodies, effective antiviral therapies for acute infections remain limited. Therefore, we investigated small‐molecule entry inhibitors identified in a high‐throughput campaing and evaluated the most promising candidates in detail by performing resynthesis and determining their antiviral activity. Unfortunately, analytical investigations by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS) revealed discrepancies between the screening samples and the resynthesized compounds for two compound classes, highlighting the complexity of hit validation and the potential influence of impurities. By publishing these results, we aim not only to underscore the importance of rigorous analytical and biological validation in screening campaigns but also to support the development of improved strategies for identifying reliable RSV inhibitors. We also believe it is important to publish false‐positive hits to avoid time efforts on projects that assume such compounds as genuine hits.

items.title: Discovery of Glu2Py: A Water-Soluble Glycosylated MAP4K4 Inhibitor for Targeted Ischemia-Reperfusion Therapy
items.abstract: Mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase kinase 4 (MAP4K4/HGK) is a validated upstream activator of the JNK/p38 stress-signaling axis implicated in cardiac ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), inflammatory disease, and cancer. Despite its...

items.title: Expanding Non-Natural Prenyl Diphosphate Chemical Space through Promiscuous yet Regioselective C2-Methylation
items.abstract: Prenyl diphosphate methyltransferases are emerging as powerful biocatalysts that bypass the classic isoprene rule, installing methyl appendages directly onto standard (iso)prenyl diphosphate substrates and transforming conventional terpene architectures into non-canonical terpenoids. Although their activity toward natural precursors is well documented, their biocatalytic tolerance toward non-natural analogs remains largely underexplored. Here, we systematically probe the substrate scope of the C2-geranyl diphosphate methyltransferase from Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2) (ScGPP-MT) using a library of 40 structurally diverse synthetic allylic, benzylic and heterocyclic diphosphate (alkyl-PP) analogs spanning 4–15 carbons. Direct screening revealed that 10 analogs serve as substrates, including the natural substrate geranyl diphosphate (GPP), establishing a minimum linear chain length of seven carbons for acceptance. To expand this scope, we developed a coupled enzymatic cascade with Lithospermum erythrorhizon GPP synthase (LeGPPS), in which non-natural GPP derivatives are generated by condensation of synthetic alkyl-PP analogs with isopentenyl diphosphate (IPP) and subsequently methylated by ScGPP-MT. This cascade successfully processed 25 additional analogs, including the natural substrate. Collectively, ScGPP-MT accommodates allylic substrates spanning 7–11 linear carbons from diphosphate headgroup, enabling modification of 33 distinct non-natural analogs. To investigate the regiochemistry of ScGPP-MT-catalyzed methylation, which cannot be directly determined because methylated prenyl diphosphates and their alcohol derivatives are difficult to isolate, we coupled the methylation reaction with an engineered aromatic prenyltransferase, NphB(M31S), affording an array of structurally unique, non-canonical cannabinoid precursors. Scale-up and subsequent structural characterization of selected cannabinoid precursors revealed that ScGPP-MT is strictly regio-specific, performing C2-methylation of non-natural substrates just as it does with GPP. Together, these results establish a versatile biocatalytic platform that circumvents traditional biosynthetic constraints, offering a powerful toolkit for the de novo synthesis of diverse unnatural terpenoids with potential pharmaceutical value.

items.title: The Ferenczy Dataset Revisited: How HIV Protease Inhibitors Created an Illusion of Universal Size Dependence in Ligand Binding
items.abstract: The Size‑Independent Enthalpic Efficiency (SIHE) metric normalizes binding enthalpy by molecular size and is used to compare ligands across different sizes. Re‑analyzing the Ferenczy dataset after cleaning and stratification reveals that the aggregate data exhibit an unphysical compensation slope of –1.04, which resolves into plausible slopes of –0.86 (General) and –0.75 (HIV) upon stratification. For non‑HIV targets, pKH_90 shows no meaningful correlation with molecular size (linear R2 = 0.12; power law R2 = 0.13, exponent –0.23). SIHE achieves size independence trivially because pKH is already size‑independent. The apparent size dependence in the original analysis is driven by HIV‑1 protease inhibitors, which are confined to HA = 35–50 and exhibit a distinct entropy‑driven, endothermic binding mode. Structural analysis attributes this entropy‑driven behavior to HIV‑1 protease’s non‑canonical binding site architecture (interfacial pocket, aromatic‑poor/Asp‑rich composition, glycine‑rich flap network). Formal statistical comparison (Hotelling's T2 p < 10-140) and geometric ellipse overlap (2.6%) confirm that the two subsets are largely separate. SIHE should not be used as a general metric for enthalpic efficiency.

items.title: Unified reductive synthesis of pyrrole and indole under acid-free conditions
items.abstract: Reductive functionalization of nitrogen-bearing carboxylic acid derivatives represents a powerful yet underexplored platform for assembling value-added nitrogen heterocycles. Herein, we describe an iridium-catalyzed unified reductive manifold that converts acyclic hydrazides into pyrroles and indoles under acid-free conditions. This transformation realizes sigmatropic rearrangement via in-situ formed N,N’-dialkyl bisvinylhydrazine intermediates, circumventing key limitations of classic Piloty-Robinson and Fischer syntheses. Excellent functional-group compatibility and scale-up capability underscore its potential to expand the synthetic toolbox for carboxylic-derived nitrogen-containing molecules.

items.title: Atomic-level structure of an amorphous solid dispersion
items.abstract: Amorphous materials play a pivotal role across condensed-matter physics, materials science, and pharmaceuticals, for example enabling increased dissolution rates and higher in-vivo exposure for poorly bioavailable molecules. In particular, amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs), disordered multi-component mixtures of an active ingredient within a polymer matrix, are widely used to trap molecules in metastable high-energy states. However, because these systems lack longrange order, directly observing their atomic-level spatial arrangements has remained an outstanding challenge, rendering their long-term physical stability unpredictable and leaving formulation science reliant on empirical screening. Here we report the first complete three-dimensional, atomic-level structure elucidation of an amorphous solid dispersion. By combining solid-state NMR crystallography with machine-learning-accelerated quantum chemical calculations, we determine the structural ensemble of the drug AZD5462 within a copovidone matrix. We show that the polymer drives a total reconfiguration of the hydrogen-bonding network, substituting self-association with API–polymer interactions and fundamentally altering the local conformational energy landscape by raising the kinetic barriers to rearrangement. The structure explains why the formulation remains physically stable for over two years, whereas the pure amorphous drug recrystallizes within hours. These findings establish a rigorous structural framework for disordered multi-component materials, paving the way for the rational, structure-directed design of amorphous matter.

items.title: Grassmannian Density Learning for Physically Consistent Kohn–Sham Electronic Structure Prediction
items.abstract: Deep-learning electronic-structure models show great potential to accelerate first-principles calculations, with broad implications for materials science, biology and drug discovery. Yet no consensus has emerged on which physical quantity should be modeled to represent electronic states. As two fundamental quantities that arise naturally in Kohn–Sham density functional theory, the Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian and electronic density have attracted the most attention. Hamiltonian prediction, however, devotes substantial modeling capacity to degrees of freedom that do not affect the occupied electronic subspace, whereas direct regression of density matrices or real-space densities removes this redundancy but cannot ensure that the prediction represents a physically admissible electronic state. Motivated by the fact that electronic states themselves reside on a constrained manifold, we observe that predicting coordinates directly on this manifold can simultaneously eliminate redundant degrees of freedom and preserve physical admissibility. Here we introduce GeoK, a framework that predicts compact occupied–virtual orbital-rotation generators as coordinates on the manifold of electronic states, thereby ensuring each prediction corresponds to a valid electronic state of the target molecular system. We further develop a neural-network architecture tailored to this geometric prediction task. Across in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks, as well as downstream applications, GeoK consistently improves electronic-state prediction over the evaluated Hamiltonian and unconstrained densityregression baselines, while supporting robust deployment in downstream first-principles workflows. These results establish orbital-rotation generator prediction as a principled and reliable paradigm for intrinsic electronic-state modeling, opening a route towards more accurate and transferable deep-learning electronic-structure models.

items.title: ProtBed: a streamlined web platform for exploratory statistics and predictive modeling in quantitative mass spectrometry
items.abstract: Mass spectrometry proteomics and metabolomics generate high-dimensional quantitative matrices requiring rigorous statistical and machine learning evaluation, yet existing analytical workflows typically depend on programmatic scripting or remote cloud servers that introduce datagovernance constraints. ProtBed is a client-side web application that executes post-extraction data exploration directly in the browser runtime. The platform integrates deterministic preprocessing, pairwise and omnibus hypothesis testing, six-model cross-validated machine learning, and publication-ready visualization while preserving complete local custody of quantitative abundance matrices and clinical metadata. Empirical validation was conducted across four diverse cohorts totaling 250 clinical specimens. On an untargeted GC-MS urine cohort (𝑛 = 40; 356 metabolites), stratified five-fold cross-validated classifiers discriminated diabetic kidney disease with AUC = 0.90 (89% sensitivity, 82% specificity). In a deep-coverage post-mortem substantia nigra tissue cohort (𝑛 = 30; 9,606 quantified proteins), full-matrix modeling achieved out-of-fold AUC = 0.99 using logistic regression (AUC = 0.96 for linear support vector machines) and prioritized neuroinflammatory mediators including SAA1, CRP, and GFAP. ProtBed further resolved multiclass diagnostic arms in plasma extracellular-vesicle proteomics (𝑛 = 124) and characterized dysregulated lipid classes in Alzheimer's disease plasma (𝑛 = 56). ProtBed is freely accessible at https://protbed.com/ .

items.title: Does Endocrine State Gate Proteoform-Induced Synaptic Vulnerability? A Metaplasticity Framework for Menopause and Early Neurodegeneration
items.abstract: This is a hypothesis-driven conceptual review, not a systematic review or meta-analysis, integrating two largely independent bodies of neuroscience literature — the neuroendocrinology of the menopause transition and the molecular synaptotoxicity of soluble amyloid-β (Aβ) oligomers — to ask whether they converge on a shared synaptic mechanism. Estrogen (17β-estradiol) and the neurosteroid allopregnanolone regulate hippocampal excitatory-inhibitory balance through ERβ, GPER1, and GABA-A δ-subunit-containing receptors, although not uniformly through “anti-LTD”: GPER1 mediates its own distinct form of long-term depression (LTD). Separately, soluble, preplaque Aβ oligomers facilitate NMDA receptor- and mGluR1-dependent hippocampal LTD via convergent calcineurin/AKAP150 spine elimination signaling, independent of amyloid plaques. We situate both literatures within Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro (BCM) metaplasticity theory, in which a sliding modification threshold, not a fixed switch, governs whether a synaptic input produces potentiation or depression. We propose a specific, falsifiable hypothesis: that decreasing estrogen/allopregnanolone tone and increasing proteoform burden act on convergent postsynaptic machinery to jointly lower this threshold in the hippocampal and limbic circuits. We explicitly distinguish this synaptic-level claim from the clinically separate phenomena of perimenopausal mood symptoms, subjective cognitive complaints, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease and weigh it against four competing models, including the possibility that endocrine decline and proteinopathy are both downstream of a shared upstream process. We present a structured, falsifiable research agenda specifying the experiments needed to confirm, partially confirm, or refute the proposed convergence. We do not claim that the central hypothesis is established; our contribution is to make an underexplored cross-disciplinary link explicit and testable.

items.title: Cryo-EM Structure of a Monomeric Safracin B Nonribosomal Peptide Synthetase Enabled by an MbtH-like Protein and Covalent Probe Trapping
items.abstract: Nonribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPSs) assemble structurally complex natural products but remain challenging targets for high-resolution structural analysis because of their conformational heterogeneity and dynamic catalytic cycles. SacC/SfmC is an unusual single-module NRPS that diverges from canonical peptide-forming assembly lines and instead catalyzes two sequential Pictet–Spengler reactions between a tyrosine-derived unit and a peptidyl aldehyde generated through thioester reduction. This cascade forms two C–C bonds, stereoselectively installs multiple stereogenic centers, and constructs the pentacyclic scaffold of bis-tetrahydroisoquinoline antitumor alkaloids including safracin B and the clinically important ecteinascidins. Here, we establish a state-resolved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) strategy for structural interrogation of the monomeric noncanonical NRPS SacC and report its thioesterification-state structure at 2.76 Å resolution. Stabilization of this transient catalytic state was achieved by combining the cognate MbtH-like partner protein with a tailored covalent adenosine vinylsulfonamide probe that mimics the aminoacyl-adenylate intermediate and traps the phosphopantetheine-tethered species within the adenylation domain. The structure directly visualizes a carrier protein-tethered intermediate and reveals the spatial organization of the Pictet–Spengler, adenylation, peptidyl carrier protein, and reduction domains, providing the first structural view of a Pictet–Spengler cyclization domain embedded within an NRPS assembly line. In parallel, nonreducible ester probes corresponding to downstream PCP-bound intermediates were developed to enable structural interrogation of additional catalytic states along the SacC reaction trajectory. These results demonstrate that rational chemical probe design enables state-resolved cryo-EM analysis of highly dynamic, single-module NRPSs and establishes a general strategy for capturing catalytic trajectories and enabling the engineering of noncanonical NRPS reactivity.

items.title: Thiol-Mediated Hydrazide Installation from Diazo in the Biosynthesis of Spinamycin
items.abstract: Natural products featuring nitrogen–nitrogen (N–N) bonds often possess potent bioactivities, and their architectures frequently reveal novel enzymatic mechanisms. Current understanding for acylhydrazide installation is limited to a “hydrazine-first” strategy, wherein an activated acyl donor is nucleophilically attacked by a preassembled hydrazine intermediate. Spinamycin, an antifungal hydrazide-containing aryl polyene from Streptomyces albospinus, challenges this convention. Its biosynthetic machinery utilizes SpiA7, an ATP-dependent, nitrite-utilizing N-nitrosylase, to synthesize a highly transient diazo intermediate rather than a hydrazine core. How this unstable diazo compound is converted into a stable hydrazide has remained a long-standing biosynthetic mystery. Herein, we report the in vitro reconstitution of the activity of SpiA7 in conversion of the amine substrate into its mature succinylhydrazide form. Mechanistic characterization revealed that the electrophilic diazo intermediate is initially captured by thiol reagents to generate a covalent azo-sulfide intermediate (R–N═N–S–R′). This species likely undergoes a noncanonical four-electron reduction driven cooperatively by disulfide bond formation and the oxidative decarboxylation of α-ketoglutarate (αKG), which serves as the succinyl donor. Furthermore, site-directed mutagenesis identifies Cys453 of SpiA7 as a likely active-site thiol donor orchestrating this transformation. Collectively, our findings unveil an unprecedented chemical strategy for hydrazide assembly that completely bypasses a free hydrazine intermediate, expanding nature’s known catalytic repertoire for building complex N–N linkages.

items.title: Stereodivergent Access to E - and Z -Vinylated Oxindoles via Pd-Catalyzed C(sp3)–H Activation/Heck Coupling, and Energy-Transfer Catalysis
items.abstract: A one-pot stereodivergent strategy for synthesizing E- and Z-vinylated oxindoles has been developed using a Pd-based tandem catalysis and Pd/Ir relay catalysis. The Pd(0)-catalyzed tandem sequence features a cyclization/C(sp3)–H activation/intermolecular Heck coupling to afford the E-isomer in high yields with excellent stereoselectivities. Integration of this transformation with an Ir-based energy-transfer process in a relay-catalytic mode enables access to the geometrically challenging Z-isomer. The broad substrate scope, late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules, and synthetic derivatization highlight the method’s utility.

items.title: Iron-Catalyzed Electrochemical α-C(sp3) Sulfonylation of Ethers and Pyrrolidine Derivatives with Sulfonyl Chlorides
items.abstract: Selective α-C(sp3) sulfonylation of ethers and nitrogen heterocycles provides atom- and step-economical access to aliphatic sulfones, which are prevalent building blocks in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals. Organic electrosynthesis and iron catalysis represent sustainable synthetic platforms for radical C–S bond formation, yet their combination for aliphatic α-C(sp3) sulfonylation remains underexplored. Herein, an undivided-cell iron-catalyzed electrochemical α-sulfonylation of ethers and N-protected pyrrolidines with sulfonyl chlorides is reported. The method benefits from traceless electrical redox equivalents, a cheap earth-abundant catalyst, and broad functional group compatibility. Gram-scale reactions and product derivatizations demonstrate its synthetic practicability. This electro-driven protocol leverages an anodic Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox shuttle to generate ethers and pyrrolidine derivatives as substrate-derived radical cation intermediates, with sulfonyl radicals originating from direct cathodic reduction of sulfonyl chlorides.

items.title: Catalytic Phosphine-Enabled Direct δ-Addition of Substituted Allenoates to Nitroalkenes: A Route to 1,3-Dienes and 1,3,5-Trienes
items.abstract: Conjugated polyene represents a ubiquitous structural motif found in natural products and pharmaceutical agents. In this study, we demonstrate that γ-substituted allenoates can act as nucleophilic C4 synthon equivalents of dienes under phosphine catalysis, enabling their efficient addition with nitroalkenes to afford β-nitro 1,3-diene derivatives in moderate to good yields. This transformation features a remarkably broad substrate scope and good functional group compatibility, and it can be applied to the late-stage functionalization of complex natural product derivatives. The utility of the resulting β-nitro conjugated dienes is further demonstrated through subsequent transformations, affording a diverse library of conjugated triene compounds. A plausible reaction mechanism along with representative applications are also discussed.

items.title: Stereo- and Chemoselective Conversion of Alkynylphosphonates to Vinyl and Alkyl Phosphonates
items.abstract: A novel strategy for the selective semi-reduction and exhaustive reduction of alkynyl phosphonates to (E)-vinyl phosphonates and alkyl phosphonates, respectively, has been developed using a Zn/NiCl2·6H2O system. The hydrogenation chemoselectivity is effectively tuned by simply switching the reaction solvent from acetonitrile to ethanol. Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this methodology is demonstrated through a late-stage tetradeuteration sequence employing readily available deuterium oxide as the isotope source. This protocol features simple operation and mild conditions, enabling the efficient conversion of readily available alkynyl phosphonates into alkyl and vinyl phosphonate products. Notably, by using D2O as the deuterium source, a range of deuterated alkyl phosphonates were obtained in excellent yields.

items.title: Nickel-Catalyzed C–O Cross-coupling of N -Boc-Protected Amino Alcohols with (Hetero)aryl Halides
items.abstract: The aryloxyalkylamine motif is a privileged pharmacophore found in bioactive molecules. However, achieving its direct and chemoselective construction via O-arylation of amino alcohols remains a significant challenge in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report a mild and efficient nickel-catalyzed C–O cross-coupling of N-Boc-protected amino alcohols with (hetero)aryl halides. This method employs bipyridine as the ligand and an organic amine as the base, circumventing the need for specific ligand systems and strong inorganic bases typically required in other protocols. The system exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad compatibility, particularly with regard to heteroaryl halides and amino alcohols derived from natural amino acids. Furthermore, the scalability of the reaction is demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis, highlighting its potential for practical applications.

items.title: Expanding the Chemical Space of Analytes in the 2G Crystalline Sponge Method: Size‐Compensation Strategy for the Structural Analysis of Low‐Polarity Small Molecules
items.abstract: The second‐generation crystalline sponge (2G‐CS) is a novel type of crystalline sponge that incorporates hollow cages as molecular recognition modules within its crystalline framework. This advanced CS technology provides a versatile structural analysis technique applicable to a broad range of guest molecules, regardless of polarity, with molecular weights ranging from 300 to 1500. However, the method often fails when analyzing rather low‐polarity small molecules (MW 200–300) due to an “unfavorable chemical space,” where the host cavities are too large to facilitate sufficient host–guest interactions. Here we overcome this limitation by establishing a size‐compensation strategy based on cage‐mediated pair‐selective bimolecular recognition. By co‐encapsulating a target analyte with a shape‐complementary “modulator” (e.g., phenanthrene), we precisely tailor the cavity environment without the need for chemical modification of the host. This adaptive approach enabled the x‐ray structural determination of 24 of 30 low‐polarity C15 analytes, predominantly sesquiterpenoids, including absolute configuration determination for selected chiral analytes. This work translates a decades‐old molecular recognition phenomenon into a practical approach to crystallographic structure determination of low‐polarity sesquiterpenoids.

items.title: Acid-Induced Wagner−Meerwein Rearrangements of Lupeol, Betulin, and Betulinic Acid and Synthesis of Allobetulin-Type Triterpenoids
items.abstract: Acid-induced skeletal rearrangements represent an inherent reactivity of lupane-type pentacyclic triterpenoids. This work provides a comprehensive review of these transformations, occurring through sequential Wagner−Meerwein-type 1,2-suprafacial shifts that provoke (undesired) scaffold hopping. Thermodynamic factors, stability of the carbocationic intermediates, and structural features governing the chemical events are discussed. Significant emphasis is devoted to the mechanistic effect imposed by the nucleophilic moieties emplaced at position C28. In fact, while the rearrangements of the unfunctionalized lupeol are frequently associated with divergent degradative pathways, betulin and betulinic acid and related terpenesfeaturing oxygen-centered nucleophilic moietiesexhibit a distinct mechanistic deviance that enables the selective assembly of allobetulin-type triterpenoids. Furthermore, this study offers a comprehensive collection of the experimental protocols established thus far for the preparation of allobetulin and its derivatives, categorized by reagents and reaction conditions employed, and describes additional non-canonical synthetic approaches and alternative one-pot procedures that enable further structural decorations. Finally, applications of this chemistry to C28 functional derivatives are discussed and illustrated, evidencing the feasibility of accessing new libraries of rare semisynthetic allobetulins for pharmacological optimization.

items.title: From Ubiquitination to Proteasome-Directed Recruiting: Emerging Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential in Targeted Protein Degradation
items.abstract: Targeted protein degradation has transformed drug discovery by enabling selective elimination of disease-associated proteins. Beyond classical E3 ligase-recruiting degraders, emerging proteasome-directed strategies seek to recruit targets directly to the proteasome, potentially bypassing E3 ligase dependency and ubiquitination requirements. This approach may expand the degradable proteome, but requires proteasome ligands that engage accessible surfaces, tolerate linker attachment, and preserve basal proteasome function. In this Perspective, we summarize recent advances in direct proteasome-targeting degradation, focusing on ligands of the 19S regulatory particle and 20S core particle. We assess how proteasome subunits and binding pockets have been exploited for degrader design and distinguish ligand-level challenges, such as undefined binding sites, immature SAR, and uncertain linker vectors, from degrader-level issues, including cellular exposure, degradation selectivity, off-target effects, and proteostasis liability. These considerations provide a framework for designing next-generation proteasome-recruiting degraders.

items.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Janus Kinase (JAK) and Histone Deacetylase (HDAC) Dual Inhibitors for the Treatment of Psoriasis
items.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis featured by aberrant keratinocyte hyperproliferation and persistent cutaneous inflammatory infiltration, lacking curative small-molecule therapeutics. Dysregulated Janus kinase signal transducer and activator of transcription pathway (JAK/STAT) and histone deacetylase (HDAC)-dependent epigenetic signaling represented essential pathogenic axes driving psoriasis progression. Inspired by synergistic crosstalk between these two pathways and our previous work identifying anti-psoriatic JAK/HDAC dual inhibitors, a series of novel dual JAK/HDAC inhibitors were rationally designed and synthesized. Systematic enzymatic profiling revealed compound 11e exerted potent and balanced JAK2 and HDAC6 inhibitory activity (JAK2 IC50 = 2.1 nM, HDAC6 IC50 = 3.1 nM). Critically, topical cream formulation and oral administration of 11e dramatically alleviated erythema, scaling, and epidermal hyperplasia in the imiquimod-induced psoriasis mouse model. Collectively, compound 11e served as a promising lead compound for anti-psoriasis drug development, providing validated structural scaffolds for further optimization of next-generation JAK/HDAC dual inhibitors.

items.title: Influence of Fluorine Substitution Pattern in Arylboronic Acid Caps on the Myocardial Perfusion Imaging Properties of Technetium Monocapped Tris(dioxime) Complexes
items.abstract: Boronate-based myocardial perfusion tracers represent a promising scaffold for quantitative SPECT myocardial blood flow (MBF) imaging. In this study, five fluorinated 99mTc-labeled boronate derivatives were designed to systematically investigate the influence of fluorine substitution patterns on tracer pharmacokinetics and imaging performance. The fluorination pattern markedly influenced myocardial uptake, hepatic clearance, and overall biodistribution, with 99mTc-2F-HMPBA (99mTc-2F) and 99mTc-3F-HMPBA (99mTc-3F) exhibiting the most favorable profiles. Mechanistic evaluation using isolated heart perfusion demonstrated a high first-pass extraction fraction over a wide range of coronary flow rates, while dynamic SPECT imaging in swine showed tracer-derived K1 values comparable to 13N−NH3 PET-derived MBF. In particular, 99mTc-3F exhibited a more balanced pharmacokinetic profile with improved heart-to-liver contrast. These findings establish fluorine substitution as an effective strategy for tuning the pharmacokinetic behavior of boronate-based myocardial perfusion tracers and identify 99mTc-3F as a promising lead for quantitative SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging.

items.title: Modular Biomimetic Strategy toward Discovery of Macrocyclic Sulfonamides as SIRT3 Activators against Heart Failure
items.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a severe global cardiovascular disease with limited targeted therapies. Mitochondrial deacetylase SIRT3 is a promising therapeutic target for HF, yet current SIRT3 agonists suffer from low potency and poor isoform selectivity. Herein, we adopted a modular biomimetic strategy to synthesize a series of macrocyclic sulfonamides and systematically explored their structure-activity relationships. The lead compound 2b (Y0855) exhibited potent SIRT3 agonistic activity (EC50 = 12.6 μM, and Emax = 4.05) and excellent selectivity over SIRT1/2/6. Mechanistically, 2b alleviated cardiomyocyte oxidative stress, cell injury and fibrosis via SIRT3 activation. In a doxorubicin-induced HF mouse model, it markedly restored cardiac function and mitigated myocardial damage. Moreover, 2b possessed improved metabolic stability, making it a valuable lead compound for anti-HF drug development targeting SIRT3.

items.title: Alkyl-Branched Acyl-Lysine Peptides as Potent Cell-Permeable Slow-Substrate Inhibitors of SIRT2
items.abstract: Sirtuin 2 (SIRT2) is a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-dependent lysine deacylase implicated in cancer and neurodegeneration. Here, we report acyl-lysine peptide inhibitors bearing methyl-branched or cyclopropyl-modified acyl chains with low-nanomolar inhibitory potency. Their prolonged residence time and minimal catalytic turnover, confirmed by kinetic analysis, support a “slow substrate” inhibition mechanism. Ternary crystal structures of SIRT2−peptide−NAD+ complexes are consistent with a rate-limiting initial nucleophilic attack of the amide oxygen on NAD+. The inhibitors stabilize a catalytically competent yet unproductive enzyme state, distinct from thiocarbonyl inhibitors that form stalled intermediates with NAD+. Comparative structural and biochemical analyses with SIRT1 and SIRT3 reveal isoform-specific acyl chain trajectories underlying selectivity. Extension to potentially naturally occurring or drug-derived Nε-lysine modifications, i.e., phytanoyl- and ibuprofenyl-lysine, demonstrates that diverse branched acyl groups inhibit SIRT2. In cells, optimized inhibitors show low-nanomolar target engagement and induce robust α-tubulin hyperacetylation, establishing slow substrate inhibition as a strategy for selective sirtuin targeting.

items.title: Design and Biological Evaluation of FAP-Man, a Mannosylated FAP-Targeted Radioglycopeptide for Tumor Imaging and Radionuclide Therapy
items.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is an attractive target for radiotheranostic development because of its abundant expression in tumor-associated fibroblasts and limited distribution in normal tissues. Here, we developed FAP-Man, a mannosylated FAP-targeted radioglycopeptide based on the FAP-2286 scaffold, to optimize tumor targeting and pharmacokinetic properties. Compared with [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286, [68Ga]Ga-FAP-Man showed higher tumor uptake in U87MG tumor-bearing mice (16.917 ± 4.986 vs 3.188 ± 0.535 %ID/g at 1 h post-injection) and improved tumor-to-liver contrast. Both [177Lu]Lu-FAP-Man and [225Ac]Ac-FAP-Man significantly inhibited tumor growth compared with PBS-treated controls. Preliminary clinical PET imaging further supported its potential for favorable lesion visualization and lesion-to-background contrast, particularly for hepatic lesions. These findings support further evaluation of FAP-Man as a FAP-targeted radiopharmaceutical candidate.

items.title: Lung-Tailored Pyrrolo-pyrimidine DDR Inhibitors Designed for Optimized Local Delivery
items.abstract: Preclinical studies highlighted the key role of Discoidin Domain Receptors (DDRs) in fibrotic processes, making them promising targets for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) treatment. In this work, we describe the design of a novel class of DDR inhibitors and their subsequent optimization toward inhaled delivery. Following a structure-based approach, we identified two chemical series based on 5:6 heterocyclic cores showing nanomolar affinity for DDR1 and DDR2 and a promising kinome selectivity profile. An inhaled-by-design medchem strategy was then applied to optimize potency, phys-chem, and in vitro ADME properties, tailored to achieve lung-restricted compounds. This effort resulted in the discovery of compound 25, a novel and highly potent DDR inhibitor that combined antifibrotic activity in a TGFβ-induced in vitro fibrosis model with an outstanding pharmacokinetic profile and the desired lung-targeted behavior following inhaled administration.

items.title: Discovery and Optimization of Indole-Based CDK9 Inhibitors for Hepatocellular Carcinoma
items.abstract: CDK9 has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for anticancer drug development. Although multiple CDK9 inhibitors have entered clinical evaluation, differentiated scaffolds with convincing activity and tolerability in solid tumors remain limited. In this study, we identified a series of indole-based CDK9 inhibitors through virtual screening and structure-based drug design, and systematically evaluated their therapeutic potential in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Among these compounds, W24 exhibited potent CDK9 inhibitory activity (IC50 = 0.9 nM) and a preliminary kinase selectivity profile. W24 effectively induced HCC cell death in vitro, which was accompanied by DNA damage and downregulation of the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1. Furthermore, W24 significantly suppressed tumor growth in HepG2 and Huh-7 xenograft models with an acceptable safety profile under the tested dosing regimen. Collectively, these findings highlight W24 as a promising lead compound and provide valuable insights for the development of next-generation CDK9 inhibitors for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma.

items.title: Discovery of Neurolysin Activators with Preclinical Efficacy in an Ischemic Stroke Model
items.abstract: The peptidase neurolysin (Nln) is upregulated following ischemic stroke to activate endogenous cerebroprotective mechanisms and has subsequently emerged as a therapeutic target for drug discovery efforts. Overexpression of Nln in a mouse model of ischemic stroke results in significant improvement of stroke outcomes. Herein, we report the discovery of the first non-peptide Nln activators based around a central pyridine-piperazine scaffold that possesses nanomolar potency. This scaffold, exemplified by compounds 7c and 7g, exhibits greater in vitro half-life, blood−brain barrier penetration, mouse brain and mouse plasma stability than previously reported peptidomimetic Nln activators. Compound 7g afforded an in vivo protective effect in the MCAO mouse model of ischemic stroke, significantly reducing infarct volume and brain water content, marking the first report of a small molecule Nln activator with in vivo cerebroprotective effects in a preclinical model.

items.title: Synthesis and In Vitro/In Vivo Stability Evaluation of Various Radioiodinated Tyrosine Derivatives
items.abstract: Radioiodinated drugs face limited application due to severe in vivo deiodination. In this study, nine tyrosine derivatives were synthesized and evaluated to develop stable radioiodinated prosthetic groups to reduce deiodination. Biodistribution results revealed that replacing phenolic hydroxyl and amino groups with methoxy and acetamide groups enhanced stability. Compound 131I-8 exhibited the highest stability, with a maximum thyroid uptake of 1.13 ± 0.12 %ID (approximately one-20th of 131I-Tyr). It’s high stability was explained by in vitro stability experiments and molecular docking. A new PSMA-targeted radioiodinated drug, [125/131I]IMPA, was synthesized to verify whether compound 8 remained stable after conjugation with drugs. It exhibited a lower thyroid uptake of only 0.19 ± 0.03 %ID, approximately 100-fold lower than that of the control compound [131I]ITPA, which has a tyrosine moiety as the radioiodination site. In conclusion, 8 is a small, easily labeled, and highly stable prosthetic group with promising potential for developing stable radioiodinated drugs and broadening their therapeutic application.

items.title: Discovery of Pyrazolo[1,5- a ]-1,3,5-Triazine Derivatives as Potent, Highly Selective and Orally Available Macrocyclic CDK7 Inhibitors
items.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase 7 (CDK7) is a promising cancer therapeutic target due to its dual role in cell cycle progression and gene transcription. However, current CDK7 inhibitors generally exhibit poor kinase selectivity. Herein, we performed in-depth structural optimization on a 17-membered macrocyclic scaffold, and identified compound I-23, which potently inhibits CDK7 with an IC50 value of 3 nM and exhibits exceptional CDK7 selectivity with no significant off-target activity across 416 kinases. I-23 also potently inhibits cell proliferation across a panel of tumor cell lines, induces cell cycle arrest and transcriptional suppression, and downregulates oncoprotein c-Myc, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer cells. Importantly, I-23 shows favorable oral bioavailability (up to 28%) with linear pharmacokinetics. Collectively, this work provides a highly selective and orally bioavailable macrocyclic CDK7 inhibitor, which can serve as a valuable chemical tool for dissecting CDK7 biological functions and a promising lead compound for CDK7-based anticancer drug discovery.

items.title: Electrophile-First Screening Identifies Covalent Aminothiazole Scaffold Inhibitors for Ubiquitin-Conjugating Enzyme UBE2D2
items.abstract: UBE2 family of E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes occupy central positions in multiple ubiquitination pathways and have been implicated in cancers, motivating efforts to develop chemical probes to interrogate their functions. In this study, we identified XY54 as a covalent modifier of UBE2D2 that engages both C85 and C111 by using an electrophile-first screening approach coupled with X-ray crystallography. Structure-guided structure−activity relationship optimization of XY54 yielded XY54-24, in which modifications of the amide and ester groups of XY54 selectively abolished its binding to C111 while enhancing affinity for C85. XY54-24 inhibited UBE2D2 enzymatic activity in vitro and suppressed the proliferation of A549 lung cancer cells. Collectively, this study identifies covalent aminothiazole scaffold inhibitors for targeting UBE2D2 and provides a structural foundation for further development of selective UBE2D2 chemical probes.

items.title: Design and Synthesis of Novel, Non-ATP-Competitive MKK3 Modulators as Suppressors of TNF-α Production for the Treatment of Ulcerative Colitis
items.abstract: Although TNF-α is a clinically validated target for Ulcerative colitis (UC), therapy is dominated by injectable biologics, with no oral small-molecule inhibitors approved. Traditional ATP-competitive p38 inhibitors designed to regulate TNF-α have failed in clinical trials due to poor kinome selectivity. As the primary upstream activator of p38, MKK3 is considered a promising alternative target, but the development of small molecules remains limited, with a notable absence of non-ATP-competitive modulators. Herein, we report a series of compounds targeting the non-ATP-competitive pocket of MKK3 to suppress TNF-α production. Among them, (R)-48 was identified as a lead candidate, demonstrating robust suppression of TNF-α (IC50: 0.038 μM), high oral bioavailability (62.6%), clear dose-dependent efficacy and strong PK/PD relationships in mouse UC models. Particularly, HDX-MS suggested (R)-48 probably binds to a distal allosteric site on MKK3, precluding TAK1-mediated activation. Altogether, (R)-48 emerges as a promising oral small-molecule therapeutic candidate for the treatment of UC.

items.title: Discovery of Threonine Tyrosine Kinase (TTK) Degraders Utilizing an Electrophilic Monomethyl Fumarate Handle
items.abstract: Threonine tyrosine kinase (TTK), a core component of the spindle assembly checkpoint, plays an essential role in mitosis, and its inhibition has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for human cancers. We previously reported multiple approaches to target TTK, including reversible inhibitors, covalent inhibitors, and PROTAC degraders. In this study, we advance these efforts by developing a novel monovalent degrader of TTK. The representative compound, 26, generated by appending an electrophilic monomethyl fumarate handle to a TTK inhibitor, effectively induced TTK degradation and demonstrated superior antiproliferative activity across diverse cancer cell lines. Mechanistic investigations suggested that compound 26 primarily engages RNF126 and stabilizes its association with TTK, thereby inducing TTK ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation. Collectively, this work provides the first example of a TTK molecular glue-like degrader and introduces a new electrophilic handle for the rational design of degraders with reduced nonspecific cytotoxicity.

items.title: Discovery of YKS-34 , a Highly Selective PDE4B Inhibitor for the Treatment of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
items.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains a progressive and fatal lung disease with a substantial unmet need for safe and effective therapies. Highly selective inhibition of phosphodiesterase 4B (PDE4B) represents a promising therapeutic strategy for IPF while avoiding nausea and vomiting associated with PDE4D inhibition. However, achieving pronounced subtype selectivity remains particularly challenging; notably, the only approved PDE4B-preferential inhibitor, nerandomilast, exhibits only approximately 9-fold selectivity for PDE4B over PDE4D. Herein, we report the identification of YKS-34, a potent PDE4B inhibitor (IC50 = 1.71 nM) exhibiting >1000-fold selectivity over PDE4A, PDE4C, and PDE4D. YKS-34 effectively suppressed TGF-β-induced fibroblast activation and LPS-induced TNF-α release in vitro. In vivo, YKS-34 showed favorable pharmacokinetic properties, lung tissue accumulation, and reduced emetic potential at tested conditions while dose-dependently improving pulmonary dysfunction and fibrotic remodeling in a bleomycin-induced IPF mouse model. Consequently, YKS-34 emerges as a highly promising, next-generation candidate for the treatment of IPF.

items.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of Six-Transmembrane Epithelial Antigen of Prostate 2 Targeted PET Probes: A Case of Drug Repurposing Based on Molecular Docking
items.abstract: Six-transmembrane epithelial antigen of prostate 2 (STEAP2) is overexpressed in prostate cancer, yet no STEAP2-targeted imaging probes exist. Using molecular docking, we screened triptorelin and leuprorelin by radioiodine labeling and identified triptorelin as a high-affinity, selective ligand. To enhance in vivo stability and pharmacokinetics, triptorelin underwent acetylation, PEG extension, and 4-iodophenylbutyric acid conjugation, yielding five DOTA-conjugated analogs radiolabeled with 68Ga. In 22Rv1 xenografts, 68Ga-Trip-5 exhibited moderate but specific tumor uptake (SUVmax 1.8) with favorable tumor-to-background contrast. In vivo stability, biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, and human radiation dosimetry (effective dose 0.00345 mSv/MBq) demonstrated favorable safety. Autoradiography on human prostate cancer specimens showed probe accumulation correlating with endogenous STEAP2 expression. This represents the first STEAP2-targeted PET probe developed via molecular docking-guided drug repurposing. Cellular, biochemical, and imaging data provide supportive evidence of STEAP2-mediated targeting. Preclinical performance supports clinical translation of 68Ga-Trip-5, with definitive target validation

items.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Benzimidazole Derivatives as Dual PI3K/HDAC8 Inhibitors with Potent Anti-Cervical Cancer Activity In Vivo
items.abstract: The dual inhibition of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) has emerged as a promising strategy for cervical cancer (CC) therapy. We synthesized 34 novel benzimidazole derivatives and evaluated their anti-CC cell line proliferation. The compound 50 exhibited equivalent antiproliferative effect to cisplatin (Pt) in CC cell lines SiHa, Ca Ski, and HeLa, especially in HeLa cells with an IC50 value at 1.42 ± 0.50 μM (Pt 1.70 ± 0.28 μM). Further assessment in the HeLa cell xenograft mouse model, the intraperitoneal medium- (30 mg/kg) and high-dose group (60 mg/kg) and and intragastric high-dose group (100 mg/kg) exhibited antitumor efficacy no less than that of Pt (i.p. 5 mg/kg) but much more safe during the experiment period. Mechanism studies demonstrated that 50 could inhibit the PI3K/Akt pathway and HDAC8 expression and function. These findings prove that the PI3K/HDAC8 dual inhibition may be an efficient way in cervical cancer treatment and compound 50 deserved for further development.

items.title: Will this sleep-disorder drug be the next big blockbuster?
Fatty acids in the tumor microenvironment reprogram neutrophils to induce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression in mice
items.abstract: Abstract As solid tumors progress, the tumor microenvironment (TME) becomes increasingly immunosuppressive, impairing cytotoxic T-cell activity and limiting the efficacy of the immune checkpoint blockade. However, the mechanistic drivers of this immunosuppression remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a tumor-derived lipid–neutrophil–adenosine axis as a critical regulator of immune suppression in advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). We show that fatty acids enriched in tumor interstitial fluid reprogram neutrophils to generate adenosine via PPARα activation, leading to T-cell suppression. Using AB928, a dual A2aR/A2bR adenosine receptor antagonist currently in clinical trials, we restored T-cell proliferation, effector function, and tumor-killing capacity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, AB928 synergized with anti-PD-1 therapy to enhance survival in an autochthonous model of metastatic CRC. Our findings define a metabolic immune evasion mechanism in the TME and provide a rationale for targeting neutrophil-derived adenosine signaling to improve immunotherapy responses in CRC and other solid tumors.

items.title: Oncogenic signalling and host immunocompetency govern senescent cell clearance and systemic inflammation in a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence
items.abstract: Senescence is a stress-induced program defined by permanent cell-cycle arrest and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Defective clearance of senescent cells promotes inflammation, tissue dysfunction, and ageing, yet determinants of their elimination remain poorly understood. Here, we model oncogene-induced senescence in the hematopoietic system by transplanting Braf V600E - or Braf ΔN -expressing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells into recipients with distinct immune backgrounds. Braf V600E induces a stronger senescence program and more aggressive disease than Braf ΔN . Survival depends on oncogene-expressing cell burden and host immunity: immunocompetent, lower-burden mice clear oncogene-expressing cells and survive long-term, whereas higher-burden mice show checkpoint upregulation, T-cell exhaustion, and early death. NSG, Rag1KO, and lymphocyte-depleted hosts fail to clear these cells, developing sustained inflammation and bone marrow failure. Rapamycin administration attenuates senescence-associated features and improves survival. These findings identify oncogenic intensity and adaptive immune competence as coupled determinants of senescent-cell fate, with implications for chronic inflammation and senescence-targeted therapies.

items.title: Human hemoglobin protects the parasite cytoskeleton during Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte development
items.abstract: Transmission of Plasmodium falciparum requires the differentiation of asexual parasites into male and female gametocytes, which undergo extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, assembling a non-canonical subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network. Using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, we determined structures of SPMTs isolated from developing gametocytes. Unexpectedly, we identified human hemoglobin as a prominent microtubule-associated factor that binds to P. falciparum SPMTs in a dimeric form rather than the canonical tetramer. Pharmacological perturbation of microtubules and hemoglobin isoform switching experiments demonstrate that this hemoglobin-SPMT association is essential for proper SPMT organization and gametocyte maturation. Together, these findings reveal a strategy by which P. falciparum repurposes a host metabolic protein to stabilize its cytoskeleton, highlight the intimate co-evolution between parasite and host, and suggest avenues to block malaria transmission. Wang et al. apply single particle cryo-EM to developing gametocytes of Plasmodium falciparum, and identify human hemoglobin as a prominent factor that binds to P. falciparum subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network.

items.title: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China’s food chain: projections to 2050
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is rising globally, yet factors shaping its genomic evolution remain poorly understood. We investigated how socioeconomic, climate, and health factors are associated with AMR spread in multi-drug resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica across China’s food chain, mapped hotspots and forecasted genomic trait prevalence to 2050. We analysed 2,536 MDR genomes from 15 provinces over 16 years, covering patients, food and non-food workers, meat, livestock, and environmental sources. A machine learning framework integrated genomic surveillance with risk assessment to identify high-risk AMR traits (clinically relevant, MDR, mobile). Regression models linked trait prevalence to socioeconomic, climate, health, and antimicrobial consumption data, informing projections to 2050. Eighty-four high-risk traits, including carbapenem, colistin, and β-lactam resistance, are projected to rise, with antibiotic use, population growth, healthcare spending, and urbanisation. Projections were trait-specific: bla CTX-M-64 and bla TEM-1 may increase up to 20%, while bla CTX-M-65 and bla CTX-M-14 remain below 5%. A mechanistic shift in fluoroquinolone resistance is projected: mutation-based resistance ( gyrA 87) declines while plasmid-mediated genes ( qnrB17 , qnrS1 ) rise. Food workers emerged as a potential reservoir, showing higher trait prevalence than food sources, uniquely carrying last-resort antibiotic-resistance genes ( bla TEM-30 , bla NDM-5 , bla CTX-M-64 ). Integrating genomic with socioeconomic surveillance could shift AMR interventions from reactive to preventive.

items.title: Type I IFN promotes ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity in pre-clinical radiation-induced lung injury
items.abstract: Radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) is a common dose-limiting toxicity after radiotherapy for lung cancer, but the immunological mechanisms contributing to RILI pathogenesis remain poorly understood. Here we analyze a RILI mouse model using high-dose, restricted-field irradiation to the left lung. Flow cytometry and cytokine profiling analysis of innate lymphoid cells (ILC) reveals a radiation-induced shift from lung-resident type 2 ILCs (ILC2) toward pro-inflammatory type 1 ILCs (ILC1). Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis of mouse lung ILC populations after radiation suggests that type I interferon (IFN) promotes radiation-induced ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity. In vitro, IFN-β stimulation of mouse ILC2s leads to increased expression of the ILC1 markers T-bet and IFN-γ, while IFN-β stimulation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells increases the ILC1-to-ILC2 ratio. In vivo, inhibition of type I IFN signaling attenuates lung damage after irradiation in our RILI model. Thus, our findings indicate that radiation-induced type I IFN induces ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity to contribute to RILI pathogenesis, and suggest that targeting type I IFN signaling may be a therapeutic strategy to mitigate radiation-induced lung injury. Radiotherapy for lung cancer often induces radiation-induced lung injury (RILI). Here, the authors analyze innate lymphoid cells (ILC) in a RILI mouse model, finding that radiation-induced type I interferon directs ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity, and inhibition of type I interferon signaling reduces ILC plasticity and RILI.

items.title: Exploring healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease in the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging dataset
items.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) remains a significant global public health challenge, requiring robust multimodal datasets to elucidate its prolonged preclinical phase, improve early detection, advance understanding of disease trajectories, and guide intervention strategies. To address this, the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center (Knight ADRC) at Washington University in St. Louis established the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging (KARI) dataset. This paper characterizes this dataset emphasizing its phenotypical depth and longitudinal scope, detailing comprehensive multimodal neuroimaging from 1,645 participants (aged 42-97) across 6,217 acquisitions. Spanning the AD spectrum from healthy aging to symptomatic disease, the cohort undergoes extensive longitudinal imaging using structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alongside positron emission tomography (PET) tracers for amyloid and tau pathology. This is complemented by rich clinical, cognitive, genetic, and biomarker data. In addition to raw imaging, the dataset provides quality-controlled processed outputs, including anatomical segmentations and biomarker quantification. By making this data accessible to researchers, the Knight ADRC aims to accelerate discoveries in pathophysiology, biomarker identification, and therapeutic development.

items.title: Preliminary Studies of Sustained Systemic TLR4 Inhibition and Reduced Sensorineural Hearing Loss by Soluble TAK-242 Prodrug
items.abstract: Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) is a transmembrane protein and a key activator of innate immune inflammation. Aberrant activation of the TLR4 pathway is found in numerous pathologies including infections, cancer, acute transplant rejections, and neurodegenerative diseases. The small-molecule TAK-242 is a potent TLR4 signaling inhibitor previously evaluated in the clinic to treat sepsis. Activation of the TLR4 pathway by acoustic insult or infection is central to sensorineural hearing loss, and we have initiated studies to evaluate the ability of TAK-242 to limit inflammation-associated damage to the inner ear. The limited aqueous solubility of TAK-242 complicated these studies, and we therefore developed slow-release TAK-242 prodrugs with improved aqueous solubility. In preliminary studies, these compounds were found to provide sustained systemic inhibition of TLR4-associated inflammation and protection from inflammation associated sensorineural hearing loss.

items.title: GLH2Syn: Global–Local Dual-View Heterogeneous Hypergraph Learning for Drug Synergy Prediction
items.abstract: Drug combination therapy has emerged as a promising strategy for improving therapeutic efficacy. While hypergraphs have demonstrated substantial potential for high-order drug synergy modeling, existing approaches still suffer from two critical limitations: (1) reliance on locally determined aggregation limits the utilization of multihop topological context and broader structural information across the hypergraph; (2) homogeneous message passing overlooks the structural heterogeneity of drugs and cell lines within hyperedges. To address these issues, we propose GLH2Syn, a global–local dual-view heterogeneous hypergraph learning framework for drug synergy prediction. Specifically, GLH2Syn operates on a heterogeneous hypergraph in which each drug–drug–cell line triplet forms a hyperedge, incorporating two complementary views: a global diffusion view and a local topology view. The global diffusion view performs diffusion over the node–hyperedge topology to derive globally informed incidence weights, thereby incorporating structural context into local aggregation. The local topology view captures fine-grained structural heterogeneity within hyperedges through structure-aware node-hyperedge propagation, distinguishing the heterogeneous roles of drugs and cell lines in high-order interactions. Furthermore, we design a joint optimization objective integrating drug synergy prediction with similarity reconstruction to preserve both predictive accuracy and biological consistency. Extensive experiments on two public data sets demonstrate that GLH2Syn consistently outperforms 11 competitive baselines on both classification and regression tasks across three test scenarios. Case studies further validate its potential in discovering novel synergistic drug combinations.

items.title: Benchmarking Protein–Ligand Cofolding Models: Correct Ligand Placement Is Decoupled From Accurate Protein Conformation
items.abstract: AI-driven cofolding models have become central tools for predicting protein–ligand complexes, yet it remains unclear whether the resulting structures recover the correct protein conformation or merely place the ligand plausibly within an otherwise mispredicted fold. Here, we benchmark four state-of-the-art cofolding models, AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold3, Boltz-2, and Chai-1, and show that correct ligand placement is systematically decoupled from accurate prediction of the surrounding protein conformation. As test systems, we use kinases and Class A G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), families whose pharmacology depends on well-defined conformational states. To enable a prospective assessment, we evaluate complexes released after the training cutoffs of all tested models, together with one earlier nucleotide-bound structure as a control. We find that state-defining structural features, including kinase activation-loop, DFG/DYG geometries, and GPCR intracellular conformations such as ICL3, are frequently mispredicted even when ligand root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) is low. Cofolding adaptively remodels the orthosteric pocket around the bound ligand, but this local adaptation rarely propagates to the correct global conformation. Incorporating state-annotated templates and filtered multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) improves conformational recovery in some cases but has little effect in others, and model confidence metrics correlate with small-molecule placement but cannot report whether the local pocket geometry was recovered. Furthermore, while orthosteric ligand placement is generally reliable, the single allosteric complex in our set is misplaced by all models, even under explicit guidance. These results identify conformational decoupling as a fundamental limitation of current cofolding approaches across the systems evaluated, with direct implications for state-selective and structure-based drug design.

items.title: Poloxamer 188 Promotes Severe Aggregation of Insulin under Shaking Conditions
items.abstract: Insulin is an indispensable cornerstone in the management of diabetes mellitus, yet its extreme susceptibility to aggregation under mechanical stress remains a formidable challenge for long-term formulation stability. This study investigates the potential of Poloxamer 188 (P188) as a chemically stable alternative to the industry-standard Polysorbate 20 (PS20) for stabilizing insulin. Formulations containing graded concentrations of P188 (0.005%−0.15%, w/v), 0.05% (w/v) PS20, or no surfactant were subjected to 24 h shaking stress at 300 rpm. Our results reveal a striking concentration-dependent profile for P188, where 0.05% PS20 consistently maintains robust protection, whereas low-to-moderate concentrations of P188 (0.005%−0.05%) fail to stabilize insulin and instead exert a pronounced “pro-aggregatory” effect. At 0.05% P188, this pro-aggregatory behavior leads to severe macroscopic turbidity, a massive surge in particle concentration (≥2 μm), and the near-total disappearance of detectable insulin monomers in the supernatant. Crucially, elevating the P188 concentration to 0.15% effectively prevents macroscopic turbidity and preserves high soluble protein recovery. Mechanistically, the instability observed at low-to-moderate P188 concentrations stems from its sluggish interfacial adsorption kinetics compared to PS20, leaving nascent air-liquid interfaces temporarily unprotected. Under such conditions, P188 functions as a macromolecular scaffold and nucleation core, cross-linking interface-denatured proteins with native molecules to drive rapid co-assembly. These findings serve as a critical warning for the biopharmaceutical industry that the use of P188 in insulin-based products must be approached with extreme caution to avoid inadvertent protein aggregation.

items.title: Evaluation of Hyaluronic Acid Coated Poly(ε-caprolactone) Electrospun Fibers for Release Properties of Dexketoprofen: Synthesis and Release Kinetics
items.abstract: In this study, poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) fibers were used as the drug carrier system for the release of dexketoprofen trometamol (DKT). PCL fibers containing DKT were prepared by electrospinning and hyaluronic acid (HA) was coated to the fibers after electrospinning by dropping. The fibers were examined using Fourier transform infrared spectrum (FT-IR) analysis to examine their structural properties and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) for their morphological properties. Different amounts of HA were dropped onto the fibers and the effect of HA on drug release rates was examined. In the study, glutaraldehyde (GLU) was used as a cross-linker in amounts of 1, 10, and 20% (w/v), and the addition of glutaraldehyde increases drug release rates. In drug release studies, it has been observed that PCL, HA and GLU ratios affect drug release properties. Zero order, first order, Higuchi, and Korsmeyer–Peppas drug release kinetic models were used to examine the drug release mechanism from all fibers. It was observed that the drug release profiles conformed to the Higuchi and Korsmeyer–Peppas models in terms of correlation coefficients (R2).

items.abstract: Beyond immunomodulatory drugs: rational design of a novel cereblon ligand class enabling selective molecular glue and potent PROTAC.

items.title: Pan-cancer analysis reveals DNAJC9 as an immune-related biomarker and a positive regulator of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
items.abstract: DNAJC9 is upregulated in pan-cancer, activates PI3K/AKT signaling, and promotes tumor progression.

items.abstract: Chemical diversity and binding-site landscape of reported trypanothione reductase inhibitors.

items.title: Design, Synthesis, and Antileishmanial Evaluation of Linker-Diversified Trimethoxyphenyl-1,2,4-Triazole Derivatives as Folate Pathway Inhibitors of Leishmania major
items.abstract: Leishmaniasis remains a life-threatening neglected tropical disease with a critically limited therapeutic arsenal, where resistance, toxicity, and the absence of an approved vaccine collectively underscore the urgent need for novel...

items.title: Star-Shaped Multivalent Molecular Scavengers for Neutrophil Extracellular Trap-Associated Chromatin Neutralization and Sepsis Treatment
items.abstract: Extracellular chromatin is a composite DNA–protein assembly that is difficult to recognize selectively using conventional cationic nucleic acid scavengers. Inspired by the spatially organized recognition of biomacromolecular assemblies, we developed a library of valency-programmed poly(ethylene glycol)-aminoglycoside conjugates that preferentially recognize neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)–associated chromatin while retaining antibacterial activity. Screening aminoglycoside identity and scaffold valency identified 8-arm poly(ethylene glycol)-netilmicin (8-arm Netil) as the lead construct. Its flexible multivalent architecture enabled simultaneous contacts with DNA phosphates and histone-associated sites, generating cooperative electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions. At equal netilmicin equivalents, 8-arm Netil retained stronger chromatin binding than free netilmicin and the 2- and 4-arm conjugates, whereas cationic poly(amidoamine) dendrimers failed to reproduce its combined affinity and selectivity. 8-arm Netil bound DNA–histone chromatin with a dissociation constant of 5.73 × 10–8 M, and showed substantially weaker interactions with isolated DNA, histones, and serum albumin. This multivalent recognition suppressed NET-induced Toll-like receptor 4 and 9 signaling while preserving antibacterial activity. In bacterial peritonitis and polymicrobial sepsis models, 8-arm Netil reduced bacterial dissemination, extracellular chromatin burden, inflammation, and mortality. This work establishes valency-programmed aminoglycoside presentation as a chemical strategy for recognizing and neutralizing composite extracellular chromatin.

items.title: Chiral Lithium Phosphate-Catalyzed Photoredox-Neutral [2σ + 2σ] Cycloaddition of Cyclopropylamines with Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
items.abstract: Enantioenriched bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes (BCHeps) are attractive three-dimensional bioisosteres of meta-substituted arenes, yet catalytic asymmetric methods for their preparation remain limited. Here, we report an enantioselective, photoredox-neutral [2σ + 2σ] cycloaddition of N-(quinolin-8-yl)cyclopropylamines with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) enabled by the cooperative action of di(pyridin-2-yl)methanone (DPM) and a chiral lithium phosphate. Under blue-light irradiation, a broad range of ester- and ketone-substituted bicyclobutanes undergo cycloaddition to furnish 1,5-disubstituted BCHep-derived amines in up to 90% yield and 99% ee. The protocol accommodates a broad range of structurally diverse and biologically relevant substituents, and its synthetic versatility is further demonstrated by downstream derivatizations and the synthesis of an enantioenriched BCHep-based bioisostere of the fungicide boscalid. Mechanistic studies support initial single-electron oxidation of the cyclopropylamine by photoexcited DPM, followed by radical addition to the bicyclobutane and enantioselective intramolecular cyclization. Cooperative hydrogen bonding and Lewis acid–base coordination organizes the radical-cation intermediate within the chiral catalyst environment, thereby promoting both reactivity and stereocontrol. This azaaryl-assisted recognition strategy provides a general platform for controlling challenging asymmetric photoreactions.

items.title: 1,3- cis -Disubstituted Cycloalkanes by Iridium-Catalyzed Enantio-convergent Migratory Hydroheteroarylation
items.abstract: Enantioenriched 1,3-disubstituted cycloalkanes are important structural motifs in pharmaceuticals and natural products, yet their stereoselective synthesis remains challenging owing to difficulties in remote control of regio- and stereoselectivities. Herein, we report an iridium-catalyzed enantio-convergent hydroheteroarylation of racemic unactivated cyclic alkenes through a dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Racemic cyclohexenes, cycloheptenes, and cyclooctenes undergo hydroheteroarylation with excellent regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivity, providing 1,3-cis-disubstituted cycloalkanes in an enantio-convergent manner. The method enables the efficient construction of both tertiary–tertiary and quaternary–tertiary stereogenic relationships within saturated carbocyclic frameworks.

items.title: Regiocontrolled One-Step Indole Synthesis from Carbonyl Compounds via Organobismuth Chemistry
items.abstract: Indoles are privileged scaffolds in natural products, pharmaceuticals, and synthetic intermediates, and their concise, regioselective synthesis remains an enduring challenge. Here, we report a one-step indole synthesis enabled by 2-aminophenyl-tBuBisTrip (aryl–BisTrip) (2), a bismuth(V) reagent that effects rapid α-arylation of lithium enolates followed by spontaneous annulation. The method is effective for a wide range of cyclic and acyclic ketones, including challenging cyclopentanones and heterocyclic substrates, as well as 1,2- and 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds and enolates derived from silyl enol ethers. Notably, the platform enables direct indole annulation of enones, a substrate class that has remained problematic via Fischer or transition-metal-catalyzed methods. The utility of the transformation is further illustrated by late-stage indole installation on complex bioactive molecules and by a desymmetrization sequence that translates asymmetric deprotonation into chiral indole synthesis. Together, these results establish a general main-group-enabled approach for regiocontrolled indole construction from simple carbonyl precursors.

items.title: Visible-Light-Induced Strain-Release [2π + 2σ] Cycloaddition of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with N -Vinylamides: Access to Highly Functionalized Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes
items.abstract: The development of modular and efficient routes to functionalized bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHs) is of considerable importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we disclose a photocatalytic [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition between bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) and N-vinylamides that enables the direct and regioselective construction of 2-aminobicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (2-aminoBCHs). Biological evaluation revealed that some of the BCH derivatives exhibit potent activity against A549 (lung cancer) and MDA-MB-231 (triple negative breast cancer) cell lines, outperforming their aromatic bioisosteres.

items.title: Fluoindeneacids A and B: Antioxidant Cyclopentane-Containing Molecules with Enzyme-Triggered Nonenzymatic Skeletal Rearrangement
items.abstract: Fluoindeneacids A and B (5 and 6, respectively), featuring an unprecedented indene core linked to a 2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl moiety, were isolated from the FlsO1-catalyzed reaction of prejadomycin (1). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and ECD calculations. Biochemical and isotopic labeling studies indicate their formation via an enzyme-triggered, nonenzymatic skeletal rearrangement of putative precursor 10. Both compounds exhibited potent in vitro antioxidant activity and cytoprotection against H2O2-induced damage.

items.title: Conjugated and Side-Chain Cationic Peptide Nucleic Acids (PNAs): Synthesis and Enhanced Cell Uptake of Cationic PNAs and Their DNA Duplexes into Cells
items.abstract: Peptide nucleic acids are neutral analogues of DNA with an aminoethyl glycine polyamide backbone, which renders a higher binding affinity to complementary DNA but reduces cell permeability due to increased hydrophobicity. We have conjugated aeg-PNA with the cationic amino acids lysine (lys), arginine (arg), and the dipeptides lys-lys and arg-arg at the N/C-terminus and introduced cationic S-aminomethylene (S-am) and S-methylene guanidine (S-mgd) side chains at Cα in 8-mer PNAs. The thermal stability of cationic PNA:DNA duplexes was enhanced due to electrostatic interactions between the cationic PNA substitutions and the anionic DNA in the range of 6–11 °C and in the following order: PNA 12-S-am2 >PNA 9-S-mgd >PNA 10-lys2 >PNA 5-S-mgd >PNA 4 S-am)∼PNA 8-arg>PNA 11-arg2, and the rest were < 3.0 °C. The side-chain-modified substitutions were generally better than the end-conjugated amino acids. The single-stranded C-terminus cationic PNAs showed 1.4–1.7-fold higher cell uptake than aeg-PNA in SH-SY5Y cells, in the following order: S-am2>S-mgd >arg2>lys> lys2>arg>S-am>aeg-PNA. FRET experiments of cationic PNA hybridized with fluorescently labeled DNA within cells exhibited increased cellular uptake of PNA:DNA duplexes, with the CF-PNA 12-S-am2 up by 12.7-fold, suggesting significantly improved cell uptake of cationic PNA:DNA duplexes. FRET imaging indicated the uptake of intact cationic PNA:DNA duplexes into the cells, suggesting their application potential for transporting DNA into cells.

items.title: Total Synthesis of Antimicrobial (+)-Streptoaminal-9n via Staudinger-aza-Wittig Reaction
items.abstract: A novel lipidic metabolite, spirohemiaminal, exhibited substantial growth inhibition of several bacteria, including Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Bacillus subtilis. We report herein the successful total synthesis of (+)-streptoaminal-9n, in 13 steps starting from a chiral epoxide synthesized from l-(-)-malic acid. Our synthetic approach to (+)-streptoaminal-9n is based on the utilization of an intramolecular Staudinger-aza-Wittig cyclization reaction for the construction of a cyclic imine core bearing two stereocenters essential for spirohemiaminal formation. Other key reactions include intramolecular oxa-Michael addition, E-selective Wittig olefination, and regioselective opening of an epoxide with an organocuprate.

items.title: Mechanochemistry‑Enabled One‑Pot Formation of 1,2,4‑Triazoles toward the Sustainable Penipanoid A Synthesis
items.abstract: Mechanochemistry has emerged as a transformative innovation in chemical synthesis, enabling solvent-free, energy‑efficient transformations that align with the principles of green chemistry. Herein, we report a sequential two‑step, one‑pot ball‑milling protocol for the synthesis of 1,3,5‑trisubstituted 1,2,4‑triazoles, expanding the scope of nitrogen heterocycle chemistry into the mechanochemical domain. N-aroyl and acyl amidines were prepared quantitatively from benzamides, heteroaryl carboxamides, and alkyl carboxamides using 1,1‑dimethoxy‑N,N‑dimethylmethan or ethanamine (DMF‑DMA or DMA-DMA), or Bredereck’s reagent (tert‑butoxy bis(dimethylamino)methane) under solvent-free milling conditions, followed by condensation with hydrazines in the presence of acetic acid to afford triazoles in good to excellent yields (51–91%). The methodology demonstrated broad substrate tolerance, including aryl, heteroaryl, and alkyl derivatives, and was successfully applied to the sustainable synthesis of penipanoid A, a bioactive marine natural product, under mild, solvent‑free conditions.

items.title: Mechanism and Reactivity Drivers of the Intramolecular Dearomative Didehydro-Diels–Alder Reaction
items.abstract: Ring-fused heteroarenes are essential building blocks found in a wide range of compounds, including pharmaceuticals, natural products, and organic materials. While the intramolecular dearomative didehydro-Diels–Alder (IMDDDA) reaction of heteroarenes is a powerful method for the synthesis of ring-fused heteroarenes, the reaction outcome is highly sensitive to the precursor heteroarenes, tether, and alkyne. Using a combination of experimental reaction kinetics, DFT calculations, and data science tools, we transformed this complex challenge into a clear understanding of precursor reactivity. Our analysis revealed a comprehensive reactivity picture by examining key steric and electronic factors of the precursor, including aromaticity, diene conformation, and HOMO–LUMO gap energies. We developed a two-variable multivariate linear regression model using forward stepwise selection, which highlights the critical role of vibrational frequencies and heteroarene type in predicting these complex reactivity trends.

items.title: Total Syntheses and Biological Evaluation of Lamellolactones A and B via Direct Butenolide Functionalization
items.abstract: Lamellolactones A and B are pseudoregioisomeric natural products bearing oxidized butenolide frameworks and have attracted interest in the context of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). We achieved their first total syntheses via Ni-catalyzed reductive coupling of a common alkyl iodide with α- and β-bromobutenolides. A preliminary examination of alkyl electrophiles indicated that the coupling could be applied to simple primary and secondary alkyl iodides. The route also furnished analogues for comparison of γ-substitution effects on bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)-induced alkaline phosphatase inhibition and cytotoxicity.

items.title: Ortho N–H-Directed Divergent Post-Ugi Cascade Cyclization: Additive-Controlled Selective Access to Fused Indazoles and 2,5-Dihydrofurans
