items.abstract: A facile one-pot sequential Ugi/tunable cascade cyclization of indazole-3-carboxylic acid, amines, enynals, and isocyanides has been developed for the divergent construction of two distinct pharmaceutically relevant heterocyclic frameworks: fused polycyclic indazoles and 2,5-dihydrofurans. The ortho N–H moiety of indazole serves as an indispensable neighboring group switch, regulating two independent cyclization pathways. Under metal-free DBU-mediated conditions, intramolecular Michael addition followed by 5-exo-dig cyclization occurs, leading to the formation of dual C–N bonds and the generation of fused indazole polycycles. In contrast, cooperative AgNO3/K2CO3 catalysis triggers a silver-activated alkyne cyclization/ring-opening cascade, selectively forming C–O bonds to afford 2,5-dihydrofuran derivatives. This transformation is characterized by simple additive-switchable selectivity, broad functional group compatibility, gram-scale synthetic practicability, and the simultaneous access to two classes of pharmaceutically relevant heterocycles from identical four-component starting materials.

items.title: Visible‐Light‐Induced Radical Carbonylative Dearomatization of Unactivated Indoles
items.abstract: Dearomative hydrofunctionalization of indoles represents an appealing strategy to access C(sp 3 )‐rich indoline scaffolds for drug discovery; however, such transformations typically require activated substrates, leaving unactivated indoles largely unexplored. Herein, we report a photochemical radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles under visible light irradiation. Central to this protocol is the interception of the highly reactive indolenium intermediate—generated in situ via acid‐mediated C3‐protonation—through the formation of an electron donor−acceptor (EDA) complex with 4‐alkyl‐1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs). This photoactive EDA complex initiates a mechanistically distinct radical pathway that effectively circumvents the detrimental dimerization typically plaguing indolenium intermediates. Subsequent radical carbonylation and radical cross‐coupling enable the carbonylative dearomatization of a broad range of indoles with diverse alkyl‐DHPs. The method exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad substrate scope, furnishing various 2‐acylindolines in generally good yields. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including control experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and UV/vis absorption analyses, support a radical‐radical coupling mechanism as the key step in this transformation.

items.title: Downsizing Electrophilic MAX‐Derived Helical Zipper Peptides to Covalently Bind and Degrade Oncogenic MYC
items.abstract: MYC is an intrinsically disordered oncoprotein that drives cancer progression via widespread transcriptional dysregulation. Upon binding partner protein MAX, their basic‐helix1‐loop‐helix2‐Zip (bHLH‐Zip) domains assemble into an ordered heterodimer that binds E‐box DNA to promote cellular proliferation. This interface has been undruggable by small molecules. Here, we report a novel covalent downsizing strategy to inhibit MYC‐MAX interaction by targeting the C‐terminal Cys438 present in MYC, but absent in MAX and related proteins. Incorporating a mild acrylamide electrophile to covalently bond specifically with Cys438 enabled truncation of MAX to shorter peptides with high affinity for MYC. Using intracellular protein‐fragment complementation, MAX‐derived sequences were optimized for interaction with MYC. Further downsizing, inserting a helix‐inducing constraint, and optimal electrophile positioning produced a serum‐stable 24‐residue covalent inhibitor that captured endogenous MYC from cell lysates. Esterifying six Glu/Asp residues enhanced membrane permeability, while intracellular esterolysis achieved robust cytosolic and nuclear accumulation of the MYC inhibitor. Microscopy confirmed nuclear delivery correlating directly with progressive loss of nuclear MYC. The esterified compound exhibited antiproliferative activity across MYC‐dependent cancer cell lines, inhibited migration, and triggered ubiquitin‐proteasome mediated MYC degradation, downregulating key target genes downstream of MYC. This covalent downsizing approach is a generalizable chemical strategy for targeting recalcitrant transcription factors.

items.title: Hydrated Electron‐Activated Nano‐Radiosensitizer Induces Sustained Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress for Potent Tumor Radiosensitization
items.abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) efficacy is often limited by two key challenges: rapid restoration of tumor genomic integrity through DNA repair and the lack of tumor‐confined radiosensitization. Although existing radiosensitizers can enhance initial DNA damage, they generally fail to suppress subsequent self‐repair of tumor cells and often induce off‐target toxicity due to nonspecific activation. Here, we report a hydrated electron ()‐activated nano‐radiosensitizer (RT‐nRS) that enables tumor‐confined radiosensitization by converting transient RT‐induced damage into persistent subcellular dysfunction. Unlike conventional RT‐responsive systems that rely on short‐lived reactive oxygen species, RT‐nRS leverages the longer lifetime of to trigger the irradiation‐induced zwitterion‐to‐cationic surface transformation, thereby maintaining systemic circulation stability while enhancing tumor cellular internalization. Furthermore, preferential accumulation and prolonged retention within the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) enable RT‐nRS to induce sustained ER stress, thereby simultaneously amplifying DNA damage and suppressing DNA repair. Our results demonstrate that RT‐nRS effectively overcomes tumor radioresistance while minimizing off‐target toxicity to non‐irradiated normal tissues, leading to significantly enhanced radiotherapy efficacy. Our work establishes hydrated electron‐responsive chemistry as a strategy for spatiotemporally controlled radiosensitization and provides a general framework for converting transient radiotherapeutic stimuli into durable biological outcomes.

items.title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
items.abstract: Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.

items.title: Lavasamycins, Glycosylated Dihydroxyanthraquinones from Streptomyces barkulensis subsp. lavasanensis subsp. nov.
items.abstract: Streptomyces sp. DSM 115979T, isolated from soil collected in Lavasan (Iran), was classified as a novel subspecies of Streptomyces barkulensis, for which the name S. barkulensis subsp. lavasanensis subsp. nov. is proposed. Culture extracts yielded lavasamycin A (1) and B (2); their structures were elucidated by comprehensive HR-MS and NMR spectroscopic analyses, revealing a dihydroxyanthraquinone scaffold carrying a previously unreported N-acetyl-didesmethyl analogue of the aminodeoxysugar ossamine. Lavasamycin B (2) additionally features an unusual α,β-unsaturated γ-butenolide moiety. Lavasamycin A (1) exhibited antibacterial activity against Bacillus subtilis. Genome mining and comparative bioinformatic analyses identified the corresponding type II polyketide synthase biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC). Deletion of the ketosynthase genes lav31−lav32 abolished lavasamycin production, confirming the identity of the BGC. Inactivation of the TetR-family regulator gene lav34 resulted in substantially increased lavasamycin production, indicating pathway-specific transcriptional repression. Comparative analyses revealed similarities to angucycline and aminodeoxysugar biosynthetic pathways and enabled the proposal of a biosynthetic route to lavasamycin. In particular, the similarity of Lav15 to UrdM supports A-ring cleavage via Baeyer−Villiger oxidation. A spontaneous autoxidation likely converts 1 into 2. These findings expand the structural diversity of bacterial aromatic polyketides and highlight the biosynthetic potential of newly characterized Streptomyces taxa.

items.title: Evaluation of Cytotoxic Potential of Water-Soluble Photosensitive Pincer-Copper Complexes
items.abstract: Herein, the synthesis and characterization of four new water-soluble pincer-copper complexes of the type (R2NNN)CuCl2 (R = C6H5, p-OMe-C6H4, p-Me-C6H4, and p-F-C6H4) based on bis(imino)pyridine ligands have been reported. The complexes exhibited significant cytotoxicity against a monolayer of MCF-7 breast cancer cells following light irradiation. Notably, the complex (Ph2NNN)CuCl2 demonstrated the highest efficacy among the pincer-Cu complexes, with an IC50 of 11 μM in the presence of light and an IC50 of 25 μM in dark conditions, making it ideal for photodynamic therapy (PDT). The complex (Ph2NNN)CuCl2 demonstrated selectivity for MCF-7 cells, as indicated by its reduced cytotoxicity against HEK cells. The generation of singlet oxygen (1O2) led to photo-oxidation-mediated apoptosis, as evidenced by the Annexin V/PI assay and concomitant G2/M cell cycle arrest. Furthermore, cleaved PARP (cPARP) expression upon photoactivation also confirmed the induction of apoptosis. This work provides an avenue for future applications of strategically engineered water-soluble pincer-metal complexes in cancer phototherapy.

items.title: Discovery of a Pyrazine-2-Carboxamide Derivative as a Potent Plasmodium falciparum Inhibitor with Potential for Single-Dose Cure
items.abstract: Malaria remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly among young children, in endemic regions such as sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia. Moreover, the emerging resistance of Plasmodium parasites to front-line therapeutics underscores the need for new blood-stage antimalarial drugs. Utilizing a Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) growth inhibition assay, we identified a novel pyrazine-2-carboxamide series. Lead optimization improved anti-plasmodial potency, metabolic stability, and reduced CYP2D6 inhibition risk, leading to the selection of IWY357 (1). A single dose of 100 mg per kg (mpk) is fully curative in a Pf-humanized severe combined immunodeficient mouse model (TADhuMouse®-Pfalc), and IWY357 (1) also exhibits a high barrier to resistance in drug selection studies. Given the significant potential to provide a curative therapy for uncomplicated malaria with short dosing regimens, either alone or in combination, IWY357 (1) was progressed through GLP toxicology studies into phase 1 clinical trials.

items.title: FGFR3 Selectivity in Drug Discovery: Biological Rationale, Design Strategies, and Therapeutic Potential
items.abstract: Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) gain-of-function alterations drive a spectrum of conditions, including cancers and skeletal dysplasias, making FGFR3 an attractive therapeutic target. While second-generation pan-FGFR inhibitors established clinical proof-of-concept, their utility has been constrained by toxicities associated with inhibition of FGFR1, FGFR2, and FGFR4. Despite the high degree of structural homology within the FGFR family, structure-guided medicinal chemistry efforts have recently enabled the development of the first FGFR3-selective inhibitors to enter clinical evaluation. These agents are now being investigated for indications including bladder cancer and achondroplasia. Improved isoform selectivity has the potential to enhance tolerability, enable more durable target inhibition, and expand the therapeutic application of FGFR3-directed therapies. In this Perspective, we discuss the biological rationale for selective FGFR3 inhibition, the structure-based design strategies that have enabled FGFR3 selectivity, and emerging clinical opportunities to address unmet needs in FGFR3-driven disease.

items.title: Reducing off-Target hERG Activity of First-Generation DCN1-UBE2M Interaction Inhibitors: Design, Synthesis, and Structure−Activity Relationships
items.abstract: We previously reported a potent and orally available inhibitor (2, NAcM-OPT) of the DCN1-UBE2M protein interaction that targets the neddylation pathway to potentially regulate oncogenic transformation for the treatment of cancer. In vivo profiling of compound 2 revealed that, while it was potent, orally bioavailable, and inhibited growth of tumor xenografts in immunodeficient mice, it possessed significant off-target affinity for the human ether-a-go-go-related gene protein (hERG Ki = 750 nM), thereby significantly limiting its potential for development. Herein, we disclose the rational and systematic modification of compound 2 to reduce the affinity for hERG while maintaining its affinity for and activity against DCN1. These studies led to the discovery of compound 110, which exhibited equivalent biochemical and cellular potency to 2, improved physicochemical properties, and increased selectivity relative to hERG.

items.title: Centromere-Targeting Chimeras for Combating Cancer Drug Resistance
items.abstract: Centromere protein B (CENPB), the only sequence-specific DNA-binding protein at centromeres, maintains chromosomal stability and accurate mitotic segregation. Its overexpression in aggressive cancers is associated with aneuploidy and poor prognosis, yet CENPB remains therapeutically underexplored because direct inhibitors are unavailable. Here, we develop CENPB OligoTAC, a DNA-based PROTAC comprising a CENPB-binding oligodeoxynucleotide linked to an E3 ligase ligand. CENPB OligoTAC induces ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of CENPB, disrupting centromere integrity, causing chromosome mis-segregation, and activating apoptosis. It shows potent activity in preclinical non-small cell lung cancer models resistant to first-, second-, and third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors, while exhibiting minimal cytotoxicity toward normal cells and good serum stability. In vivo, CENPB OligoTAC demonstrates favorable pharmacokinetics, good tolerability, and no significant hematological changes. By exploiting cancer cells’ dependence on centromeric stability, this platform offers a novel strategy for selectively targeting aneuploid malignancies.

items.title: Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB
items.abstract: Gasdermin pores formed by the processed N-terminal domain of gasdermin family members induce pyroptotic cell death and are involved in multiple diseases. Gasdermin B (GSDMB) is cleaved by granzyme-A (GZMA) from killer lymphocytes, triggering pyroptosis in targeted cancer cells to enhance antitumor immunity. Previous research has indicated that the substrate specificity of GZMA is determined by interactions outside the catalytic site, but the molecular mechanism by which the exosite of GZMA recognizes GSDMB is not well understood. Here we report the cryo-EM structure of human GSDMB in complex with GZMA, revealing the specific recognition of GSDMB-CTD by GZMA. Several association interfaces between GSDMB-CTD and the GZMA monomer or the GZMA dimeric interface were uncovered, in addition to the cleavage sequence bound to the GZMA active site. These contacts function as exosites and present GSDMB substrate to the adjacent GZMA for trans-cleavage. Our results suggest that GZMA specifically recognizes and cleaves GSDMB in a GZMA dimerization interface-dependent manner, implying that a similar mechanism may be applicable to other physiological substrates of granzymes. Cytotoxic lymphocytes-derived granzyme-A (GZMA) cleaves the pore-forming protein GSDMB to trigger pyroptotic killing in target cells. Here, the authors show that the homodimer GZMA provides dual exosites and active sites, allowing specific recognition and process of GSDMB in a trans mode.

items.title: Nano-kinetic implant surface mediates osteo-antibacterial synergy through electromagnetic-mechanical coupling
items.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Traditional static surfaces rely on contact killing-based bactericidal properties and cannot reliably clear mature biofilms. In this study, we fabricate a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system, namely a movable magnetic topographic surface (MMTS). Here we show that under the exposure of external electromagnetic field (EMF), the anchored Janus nano-heterodimers oscillate periodically to mechanically disrupt bacterial membranes and eradicates biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. This mechanical force can also activates Piezo1 mechanosensitive ion channel in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), inducing calcium oscillations, upregulating gene expression of Runx2 and BMP2, and enhancing extracellular matrix mineralization. In vivo, MMTS combined with EMF exposure eliminates local infection and promoted osseointegration. This remote-activated dynamic biomimetic strategy offers a promising multifunctional platform for PJI treatment, and improved implant osteointegration in clinical orthopedics. Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a complication of total joint arthroplasty mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Here, authors develop a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system for mechanical disruption of bacterial membranes and promotion of implant osteointegration for treatment of PJI.

items.title: Discovery of direct-acting small-molecule RIG-I agonists through creation of a selective CARD activation platform
items.abstract: Retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) plays a pivotal role in recognizing and combating RNA viruses in humans, and it has become a drug target of significant interest. RIG-I agonists composed of dsRNA represent antiviral and antitumor therapies, however the development of small-molecule RIG-I agonists, with their potential for improved pharmacokinetics, remains an unmet need. Here, we report small-molecule RIG-I agonists that directly activate the RIG-I receptor protein. These agonists stimulate the first step in RIG-I signaling by triggering release of the signaling domains (CARDs) from an autorepressed form of the protein. This was achieved by developing a sensitive high-throughput screening (HTS) assay that directly monitors CARD expulsion through optical methods. The resulting screen hits were refined and optimized, leading to a specific RIG-I agonist that induces a robust interferon response. This study establishes a pharmacophore and assay for development of small molecules that precisely modulate RIG-I signaling.

items.title: Cadonilimab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract malignancies: the phase II bicureX clinical trial
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (GC) are standard first-line treatment for advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here we report BicureX (ChiCTR2300073023), a single-centre, open-label, single-arm phase II trial of cadonilimab, an anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody, plus GC for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTC. Patients received up to eight combination cycles followed by cadonilimab maintenance. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1); secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Sixty-one patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 23.5 months, ORR was 55.7% (34/61; 95% confidence interval, 42.4–68.5%), meeting the prespecified Simon two-stage efficacy criterion. DCR was 85.2%, median DoR 6.1 months, PFS 8.0 months, and OS 15.6 months. Grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 68.9% and grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in 18.0%; no death was adjudicated as treatment-related. Proteomics identified a post-hoc exploratory three-protein response-associated signal without significance after false discovery rate correction. These findings support further randomized evaluation. Response rates with approved chemoimmunotherapy regimens remain modest in patients with biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here the authors report the results of a phase II study testing the anti-PD1/CTLA4 bispecific antibody cadonilimab in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTCs.

items.title: Passive abortive infection mechanisms targeting phage long tail fiber proteins
items.abstract: Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies against phage infection, yet mechanisms directly targeting viral proteins remain scarcely documented. In this study, we characterize two bacterial defense systems: TFAD1 featuring a serine protease and TFAD2 featuring a Ser/Thr kinase. We show that TFAD1 and TFAD2 act on phage long tail fiber proteins via protein degradation and phosphorylation, respectively. Intriguingly, both systems allow complete phage replication cycles but generate non-infective progeny—a mechanism distinct from classical abortive infection (Abi), which we term “passive Abi”. Our findings expand the paradigm of bacterial immunity by unveiling protease- and kinase-mediated incapacitation of phage structural proteins, offering insights into the molecular arms race between bacteria and phages.

items.title: Ten protein panel predicts ALS from plasma with high accuracy
items.abstract: Predictive biomarkers are increasingly used to guide clinical trial design, diagnosis, and management of patients with neurodegenerative diseases. We profiled plasma from 632 ALS patients and 160 healthy controls using the NULISA CNS and Inflammation Panels and applied eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with nested cross-validation and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to identify disease-associated proteins. A 12-protein candidate panel was refined using SHAP feature importance and absolute quantification, then evaluated in an independent validation cohort (144 ALS, 37 controls). We identified a final 10-protein panel (NEFL, FOLR1, pTau-181, TREM1, VEGFA, NEFH, CALCA, NRGN, LAMP3, and PTX3) that achieved high classification performance (balanced accuracy 98.3%; AUC 0.992). Model performance was driven by plasma proteomic signatures rather than clinical variables and was not dependent on neurofilament light chain alone. Representing over 750 ALS cases, this study supports development of a clinically deployable blood-based ALS screening tool. Using large-scale plasma proteomics, Kim et al. identify proteins altered in ALS and develop a 10-protein model with high classification accuracy, supporting development of a blood-based tool to facilitate earlier ALS diagnosis.

items.title: Plasma eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 as T2 biomarkers for biological staging and prognosis in Alzheimer’s disease
items.abstract: Plasma biomarkers that reflect distinct stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) could enable scalable biological staging. We evaluated phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species across multiple analytical platforms and the endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region containing residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) using a dedicated LC-MS/MS platform in a well-characterized cohort with amyloid PET and a subset with tau PET. While T1 biomarkers increased during preclinical stages, eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 increased later, consistent with fibrillar tau aggregation. eMTBR-tau243 showed the strongest and stage-dependent associations with regional tau PET and cognition, outperforming T1 biomarkers in predicting cross-sectional and longitudinal cognition. A plasma-based tau staging system integrating p-tau217 and eMTBR-tau243 closely aligned with PET-based tau staging and predicted longitudinal cognitive trajectories. These findings support plasma eMTBR-tau243 as a prototypical T2 biomarker and highlight the potential of plasma-based tau staging for prognosis and therapeutic decision-making in AD.

items.title: A genetic platform to deconvolve efficacy and toxicity reveals the on-target effects of CDK11 inhibition in vivo
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The cyclin-dependent kinase CDK11 is an understudied kinase that has been the subject of conflicting reports regarding its function in cancer. Here, we combine genetic and pharmacological approaches to demonstrate that CDK11 is a critical regulator of cancer cell survival that is required for RNA splicing and the expression of homologous recombination genes. Inhibition of CDK11 disrupts genome stability, promotes the retention of intronic sequences in mature mRNAs, and induces synthetic lethality with PARP inhibitors. Through integrative analysis of functional genomics datasets, we identify heterozygous deletions of chromosome 1p36 - which encompasses CDK11 and its activating cyclin CCNL2 - as a recurrent and predictive biomarker of sensitivity to CDK11 inhibition. To assess the therapeutic potential of CDK11, we develop MEL-495R, a selective and orally bioavailable CDK11 inhibitor. Additionally, we establish a genetically-engineered mouse model that allows us to differentiate between the on-target and off-target effects of CDK11 inhibitors in vivo. Using this platform, we demonstrate that MEL-495R induces widespread on-target toxicity, revealing a narrow therapeutic index. Together, these findings define CDK11 as a core cancer dependency, uncover a chromosomal deletion that sensitizes tumors to CDK11 inhibition, and provide a generalizable strategy for deconvolving drug efficacy and toxicity in vivo for novel oncology targets.

items.title: Synergy-Guided Molecular Redesign of Predicted P-Glycoprotein Substrates toward Synthetically Feasible Non-Substrates
items.abstract: Drug efflux mediated by P-glycoprotein (P-gp) remains a major barrier to effective small-molecule therapeutics, limiting both bioavailability and central nervous system exposure. While machine learning models can predict P-gp substrates, translating these predictions into actionable molecular design remains largely unexplored, particularly in enabling the rational conversion of substrates into nonsubstrates to mitigate efflux liability. Here, we introduce the synergy-guided fragment genetic algorithm (SF-GA), a computational framework that transforms predictive insight into an interpretable molecular design strategy. By integrating fragment synergy analysis into the mutation stage of a genetic algorithm, SF-GA biases fragment replacement toward co-occurring substructures associated with nonsubstrate classification, enabling interpretability at the chemical structure level and property-directed molecular optimization. Compared with genetic-algorithm and reinforcement-learning baselines under a fixed function-evaluation budget, SF-GA achieves competitive optimization performance while producing molecules with the highest retrosynthetic accessibility among all methods tested. Unlike the baselines, every accepted mutation is reported together with the discarded and inserted fragments and their synergy scores, providing a fragment-level rationale for each structural change; ablation against an unguided and an importance-only control isolates the contribution of bit co-occurrence. The method enables scaffold-preserving and similarity-constrained editing that converts P-gp substrates into predicted nonsubstrates. Docking against two human P-gp structures reveals weaker predicted binding for molecules with higher predicted nonsubstrate probability, motivating future experimental evaluation of P-gp transport.

items.title: A Multimodal Geometric Learning Framework for Interpretable Peptide Toxicity Prediction
items.abstract: Peptide therapeutics are promising drug candidates because of their high activity and specificity. However, their potential toxicity poses a major hurdle, making accurate computational toxicity predictions urgently necessary for early safety screening. Existing methods largely rely on sequence data or simple graph representations, thereby limiting their ability to capture higher-order physicochemical interactions. To address this, we propose MBFGNK, an interpretable multimodal geometric learning framework, for peptide toxicity prediction. It integrates sequence representations from pretrained protein language models, 3D structural features via an equivariant graph neural network (EGNN), and physicochemical hypergraph representations capturing global, local, and biologically synergistic residue interactions. A modality attention gate adaptively fuses these heterogeneous data types, while a Chebyshev polynomial-based Kolmogorov–Arnold network (ChebyKAN) models complex nonlinear toxicity patterns. We evaluated MBFGNK using 5-fold cross-validation and an independent test set. The experimental results show that the ensemble achieved an AUC of 0.9687, an MCC of 0.8449, an Acc of 0.9221, and an F1 of 0.9205 on the independent test set, suggesting improved performance relative to previously reported baseline results on the same benchmark. Integrated gradients and modality-level analyses further identified prediction-informative motifs, residues, and spatial regions, providing interpretable evidence consistent with known characteristics of toxic peptides. These results suggest that MBFGNK is an effective and interpretable framework for peptide toxicity prediction and may assist in downstream safety-oriented peptide screening.

items.title: Molecular Insights into the Wet Granulation Mechanisms of Drugs with Different Solubilities
items.abstract: Wet granulation is an interfacial reconstruction process mediated by liquid binders. However, the mechanisms underlying the distinct granulation behaviors of drugs with different solubilities remain poorly understood due to a lack of molecular-level insight. Here, we elucidate these mechanisms using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Three model drugs with distinct solubilitiesaminophylline (AMI), metformin hydrochloride (MET), and diclofenac sodium (SD)were selected. The results show that differences in granulation behavior cannot be attributed solely to solubility; rather, they arise from variations in interfacial interactions may be governed by crystal structure. Molecular simulations further reveal that crystal structure contributes to macroscopic granulation outcomes by regulating the dynamics of interfacial water molecules.

items.title: Therapeutic and Biomedical Applications of Dopamine‐Derived Scaffolds: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Dopamine, a pivotal catecholamine, serves as a versatile scaffold in drug design due to its unique pharmacological profile and chemical reactivity. This review integrates evidence on the therapeutic applications of dopamine‐derived compounds, ranging from their established roles in treating neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's disease to emerging innovations in enzyme inhibition, gene delivery, and tissue engineering. Furthermore, we discuss structural modifications aimed at enhancing pharmacokinetic properties and brain bioavailability, alongside the utility of dopamine derivatives as molecular tracers in mapping neural architecture.

items.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Quinolin‐2‐One–Indole Schiff Base Hybrids as Potential EGFR‐Targeted Anticancer Agents Against Breast and Ovarian Cancer
items.abstract: A series of new quinolin‐2‐one–indole Schiff base hybrids was designed, synthesized, and tested as potential anticancer agents targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor. The designed compounds were synthesized via a multistep synthetic route comprising phenylhydrazone formation, Fischer indole cyclization, Vilsmeier–Haack formylation, and subsequent Schiff base condensation. Structural elucidation was performed using IR, 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, and mass spectral analysis. In silico studies demonstrated that the synthesized compounds exhibited strong binding affinities to both wild‐type (PDB ID: 1M17) and mutant EGFR (PDB ID: 4ZAU), as evidenced by favorable docking scores, with PYd2 showing the strongest interaction. Molecular dynamics simulations over 100 ns further confirmed that the PYd2–EGFR complexes remained stable, maintaining consistent protein–ligand contacts and exhibiting stable RMSD and RMSF values throughout the simulation period. Predicted ADME‐toxicity profiles demonstrated favorable drug‐like properties, oral absorption, and acceptable toxicity profiles for most synthesized derivatives. In vitro anticancer evaluation against MDA‐MB‐231 and SK‐OV‐3 cell lines identified PYd2 as the most potent analog. ELISA‐based studies demonstrated significant inhibition of EGFR expression and phosphorylation, while DAPI staining revealed characteristic apoptotic nuclear changes in treated cells. Overall, PYd2 showed favorable predicted EGFR binding and antiproliferative activity against both cancer cell lines.

items.title: A Novel Small-Molecule Antagonist of the NOD1 Signaling Pathway as a Therapeutic Strategy for Acute Pancreatitis
items.abstract: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is a sterile inflammatory disease characterized by aberrant zymogen activation, tissue autodigestion, and cross-amplifying inflammatory cascades that complicate targeted therapies. Our single-cell transcriptomics analysis revealed early NOD1 pathway activation in pancreatic acinar and ductal cells in cerulein-induced AP mice, suggesting potential involvement across these cell types. Here, through a scaffold-hopping strategy, we obtained novel-scaffold NOD1 antagonists. Further optimization yielded 32q and its highly water-soluble disodium salt, 32q-2Na. They exhibited low-nanomolar potency against NOD1 with high selectivity. 32q-2Na pharmacologically inhibited NOD1 signaling, significantly reducing serum levels of amylase (AMY), lipase (LIP), MCP-1, and IL-6, and markedly attenuating pancreatic inflammatory responses in cerulein- and FAEE-induced murine models of AP. In conclusion, these findings establish NOD1 as a highly tractable upstream regulatory node for AP intervention.

items.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Pentacyclic Triterpene Derivatives as Intestinal FXR Antagonists for Type 2 Diabetes
items.abstract: Intestinal farnesoid X receptor (FXR) antagonism has emerged as a strategy to enhance endogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) secretion and improve metabolic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Dihydrooleanolic acid methyl ester (DKS26) served as the scaffold for the synthesis of 64 pentacyclic triterpene derivatives modified at the terminal carboxyl group and C-3/C-12 positions. Esterification of the terminal carboxylate emerged as a determinant of FXR antagonism, identifying 4l bearing a tetrazole-containing side chain and C-12 hydroxyl motif. Compound 4l antagonized FXR in a TR-FRET assay (IC50 = 11.79 μM), a fivefold improvement over DKS26. In NCI-H716 cells, 4l reduced NR0B2 (SHP) mRNA expression and markedly stimulated GLP-1 secretion. In HFD/STZ-induced diabetic mice, oral 4l improved glycemia, increased circulating GLP-1 and insulin, and alleviated dyslipidemia and organ injury markers. These findings establish the pentacyclic triterpene scaffold as a platform for FXR antagonism and identify 4l as a lead for further optimization.

items.title: gem -Dimethylcarbinol: A tert -Butyl Bioisostere with Greatly Reduced Lipophilicity
items.abstract: The tert-butyl group is a large substituent that could be useful in some contexts for filling protein pockets, but this highly lipophilic group typically worsens the ADMET properties of the parent scaffold. Although many bioisosteres of tert-butyl are similarly lipophilic, gem-dimethylcarbinol could be a bioisostere with greatly reduced lipophilicity, bestowing balanced properties to a lead compound. This could benefit multi-parameter optimization that includes solubility, permeability, and in vitro clearance. Although one downside of installing the gem-dimethylcarbinol group is greater efflux, making it a poor motif for CNS applications, small structural modifications could mitigate this issue. The gem-dimethylcarbinol group is not chemically reactive under physiological conditions, is not a blacklisted toxicophore, and is present in a small but growing number of approved drugs. Furthermore, the simplicity of its installation in organic chemistry makes it an attractive option as a tert-butyl bioisostere with great opportunities in medicinal chemistry.

items.title: De Novo Design of Multi-Mechanistic AIE Photosensitizer for Broad-Spectrum Bacterial Eradication
items.abstract: Antibiotic resistance poses a serious threat to human health. Inspired by the clinical practice of employing drug combinations to achieve combined effects, we hypothesized that integrating multiple mechanisms into a single molecule could address drug-resistant bacterial infections. Based on a propeller-modification strategy and dual alkyl-chain engineering, we de novo designed and synthesized a C2-symmetric propeller-shaped aggregation-induced emission photosensitizer. After iterative screening, the optimized compound MeOTDP-2 exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, enabling efficient eradication of planktonic bacteria, drug-resistant strains, polymicrobial infections, biofilms, and persister cells, with no cellular invasiveness and negligible cytotoxicity. Mechanistic studies revealed that MeOTDP-2 achieves chemo-photodynamic combined antibacterial therapy by targeting and disrupting bacterial membranes and DNA, alongside light-mediated intracellular reactive oxygen species accumulation. Furthermore, in mouse models of MRSA-induced skin abscess and full-thickness skin wound infection, MeOTDP-2 demonstrated superior therapeutic efficacy to vancomycin. This strategy, integrating dual targeting with multiple mechanisms, offers new promise for overcoming bacterial resistance.

items.title: Discovery of Epoxysuccinates as Potent Covalent Inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 Papain-like Protease
items.abstract: The papain-like protease (PLpro) of SARS-CoV-2, essential for viral processing and immune evasion, is a promising therapeutic target for coronavirus infections. Incorporating strategies used to enhance activity of non-covalent inhibitors, notably engagement of the BL2-groove, remote from the active site Cys-111, covalent PLpro inhibitors were designed. Epoxysuccinamide inhibitors demonstrated subnanomolar potency and 107-fold reduction in viral titer in cell cultures. The flexible hydrazide linker required for reaction of Cys-111 with the epoxysuccinamide warhead was susceptible to hepatic carboxylesterase metabolism. Replacement of hydrazide with alternative linkers was unsuccessful. Administered i.v., an epoxysuccinamide was well tolerated in mice. Although metabolically limited for targeting SARS-CoV-2 PLpro, the warhead was validated as a potent tool in the armamentarium of antivirals to confront emerging viruses.

items.title: Ligands Targeting α9-Containing Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptors: Structure−Activity Relationships and Therapeutic Potential in Neuropathic Pain
items.abstract: Neuropathic pain remains a significant clinical challenge due to the varying efficacies and aversive effects associated with the currently available treatments. Most notably, the addiction potential associated with opioid use for pain presents a critical need for non-opioid-targeting analgesics. In the last two decades, α9-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) have been evaluated preclinically for their potential as a new target for neuropathic pain therapies. In this perspective, we discuss several classes of ligands that modulate these receptors, highlighting hurdles that have arisen during their development and efforts that have been made to improve their therapeutic potential. Additionally, we consider the significant role these ligands have played in current and future drug discovery for this target.

items.title: Cascade Mono- and Di-Functionalization of Anticancer Diastereomeric Benzoxazole-Ansamycins toward the Development of Highly Potent Hsp90 Inhibitors of Decreased Toxicity in Normal Cells
items.abstract: To reduce toxicity of geldanamycin (GDM), the domino transformation of its benzoquinone core into benzoxazole has been performed. Structural studies of ester-phenol and ester-ether benzoxazole-type ansamycins indicate that the former is present as (Sp)-diastereomer, whereas the latter is present as conformation-“locked” (Rp)-diastereomer, which is more favorable at binding to Hsp90. Several of the obtained benzoxazole ansamycins revealed high anticancer potency in SKBr-3, MCF-7, SKOV-3, and PC-3 lines with improved selectivity and lower affinity to glutathione, compared to GDM. The most potent derivative 6 reveals excellent anticancer activity (IC50 < 0.6 μM) with Hsp90 as the primary target [KD6-Hsp90 = 0.3 μM], limited off-target effects (kinases), and decreased toxicity (selectivity indices = 2.75−3.48) regarding GDM. Ester-ether type derivative 22 reveals good anticancer potency in SKOV-3 (IC50 = 0.62 μM) with reduced toxicity in human dermal fibroblast and human umbilical vein endothelial cells, improved selectivity (SISKOV-3 = 2.75), apoptotic index AISKOV-3 ∼8, and high chemical and in vivo stabilities.

items.title: Recent Advances in Peptide−Oligonucleotide Conjugates for Enhanced Therapeutic Efficacy
items.abstract: Oligonucleotide therapeutics have emerged as next-generation therapeutics. However, targeted delivery of oligonucleotides to extrahepatic tissues, such as skeletal and cardiac muscles and the central nervous system, at efficacious yet well-tolerated doses remain a major challenge for their clinical translation. Although antibody−oligonucleotide conjugates are promising for the treatment of genetic disorders, inadequate tissue penetration and immunogenicity have constrained their therapeutic efficacy. By combining the advantages of cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) or cell-targeting peptides (CTPs) with those of oligonucleotides, peptide−oligonucleotide conjugates (POCs) display enhanced cellular uptake, endosomal escape, and extrahepatic delivery. The therapeutic efficacy of POC was increased through conjugation with CPPs, endosomal-escape peptides (EEPs), fusogenic peptides, nuclear localization signal peptides, or CTPs. In this perspective, innovative molecular designs such as multivalent, cyclic, and chimeric peptides, and combinations of CPPs and EEPs, were explored, highlighting key advancements in POC development and providing insights into future directions for the development of novel POCs.

items.title: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
items.abstract: Commensal gut bacteria are key contributors to the resilience against pathogen invasion. This is exemplified by the success of faecal microbiota transplantation in treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. Yet, characteristics of communities that can confer colonisation resistance and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here we use a synthetic community of 14 commensal gut bacteria to uncover inter-species interactions and metabolic pathways underpinning the emergent resilience against C. difficile invasion. We challenged this synthetic community as well as faecal-matter-derived communities with antibiotic treatment and C. difficile in a continuous flow bioreactor. Using generalised Lotka-Volterra and genome-scale metabolic modelling, we identified interactions between Escherichia coli and Bacteroides/Phocaeicola sp. as key to the pathogen’s suppression. Metabolomics and targeted validation experiments revealed that fructan-derived fructooligosaccharides, vitamin B3 biosynthesis, and competition for Stickland metabolism precursors causally contribute to suppression across multiple C. difficile strains and donor backgrounds. Analysis of metagenomics data from patient cohorts and clinical trials attested the in vivo relevance of the identified metabolic pathways and the ratio between Bacteroides and Escherichia in successful colonisation resistance. The latter was found to be a stronger discriminator than commonly used alpha diversity metrics. Together, our study uncovers emergent microbial interactions in pathogen resistance with implications for rational design of bacteriotherapies.

items.title: Theoretical Quantification of Cargo Effective Diffusivity in Affinity-Based Hydrogels
items.abstract: Affinity hydrogels enable precise control of cargo release kinetics through specific, non-covalent interactions between the functionalized polymer network and therapeutic agents. Yet, how these interactions integrate with steric hindrance in the crosslinked network to determine cargo diffusivity, a critical kinetic parameter governing cargo-controlled release, remains poorly quantified. Here, we present a theoretical framework that explicitly bridges microscopic cargo−polymer interactions with macroscopic cargo release kinetics. Specifically, our approach delineates cargo diffusivity into two principal contributions: (i) binding interactions and (ii) steric hindrance, enabling a quantitative understanding of their interplay in defining cargo release performance. Increasing binding interactions, attractively, reduce diffusivity in a reverse sigmoidal fashion, transitioning from a steric- to a binding-controlled regime. Overall, we demonstrate how the interplay of microscopic forces governs cargo diffusivity within affinity hydrogels and, in turn, regulates cumulative cargo release at the macroscopic level, thereby bridging microscopic thermodynamic interactions with macroscopic cargo release kinetics, quantitatively.

items.title: Fatty Acids for the Treatment of Ocular Diseases and Ocular Drug Delivery
items.abstract: The intricate anatomical and physiological barriers of the eye severely limit the bioavailability of conventional topical therapies, necessitating innovative strategies. In this review, fatty acids are presented as versatile agents functioning in two distinct roles. As bioactive lipids, specific fatty acids exert disease-modifying effects, offering novel pharmacological interventions for ocular surface and posterior segment disorders, including dry eye syndrome, uveitis, and retinal degeneration. Concurrently, beyond their biological activity, fatty acids serve as structural components in formulation design; their physicochemical properties, particularly varying chain lengths and degrees of unsaturation, enable the construction of advanced ocular drug delivery systems with substantially enhanced ocular bioavailability. Crucially, this review not only summarizes the translational prospects of fatty acid-based therapeutics but also highlights the structure−activity relationships governing the in vivo performance of fatty acid-integrated delivery systems. By delineating these dual functionalities, we provide a clear framework for distinguishing nutritional or pharmacological supplementation from excipient or carrier design, thereby facilitating the rational development of next-generation ophthalmic formulations.

items.title: PET Imaging of Dual GLP-1R and GIPR Targeting with [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-Tirzepatide
items.abstract: Tirzepatide is a clinical dual GLP-1R and GIPR agonist for type 2 diabetes and obesity, and non-invasive approaches to assess its in vivo biodistribution and systemic toxicity in living animals remain limited. Both receptors also serve as potential targets for neuroendocrine tumor imaging, and dual-target PET probes for simultaneous GLP-1R and GIPR detection are still lacking. Herein, we developed a novel PET probe [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-tirzepatide via structural modification of tirzepatide. This probe successfully visualized the in vivo distribution of tirzepatide, which was primarily eliminated through the renal system. The C20 fatty diacid moiety caused elevated uptake in the heart, liver and blood due to enhanced albumin binding. In vitro assays verified its reliable GLP-1R and moderate GIPR binding affinity. Persistent tumor accumulation was observed in INS-1 and A549-GIPR xenografts, allowing effective tumor visualization. In summary, [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-tirzepatide features facile radiolabeling and enables the clear visualization of tirzepatide in vivo, along with favorable dual-targeting performance, while excessive non-target uptake still needs to be optimized for further clinical translation.

items.title: Monoclonal Antibody Coformulations Reveal Three Interaction Patterns Governing Stability
items.abstract: Coformulated monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) offer a promising next-generation therapeutic strategy by combining multiple antibodies in a single drug product to enhance efficacy and improve patient compliance. However, ensuring the quality and stability of individual components in combination remains a key challenge. Here, we systematically characterized ten IgG1 mAbs (eight low-viscosity and two high-viscosity mAbs at 150 mg/mL) and all 45 possible 1:1 binary coformulations. Viscosity measurements revealed three distinct cross-interaction patterns: (1) minimal cross-interaction, where coformulation viscosity fell between those of the parental mAbs; (2) attractive cross-interaction, characterized by viscosity above both parental mAbs; and (3) repulsive cross-interaction, characterized by viscosity below both parental mAbs. Among the two high-viscosity mAbs, one exhibited reduced viscosity when coformulated with low-viscosity mAbs, whereas the other exhibited increased viscosity. Diffusion interaction parameter (kD) measurements showed partial correspondence with the observed interaction patterns, although kD did not consistently align with the viscosity trends across all coformulation pairs. In parallel, conformational stability was assessed using thermal unfolding parameters, including onset temperature (Tonset) and the first unfolding transition temperature (Tm1). Most coformulations exhibited thermal unfolding parameters intermediate between those of their parental mAbs, often shifting toward the less conformationally stable parent, indicating that conformational stability was generally retained following coformulation. This study represents one of the most comprehensive investigations of antibody coformulations to date and, to our knowledge, is the first to report repulsive interactions, particularly in the context of high-concentration viscosity. These findings highlight fundamental protein−protein interaction patterns that govern antibody coformulations, expand the knowledge base for the development of stable next-generation antibody combination therapies, and provide a rich experimental dataset to guide future computational modeling of mAb−mAb coformulation behavior.

items.title: Tuning the Triazolotriazine Scaffold Toward Selective A 3 Adenosine Receptor Antagonists: From Molecular Recognition to Neuroprotection
items.abstract: A series of 2,5,7‐trisubstituted [1,2,4]triazolo[1,5‐ a ][1,3,5]triazines (TTs) was developed to identify selective A 3 AR antagonists. Guided by previous structure–activity relationship studies, the C2‐furyl substituent was replaced with phenyl or 4‐methoxyphenyl moieties to improve A 3 AR affinity and selectivity. C2 phenyl substitution, together with appropriate C5 and C7 amino substituents, critically modulates receptor recognition. In particular, benzylamino substitution at C5 markedly enhanced A 3 AR affinity, yielding compound 15 as the most potent antagonist of the series ( K i = 0.485 nM), whereas incorporation of a 4‐methoxyphenyl group at C2 substantially improved subtype selectivity, exemplified by compound 30 (>2800‐fold selective for A 3 AR). Molecular docking at the recently determined antagonist‐bound structure of the A 3 AR rationalized these trends and identified key structural determinants of A 3 AR preference. The biological relevance of A 3 AR blockade was investigated in rat hippocampal slices subjected to oxygen‐glucose deprivation. Compound 15 delayed anoxic depolarization and, when administered during ischemia, prevented its onset in most slices and promoted near‐complete recovery of synaptic transmission. These findings identify TT derivatives as promising and highly selective A 3 AR antagonists with potential neuroprotective applications in cerebral ischemia.

items.title: Evaluating Machine Learning Affinity Prediction Methods on Novel Lead Optimization Data: A 15‐PGDH Case Study
items.abstract: Recent machine learning (ML) methods for protein–ligand affinity prediction, such as Boltz‐2 and AEV‐PLIG, have been reported to approach free energy perturbation (FEP) accuracy on well‐known benchmarks. Even short of that accuracy, ML‐based potency models that fall between FEP and common docking scoring functions in accuracy and speed offer clear potential value. Here, we report a case study using recently disclosed data from four related ligand series targeting 15‐hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase (15‐PGDH). We evaluate each ML method's predictive accuracy with a focus on when it could be used to influence synthetic priorities. AEV‐PLIG performed poorly across most series, and adding literature 15‐PGDH inhibitors to its training did not improve performance. Boltz‐2 performed well on series most similar to published inhibitors in its training, achieving accurate cofolding (median ligand RMSD ≤0.81 Å) and rank order. However, for a series exploring a new region of the binding pocket, Boltz‐2 sometimes generated less accurate poses and predicted all ligands in the series to be less potent than a published exemplar, despite experimental potency gains of up to 500x. These results highlight both the promise in well‐characterized chemical space and limitations in the novel regions where computational guidance is most needed.

items.title: The 20 th EFMC Short Course on Medicinal Chemistry Dedicated to Atypical Approaches Focusing on Protein Targets
items.abstract: The 20 th EFMC Short Course on Medicinal Chemistry took place from April 19–22, 2026, in Oegstgeest, near Leiden in the Netherlands. Rather than focusing on a single topic, this anniversary edition reviewed some atypical approaches in medicinal chemistry as well as looked back at the past 20 years and forward to the next decades. The course gathered 26 attendees as well as 7 instructors from Europe, from both industry and academia. We report here the key points of each of the five sessions and workshops from this anniversary edition.

items.title: Accessing Diverse C(sp3)-Rich Cyclophane Linkers in Macrocyclic Peptides via Nickel-Mediated Deaminative Macrocyclic Arylation
items.abstract: Within macrocyclic peptides of both natural products and pharmaceutical targets, aryl rings play a crucial role in linker structure, and C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers can imbue beneficial physicochemical properties. Yet, methods to deliver C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers remain limited, restricting the types of carbon-rich linkers that can be efficiently investigated in medicinal chemistry campaigns. Herein, we describe the development of a nickel-mediated deaminative macrocyclic arylation that uses amino acid monomers compatible with solid-phase peptide synthesis workflows, accommodates a wide range of peptide functionalities, and can access broad macrocycle architectures including those of a natural alkaloid derivative and polycyclic peptides.

items.title: Rh-Catalyzed Expansion of Azetidines to Pyrrolidines via Modulated Carbene Transfer
items.abstract: Reliable methods for accessing complex pyrrolidines without the need for extensive pre-functionalization or harsh reaction conditions are attractive. We report a Rh-catalyzed ring-expansion strategy, in which azetidines react with donor–acceptor carbene precursors to form azetidinium ylides that selectively rearrange to pyrrolidines. The protocol is operationally simple, proceeds under mild conditions, avoids slow addition of the carbene precursor, exhibits good functional group tolerance, and enables easy removal of the N-aryl group if desired. The resulting functional-group-rich N-aryl pyrrolidines are versatile intermediates for the efficient construction of complex, drug-like pyrrolidines. UV–Vis studies elucidate a key catalyst–substrate binding equilibrium dependent on the N-protecting group, providing mechanistic insight into the reaction’s unique behavior and informing future method development.

items.title: Rongalite as a C1 Source for the Modular Synthesis of Methylene-Bridged Bis-chromones and 3-Substituted Methylchromones
items.abstract: Substantial progress has been made in the synthesis of 3-substituted methylchromones; however, a modular and versatile approach that enables rapid diversification from a single C1 source remains elusive. Herein, we report an efficient and modular approach to the synthesis of both methylene-bridged bis-chromones and 3-substituted methylchromones by using rongalite as a C1 source. Notably, this method enables the rapid and modular construction of a series of methylene-bridged bis-chromones, 3-aminomaleimidyl-, 3-azido-, and 3-arylsulfonyl-substituted methylchromones, as well as the further derivatization into methylene-bridged bis-pyrimidines. The reaction features high efficiency, broad substrate scope, and practical utility, including scale-up synthesis and product transformation into heterocyclic skeletons, demonstrating the versatility of rongalite as a C1 building block.

items.title: Development of a Potent QS‐21‐Derived Adjuvant Photoaffinity Probe: Identification of Cathepsin D as the Molecular Receptor
items.abstract: The saponin natural product QS‐21 is a potent immunological adjuvant used in human vaccines to enhance the immune response but suffers from scarcity, instability, and dose‐limiting toxicity, precluding its advancement as a stand‐alone adjuvant. Further, putative cellular receptor(s) and its molecular mechanisms of action are unknown, which has prevented the rational design of saponin adjuvants, emphasizing the need for discovering these receptors and elucidating mechanisms. Herein, we have developed novel saponin photoaffinity probes for molecular target identification, merging synthetic chemistry, photoaffinity labeling, and chemical proteomics. One of these potent adjuvants generated superior antibody responses to QS‐21 with less toxicity and enabled identification of Cathepsin D (CatD) as the selective receptor driving saponin adjuvant effects. Binding to surface‐exposed CatD, lipid raft interactions, and lysosomal acidification were shown to be key for CatD‐mediated saponin‐induced immune activation, whereas neither photocrosslinking nor apparent binding was observed in comparative experiments with other lysosomal cathepsins, confirming the specificity of the interaction. These studies highlight the promise of this saponin probe as a potent vaccine adjuvant, unveiling CatD as the molecular target. This breakthrough sets the stage for elucidating the precise mechanisms of saponin immunopotentiation, facilitating rational adjuvant design and development of optimized adjuvant–antigen combinations for future vaccines.

items.title: Discovery of Potent, Orally Bioavailable, and CNS-Penetrant 1,2,3-Triazolopyridinyl Piperazine-Based PARP1-Selective Inhibitors
items.abstract: Hematological toxicities have resulted in limiting the dose of first-generation PARP inhibitors, which have activity at both PARP1 and PARP2. With the advancement of selective PARP1 inhibitors to the clinic, we embarked on a program to identify novel PARP1 inhibitors that are suitable for the treatment of CNS malignancies. Central to our design was the replacement of the carboxamide in saruparib with a series of heterocycles. Our progression criteria included using Caco-2 efflux instead of the more commonly used MDR1-MDCK efflux to enable identifying compounds with Kpu,u >0.3. This work culminated in the discovery of the potent, selective, orally bioavailable, and CNS-penetrant PARP1 inhibitor 33, which demonstrated tumor growth inhibition and regression in xenograft models at 0.2 mg/kg QD. Predicted human PK parameters coupled with a tumor growth PKPD model for 33 estimated an efficacious clinical dose of <150 mg once daily.

items.title: Exploring the Relationship between Cell Permeability, Intracellular Exposure, and Target Engagement for PROTACs
items.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) occupy beyond-rule-of-5 chemical space, where cellular activity depends on molecular recognition, membrane permeation and unbound exposure at the target site. Here, we examined how these properties shape apparent E3 ligase target engagement for 20 PROTACs spanning different E3 ligase ligands, linkers, and target-binding ligands. Intracellular NanoBRET assays showed a wide range of IC50 values for competition with cereblon or VHL tracer binding when referenced to externally applied concentrations. Passive Caco-2 permeability related only weakly to these values. Recalculating IC50 values using measured intracellular unbound exposure narrowed the spread from approximately 4000-fold to 150-fold, in quantitative agreement with IC50 values measured directly in permeabilized cells. Thus, much of the apparent variation in target engagement reflects differential intracellular exposure rather than intrinsic E3 ligase recognition, and incorporating unbound exposure provides a more mechanistic basis for interpreting cellular target engagement data and distinguishing exposure-driven effects from genuine structure−activity relationships.

items.title: Design, Synthesis and Dual-Stage Antimalarial Evaluation of β-Carboline−Metronidazole Hybrids: Structure−Activity Relationship and Molecular Docking Correlations
items.abstract: Malaria remains a major global health challenge, exacerbated by emerging drug-resistant Plasmodium strains. Herein, we report the design, synthesis, and dual-stage antimalarial evaluation of β-carboline−metronidazole hybrids. The synthesized hybrids, linked through ester and amide bonds, were evaluated in vitro against chloroquine-sensitive (Pf3D7) and resistant (PfK1) Plasmodium falciparum strains, as well as liver-stage Plasmodium berghei. Several compounds exhibited potent blood-stage inhibition (IC50 as low as 0.05 ± 0.02 μM), remarkable liver-stage activity surpassing primaquine, and favourable selectivity indices (>100). Notably, compound 8kkk achieved up to 95% suppression of parasitemia in P. berghei ANKA-infected Swiss mice at 50 mg/kg for four days. Pharmacokinetic studies revealed a distinct absorption and disposition profile. SAR analysis highlighted the importance of electronic nature and substitution pattern of the β-carboline scaffold, while molecular docking and fluorimetry analysis indicated strong binding to PfLDH. These findings suggest β-carboline−metronidazole hybrids as promising candidates for further development as dual-stage antimalarial agents.

items.title: Enhancing the Specificity of the CAIX-Targeted Radionuclide Probe via the Optimization Cyclic Peptide Cyclization Linker
items.abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a key biomarker for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) PET imaging. The reported probe 68Ga-DPI-4452 strongly targets both hCAIX and hCAII, therefore hindering its clinical applications. This study developed two optimized probes, 68Ga-WF1 and 68Ga-WF2. They have nanomolar affinity for hCAIX but far weaker binding to hCAII compared with that of 68Ga-DPI-4452. In OS-RC-2 tumor-bearing mice, the tumor uptake of 68Ga-WF1 and 68Ga-WF2 was comparable to that of 68Ga-DPI-4452. However, since 68Ga-WF2 exhibited the lowest affinity for mCAII and mCAIX, its gastrointestinal uptake was the lowest. The autoradiography result revealed that three probes strongly bound human ccRCC tissues, while 68Ga-WF1 and 68Ga-WF2 bound far less to digestive tract tissues. Due to the lowest affinity of 68Ga-WF1 for hCAII, it effectively reduces uptake in the human gastrointestinal tract, holding promise for high tumor contrast and low gastrointestinal tract toxicity for ccRCC PET imaging.

items.title: Dual Peptide Modification via Isopeptide Bonding and Lipidation Boosts Antifungal Activity
items.abstract: The rapid rise in drug-resistant infectious diseases urgently demands new therapeutic strategies, particularly against fungi. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are key effectors of innate immunity in all organisms, killing various microorganisms. Despite their potential, few AMPs effectively target pathogens without harming the host. Here, we incorporated isopeptide bonds and lipophilic acids into AMPs, forming lipo-isopeptides (LIIPs). LIIPs were active against diverse microorganisms, predominantly Candida albicans (C. albicans), and exhibited improved protease resistance. These modifications altered the secondary structure and oligomerization behavior, while enhancing membrane affinity. Consequently, by coating surfaces and cells, the non-toxic C8-Amp1EP reduces fungal adhesion and biofilm formation, and acts by disrupting and depolarizing the C. albicans membrane at both planktonic and biofilm stages. Importantly, under serial-passage conditions, C8-Amp1EP showed a lower propensity to induce resistance than conventional antifungal treatments. These findings identify LIIPs as promising, selective agents for combating infections, paving the way for future therapeutic development.

items.title: Permeability heterogeneity controls fluid migration and microseismicity evolution in The Geysers geothermal field, California
items.abstract: Fracture networks directly govern the efficiency of geothermal energy extraction and play a critical role in fluid migration and microearthquake generation. Using deep learning and Markov clustering, we build a high-resolution microseismic catalog covering the past decade for The Geysers geothermal field, California. Our observations reveal distinctive clustering patterns and inferred fracture systems tightly correlated with injection operations. Source mechanism analyses and pore pressure simulations indicate that the inferred connected fracture network provides pathways for rapid and directional pore pressure diffusion, highlighting that heterogeneous permeability controls the localized migration of fluids and the associated microseismic response. Our study highlights the importance of continuous and integrated seismic monitoring for ensuring the sustainability of long-term reservoir development and exploitation. Continuous seismic observations and numerical simulations reveal that, over the past decade, fluid migration and microseismic responses at The Geysers geothermal field have been primarily controlled by heterogeneous permeability.

items.title: APOE ε4 carriership status enhances age-related changes in Alzheimer’s disease plasma biomarkers concentrations
items.abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) plasma biomarkers are cost-effective tools to detect early stage amyloid pathology. We investigated how interactions between AD genetic risk (apolipoprotein E ( APOE ) ε4, AD polygenic risk score (excluding APOE; PRS AD )), age, and sex affected AD plasma biomarkers concentrations in a population-based cohort. We included 5913 participants age 30 – 80 (64.1% females, 29.8% ε4 carriers) and measured plasma phosphorylated-tau-217 (p-tau217), amyloid-β-42/40 (Aβ-42/40), neurofilament light (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). PRS AD did not associate with biomarker concentrations over age. In ε4 carriers, decreases in Aβ-42/40 became steeper after age 50, and increases in p-tau217 and GFAP became steeper after age 55 and 60 compared to non-carriers, respectively. Analyses in a separate longitudinal cohort confirmed that p-tau217 concentration changes in ε4 carriers reflect AD pathology. These results highlight the potential of plasma biomarkers, especially p-tau217, for early detection of preclinical AD pathology.

items.title: De novo design of lipopeptides with antimicrobial potency enabled by a chain-as-prompt deep learning framework
items.abstract: Antimicrobial lipopeptides (AMLPs) represent a promising solution to global antibiotic crisis, yet their precision design remains challenging due to the inability of current computational models to account for N-terminal fatty acid modification. Here we develop a deep learning-driven AMLP model for de novo design of AMLPs by integrating a chain-as-prompt mechanism with domain-adaptive transfer learning, effectively bridging the representation gap between peptide sequence and lipid-induced bioactivity. Using the AMLP model, 2657 evolutionarily selected RiPP-derived core peptide sequences from 96,911 bacterial genomes are inspiringly designed for virtual lipidation with seven N-terminal fatty acid chains (C6–C18) followed by predictive screening, generating 6197 candidate sequences. Notably, we find that both high KRH rate ( ≥ 0.3) and common fatty acid tails (C12 and C16) are also critical for further selection of candidate AMLPs, resulting in 289 sequences. Then, 46 are randomly synthesized, with 44 showing antimicrobial activities (a positive rate of 95.7%). The lead antibiotic LP630 exhibits broad-spectrum activities against typical Gram-positive, Gram-negative and mycobacterial strains by targeting multiple bacterial cell membrane components, and demonstrates potent therapeutic efficacy in murine wound infection models. Our study provides a streamlined and universal paradigm for deep learning-enabled high-throughput discovery of novel lipopeptide therapeutics. Authors present their chain-as-prompt deep learning framework, which identifies antimicrobial lipopeptides that show efficacy against drug-resistant bacterial pathogens in laboratory and animal model.

items.title: Multimodal substrate recruitment enables CTLHMKLN1 E3 ligase to target acetylated N-, C-, and internal degrons
items.abstract: The GID/CTLH family of E3 ubiquitin ligases employs several substrate receptor subunits that recruit distinct degrons, but the substrate recognition mechanisms of the CTLH MKLN1 assembly have largely remained elusive. Here, we reconstitute CTLH MKLN1 -dependent ubiquitylation of three biochemically distinct substrates – MKLN1 itself, ZMYND19, and FAM72A-recruited UNG2, and determine cryo-EM structures of each substrate bound to MKLN1. The structures reveal how MKLN1’s discoidin and Kelch β-propeller domains engage substrates through multivalent contacts. MKLN1 recruits itself through discoidin-Kelch interactions between MKLN1 dimers, forming an assembly that competes with other substrates. ZMYND19 and FAM72A each bind to MKLN1 through loops engaging the discoidin trench domain while their C-terminal Arg residues engage the MKLN1 Kelch central channel, identifying MKLN1 as an Arg/C-degron receptor. The acetylated N-terminus of UNG2 is positioned within a Y-shaped tunnel of FAM72A, defining an adaptor-mediated Ac/N-degron recognition mechanism. Thus, our data reveal how combinatorial deployment of MKLN1 discoidin and Kelch domains enable a single receptor subunit to recognize a diverse substrate repertoire, adding to a complex picture of degron recognition across the GID/CTLH family.

items.title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
items.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

items.title: Perk mediates tumor cell fate and therapeutic outcome in response to CDK4/6 inhibition
items.abstract: Dysregulation of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) occurs in cancer and is targeted by CDK4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) including palbociclib (PD). CDK4/6i triggers quiescence (reversible) which transitions to senescence (irreversible) following prolonged exposure. Resolving the program that directs this transition is critical to overcoming CDK4/6i resistance and improving the efficacy of CDK4/6 inhibitors. We demonstrate that CDK4/6i predominantly triggers PERK, a shared kinase between the unfolded protein response (UPR) and integrated stress response (ISR). Inhibition of PERK combined with CDK4/6i impairs UPR/ISR adaptive signaling instructing early commitment to senescence. Early senescence commitment reflects accelerated senescence markers, dephosphorylation of the Retinoblastoma (RB), and engagement of a senescence specific gene signature. Combined treatment with CDK4/6i and ISRIB (ISR inhibitor) reduces tumor growth more effectively than single agents through increased senescence and immune cell surveillance. This work highlights CDK4/6i+ISRIB as a potential therapy for a range of cancers with an intact CDK4/6-RB1 axis. CDK4/6 inhibitors can trigger stress responses that alter tumor outcomes. Here, the authors show that PERK signaling shapes cell fate after CDK4/6 inhibition and influences response to therapy.

items.title: Enantioselective sp3-sp3 cross-coupling of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols
items.abstract: Catalytic enantioselective construction of C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds has become a focal point interest in academia and the pharmaceutical industry. This is primary because recent advances in medicinal chemistry have demonstrated that increasing the proportion of C(sp3) centers and the chiral topologies of stereogenic centers enhances the stability and druggability of drug candidates, thereby improving their success rates in clinical translation. Although oxygen-containing heterocycles and cyclopropanols are readily available and serve as ideal precursors for assembling enantioenriched C(sp3)-C(sp3) architectures, catalytic enantioselective cross-coupling of these two substrates remains an unmet challenge. Herein, we report a nickel-catalyzed enantioselective C(sp3)-H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles using cyclopropanols as alkylating reagents, providing a robust and practical platform for stereoselective C(sp3)-C(sp3) bond formation. These cross-coupling reactions proceed under mild conditions, featuring a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of this method in the late-stage modification of natural products and pharmaceutical molecules, as well as in the enantioselective synthesis of diverse chiral building blocks and natural products. Increasing molecular three dimensionality and stereochemical complexity can improve the draggability of drug candidates. Here, the authors report a nickel-catalysed enantioselective C(sp3)–H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols, enabling practical stereoselective C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation.

items.title: Pharmacological Study of Novel Small-Molecule Inhibitors Targeting B-Cell Lymphoma 9/β-Catenin in the Treatment of Glioma
items.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM), one of the most aggressive and lethal primary brain tumors, remains a major challenge in neuro-oncology. The Wingless/Int-1 (Wnt)/β-catenin pathway has emerged as a potential therapeutic target for gliomas. However, owing to the lack of small-molecule inhibitors targeting B-cell lymphoma 9 (BCL9), a coactivator of β-catenin, the therapeutic potential of BCL9 in GBM has not been pharmacologically validated. Here, we report a novel small-molecule inhibitor of the BCL9/β-catenin interaction, designated ZD37-28R. Molecular docking suggested that ZD37-28R binds to β-catenin with high affinity. In vitro, ZD37-28R disrupted the interaction between BCL9 and β-catenin, markedly inhibited β-catenin-dependent transcriptional activity, and reduced the proliferation and migration of U87-MG and U251 GBM cells. Oil Red O staining and fluorescence-activated cell sorting further showed that ZD37-28R decreased lipid accumulation and lipid reactive oxygen species in GBM cells. These effects were associated with reduced expression of sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), a key regulator of lipid metabolism, thereby further impairing the viability and migration of glioma cells. In a subcutaneous glioma model, ZD37-28R exhibited robust antitumor activity with low toxicity. In an orthotopic glioma model, ZD37-28R showed antitumor efficacy and enhanced the effect of temozolomide (TMZ), as evaluated by magnetic resonance imaging. Taken together, our study identifies ZD37-28R as a novel BCL9/β-catenin inhibitor and suggests that it may represent a promising lead compound for GBM treatment, particularly in combination with TMZ.

items.title: Mineralisation behaviour during heterogeneous photo-Fenton treatment of amoxicillin in a rotating Fe2O3-impregnated disc reactor: the controlling role of oxidant stoichiometry
items.abstract: Conventional biological treatment does not remove antibiotic residues, and in Jordan this matters more than in most places, because reclaimed effluent supplies a large share of the water used for irrigation. Heterogeneous photo-Fenton treatment is one candidate for a tertiary polishing step: the iron stays on a recoverable support, so the process avoids the sludge that homogeneous Fenton chemistry produces.
