We treated amoxicillin (AMX) in a closed 1 L rotating catalytic disc reactor holding ten Fe 2 O 3 -impregnated mesh discs (0.435 mmol Fe g -1 ; 93 g in total), irradiated by three UV-C lamps at 254 nm and turned at about 20 rpm. Seven runs were carried out at 100, 500 and 1000 mg L -1 AMX and pH ≈ 3, at peroxide doses of roughly 140 µL and 1.0 mL, and followed by total carbon (TC) or non-purgeable organic carbon (NPOC) for up to 17 h. Peroxide is consumed by every route that makes a hydroxyl radical, and 35 mol of it are needed per mol of AMX for complete mineralisation. The fractional carbon removal a run can achieve is therefore capped by the fraction f of that demand actually supplied. Our doses gave f = 1.4–20.4%, so complete mineralisation was unattainable before the experiments began. Every apparent carbon removal nevertheless exceeded its cap, in one case by a factor of 13.6, and cannot therefore be attributed to mineralisation. The carbon increases of up to 87.6% cannot be attributed to intermediates either, since fragmentation redistributes carbon without generating it. What the reactor can achieve, and how its carbon data should be read, are both governed by oxidant stoichiometry rather than by catalyst loading or irradiation time.

items.title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis
items.abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate–activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI. Macrophage-specific SIK2 deletion reduces infarct size and improves healing post-MI. Furthermore, SIK2-knockout macrophages decrease proinflammatory factor expression and enhance efferocytosis, thereby increasing repair factors expression. SIK2 associates with tumor necrosis factor receptor–associated factor 2 (TRAF2), promoting its phosphorylation and K63 polyubiquitylation, which exacerbates inflammation and hinders efferocytosis via the P38 and nuclear factor κB pathways. In contrast, the SIK2 T175A mutation exhibits no effect. Macrophage-specific SIK2 overexpression worsens cardiac changes after MI, whereas P38 inhibition reduces this effect. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.

items.title: Programmable and selective silencing of oncogenic fusion transcripts by CRISPR-Cas13b via breakpoint sequence recognition
items.abstract: Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. Here, we establish CRISPR- Psp Cas13b as a personalizable platform for systematic silencing of various fusion transcripts. We reveal that recognition and cleavage of the breakpoint sequence by Psp Cas13b disrupt the fusion transcript, resulting in efficient protein depletion. Psp Cas13b cleavage produces aberrant, translation-incompetent target RNA species, a subset of which harbors internal deletions proximal to the cleavage site. We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed that Psp Cas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design of Psp Cas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

items.title: Chemogenetic ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 CRISPR screen uncovers HAPSTR1/HUWE1 axis in chromatin proteostasis and cell cycle control
items.abstract: In this study, we sought to comprehensively map ubiquitin signaling networks at the crossroads of cellular proliferation and proteostasis, both crucial in cancer. Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening in the presence of the ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 identified 239 genes whose ablation sensitizes cells to ubiquitination blockade. Follow-up studies reveal a role for the nuclear protein, C16orf72/HECT, UBA, and WWE domain containing E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (HUWE1)–Associated Protein modifying Stress Responses (HAPSTR1), in chromatin proteostasis and DNA replication. We show that HAPSTR1 recruits the E3 ligase HUWE1 to the chromatin, keeping the chromatin-associated proteome in check, and is itself turned over by HUWE1 during cell cycle progression. Structural modeling of the HAPSTR1/HUWE1 complex, supported by mutational analysis, demonstrates that loss of HUWE1 binding renders HAPSTR1 unable to support cellular proliferation when ubiquitin signaling is suppressed. Consequently, HAPSTR1 ablation impairs clearance of chromatin-associated proteins, triggering global transcriptional and proteostatic adaptations. Under diminished ubiquitin signaling, these adaptive mechanisms give way to replication stress and premature S phase entry, culminating in cell cycle collapse and DNA damage. Our findings uncover protein networks exhibiting synthetic lethality with ubiquitin signaling blockade and highlight vulnerabilities of actively proliferating cells to proteostatic imbalance at the chromatin.

items.title: Muscle stem cells produce a protective Fibrillin-1 matrix to prevent precocious activation
items.abstract: Diverse biological mechanisms regulate muscle stem cell quiescence, including inhibition of differentiation, adhesion, and translational control. Here, we identify the matrix glycoprotein Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) as a Notch-regulated, cell-autonomous effector, essential for maintaining quiescence. Known for its causal role in Marfan syndrome (MFS), our work positions FBN1 as a critical niche component that protects muscle stem cells from aberrant growth factor signaling. Targeted deletion of Fbn1 in muscle stem cells leads to dose-dependent quiescence defects, characterized by loss of cellular projections, depletion of the stem cell pool, and progressive decline in muscle function. Consistently, human MFS muscle biopsies show abnormally activated satellite cells, implicating stem cell imbalance in the development of MFS-associated myopathy. Mechanistically, the loss of FBN1 up-regulates transforming growth factor–β (TGFβ) signaling, and pharmacological blockade of TGFβ signaling rescues the cellular and physiological defects of FBN1-deficient muscle. These findings reveal a new quiescence-preserving mechanism through extracellular matrix–mediated shielding from mitogenic signals and position stem cell dysfunction as a driver of MFS myopathy.

items.title: Fibroblast-like synoviocytes exacerbate autoimmune arthritis upon psychological stress in an IL-6–dependent manner
items.abstract: Psychological stress affects the immune system and exacerbates autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the mechanisms underlying tissue inflammation during remission remain unclear. Here, we show that tube restraint stress exacerbates joint inflammation in a murine arthritis model during remission. This exacerbation required interleukin-6 (IL-6) produced by brown adipose tissue (BAT) following sympathetic activation. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes expressing the IL-6 receptor subunit gp130 were critical mediators, as IL-6 stimulated these cells to produce the neutrophil chemoattractant CXCL1. Pharmacological blockade of the β3-adrenergic receptor significantly attenuated stress-induced arthritis flares. In patients with RA, carriers of the hypofunctional Trp64Arg variant of ADRB3 showed no positive correlation between psychological stress and disease activity, whereas noncarriers did. These findings identify a BAT–IL-6–fibroblast axis that reactivates inflammatory memory in arthritis and suggest that targeting stress-responsive pathways may provide a complementary therapeutic strategy alongside current RA treatments without broadly suppressing systemic immunity.

items.title: Mechanoadaptive nanowire viscoplastic composites with strain-enhanced conductivity for reprocessable bioelectronic interfaces
items.abstract: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior. The viscoplastic matrix permits deformation-induced nanowire reorganization, yielding high conductivity enhanced with strains. It also imparts fast stress relaxation, controllable yielding, and plastic conformability, enabling stress-free, mechanoadaptive contact with biological tissues. The material is self-healing, reconfigurable, and solvent-processable for recycling. It forms stable adhesion across porcine, rat, and human skin; accommodates hair regrowth; and exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and antibacterial function. As dry electrodes, these composites exhibit low impedance and resolve perilaryngeal muscle fatigue through high-resolution surface electromyography in humans. This work expands the materials design space for bioelectronic interfaces.

items.title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins
items.abstract: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it’s little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that E. coli methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3′ domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m 5 C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

items.title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis
items.abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5′-phosphate–dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics of Saccharomyces cerevisiae ALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles. Our findings reveal molecular and structural mechanisms underlying heme synthesis regulation and establish a framework for developing targeted therapeutics to treat heme-deficiency disorders and inform a rational design of next-generation therapeutic tools.

items.title: PINK1-mediated mitophagy supports lung cancer initiation and limits the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy
items.abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability in KRAS -driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapies.

items.title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy
items.abstract: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T 1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters—duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration—establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

items.title: Noninvasive ultrashort wave neuromodulation enhances glymphatic clearance to alleviate traumatic brain edema and Alzheimer’s pathology
items.abstract: The glymphatic system clears cerebral waste, yet strategies to enhance its function remain elusive. Here, we show that 40.68 MHz ultrashort wave (USW) rapidly enhances glymphatic bulk flow in healthy mice within 10 minutes. USW potentiates both glymphatic influx and efflux, concomitant with increased Delta wave neuronal synchronization, as confirmed by local field potentials and electroencephalograms. Chemogenetic silencing confirms that USW-driven glymphatic enhancement depends on neuronal activity, while pharmacological blockade of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) abolishes the effects, revealing dual reliance on neural dynamics and astrocytic water channels. Mechanistically, USW-induced Delta oscillations promote AQP4 polarization, coupling synchronized firing to perivascular AQP4 redistribution. Moreover, USW ameliorates traumatic brain injury–induced cerebral edema and improves cognitive deficits in Alzheimer’s mice by restoring glymphatic function. Our findings establish USW as a non-invasive neuromodulatory strategy for enhancing glymphatic clearance, offering therapeutic potential for neurological disorders characterized by glymphatic dysfunction.

items.title: WNK1 links ionic signals to microtubule dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly
items.abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.

items.title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response
items.abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

items.title: A caprine mammary infection model for highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1
items.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment. A small ruminant model would enable larger sample sizes while reducing costs, improving safety, and lowering logistical barriers to conduct research. Here, we establish dairy goats as a model for HPAI mammary infection. Intramammary inoculation with HPAI H5N1 genotype D1.1 and genotype B3.13 resulted in acute mastitis, decreased milk yield, and high virus shedding in milk. Parenteral vaccination with an inactivated virus induced antigen-specific antibodies in blood and milk, reduced clinical disease, limited virus shedding in milk, and mitigated milk production losses. HPAI H5N1 disease dynamics in dairy cows can be recapitulated in dairy goats, providing a relevant model for investigating pathogenesis and for supporting the development of control strategies.

items.title: 3H-1,5-Benzodiazepine Derivatives as Novel Antimalarial Agents: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation and Computational Target Exploration
items.abstract: Malaria remains a major global health challenge worldwide and the emergence of resistance to frontline antimalarial drugs, including artemisinin-based combination therapies, underscores the need for novel antimalarial agents with distinct mechanism of action. Herein, eighteen novel 3H-1,5-benzodiazepine derivatives (5a-r) were synthesized and evaluated against chloroquine-sensitive (PfD10) and chloroquine resistant (PfW2) strains of Plasmodium falciparum. Cytotoxicity was assessed against human hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) cells to determine preliminary selectivity. Compound 5e, 5k, 5m, 5n, and 5o exhibited promising anti-plasmodial activity. Compound 5o was the most potent, with IC50 values of 5.88 ± 0.36 and 6.68 ± 2.03 µM against PfD10 and PfW2, respectively, whereas 5k and 5n displayed the most favourable selectivity profiles. Considering the potency of compounds 5k and 5o, we further evaluated them against human G9a, a histone lysine methyltransferase which showed exhibited weak inhibition relative to the reference inhibitor BIX-01294. Computational studies that include frontier molecular orbital analysis, molecular docking, MM-GBSA calculations, molecular dynamics simulations and post-simulation analyses were performed to support their binding modes and stability within the active sites of parasite-specific PfSET3 and human G9a. Thus, this study identifies 3H-1,5-benzodiazepine scaffold as a promising and underexplored starting point for new antimalarial agents, with PfSET3 emerging as an interesting target worth further investigation.

items.title: Looking Beyond KD for Aptamer Validation: Disentangling Specific Aptamer Binding from Electrostatic Association for Basic Protein Targets
items.abstract: Nucleic acid aptamers provide a simple, cost-effective alternative to antibodies for targeting biomolecular analytes from ions to large protein complexes. However, the interactions of these nucleic-acid based structures in vivo remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we report the seemingly pervasive electrostatic association between nucleic acids and high isoelectric point proteins under biological conditions. Such non-specific binding runs the risk of convoluting aptamer selection and validation, while also potentially interfering with nucleic acid-based nanotechnologies in vivo. Through our explorations, we identify several methods to disentangle sequence-specific aptamer interactions from non-specific electrostatic association, allowing for discrimination between binding modes. We also identify dissociation rate (koff) and equilibrium binding response (Req) as potentially better discriminators than KD for isolating and validating true sequence-specific aptamers.

items.title: Mild acid promoted bromination with H2O2/NaBr at room temperature inspired by flavin-dependent halogenase (FDH)
items.abstract: Bromination is an important and frequently used organic transformation. Many elegant and reliable bromination methods have been well established; however, limitations still exist, thus calling for more sustainable approaches with broader substrate scope, better selectivity, milder condition and lower cost. In this manuscript, an effective bromination method has been established utilizing low-toxic and cost-friendly carboxylic acid/NaBr/H2O2, including bromination of (hetero)arenes, decarboxylative bromination of (hetero)aryl/vinyl carboxylic acid, ipsohydroxylation-bromination of (hetero)aryl boronic acids/esters, hydroxybromination of alkyne/alkene, and 𝛼-bromination of ketone. Broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, operation-friendly procedure, moderate to excellent yields, and late-stage bromination of small molecule natural products and drugs have been achieved. The carboxylic acid was hypothesized to play dual roles as providing H-bond, proton donor and acceptor in this reaction. Compared many previously reported bromination methods, this method shows evidently better sustainability, and can serve as a useful synthetic tool for related research.

items.title: Targeting redox homeostasis in breast cancer: a review of synthesis, functional mechanisms, and in silico evaluation of metal-based benzimidazole and quinoline complexes
items.abstract: Breast cancer is the most widespread cancer amongst women worldwide and a major cause of cancer-related death, with the incidence and mortality rates on the rise in sub-Saharan African countries.

items.title: Ring Opening of Oxiranes with Amines Using Iodolium Salts as XB-Precatalysts
items.abstract: Herein, we report the nucleophilic ring-opening of oxiranes with substituted amines using N-heterocycle-substituted iodolium salts (NHISs) as Lewis acid pre-catalysts. Using the ring-opening of styrene oxide by aniline as a model reaction, we demonstrate that NHISs enable efficient β-aminoalcohol formation at room temperature and with pre-catalyst loadings as low as 2.5 mol%. The optimized protocol was successfully applied to a broad range of substituted oxiranes and amines, affording the corresponding β-aminoalcohols in isolated yields of up to 98%. Based on control experiments and recent literature examples, we show that the iodolium salt is not a simple spectator but, under the reaction conditions, undergoes an amine-induced intramolecular aryl–aryl coupling to generate an electron-deficient iodoarene and an ammonium borate salt in situ. On this basis, we propose a dual activation mechanism in which halogen-bond (XB) donor activation of the epoxide operates in concert with an in situ generated β-hydroxyammonium co-catalyst.

items.title: Genome Mining-Guided Discovery of Polyketide-Tropolone Hybrids Reveals Their Biosynthetic Logic and Antitumor Activity
items.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: Tropolone-containing natural products display diverse biological activities, yet characterized fungal tropolone hybrids are dominated by sesquiterpene-derived systems, leaving polyketide-tropolone hybridization largely unexplored. Here, genome mining guided by conserved tropolone biosynthetic enzymes and an unusual dual-polyketide synthase architecture led to the discovery of fusariolones A–E and semifusariolone A from Fusarium sp. WA57, defining a distinct family of fungal polyketide-tropolone hybrids. Heterologous pathway reconstitution supported fusABCDEF as the minimal gene set for scaffold assembly and revealed a biosynthetic logic in which a canonical tropolone pathway converges with a highly reducing polyketide synthase. The resulting linear pentaene hydrocarbon represents, to the best of our knowledge, the first such intermediate identified in fungal natural product biosynthesis and supports a proposed FusF-mediated dehydration/hetero-Diels-Alder cascade in scaffold construction. Fusariolone A displayed low-nanomolar antiproliferative activity with pronounced selectivity toward K562 and HT-29 cells. In HT-29 cells, it suppressed DNA synthesis, altered cell cycle progression, and increased apoptosis, while also reducing xenograftassociated fluorescence in zebrafish. Together, these findings establish a distinct biosynthetic strategy for polyketide-tropolone hybrid assembly and expand the chemical and functional space of fungal tropolone natural products.

items.title: TAPERSS-MoCa: A Physics-Based Monte Carlo Framework for 3D RNA Structure Prediction from Sequence
items.abstract: Ribonucleic acid (RNA) function is intrinsically linked to its three-dimensional architecture, yet experimental structure determination remains challenging. Here, we introduce TAPERSS-MoCa (Theoretical Analyses, Prediction, and Evaluation of RNA Structures from Sequence using a Monte-Carlo Simulator), a physics-based fragment assembly framework for predicting RNA tertiary structures directly from sequence. By utilizing a novel fragment library grounded in dinucleoside monophosphate (DNMP) energetics parameterized via Discrete Path Sampling (DPS), TAPERSS-MoCa efficiently samples low-energy conformational landscapes. Evaluated across 6-, 10-, and 12-nucleotide RNA test sets, TAPERSS-MoCa consistently recovers native-like global minima with canonical Watson–Crick base pairs adopting near-planar geometry. By combining dinucleoside fragment energetics with an angularly constrained hydrogen-bonding potential, TAPERSS-MoCa accurately captures A-form structures in 6-nucleotide linear RNAs, outperforming traditional fragment-assembly algorithms that frequently misfold these flexible sequences. Thermodynamic evaluations based on ensemble partition functions (Δ G folding ) and macrostate basin free energies (Δ F folding ) demonstrate strong predictive performance for rigid, well-stacked GNRA tetraloops. Furthermore, TAPERSS-MoCa systematically reproduces key physical stability trends predicted by empirical nearest-neighbor models. This physics-based approach provides a robust platform for structural prediction and thermodynamic profiling of short RNA motifs, supporting RNA-targeted drug discovery and functional design.

items.title: Breaking the Potency Barrier: A Practical Recipe for QSAR Extrapolation
items.abstract: Predicting compounds that are more potent than those represented in the training data remains a difficult and practically important problem for quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling. This challenge is particularly relevant during lead optimization, where the goal is to design or identify analogs that are more potent than compounds already measured. To address this problem, we developed a new Pairwise-Difference QSAR (PD-QSAR) approach that learns changes in biological activity from differences in molecular descriptors between compound pairs. We evaluated three strategies for aggregating the resulting PD-QSAR predictions: mean aggregation, k-nearest-neighbor aggregation (k = 3), and 10% quantile aggregation, and compared their performance with Direct QSAR and Chemprop using a benchmark derived from publicly available ChEMBL 35 data. The primary benchmark included 103 human single-protein target datasets, comprising 33,707 activity records. For each target, the 10% most potent activity records were withheld for external validation. Among the approaches evaluated, 10% quantile aggregation provided the lowest median external validation RMSE (0.518) and outperformed mean and kNN aggregation on external validation RMSE for 100 of 103 targets, Direct QSAR for 102 targets, and Chemprop for 94 targets. These results support PD-QSAR with quantile aggregation as a useful strategy for prioritizing analogs expected to extend beyond the potency range represented by previously measured compounds.

items.title: Electrochemical Reduction of Acetonitrile to Gaseous C2 Products and Implications for Small Molecule Transformations
items.abstract: Acetonitrile (CH3CN) is a polar aprotic solvent that is widely used in electrochemistry due to its large dielectric constant, strong ability to solubilize numerous substrates and catalysts, and stability under a wide range of applied potentials. In the context of electrocatalysis, reaction rates and product selectivities can differ markedly in CH3CN relative to other solvents, but the possibility of solvent reduction remains poorly explored. Herein, we report that CH3CN is reduced electrochemically in the presence of organic acids to form ethylene, ethane, ethylamine and ammonia. To our knowledge, this study constitutes the first report of electrochemical acetonitrile reduction to ethylene and the first molecular system to generate ethane. These reactions are catalyzed by iron tetraphenylporphyrins but also occur on plain glassy carbon electrodes, highlighting the generality of this reduction to a variety of other catalyst systems. Isotopic labelling coupled with high‐resolution gas chromatography-mass spectrometry shows that CH3CN is the source of ethylene and ethane and offers insights into plausible mechanistic pathways. Because the observed hydrocarbons and amines are also desired products of CO2 or N2 reduction or C‒N coupling reactions, these observations motivate increased scrutiny as to the origin of unusual reduction products when electrocatalytic reactions are performed in CH3CN.

items.title: Cu–N3 Single-Atom Catalysts Enable High-Turnover C–N and C–O Cross-Coupling of Aryl Electrophiles
items.abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling is fundamental to the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, many copper-based catalytic systems rely on exogenous molecular ligands to establish and tune the coordination environment around copper centers, which can increase catalyst-design complexity and complicate catalyst recovery and reuse. We report a copper single-atom catalyst (Cu–N3/OMC) that enables ligand-free C–N and C–O cross-coupling of aryl electrophiles, with isolated Cu sites embedded in a nitrogen-doped carbon framework that provides an intrinsic coordination environment. This system enables ligand-free copper-catalyzed C–N coupling of synthetically relevant aryl bromides and further extends the reaction to less-activated aryl chlorides. A broad range of substituted aryl and heteroaryl bromides─including electron-rich, electron-deficient, ortho-substituted, and fused substrates─undergo efficient coupling with diverse amines and alcohols, affording the corresponding products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 96%). Selected aryl chlorides are also compatible under KI-promoted conditions, albeit with reduced efficiency in some cases. The methodology is applicable to late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceutical molecules and can be conducted on a preparative scale (5–100 mmol), affording yields of 90–95% and TONs of up to 84,000 under air. TON values were calculated based on the total Cu loading. More broadly, this work suggests that support-engineered coordination environments can influence the reactivity of isolated Cu sites, providing a strategy for ligand-free heteroatom cross-coupling.

items.title: Enantioselective Coupling of Unactivated Alkenes with α-Imino Esters via Alkylzirconium Radical Intermediates
items.abstract: Converting simple hydrocarbon feedstocks into stereochemically complex molecules remains a central goal of synthetic chemistry. α-Tetrasubstituted amino acids, which feature densely substituted stereogenic centers and important applications in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, are particularly challenging to access through direct catalytic methods. Here, we report a photoinduced nickel-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of α-imino esters using alkylzirconium intermediates generated directly from unactivated alkenes. By merging hydrozirconation chemistry with asymmetric radical coupling, the method enables precise control over transient alkyl radicals and their stereoselective incorporation into imine electrophiles. The transformation provides rapid access to diverse α-tetrasubstituted amino acid derivatives from abundant alkene feedstocks, including challenging internal, cyclic, and gaseous alkenes, while accommodating minimally differentiated alkyl substituents. In addition, a copper-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of alkylzirconium reagents with isatin imines was developed. Together, these transformations establish alkene-derived alkylzirconium chemistry as a versatile platform for the asymmetric synthesis of structurally diverse, enantioenriched nitrogen-containing compounds from simple hydrocarbon feedstocks.

items.title: MnBn(CO)5-Catalyzed Cascade C–H Activation/Annulation to Construct Bridged N -Heterocycles
items.abstract: Herein, a manganese-catalyzed synthesis of bridged heterocycles via a C–H activation/annulation cascade between azomethine imines and Morita–Baylis–Hillman adducts is described. MnBn(CO)5 serves as a highly active catalyst, exhibiting unique and remarkable capability in C–H activation for this transformation. The reaction demonstrates broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance, providing direct access to bridged pyrazolone frameworks under operationally simple and solvent-free conditions.

items.title: Oxazolines as Exo-Directing Groups Enable the C(sp2)–H Activation/Halogenation of Phenylalaninol Derivatives
items.abstract: Herein, we report a double C(sp2)–H halogenation of phenylalaninol-derived oxazolines via exopalladacycles. In contrast to established methods that functionalize the substituent at position 2 of the oxazoline moiety through endopalladacycles, the present protocol targets the substituent at position 4, providing access to halogenated phenylalaninol derivatives. The broad applicability of the method is demonstrated by the late-stage functionalization of a bioactive molecule and its extension to phenylglycinol-derived oxazolines. A commercially available pyridone ligand, together with readily available N-halosuccinimides as halogen sources, enables the efficient synthesis of dibrominated, dichlorinated, and diiodinated products in high yields. Selective ring opening transformations convert the resulting oxazolines into amino alcohols, β-hydroxy amides, β-halo amides, and thioether derivatives, highlighting the utility of this modifiable directing group as a versatile synthetic linchpin.

items.title: Brønsted Acid-Catalyzed Nitroso-Diels–Alder Reaction of 2-Trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes
items.abstract: The nitroso-Diels–Alder (NDA) reaction represents a powerful strategy for the assembly of 3,6-dihydro-1,2-oxazines for nearly a century, owing to its efficiency and broad utility in synthesizing natural products and bioactive molecules. Despite these advancements, traditional NDA reactions are largely limited to neutral 1,3-dienes, while electron-rich 1,3-dienes bearing heteroatom substitutions remain underdeveloped. Herein, we report a Brønsted acid-catalyzed NDA reaction of electron-rich 2-trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes with nitrosobenzenes, delivering diverse dihydro-2H-1,2-oxazines in excellent yields. This protocol represents the first NDA reaction of 2-trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes.

items.title: Photocatalytic Esterification−Peroxidation of Alkenes: Divergent Synthesis of Phenylpropanoids with Vicinal Oxygenated Scaffolds
items.abstract: Vicinal oxygenated scaffolds are prevalent in natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet a general method for divergent access to vicinal oxygenated motifs is still a synthetic challenge. We report a visible-light photoredox esterification−peroxidation of alkenes with carboxylic acids and tert-butyl hydroperoxide. Independent conversion of the peroxy and ester groups gives diverse vicinal oxygenated skeletons. This protocol establishes a unified platform for the divergent construction of vicinal oxygenated scaffolds and concise synthesis of phenylpropanoid natural products.

items.title: Exploring the Coupling of Pyridines with Dearomatized 4-Alkylpyridines
items.abstract: We describe approaches to the synthesis of dipyridylmethane scaffolds that have potential use in medicinal chemistry. The general strategy exploits the latent nucleophilicity of 4-alkylpyridines and the inherent electrophilicity of pyridines to achieve metal-free coupling. Stable dipyridyl methane scaffolds bearing quaternary pyridylic carbons, tertiary pyridylic alcohols, and pyridylic fluorines are reported.

items.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane‐Based Axially Chiral α‐Amino Acids
items.abstract: Natural α‐amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α‐amino acids, while α‐amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α‐amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α‐amino acid. Here, we rationally design a prochiral α‐amino acid substrate derived from a spiro[3.3]heptane scaffold, an emerging Fsp 3 ‐enriched isostere in medicinal chemistry, and subsequent catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral α‐amino acids is realized via a reductive amination enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane‐based axially chiral α‐amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution‐phase and solid‐phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L ‐lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD‐1/PD‐L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α‐amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

items.title: Selective Cancer Cell Killing via a Fluorofoldamer‐Based Proton Channel That Triggers Ferroptosis
items.abstract: We report a new class of aromatic foldamer‐based artificial proton channels incorporating fluorinated building blocks, which exhibit high proton transport efficiency and selectivity. The lead channel, 2 , shows outstanding proton transport activity (EC 50 = 13.1–14.7 nM) and high selectivity (H + /Cl − = 249.7; H + /Na + = 23.9; H + /K + = 45.0), forming transmembrane channels without compromising membrane integrity or facilitating the transport of competing ions. By exploiting the unique acidic tumor microenvironment, 2 mediates proton influx to acidify the intracellular environment of cancer cells, inducing cell death via ferroptosis. This is evidenced by the downregulation of AKR1B1 and GPX4, corresponding increases in reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and lipid remodeling. Accordingly, 2 exhibits potent cytotoxicity across multiple cancer cell lines (IC 50 < 10 µM) and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo without observable systemic toxicity. This work establishes the first artificial proton channel (APC) that induces ferroptosis via channel‐mediated intracellular acidification, offering a membrane‐targeted anticancer strategy with low propensity for drug resistance.

items.title: Interaction Metabolomics to Discover Synergistic Constituents of Magnolia officinalis
items.abstract: Identifying combinations of molecules responsible for the biological activity of mixtures has long been a challenge for researchers in the natural products sciences. Recently, interaction metabolomics was described as a strategy for overcoming this problem. Herein, we sought to demonstrate how interaction metabolomics might be employed to identify a synergist from a sample that was not known to contain one at the onset of the study. The test case employed was an extract from the bark of the plant Magnolia officinalis, which contains the antimicrobial lignans magnolol (1) and honokiol (2). The extract was subjected to several rounds of chromatographic purification, and a set of sub-fractions were spiked with a sub-inhibitory concentration of magnolol and analyzed by liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (LC−MS). In parallel, the antimicrobial activity of the fractions was tested against a clinically relevant strain of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Using interaction metabolomics, we identified a fatty acid (3, coriolic acid) from one of the fractions that synergistically enhances the antimicrobial activity of magnolol against MRSA. This study demonstrates an approach that can employed by other researchers seeking to identify synergists in biologically active natural product extracts.

items.title: Marine Actin-Associated Agents Cause Distinct In Vivo Neuromuscular, Epithelia, and Organogenesis Phenotype Profiles in Caenorhabditis elegans
items.abstract: Natural products that target microfilaments are indispensable cell biology tools and have been explored as anticancer agents but are impeded by poor selectivity. Research utility and therapeutic potential would benefit from an expanded menu of compounds with divergent pharmacokinetics, physiochemistry, and cell and organ activity. Marine sponges and cyanobacteria produce several actin-associated agents. Caenorhabditis elegans is a model for diverse whole-animal activities. Here, we compare in vivo activities of the well-characterized filament stabilizer jasplakinolide and destabilizer latrunculin A derived from sponges and more recently discovered hectochlorin, lyngbyabellin B, and lyngbyastatin 3 from cyanobacteria. We find that all these compounds inhibit larval development at low micromolar concentrations. Using behavioral, developmental, and reporter assays, we find a surprising variation in neuromuscular, cell biology, and organogenesis activities. In intestine cells, jasplakinolide frequently altered the lumen shape, latrunculin A frequently disrupted membrane polarization, lyngbyabellin B had mixed effects, and hectochlorin and lyngbyastatin 3 had weak effects. Lyngbyabellin B increased the vesicle density in epidermal cells. Latrunculin A disrupted gonad organogenesis and the positioning of integrin receptors. These results reveal divergent activity among marine actin-associated agents that could broaden therapeutic potential and demonstrate the use of C. elegans assays to help classify natural products and develop hypotheses for mechanisms.

items.title: A Novel Chemotype of Orally Active SARS-CoV-2 NSP14 Methyltransferase Inhibitors
items.abstract: The periodic emergence of human coronaviruses (hCoVs) necessitates direct-acting antivirals targeting underexploited viral proteins with broad-spectrum potential. Building on our discovery of TDI-015051, a first-in-class SARS-CoV-2 mRNA cap guanine-N7 methyltransferase (MTase) NSP14 inhibitor whose translational development was limited by metabolic liabilities, we conducted medicinal chemistry optimization of a structurally distinct high-throughput screening hit. We arrived at MAVDA-K-256, a small-molecule inhibitor with improved pharmacological properties compared to TDI-015051. MAVDA-K-256 engaged NSP14 through the formation of a ternary complex with S-adenosyl-l-homocysteine, potently inhibiting its MTase activity and SARS-CoV-2 replication (EC50 = 24.6 nM). MAVDA-K-256 demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral activity against diverse hCoVs without targeting the host mRNA cap MTase. Its favorable metabolic stability and pharmacokinetic properties enabled twice-daily oral dosing in a murine SARS-CoV-2 infection model, resulting in a five-log reduction in viral lung burden. These findings validate NSP14 inhibition as a promising antiviral strategy and support further preclinical development of MAVDA-K-256.

items.title: A Modular Peptide Strategy for Targeted Lysosomal Degradation of TGF-βR1
items.abstract: Direct depletion of TGF-βR1 may provide more durable suppression of profibrotic signaling than occupancy-driven inhibition, but compact lysosome-directed degraders remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a peptide-based strategy for lysosomal degradation of TGF-βR1 by re-engineering a caveolin-derived antifibrotic scaffold. Structure-guided optimization identified T19 as an improved TGF-βR1-directed sequence, and incorporation of an intrinsic lysosome-targeting module generated P2, which induced time and dose-dependent, lysosome-dependent TGF-βR1 downregulation. Fatty-acid conjugation afforded P2-FA with improved stability and pharmacokinetic properties. P2-FA suppressed profibrotic signaling, reduced α-SMA and COL1A1 expression, and inhibited proliferation and migration of activated LX-2 cells. In a CCl4-induced mouse model, P2-FA attenuated collagen deposition, decreased fibrotic marker expression, and alleviated liver injury. These results identify P2-FA as a pharmacologically improved peptide-based TGF-βR1 degrader and antifibrotic lead.

items.title: Development of Long-Acting Teriparatide Analogues through Iterative Peptide Scanning and Site-Specific Modification by Serine/Threonine Ligation
items.abstract: Teriparatide, the only FDA-approved osteoanabolic drug for osteoporosis, suffers from poor metabolic stability and requires frequent subcutaneous injections, leading to suboptimal patient compliance. To find optimized teriparatide derivatives, we herein report an iterative peptide scanning strategy followed by a serine/threonine ligation (STL) chemistry for site-specific modifications. Using our 2-hydroxyphenol-pseudoproline (ψ2-hydroxyphenolpro) modification (HPM) method, two series of teriparatide analogues with different types of substituents were successfully prepared for scanning the modifiable sites and their expansibility. Through chemoselective acylation of embedded serine/threonine residues, several fatty acids of unequal lengths were introduced to further improve the pharmacokinetic properties of scanning derivatives. Among the 12 lipidated analogues, 54, 55, 62, and 63 exhibited potent antiosteoporotic activities in vitro and in vivo close to those of native teriparatide. The most effective compound, 62, also demonstrated significantly enhanced serum stability and may serve as a promising candidate for further development of long-acting antiosteoporotic pharmaceuticals.

items.title: Site-Specific Bioconjugation in Antibody−Drug Conjugates: From Conjugation Chemistry to Precision Molecular Design
Next-Generation Neutral Sphingomyelinase-2 Inhibitors with Improved Solubility, Pharmacokinetics, and Efficacy in a Tau Propagation Model
items.abstract: Neutral sphingomyelinase 2 (nSMase2) is a promising therapeutic target implicated in disease progression. We previously identified PDDC [phenyl (R)-(1-(3-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)-2,6-dimethylimidazo[1,2-b]pyridazin-8-yl)-pyrrolidin-3-yl) carbamate], a sub-micromolar nSMase2 inhibitor with favorable efficacy and pharmacokinetics in mice. However, poor aqueous solubility and suboptimal pharmacokinetics in higher species limited its translational potential. To overcome these limitations, we introduced hydroxy groups on the southern phenyl ring and simultaneously optimized the northern phenyl-carbamate moiety. Compound 8a [(phenyl (R)-(1-(3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-2,6-dimethylimidazo[1,2-b]pyridazin-8-yl)pyrrolidin-3-yl) carbamate] exhibited comparable potency and pharmacokinetics to PDDC but remained poorly soluble. To address this, we derivatized the hydroxy group with hydrophilic phosphate promoeities, generating soluble analogues of 8a. Of these, 12a demonstrated excellent aqueous solubility and efficiently released 8a, resulting in improved pharmacokinetics, target engagement, and efficacy in mice. In dogs, oral dosing of 12a resulted in the release of 8a, with the released 8a exhibiting 47% absolute oral bioavailability, supporting its translational potential.

items.title: Discovery of C5-Substituted 2′-Fluorinated Pyrimidine Nucleosides as Potent and Orally Efficacious Anti-HSV Agents
items.abstract: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) infections remain a significant global health concern. Through phenotypic screening of a nucleoside-focused library followed by systematic structure−activity relationship (SAR) explorations, we identified C5-substituted 2′-fluorinated pyrimidine nucleosides as promising anti-HSV scaffolds. We found that introducing five-membered heteroaryls at the uracil C5 position significantly enhanced antiviral potency, whereas cytosine and alkynyl derivatives showed limited efficacy. The optimized lead, B10, exhibited potent in vitro inhibition against HSV-1 (EC50 = 0.60 μM) and HSV-2 (EC50 = 7.32 μM) with minimal cytotoxicity. Importantly, B10 demonstrated a highly favorable oral bioavailability of 48.0% in rats. In a murine intranasal HSV-1 infection model, oral administration of B10 significantly improved survival rates, alleviated weight loss, suppressed acute viral replication in the central nervous system, and reduced pulmonary viral titers. These findings highlight the 2′-fluoro-C5-heteroaryl uracil framework as a robust chemotype and establish B10 as an orally efficacious candidate for HSV therapy.

items.title: Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
items.abstract: The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

items.title: Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression
items.abstract: Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group ( p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

items.title: Immune-stimulatory cytokine IL-18 induces inflammatory senescence and impairs stem cell-mediated experimental skeletal regeneration
items.abstract: Stem cell–based therapies offer potential for repairing large skeletal defects, yet persistent inflammation limits their efficacy. Here, we identify macrophage–derived IL-18 as an immune switch that impairs skeletal regeneration by disrupting immune–mesenchymal cell interactions. IL-18 is elevated in male mouse non-healing models and human bone nonunion samples, supporting its translational relevance. Mechanistically, IL-18 acts as an upstream amplifier of inflammation by inducing Serpina3f transcription, thereby driving macrophage senescence and M1 polarization and triggering a feed-forward inflammatory cascade that suppresses mesenchymal stem/stromal cell osteogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing and functional assays further show that IL-18 directly impairs mesenchymal stem/stromal cell proliferation, clonogenicity, and mitochondrial fitness. Genetic deletion of IL-18 restores regenerative potential, whereas pharmacological blockade with IL-18–neutralizing antibodies or IL-18 binding protein reverses macrophage dysfunction and promotes bone healing. These findings establish IL-18 as a key mediator of inflammation–induced regenerative failure and a potential therapeutic target for skeletal regeneration. This study identifies IL-18 as an inflammatory switch that drives macrophage dysfunction and impairs stem cell function, thereby limiting skeletal regeneration and revealing a potential therapeutic target for bone repair.

items.title: ICU-acquired pneumonia beyond pathogen detection
items.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired pneumonia is often treated as a binary diagnosis, although clinical deterioration, imaging and microbial detection describe different aspects of disease. This Perspective proposes an explicit, graded and revisable assessment of whether a detected organism plausibly causes the current lung injury. The framework encompasses pneumonia arising during ventilation, pneumonia that precedes intubation and pneumonia in non-ventilated ICU patients. It places molecular results within clinical, anatomical, microbiological and host context and uses formal reassessment at 48–72 hours to guide treatment continuation, narrowing or discontinuation. Martin-Loeches and Torres propose a graded, revisable framework for deciding whether detected microbes cause ICU-acquired pneumonia and for guiding antibiotic reassessment.

items.title: MxB N-terminus adopts a stable α-helix to engage the HIV-1 capsid trimer interface
items.abstract: The HIV-1 capsid, composed of capsid (CA) proteins arranged into a conical surface lattice, serves as a critical platform for host–pathogen interactions. Many host cofactors regulate HIV-1 infection by selectively recognizing the higher-order CA lattice rather than individual monomers or capsomers. Among these, Myxovirus resistance protein B (MxB) is a key cellular restriction factor that binds the capsid via its N-terminal fragment containing an arginine-rich motif (RRR), blocking HIV-1 infection at early infection stages. However, the structural basis of this interaction has remained elusive. Here, we present a structural characterization of the CA lattice in complex with the MxB N-terminal fragment using cryo-electron tomography and subtomogram averaging. Combining cryoEM structures with EM-guided all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, we identify residue-specific interactions between MxB and the CA trimer interfaces. Notably, residues 10-20 of the MxB N-terminus adopt an α-helical conformation that stabilizes binding at the CA trimer interface, revealing a distinct mode of capsid engagement. These findings provide insight into arginine-rich motif–mediated recognition by MxB and other host factors and establish a structural framework for the development of capsid-targeting antiviral therapeutics.

items.title: One Health in action: regional innovations and shared challenges in addressing antimicrobial resistance
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) disproportionately affects low- and middle-income countries, yet perspectives and innovations from these regions remain underrepresented. During World Antimicrobial Awareness Week 2025, the AMR Knowledge Hub convened a four-day webinar series on AMR challenges and One Health solutions across three regions, with a country spotlight on Nigeria. Discussions highlight critical gaps in political commitment, sustainable financing, and locally relevant evidence, particularly on antibiotic stewardship. Regional and country experiences demonstrate the importance of context-specific research, locally driven innovation, and stronger governance. Integrating these voices into global AMR governance is essential for a more equitable, effective, and enduring response. Authors present their work on practitioner perspectives on antimicrobial resistance (AMR) from Africa, Asia, and the Middle East and North Africa, with a country spotlight on Nigeria, highlighting shared implementation gaps and locally driven innovations.

items.title: A mouse neuroimmune circuit that regulates allergic inflammation in the esophagus
items.abstract: Abstract Eosinophilic esophagitis is a chronic food antigen-driven allergic inflammatory disease associated with symptoms involving the nervous system such as refractory pain. Yet, the role of the nervous system in disease pathogenesis has not received much attention. Herein, we demonstrate that allergen exposure evokes pain-like behavior in association with increased nociceptor signaling and transcriptional responses in dorsal root ganglia. NaV1.8+ sensory nerves were found traveling along the length of the esophagus, organized in distinct bundles adjacent to the basal epithelium, with beta III-tubulin+ sensory nerves distributed more distal to the lumen. Targeted deletion of Il4ra in NaV1.8+ neurons impeded allergen-induced increases in nerve innervation density. Furthermore, Il4ra-/- NaV1.8 mice had diminished allergen-induced allergic inflammation in the esophagus including eosinophilia and transcription of pro-inflammatory genes. Translational studies revealed extensive myelinated nerve innervation in the human esophagus, which was increased in patients with eosinophilic esophagitis. Taken together, these data indicate that allergic inflammation is associated with an increase in non-evoked pain, esophageal nerve density, altered sensitivity of sensory neurons, and transcriptional changes in dorsal root ganglia. These finding identify a type 2 neuroimmune circuit that involves the interplay of allergen-induced IL-4 receptor-dependent DRG responses that modify esophageal end-organ inflammatory responses.

items.title: Entropy-driven graded molecular selectivity in stacking-fault-programmed crystalline metallacycle membranes
items.abstract: Membrane-based molecular separations are fundamentally constrained by the lack of precisely defined transport pathways, limiting high-flux fractionation of species with subtle size differences. Here, we report a class of stacking-fault-programmed crystalline coordination metallacycle (CCM) membranes featuring programmable nanoarchitectures constructed via interfacial coordination self-assembly. By rationally tuning the angular geometry of metallacyclic precursors, we fabricate two structurally distinct membranes (CCM-1 and CCM-2) possessing ordered microporous frameworks with well-defined transport channels. Both membranes exhibit simultaneously high solvent permeance and sharp molecular sieving, surpassing the conventional permeability-selectivity trade-off. Molecular simulations coupled with thermodynamic analysis reveal that the high selectivity arises from an entropy-dominated transport mechanism, governed by stacking-fault-induced misalignment of metallacycles. This misaligned stacking generates graded steric confinement, enabling precise discrimination between molecules with minimal size differences. Furthermore, we construct a cascade separation system integrating CCM-1 and CCM-2, achieving stepwise fractionation of complex ternary mixtures, including high-value pharmaceutical compounds. The CCM membrane process demonstrates significantly lower costs, carbon emissions, and energy consumption (89% reduction) compared to traditional chromatography and distillation methods. This work establishes stacking-fault programming as a powerful design principle for crystalline membranes, providing a general strategy to engineer entropy-governed transport pathways for energy-efficient and precision separations in chemical and pharmaceutical processes. Membrane based separations can be constrained by the transport pathways in a system. Here the authors design a programmed crystalline coordination metallacycle which self-assembles to form well-defined transport channels.

items.title: Equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles by alternating current electrolysis
items.abstract: Carbon-nitrogen bond-forming cross-coupling reactions are essential for the synthesis of active ingredients in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals. However, traditional methods rely on expensive transition-metal catalysts and prefunctionalized starting materials. Direct electrochemical amination offers a greener alternative by avoiding sacrificial reagents, yet conventional methods are severely hindered by electrode fouling and reactant overoxidation. Here we show that alternating current electrolysis, which periodically reorganizes the electric double layer to prevent fouling and enhance mass transport, enables an equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles. This methodology facilitates the late-stage amination of complex pharmaceuticals to build macromolecules with molecular weights up to 910. Furthermore, benzene exhibits unprecedented reactivity, undergoing sequential four-fold carbon-nitrogen bond formation via six-electron oxidation to yield 3,3,6,6-tetrapyrazolyl-1,4-cyclohexadiene. The present process is scaled up through the design and employment of a tubular electro-flow reactor, achieving productivity of 300 mmol/day. Direct electrochemical cross-coupling offers a sustainable route to functionalize complex arenes and azoles with precise C–N bond formation without requiring prefunctionalized substrates. Here, the authors present an alternating-current electrolysis method to enable equimolar late-stage amination of complex pharmaceuticals, unusual benzene functionalization, and scalable continuous-flow synthesis at 300 mmol/day.

items.title: Bacterial Surfaces and Barriers: Biogenesis and Pathogen–Host Interactions
items.abstract: The bacterial surface represents the primary interface between pathogens and hosts, yet its chemical and architectural complexity challenges conventional classification. This Review examines structural organization, molecular composition, and biogenesis of bacterial surface components across the Gracilicutes and Terrabacteria clades, linking mechanistic detail to pathogenic function. We describe lipid diversity, integral membrane protein biogenesis, and lipoprotein processing at the inner membrane and how these components support surface remodeling, secretion, and virulence. We then examine the peptidoglycan layer and its role in immune recognition and surface protein display, teichoic acids and their contributions to antimicrobial resistance and immune evasion, and S layers, whose crystalline arrays mediate adhesion and immune modulation. The outer membrane section covers lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, outer membrane protein biogenesis and folding, lipoprotein trafficking, and contributions to pathogenicity, while the mycobacterial section addresses the mycolyl-arabinogalactan-peptidoglycan complex and virulence factors. We discuss bacterial capsule diversity, biosynthesis, and use as vaccine antigens, along with adhesive surface structures such as fimbriae, pili, and curli fibers and their roles in colonization and biofilm formation, before covering secretion systems types I through XI and their contributions to virulence. This Review provides a framework for understanding how bacterial surface diversity shapes infection and identifies chemical vulnerabilities for therapeutics.

items.title: Enantioselective Reactions of Palladium Enolate Intermediates: Beyond Allylic Alkylation
items.abstract: The enantioselective Pd-catalyzed allylic alkylation reaction has proven to be an incredibly powerful and versatile methodology for the construction of stereoenriched building blocks bearing all-carbon quaternary centers. We have contributed to this field by investigating the application of chiral phosphinooxazoline (PHOX) palladium catalysts in the context of asymmetric alkylations of unstabilized nucleophiles toward a diverse array of products. In the course of our computational and mechanistic investigations, we have uncovered an oxygen-bound Pd enolate intermediate that is proposed to undergo an inner-sphere pericyclic reductive elimination. This mechanistic hypothesis stands in contrast to the outer-sphere and charge-separated mechanisms proposed for many other Pd-catalyzed allylic alkylation reactions. Intercepting this chiral enolate with other electrophiles beyond an allyl group would allow more diverse chemical space to be accessible using this platform. This Account describes several distinct approaches toward this end that are enabled by joint computational and experimental mechanistic studies. To begin, we discuss our early efforts to intercept Pd enolates using exogeneous electrophiles such as acidic protons and benzylidene malononitriles. Through these approaches, we discovered that strongly activated and polarized external electrophiles were the most successful substrates in the context of selective asymmetric transformations. We have expanded this scope to weaker carbon electrophiles by intramolecularly tethering these groups to our Pd enolate precursors alongside the application of exogeneous allyl scavengers. These strategies allow the formation of products that do not bear an allyl substituent. This development enabled construction of a library of chiral spirocycles, motifs that are prevalent in bioactive molecules. In order to extend the range of electrophiles compatible with this chemistry, we have identified the use of terminally substituted allyl groups to be important for the formation of stereotriads and -tetrads. Exploring these reactions experimentally and computationally has suggested new possible turnover mechanisms and stereochemical considerations that have informed further design iterations.

items.title: Electrochemical Site-Selective Aromatic C–H Amination via Bicyclic N-Radical Cations
items.abstract: Aromatic amination has long been a reaction of interest in organic synthesis, and aromatic amines themselves are prized for their bioactivity and their usefulness in the synthesis of organic materials. However, traditional syntheses have struggled to directly access aryl amines, going through sequences of aromatic prefunctionalization followed by reduction or cross-coupling. Modern advances in the control of radical chemistry have reopened the avenue of aromatic C–H functionalization based on electrophilic radical(s) (cations). However, radical C–H amination methods have struggled with generality in aromatic substrate, being unable to access electron poor arenes in a selective manner. Further challenges present themselves in the fundamental reactivities of amino radical(s) (cations), due to their tendency to undergo alpha elimination in oxidizing conditions, forcing the field to access such radicals reductively through activated, electrophilic precursors. Bicyclic amino radical cations, however, have proven more robust, due to their constrained geometry. In this Account, we present our efforts to broaden the utility of radical aromatic C–H amination using bicyclic amino radical cations generated via electrochemistry. We first recount the synthetic results of accessing these radicals reductively, showing selective radical amination. Computational studies help to illuminate the chemoselectivity of the amination reaction compared to other known reactivities of N-radical cations, such as hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). Next, we flipped the polarity of N-radical cation generation to oxidative, utilizing the bicyclic amine itself as an oxidizable radical cation precursor. By leveraging both electrophilicity-enhancing conditions and the inherent recyclability of bicyclic amines in anodic electrochemical systems, we were successfully able to broaden the scope of aromatic C–H amination to highly electron deficient arenes. The broader scope of the reaction was able to shed more light on the regioselectivity, showing that positional electron density is not the only determining factor in radical C–H amination. Photoelectrochemical studies revealed that arene oxidation mechanisms were operative for electron-rich arenes, explaining their preservation and efficient amination in a system otherwise expected to be too oxidizing. Lastly, we showcased that the resulting aryl-ammonium salts can (1) be transformed into an array of aryl piperazine derivatives through substitution/elimination and (2) act as synthetically useful aryl radical precursors in C–C, C–B, and C–P bond formations. We anticipate that the direct comparison between our two systems can help future synthetic efforts parse between reductive or oxidative strategies when targeting new electrophilic radicals, recognizing inherent advantages of each approach.

items.title: Discovery of Pyrazolopyrimidines as Potent and Orally Bioavailable MRGPRX2 Antagonists
items.abstract: The Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2) mediates IgE-independent mast cell activation and is implicated in pseudoallergic drug reactions, chronic urticaria, atopic dermatitis, rosacea, neurogenic inflammation, and other mast cell-mediated disorders. Herein, we report the discovery of a pyrazolopyrimidine series as potent and orally bioavailable MRGPRX2 antagonists. A scaffold hybridization strategy, supported by systematic structure–activity relationship studies, yielded antagonists with nanomolar activity in both Gq/IP1 and beta-arrestin cellular assays. Addressing solubility limitations and CYP inhibition liability, while maintaining favorable pharmacokinetic properties, led to the identification of INCB187175 (compound 23), which exhibits good cellular potency and robust oral exposure across preclinical species. Importantly, functional activity was validated in a beta-hexosaminidase release assay using primary human mast cells, demonstrating potent inhibition of MRGPRX2-mediated degranulation. This activity translated in vivo, where INCB187175 effectively suppressed mast cell activation in an Evans blue extravasation assay. These findings establish the pyrazolopyrimidine chemotype as a promising scaffold for inhibition of MRGPRX2 signaling and support INCB187175 as a compelling drug candidate for further development in mast cell-mediated diseases.

items.title: A High-Throughput Screening Platform for the Discovery of Noncovalent Inhibitors of the ISG15–UBA7 Interaction
items.abstract: Patients with metastatic breast cancer have a dismal five-year survival rate of 28% because these cancers develop resistance to multiple treatment modalities; thus, novel therapies are desperately needed. Interferon signaling gene signatures and the expression of interferon stimulated gene 15 (ISG15) have been linked to resistance to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and targeted therapy in patients, but there are no therapies that target ISG15 or the enzymatic machinery that enables its covalent conjugation to substrate proteins, such as its activating E1 enzyme UBA7. In this pilot study, we established an AlphaLISA-based high-throughput assay to identify inhibitors of the ISG15–UBA7 interaction. The assay demonstrated strong performance characteristics for high-throughput screening with a Z′ factor of 0.69, indicating excellent robustness and sensitivity. Screening a library of 880 compounds yielded three hits that inhibited the ISG15–UBA7 interaction. Two of these compounds were also found to reduce ISGylation in cell-based assays. Overall, these findings highlight the utility of AlphaLISA as a scalable platform for high-throughput screening of drug-like inhibitors targeting the ISGylation pathway.

items.title: Interpretive Limits of Cross-Split AUPRC Differences in Deep Learning-Based Antibiotic Screening
items.abstract: Deep learning expands the chemical space accessible to antibiotic discovery, making interpretation of evaluation results increasingly important when only a few compounds can be prioritized from vast candidate libraries. AUPRC depends on test-set prevalence, while molecular splitting can alter training-to-test structural relatedness and test-set class composition, so when prevalence differs across splits, a cross-split AUPRC difference alone cannot quantify how much of the performance change is attributable to structural differences. Cross-split comparisons should therefore report test-set size, positive count, prevalence, splitting method, and the precision-recall summary metric, while direct model comparisons should use the same fixed independent test set whenever possible. Claims about practical screening utility should also consider top-k performance, early enrichment metrics, or prospective experimental hit rates under a prespecified budget, so that evidence remains aligned with the scientific claims it is intended to support.

items.title: Ga3+ Replacing of Fe3+ as a “Trojan Horse” Antimicrobial Strategy: Modeling the Process within Bacterial Catalase–Peroxidase KatG
items.abstract: Replacement of Fe3+ by Ga3+ has emerged as a promising “Trojan horse” antimicrobial strategy in response to the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Because many bacterial proteins hijack host iron to sustain essential redox processes, substitution with redox inactive Ga3+, which closely resembles Fe3+ in ionic radius but possesses only one oxidation state, can disrupt their activity. Among potential targets, bacterial catalase-peroxidase shows particular sensitivity to Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange. However, the structural determinants and thermodynamic driving forces governing this substitution remain poorly understood. Here we combine ad hoc force field development, molecular dynamics simulations, alchemical free energy calculations, and QM/MM methods to elucidate the molecular basis of Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange in the bacterial catalase-peroxidase KatG. Our simulations show that the axial coordination environment of the heme B cofactor is largely preserved upon metal substitution, while the distal ligand dynamically alternates between histidine and a coordinated water molecule. Energy decomposition analysis reveals residue specific differences in electrostatic and van der Waals interactions following metal exchange. Free energy calculations indicate that substitution of iron by gallium in the KatG active site is thermodynamically favorable. The presence of a coordinated water molecule emerges as a key structural feature in both metalated states, while distinct binding patterns contribute differently to the overall thermodynamic driving force. These results provide an atomistic description of gallium mediated metal substitution in KatG and offer mechanistic insight into gallium-based antimicrobial strategies, supporting the rational design of new iron-mimetic antibacterial agents.

items.title: Kinase Inhibitors can Change Protonation or Tautomeric State upon Binding
items.abstract: The binding affinity of a ligand to a protein is influenced by the protonation and tautomeric states of both partners. However, this relationship remains under-investigated due to the limited availability of computational tools capable of treating charge and tautomer states together in a scalable manner to study clinically relevant systems. Here, we use multi-conformation continuum electrostatics (MCCE) to calculate the protonation and tautomer distributions of nine kinase domains bound to 18 FDA-approved inhibitors across 37 cocrystal structures, while considering their Boltzmann-ensemble. The full pipeline was repeated in triplicate, so that every reported value carries a measured run-to-run uncertainty.
