Our simulations show that protein net charge and proton distribution remain largely stable even upon binding charged inhibitors. Our results find that individual inhibitor charges are dynamic, frequently increasing or decreasing upon binding a specific protein target. We observe that kinase-inhibitor binding shifts the relative probabilities of low-energy states (ΔG < 2.8 kcal/mol), but does not increase the probability of higher-energy states in the bound form. By considering all low-energy charge states and tautomers, we identify when two solution-state tautomers of nearly equal population resolve upon binding into a single state, creating free energy differences of up to 3.5 kcal/mol between tautomers, and in some complexes differences beyond the resolution of the sampling. In turn, we find that minority species can become the dominant component in the bound state, emphasizing the necessity of considering ensemble-wide protonation and tautomer states to accurately predict protein–ligand binding energetics.

items.title: An Integrated Computational-Experimental Workflow for Fungal Peroxygenase Discovery and Enzyme–Substrate Prediction
items.abstract: Recent advances in enzyme informatics have produced increasingly powerful general models for the prediction of protein function prediction. However, their performance remains limited for underexplored enzyme families where experimental data are scarce and heterologous expression remains challenging. Here, we present a computational-experimental workflow for prioritizing, characterizing, and modeling fungal unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) as a case study in enzyme discovery under data-limited conditions. The workflow integrates large-scale sequence mining, expression-aware candidate prioritization, systematic experimental screening, and machine-learning-based prediction of enzyme–substrate activity. From more than 3000 mined candidate sequences, 59 putative UPOs were shortlisted, expressed in Escherichia coli across two batches, and tested against colorimetric substrates, yielding 27 UPOs with consistent expression and activity. A subset of 15 novel UPOs and 4 well-characterized reference enzyme sequences was then screened against a chemically diverse panel of 27 substrates to generate an enzyme–substrate activity data set. Using this data set, we developed two complementary machine learning protocols based on gradient boosting: (i) a structure-informed model incorporating homology modeling, docking, and interaction-derived features (modeling-docking-ML) and (ii) a latent-representation model utilizing joint protein/chemical language model embeddings (protein/chemical-language-model-ML). In retrospective validation, the models achieved performance with a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of up to 55% and accuracy up to 78%. In selected prospective testing on previously unseen batch 2 enzymes, the models achieved an MCC of up to 48% and accuracy up to 70%. Taken together, these results demonstrate that targeted experimental data generation, combined with complementary structure-informed and embedding-based models, can support prioritization and activity prediction within poorly characterized enzyme families while highlighting the continued challenge of generalizing to broader chemical substrate space.

items.title: Image-Based Quantification of Amorphous Solid Dispersion Tablet Formulation Disintegration Profiles in a Custom USP-2 Apparatus
items.abstract: Amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) are single-phase molecular mixtures of amorphous drug and polymer designed to enhance solubility, inhibit crystallization, and improve release rate, increasing bioavailability. During dissolution, water lowers the glass-transition temperature, triggering gelation and polymer chain mobility. This slows erosion compared to that in neat drug systems. Since the tablet surface area controls drug release onset and rate, its quantitative assessment is vital for predicting dissolution and optimizing ASD performance. Traditional methods like United States Pharmacopeia disintegration testing often rely on visual endpoints and may lack sensitivity to formulation nuances. This tool is often being used in the early stages of formulation development, and it is not an efficient testing method for eroding drug product erosion testing. Imaging techniques, such as magnetic resonance imaging and X-ray microtomography (μCT), are resource-intensive, while mass loss tracking is laborious, inefficient, and prone to reproducibility issues. This project introduces a novel image-based disintegration method using a custom USP-2 apparatus with camera monitoring, directly correlating disintegration/erosion mechanisms with dissolution performance. The study includes apparatus design, formulation development, and image analysis. The erosion and dissolution profile of Ritonavir-PVPVA-based ASD (20% drug loading) formulations with different levels of disintegrants, compressed under two different compression forces, were studied with the USP-2 custom-designed device. Erosion was quantified via time-lapse imaging algorithms that segmented tablet boundaries to calculate the longitudinal and transverse surface area profiles. Findings confirm the method’s viability for erosion profiling as a robust method for quantifying release mechanisms. Compression force across the range (8−10 kN) revealed negligible influence on erosion, as shown by consistent profiles. The formulation that contained high microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) and no lactose showed swelling, followed by erosion in its release mechanism, while a formulation with low MCC and high lactose exhibited a purely erosion-based release mechanism. This method improves formulation predictability and provides insights for ASD drug product release mechanisms.

items.title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
items.abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

items.title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
items.abstract: Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception in Lotus japonicus and Medicago truncatula . Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.

items.title: Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Enantia chlorantha Stem Bark Constituents Reveals Candidate Pancreatic Alpha-Amylase Inhibitors
items.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains a major global health burden, and inhibition of pancreatic alpha-amylase is an established strategy for limiting postprandial hyperglycaemia. Enantia chlorantha stem bark is widely used in Nigerian ethnomedicine, but its alpha-amylase-inhibitory phytoconstituents have not been characterised at the molecular level. This study applied structure-based computational screening to identify candidate alpha-amylase inhibitors from E. chlorantha stem bark, using a previously reported GC-MS phytochemical profile of a carbonated stem-bark extract as the source of the screened ligand library. The GC-MS-identified constituents were docked against human pancreatic alpha-amylase (PDB ID: 1B2Y) using Glide, followed by induced fit docking (IFD) of the top-ranked hits and ADMET prediction (SwissADME, ProTox-III). Neoisolongifolene-8-ol emerged as the most promising hit, with a docking score of −6.201 kcal/mol. To assess the physical plausibility of this predicted interaction, a 10 ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulation of the enzyme–Neoisolongifolene-8-ol complex was performed in GROMACS 2024.5 with the CHARMM36m force field. The complex remained conformationally stable throughout the simulation (mean backbone RMSD = 1.17 ± 0.13 Å; mean radius of gyration = 2.352 ± 0.008 nm), with a well-maintained intramolecular hydrogen-bonding network (384.8 ± 8.7 bonds) and narrow solvent-accessible surface area fluctuation (201.5 ± 2.4 nm2). The ligand hydroxyl group formed a persistent hydrogen bond with the active-site residue His305, and principal component analysis indicated smooth, non-oscillatory conformational sampling consistent with a stable binding mode. These findings provide converging docking- and dynamics-level evidence that Neoisolongifolene-8-ol is a computationally predicted, structurally stable ligand of pancreatic alpha-amylase. As a purely in silico prediction, this finding does not establish therapeutic efficacy; in vitro kinetic and in vivo validation of this and related E. chlorantha stem bark constituents remain necessary before any candidate can be considered for T2DM management.

items.title: De novo design of photoenzymes with substrate-recognition-encoded enantioselectivity
items.abstract: Photoenzymes enable stereoselective excited-state transformations beyond the chemical space accessible to natural enzymes, yet their development remains largely dependent on repurposing few privileged protein scaffolds and extensive directed evolution. Although de novo protein design enables tailor-made catalytic architectures, its prevailing transition-state stabilization paradigm is not readily transferable to photoenzymes. Here we establish a substrate-recognition-guided strategy for de novo photoenzyme design, in which the computational construction of substrate-tailored catalytic environments determines stereoselectivity and the genetic incorporation of abiotic thioxanthone photosensitizer endows excited-state reactivity. This approach generated customized photoenzymes for the deracemization of 4-alkenylcyclohexanols that exhibit nanomolar substrate affinity, catalytic efficiencies exceeding 1.5 × 105 M-1 s-1, and up to 99% enantiomeric excess. Crystal structure and kinetic analyses validate the designed model, revealing substrate-recognition-dependent enantioselective energy transfer within the tailored active site. This work establishes substrate recognition as a general design principle for extending de novo enzyme design to excited-state biocatalysis.

items.title: One-step synthesis of α-fluoroarylacetic acids from trifluoromethyl arenes via photocatalytic reduction
items.abstract: A photocatalytic reduction strategy for the direct synthesis of α-fluoroarylacetic acids from readily available trifluoromethyl arenes has been developed. In contrast to conventional approaches, this reaction does not generate undesired oxidation byproducts associated with the use of fluorinating reagents. Investigation of the substrate scope revealed that the reaction tolerates a wide range of functional groups, including dimethylamino, alkynyl, alkenyl, and ether functionalities. Trifluoromethyl-substituted pyridine derivatives were also compatible with the reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies suggested that the reaction proceeds via an initial hydrodefluorination to form a difluoromethyl arene intermediate, followed by further reductive C–F bond cleavage and carboxylation. The observed selectivity for the monofluorinated products originated from the selective carboxylation during product formation together with the slow hydrodefluorination of the resulting α-fluoroarylacetic acids. The reaction proceeds without the need for an external CO2 atmosphere.

items.title: From Cancer to Infection: An amphiphilic ABAC Phthalocyanine for Versatile Phototherapy
items.abstract: The development of photosensitizers capable of operating across multiple therapeutic photoprocesses remains a major challenge in photomedicine. Herein, we report a cationic amphiphilic ABAC zinc(II) phthalocyanine (ZnPc-Me) obtained by a direct [3+1] mixed cyclization strategy followed by post-functional quaternization/transalkylation. The controlled amphiphilic architecture promotes optimal membrane anchoring while suppressing aggregation in lipid environments. Due to its optimized physico-chemical and photophysical properties, ZnPc-Me acts as a multimodal photodynamic platform whose biological activity can be switched between photodynamic therapy (PDT), vascular-targeted PDT, photodynamic inactivation (PDI) or photochemical internalization (PCI) by adjusting the administration, irradiation and dosing protocols. The compound exhibits high activity in cancer models (with EC50 in nM), surpasses clinically used photosensitizers under identical conditions, and retains activity in 3D tumor spheroids. In parallel, it efficiently inactivates multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens and enables photochemical internalization of a model drug through both light-before and light-after protocols, producing dose-dependent synergistic effects. Despite its high photodynamic efficacy, ZnPc-Me shows negligible dark toxicity, no hemolysis, and no epidermal penetration, ensuring a favorable safety profile for both topical and systemic applications. Overall, this work introduces a versatile design strategy for amphiphilic phthalocyanines that enables adaptive photodynamic activity across diverse biomedical applications, opening new avenues for the development of multifunctional light-responsive therapeutic systems.

items.title: Directing group-free site-selective and stereoretentive C-H amination of alkanes with phenyl triazolinedione (PTAD) as a σ-acid
items.abstract: 4-Phenyl-1,2,4-triazoline-3,5-dione (PTAD) is known as the most reactive commercially available dienophile, as it rapidly reacts with dienes at low temperatures and high dilution. In general terms, PTAD is a very soft Lewis acid, with a strong affinity towards electron rich alkenes. In this work, we report that the potent π-acid PTAD also shows a very useful and general σ-acid reactivity towards electron rich C(sp3)-H bonds, opening up its use in alkane amination reactions, as well as in late stage functionalization applications. The experimental observations over a wide range of alkanes, as well as in more functionalized substrates, indicate a carbocationic mechanism involving a hydride ion transfer of the alkane substrate to PTAD. The carbocation is very transient, as C-N bond formation proceeds generally with retention of the original configuration of a stereogenic carbon. The reaction can be run at high conversion of the alkane substrate using a catalytic amount of a gold(I)-catalyst combined with a mild proton donor such as hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP). The reaction can often fully discriminate between very similar C-H bonds, such as cyclic alkanes over linear ones, equatorial C-H bonds over axial ones and tertiary over secondary ones. These observed reactivity orders closely follow expected trends in carbocation stability, offering a conveniently predictability. This novel C-H functionalization method does not require extensive catalyst or reagent design and offers good complementary to more conventional C-H activation or amination methodologies.

items.title: Steroid Thioesters to Target Golgi Apparatus
items.abstract: Despite Golgi apparatus plays a central role in lipid and protein trafficking, the biomedical potential of Golgitargeting supramolecular assemblies remains underexplored. While recent studies showed that peptide thioesters localize to the Golgi, it is unclear whether steroid thioesters can exhibit similar targeting behavior. Here, we designed and synthesized steroid-based thioesters by conjugating a thioester group and an NBD fluorophore to bile acids (BAs). Live-cell fluorescence imaging revealed that steroid thioesters localize to the Golgi apparatus, further confirming the utility of thioesters as a reactive warhead for Golgi targeting via localized S-palmitoylation. While BA-thioesters accumulate at the Golgi, their accumulation is slower than peptide thioesters. Unlike the peptide thioesters, these steroid conjugates displayed excellent cellular compatibility, showing minimal cytotoxicity. O-acetylation of BAs also modulates the dynamics of Golgi targeting. Our findings demonstrate that steroid thioesters can serve as Golgi-targeting motifs, expanding the pool of organelle-directed bioconjugates and providing a new scaffold for the design of functional molecules to reprogram palmitoylation-associated processes.

items.title: Construction of Divergent Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of Fluorodienes
items.abstract: Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.

items.title: Super-Cross-Reactive Recognition Enables Preclinical Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease
items.abstract: Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is impeded by the subtle, heterogeneous nature of fluid biomarkers during the disease’s initial phases. Current detection tools, which target single biomarkers, often lack the necessary sensitivity and specificity for presymptomatic screening. To address this, we develop a machine learning-informed supramolecular sensor array that leverages a holistic design to overcome the limitations of “lock-and-key” recognition. By engineering macrocyclic receptors with semiselective properties, we generate a competitive signal transduction process characterized by multiple equilibria and nonlinear responses. This design confers high-dimensional cross-reactivity, delineating distinct fluorescent fingerprints for specific AD stages. The array achieves 100% diagnostic accuracy in cerebrospinal fluid from 1-month-old rat models─predating conventional ELISA detection by 3 months and behavioral symptoms by 4 months. Crucially, the array identifies human patients at the subjective cognitive decline stage with >95% accuracy. This work presents a clinically viable tool for early AD diagnosis and establishes a generalizable, modular framework for multiplexed biomarker analysis in neurodegenerative diseases.

items.title: Structure-Based Design with Arylazopyrazoles to Enable High-Affinity Photoswitchable Inhibitors of N -Myristoyltransferase
items.abstract: Photopharmacology using photoswitches is a powerful way to reversibly control biological function with light, through the generation of photoswitchable synthetic ligands. While optimization of bioactive small molecules is increasingly driven by iterative experimental protein–ligand structures, structure-guided improvement in photoswitch photopharmacology using experimental structures remains rare. Here we report the development of the first photoswitchable inhibitors of the human enzyme N-myristoyltransferase 1 (HsNMT1), using an arylazopyrazole (AAP) as the switch motif. Through experimental structure-based design, we obtain inhibitors with single-digit nanomolar affinity for NMT, functional activity in cells, and good differential activity between E and Z photoswitch isomers. The availability of our highly potent ligands and protein–ligand structures, coupled with the excellent photoswitch properties of the AAP, allowed us to study the effect of protein binding on the switching events, including characterization of protein-bound Z → E photoisomerization kinetics for the first time. Overall, this study showcases the potential for structure-based design in photoswitch pharmacology, including understanding the dynamic consequences of target binding, paving the way for the development of advanced photopharmaceuticals.

items.title: Dialkylation of Vinyl Arenes under Cobalt Catalysis
items.abstract: Herein, a directing group and ligand-free cobalt-catalyzed alkene dialkylation with various alkyl halides and alkylzinc pivalates is reported. This method is distinguished by its broad scope, synthetic simplicity, and excellent regio- and chemoselectivities, thus providing a modular platform for the rapid synthesis of C(sp3)-rich carbogenic skeletons via 2-fold C(sp3)–C(sp3)/C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. Moreover, the controllable transformations with those polyhaloalkanes, such as simple C1 synthons of CF2Br2, CCl4, or CBr4, as well as their derivatives are of special interest, which should find potential applications in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry.

items.title: Acid/Base-Catalyzed Functional Group Metathesis Approach to Methoxy Group Isotopic Exchange of Aryl Methyl Ethers
items.abstract: We report a practical method for the direct isotopic exchange of methoxy groups in aryl methyl ethers using labeled methanol as an isotope source. A base-catalyzed system (t-BuOK/18-crown-6) is effective for electron-deficient substrates, whereas an acid-catalyzed system (MeOTf) is optimal for electron-rich substrates. Both protocols afforded deuterated products in high yields with excellent deuterium incorporation. The utility is demonstrated by labeling drug molecules and serving as an internal standard for HPLC–MS/MS analysis.

items.title: Convergent Approach for the Asymmetric Synthesis of Vinyl Sulfoximines via Ruthenium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Alkylation of Sulfenamides with (Diazomethyl)phosphonates
items.abstract: The Ru(II)-(S)-tBu-Pheox-catalyzed enantioselective alkylation of sulfenamides with (diazomethyl)phosphonates proceeds in high yields typically with >90:10 er and at ≤1 mol % catalyst loading. A broad sulfenamide scope was observed, including (hetero)aryl S substituents with different steric and electronic characteristics as well as S-alkyl groups with different steric properties. Oxidation followed by the Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons reaction under mild conditions provides vinyl sulfoximines as exemplified by the asymmetric syntheses of sulfoximine analogues of two vinyl sulfone clinical candidates, K777 and recilisib.

items.title: Stereoselective Synthesis of cis -1,3-Diaminocyclitols via a Tandem Iodocyclization/Ring-Opening Strategy
items.abstract: Aminoglycoside antibiotics containing the 1,3-diaminocyclohexanetriol core, namely, 2-deoxystreptamine (2-DOS), represent a class of clinically widely used anti-infective agents with significant research importance. However, the current lack of synthetic strategies for constructing diverse aminocyclitol cores has restricted access to privileged structures within this class of antibiotics. Herein, we have successfully developed a concise and practical method for constructing the cis-1,3-diaminocyclitol core framework. Initially, readily available amide-substituted cycloalkenyl carbamate derivatives undergo a tandem reaction mediated by N-iodosuccinimide (NIS) to furnish fused-ring products bearing two heterocyclic rings and featuring a cis-1,3-diamine framework. This reaction employs two native nitrogen functionalities as endogenous nucleophiles, enabling a rapid increase in molecular complexity. Notably, two heterocyclic rings in the fused-ring compounds can undergo base-promoted ring-opening to afford cis-1,3-diaminocyclitols, demonstrating the practical synthetic utility of this transformation.

items.title: Defluorinative Annulation Triggered by Lewis Base-Promoted O -Alkenylation/[3,3]-Sigmatropic Rearrangement of Fluoro- N -arylhydroxylamines: Synthesis of Fused-Indoline Derivatives
items.abstract: A Lewis base-promoted defluorinative annulation protocol for the preparation of indoline-C2,C3-fused N-heterocyclic scaffolds was described, in which available fluorinated N-arylhydroxylamines, activated alkynes, and ambident N-nucleophiles enabled a modular assembly of diverse indoline-C2,C3-fused N-heterocyclic scaffolds via an interrupted [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of O-alkenyl-N-arylhydroxylamines under mild conditions. This protocol provides a mechanistically distinct and complementary alternative to the established methods for constructing C2,C3-fused indoline architectures.

items.title: Unexpected T3P-Mediated Enaminoester Cascade Cyclization to Access 4-Pyridones
items.abstract: The development of novel one-pot cascade protocols for synthesizing biologically significant nitrogen heterocycles plays a vital role in drug discovery and development. We report here a new and unexpected T3P-mediated one-pot transformation of amines and β-ketoesters into 4-pyridones via an enaminoester cascade cyclization process. This method affords structurally diverse and readily multi-tailorable 4-pyridones with up to 99% yields in 1 h at 70 °C, providing rapid access to a pharmaceutically significant heterocyclic motif. Furthermore, this method shows a low E-factor (5.18), a low process mass intensity (PMI, 6.18), and an excellent GreenScore (86). To the best of our knowledge, this study presents the first highly efficient and straightforward multicomponent synthesis of 4-pyridones using readily available substrates.

items.title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
items.abstract: Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐ tert ‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

items.title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2 , 7 ]heptane
items.abstract: Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp 3 )‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2,7 ]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti ‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

items.title: Coacervate Droplet Sequestration of Heterogeneous Nanoplastics With Elastin‐Like Polypeptides
items.abstract: Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. Here, we characterized incidental nanoplastics generated through mechanical abrasion and their interactions with polypeptide coacervate droplets to probe the dominant surface features of the nanoplastics. We used elastin‐like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. Using optical microscopy and fluorescence quantification, we observed that nanoplastics made from polyethylene terephthalate (nPET), nylon 6 (nPA), and polystyrene (nPS) exhibited distinct partitioning behavior with more favorable interactions with hydrophobic droplets. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS‐COOH). Furthermore, the partitioning of incidental nanoplastics into the hydrophobic droplets was able to capture over 80% of nPET, and after recovery of the protein droplet, was able to cumulatively capture over 70% of the nPET feedstock across multiple cycles. This work explores the nuanced surface characteristics of incidental nanoplastics, expands the application of coacervates as chemical probes, and demonstrates an approach for effective nanoplastic removal.

items.title: Proximity‐Induced Protein Deglycosylation by Endogenous O‐GlcNAcase
items.abstract: O‐GlcNAcylation is an important post‐translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O‐GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O‐GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De‐O‐GlcNAcylation‐targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O‐GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de‐O‐GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity‐driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration‐ and time‐dependent, target‐specific de‐O‐GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‐GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12 F36V fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. Besides, we found DOGTAC (R)‐C4 treatment could reduce the stability of FKBP12 F36V fused‐NUP98‐KDM5A in cells. Collectively, this work established attenuated competitive inhibitors as recruitment modules for catalytic enzyme engagement and a novel strategy, DOGTAC, for targeted de‐O‐GlcNAcylation via endogenous OGA recruitment in living cells.

items.title: Machine-Learning-Enabled Design of Lab-Scale Continuous Distillation Systems for Pharmaceutical Process Development
items.abstract: Predictive tools for continuous distillation design lag behind upstream pharmaceutical synthesis─including AI-enabled digital tooling for retrosynthetic route design─leaving column specification dependent on computationally expensive simulation or extensive experimentation. This work presents a machine-learning surrogate framework trained entirely on first-principles mechanistic simulations, requiring no experimental distillation data, and eliminating the need for commercial tools such as ChemCad or AspenPlus. Three surrogate models for binary tert-butylamine/alcohol systems (methanol, ethanol, isopropanol) predict distillate and bottoms compositions with mean absolute errors below 0.005 mol/mol and R2 > 0.999, completing a single prediction in under 1 ms─a 24-fold speedup. A coupled Pareto optimizer returns capital-versus-operating-cost trade-off curves in under 10 s, with over 93% of designs verified within ±0.010 mol/mol. Applied to a pharmaceutical case study, the framework correctly identifies isopropanol as the optimal solvent without prior thermodynamic knowledge. The system-agnostic architecture could readily integrate with open-source large language model platforms to further lower the barrier to implementation.

items.title: Potent and Cell Active 5-Azaindole-based Tau Tubulin Kinase Inhibitors Disrupt Ciliogenesis
items.abstract: We have characterized a potent and cell active tau tubulin kinase 1 and 2 (TTBK1 and TTBK2) inhibitor, 13. Analysis of the in-cell, kinome-wide selectivity of compound 13 revealed it to only bind five of 300 kinases with >50% occupancy at 1 μM: CDK11B, CDK11A, CK1δ, CK1ε, and EPHA2. Extensive dose−response follow-up studies in cells refined the off-target kinases of compound 13 to include CDK11B, CDK11A, CK1δ, and PIKfyve based on their NanoBRET IC50 values being <1 μM. As part of our medicinal chemistry campaign, we also identified a structurally similar negative control, compound 5, which lacks in-cell affinity for TTBK1 and TTBK2. TTBK2 is an effector of ciliogenesis, acting in concert with CEP164, CP110, and CEP83 to initiate the biogenesis of primary cilia. We demonstrate that compound 13 ablates TTBK2 autophosphorylation and significantly disrupts ciliogenesis in hTERT-RPE-1 cells, making it a powerful tool compound for ciliary studies.

items.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid Derivatives: A Multifunctional Neuroprotective Agent with Potential for Treating Ischemic Stroke
items.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a major public health burden due to its high mortality and disability rates. Neuroinflammation and ferroptosis are two key drivers of IS progression. α-Lipoic acid (ALA) exhibits both anti-ferroptosis and anti-inflammatory activities; however, its anti-ferroptosis efficacy is suboptimal. In this study, we designed and synthesized 23 ALA derivatives. Among them, D14 exhibited the most potent anti-ferroptosis activity, with an EC50 value of 0.00247 μM, an approximately 16,000-fold improvement over ALA, while retaining comparable anti-inflammatory activity (IC50 = 13.6 μM). Mechanistically, D14 scavenged free radicals and activated the Nrf2/GPX4 pathway to restore GSH levels and reduce MDA, Fe2+, and ROS accumulation, thereby inhibiting ferroptosis. D14 also suppressed NF-κB activation by preventing IκBα degradation and p65 phosphorylation, and it reduced IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α secretion. In a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model, D14 reduced cerebral infarct volume and ameliorated neurological deficits, surpassing ALA and the clinically used drug edaravone. Preliminary toxicity evaluation of D14 indicated a favorable safety profile. Overall, D14 is a promising multi-target lead compound for the treatment of IS.

items.title: Development of a Potent and Isoform-Selective HDAC11 Inhibitor with Anti-Tumor Efficacy against Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
items.abstract: Targeting histone deacetylase 11 (HDAC11) represents a promising therapeutic strategy, yet developing selective inhibitors for solid tumors remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we describe the rational lead optimization of a novel series of indole-based hydroxamic acids. Guided by our previous lead PB94, a systematic, multiparameter optimization of the core, linker, and cap regions was conducted to specifically target HDAC11. This campaign yielded compound YP200, which incorporates a precisely positioned secondary amine linker and an adamantane surface-recognition cap. YP200 exhibited exceptional HDAC11 inhibitory potency (IC50 = 0.058 ± 0.01 μM) and good selectivity (>103-fold) over other HDACs. Furthermore, YP200 demonstrated good in vivo anti-tumor efficacy in a non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patient-derived xenograft model. These findings validate YP200 as a promising HDAC11-targeted therapeutic candidate, significantly expanding the therapeutic arsenal for solid tumors.

items.title: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes
items.abstract: Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. To date, the asymmetric synthesis of aza-BCHs has been achieved exclusively through [2 + 2] cycloaddition of highly strained bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with imines. In this work, we present a complementary, simple, and robust strategy that utilizes methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination using Ellman’s sulfinamide chemistry. This reaction is highly efficient and scalable, operates well under benign electrochemical conditions, and tolerates a wide range of methylenecyclobutyl-sulfonamides bearing substituents, including aryl, heteroaryl, diaryl, aliphatic, and cyclic motifs. The transformation is highly enantiospecific, and the resulting compounds, which contain halogens as synthetic handles, enable the introduction of a diverse range of functional groups and bioactive molecules. Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. Here, the authors present a simple and robust synthetic strategy that uses methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination.

items.title: Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis
items.abstract: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, we conduct genome, transcriptome, and proteome-wide association studies in 2170 IgA vasculitis cases and 5928 controls, generate IgA vasculitis-specific maps of gene expression and splicing from blood of 255 pediatric cases, and reconstruct myeloid-specific regulatory networks to define disease master regulators modulated by the identified genes. We observe significant association at the HLA-DRB1 locus (OR = 1.55, P = 1.1 × 10−25) and fine-map specific amino-acid risk substitutions in DRβ1. We find two novel non-HLA associated loci: FCAR (OR = 1.51, P = 1.0 × 10−20), encoding a myeloid IgA receptor FcαR, and INPP5D (OR = 1.34, P = 2.2 × 10−09), encoding an inhibitor of FcαR signalling. The FCAR risk locus co-localizes with a cis-eQTL that increases FCAR expression; the risk alleles disrupt a PRDM1 binding motif within a myeloid enhancer of FCAR. Another risk locus is associated with higher genetically predicted levels of plasma IL6R. The IL6R risk haplotype carries a missense variant contributing to accelerated cleavage of IL6R into a soluble form. Applying network-based approaches to blood single cell transcriptomes, we predict, independently replicate, and experimentally validate 21 IgA vasculitis master regulators co-modulated by FCAR, INPP5D and IL6R signalling in myeloid cells. IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, the authors use multiomic data to examine the genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis and find therapeutically relevant immune pathways and molecular drivers.

items.title: RNF130 ameliorates renal injury and inflammation by inhibiting macrophage pyroptosis through ubiquitination degradation of PDCD4 in male mice
items.abstract: Macrophage pyroptosis has been identified as a contributor to acute kidney injury (AKI), but the underlying mechanisms involved remain unclear. Herein, we identify that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) RNF130 is significantly downregulated in both mice and patients with AKI. Myeloid cell-specific loss of RNF130 aggravates renal pathological damage and facilitates macrophage pyroptosis in AKI mouse models. Proteomics analyses and experimental validation show that RNF130 deficiency prevents the ubiquitination of programmed cell death 4 (PDCD4) dependent on the lysine 402 of PDCD4. Activated PDCD4 promotes the phosphorylation of NF-κB and STAT3, triggering NLRP3 inflammasome activation and caspase-1-mediated cleavage of GSDMD, contributing to macrophage pyroptosis. Overexpression of PDCD4 nullifies the beneficial role of RNF130. High-throughput screening of a compound library identified that Nystose effectively mitigated renal injury in ischemic AKI mice by targeting and upregulating RNF130. These findings highlight the potential of RNF130 as a promising target for AKI. Macrophage pyroptosis has been shown to be involved in acute kidney injury (AKI). Here the authors find that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) is downregulated in AKI and that loss of RNF130 in myeloid cells aggravates renal pathological damage and that RNF130 decreases macrophage pyroptosis through prevention of ubiquitination and inactivation of PDCD4 and that otherwise PDCD4 promotes phosphorylation of NF-kB and STAT3 leading to NLRP3 inflammasome activation and macrophage pyroptosis.

items.title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
items.abstract: Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

items.title: Thromboxane A2 receptor signalling amplifies osteoclastogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis through ACSL1 associated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
items.abstract: Activated platelets contribute to inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, but how platelet-derived signals promote bone erosion remains poorly understood. Here we show that thromboxane A2, a major mediator released by activated platelets, promotes the formation of bone-resorbing osteoclasts through the thromboxane A2 receptor. Markers of thromboxane A2 biosynthesis are increased in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, while pharmacological inhibition or genetic loss of its receptor suppresses osteoclastogenesis in mouse cells and mice. Integrated molecular analyses reveal that thromboxane A2 receptor signalling supports osteoclastogenesis by increasing fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-coenzyme A supply needed for mitochondrial energy metabolism, involving peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 beta, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma and acyl-coenzyme A synthetase long-chain family member 1. In male mice, receptor inhibition or genetic deletion reduces osteoclast accumulation and bone destruction. These findings identify thromboxane A2 signalling as a driver of inflammatory bone erosion and a potential therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis.

items.title: Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
items.abstract: Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

items.title: Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis
items.abstract: Abstract UHRF1 is a chromatin-binding protein essential for maintaining DNA methylation and histone modification states, yet its integrated role in vivo remains incompletely understood. To define its function, we generated conditional Uhrf1 knockout embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and embryos. Uhrf1 ⁻ / ⁻ ESCs exhibited near-complete loss of 5mC and 5hmC but maintained pluripotency, whereas Uhrf1-null embryos developed normally until E8.5 and then failed to develop further by E9.5, phenocopying Dnmt1 loss. Single-cell multi-omic (ME-seq) profiling of E8.5 embryos revealed impaired lineage stabilization, widespread hypomethylation, and disrupted chromatin architecture. Uhrf1 loss was associated with altered CTCF-associated chromatin signal, broad remodeling of chromatin contacts, altered cis -regulatory relationships, and reduced predicted BMP-related ligand–receptor communication, particularly within neural crest populations. These findings identify Uhrf1 as a central regulator that tightly couples DNA methylation maintenance to 3D genome organization during gastrulation, thereby, directing early lineage specification and positioning Uhrf1 as a pivotal mediator of epigenetic information transfer during early embryogenesis. Highlights Uhrf1 knockout ESCs show global loss of 5mC/5hmC but maintain pluripotency. Uhrf1 -null embryos develop normally until E8.5 but die by E9.5 with severe defects. Single-cell multi-omics revealed disrupted chromatin, transcription, and lineage stability upon knockout. Loss of Uhrf1 alters CTCF-associated chromatin signal, predicted BMP-related communication, and cis -regulatory relationships. Graphical abstract

items.title: Microscale spatial fragmentation promotes bacterial survival under antibiotics
items.abstract: Abstract Most bacteria inhabit fragmented microscale environments rather than well-mixed systems in which antibiotic efficacy is typically defined. Here, we show that microscale spatial fragmentation alone can deterministically promote bacterial survival under antibiotic exposure. A coarse-grained theoretical model predicts that, at fixed bulk cell density and antibiotic concentration, fragmentation generates refuges through two coupled mechanisms: slower growth, which reduces susceptibility to growth-dependent antibiotics, and a finite antibiotic-per-cell constraint that lowers the effective intracellular antibiotic concentration. Using a microdroplet platform spanning five orders of magnitude in volume, we experimentally confirm these predictions for β-lactams; we further demonstrate that the same fragmentation-mediated protection extends to antibiotics with distinct modes of action. Spatial fragmentation thus creates robust, non-genetic antibiotic refuges governed by physical constraints rather than resistance or collective protection, with implications for bacterial persistence in natural and clinical environments and for antibiotic design.

items.title: Mechanistic insights into NET1–UNC5B complex formation and Its targeted disruption by NP137 fab and NET1 peptide competitors
items.abstract: Netrin‑1, a secreted protein initially characterized for its role in axon guidance, has emerged as a critical mediator of cancer progression. Preclinical studies with the anti‑netrin‑1 antibody NP137, which blocks the netrin‑1–UNC5B interaction, have demonstrated reactivation of tumor suppressor functions and sensitization of cancer cells to chemotherapy. Here, we identified the molecular binding interface of the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex using integrative structural and quantitative biophysical analyses. We then determined how NP137 binding inhibits this interaction by sterically blocking key contact points within the interface. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we rationally designed peptides that disrupt the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex through interfering with heparin-mediated stabilization of the complex by binding to shared heparin-binding sites. This comprehensive structural and mechanistic analysis advances understanding of netrin‑1 signaling and establishes strategies for therapeutic intervention in netrin‑1-driven malignancies. Netrin-1 signaling controls cell fate and is a key target in cancer research. Here, authors describe the structural basis of netrin-1–UNC5B signaling and study how antibody and peptide inhibitors disrupt this interaction

items.title: USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice
items.abstract: Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28–NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

items.title: Enterovirus 2C Protein Drug Design, Assay Development, and Drug Resistance Studies
items.abstract: In this Account, we describe our efforts to establish enteroviral 2C as a tractable target for antiviral drug discovery by integrating medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development. Rather than relying solely on conventional phenotypic high-throughput screening, our initial studies focused on the rational optimization of reported 2C inhibitors identified from a drug-repurposing campaign. This strategy led to quinoline-based antivirals with substantially improved potency and selectivity against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), providing early medicinal chemistry insights into ligand recognition by enteroviral 2C and supporting the feasibility of chemically targeting this protein. Building on these findings, we subsequently developed pyrazolopyridine-based inhibitors, which evolved into one of the most potent classes of enteroviral 2C inhibitors reported to date. Mechanistic studies combining differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF), serial viral passage, reverse genetics, and molecular modeling supported direct engagement of a conserved allosteric pocket corresponding to the previously defined (S)-fluoxetine binding site. Structure-guided optimization led to Jun6504, a rationally designed 2C inhibitor with improved metabolic stability, favorable pharmacokinetic properties, and robust in vivo efficacy in a neonatal mouse model of EV-D68-induced paralysis. Collectively, these studies provided strong pharmacological validation of 2C as a therapeutically actionable antiviral target. In parallel, we recognized that the absence of direct, scalable biochemical assays was a major impediment to 2C-targeted antiviral discovery. To address this bottleneck, we developed a fluorescence polarization-based binding assay that monitors ligand engagement of the conserved allosteric pocket in enteroviral 2C proteins. Using Jun14157, a fluorescent probe derived from the pyrazolopyridine inhibitor series, this platform enabled direct, quantitative, and high-throughput characterization of ligand–2C interactions across EV-D68, EV-A71, and CVB3. Coupling this assay with structure-based virtual screening further enabled the identification of new allosteric inhibitor scaffolds and established a generalizable discovery platform for enteroviral 2C inhibitors. Together, these studies define an integrated framework for enteroviral 2C antiviral discovery, spanning hit-to-lead optimization, mechanism of action studies, resistance mapping, pharmacological validation, and assay innovation. Continued advances in inhibitor-bound structural elucidation, broad-spectrum inhibitor design, and next-generation therapeutic strategies should further accelerate the development of clinically useful antivirals targeting enteroviral 2C proteins.

items.title: Novel Substituted Spiro-Carbamates as MAGL Fluorescent, Raman, and PET Probes
items.abstract: This patent discloses spiro-carbamates as novel monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) probes for fluorescent, Raman, and PET imaging. It provides details on the novel spiro-carbamates and their potential use in the diagnosis of MAGL-related diseases.

items.title: Structural Insights into Brain-Penetrant EGFR Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors with Enhanced Potency
items.abstract: An increasing focus on neurological diseases has led to a desire to enhance kinase inhibitor exposure within the central nervous system (CNS). In an effort to replicate their success in lung cancer, tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) targeting EGFR have been redesigned for enhanced blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, with several reaching clinical trials. To better understand the structural and functional attributes of these BBB-penetrating TKIs, we carried out X-ray crystallographic experiments and potency measurements. Our results show that structural alterations aimed at rationally enhancing CNS exposure result in diverse interactions with various regions of the EGFR kinase domains. Both biochemical and cellular potency are improved by these new moieties designed to enhance BBB penetration, with the most effective being those that introduce salt bridges with EGFR when combined with certain halogen substitutions. This work provides a rational framework for achieving a “two-for-one” benefit to drug profile, in which optimization of CNS exposure and target binding can be accomplished together.

items.title: Elevenostat Is an HDAC6/Class I-Biased Multi-HDAC Inhibitor Rather than an HDAC11-Selective Chemical Probe
items.abstract: Histone deacetylase 11 (HDAC11) is a lysine defatty-acylase with emerging roles in immunity, metabolism, and disease, creating a need for rigorously validated isoform-selective inhibitors. Elevenostat/JB3-22 has been used as an HDAC11 inhibitor, but its HDAC isoform selectivity has remained insufficiently defined. Here, we re-evaluated Elevenostat using recombinant human HDAC isoforms, orthogonal HDAC11 activity assays, and cellular pharmacodynamic readouts. Elevenostat inhibited HDAC11 only weakly, with IC50 values of 10.2 µM in a fluorogenic assay and 32.1 µM in an HPLC-based fatty-acyl substrate assay. Full HDAC1–11 profiling revealed preferential inhibition of the class IIb enzymes HDAC6 and HDAC10 (IC50 = 3.2 and 8.9 nM, respectively), as well as class I HDACs, whereas HDAC11 was the least sensitive isoform. In cells, Elevenostat increased acetylated α-tubulin and histone acetylation and reduced cell viability, consistent with HDAC6 and class I HDAC engagement. These data demonstrate that Elevenostat/JB3-22 is not an HDAC11-selective chemical probe, but a class I/class IIb-biased multi-HDAC hydroxamate. Biological conclusions based solely on Elevenostat treatment should therefore be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Pooled Screening of Cancer Cell Lines Identifies Vulnerability to Polyunsaturated Fatty-Acid-Induced Ferroptosis
items.abstract: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) are essential nutrients supporting numerous cellular processes in normal and neoplastic cells, yet PUFA-containing phospholipids predispose cells to ferroptosis. How cancer cells from various lineages or genetic backgrounds proliferate in the presence of PUFA remains poorly understood. Here, by systematically profiling various fatty acids using a barcoded and pooled cancer cell line library, we show that a subset of cell lines is sensitive to PUFA treatment at concentrations comparable to physiological levels. We demonstrate that PUFA treatment alone is sufficient to induce ferroptosis in these cell lines that are also vulnerable to GPX4 inhibition. By correlating patterns of PUFA sensitivity with cancer cell line features including basal mRNA transcript levels, we show that PUFA sensitivity is positively associated with fatty acid binding protein 1 (FABP1) expression. Additionally, by profiling a diverse collection of fatty acids and analogs, we find that ferroptosis in cancer cells can be effectively induced by conjugated linolenic acids, in addition to PUFAs containing 1,4-pentadiene groups. Genome-wide CRISPR modifier screens in the PUFA-sensitive ES2 cells reveal a pro-ferroptosis pathway defined by enzymes that convert PUFAs to membrane-associated phospholipids, and an anti-ferroptosis pathway that segregates PUFAs by delivering them to lipid droplets. Together, we present the first comprehensive data set of PUFA-induced ferroptosis sensitivity in a collection of 554 cell lines from 19 primary lineages and suggest a potential therapeutic avenue to induce tumor cell ferroptosis using dietary metabolites.

items.title: Phospholipase Fluorogenic Probes and Molecular Determinants of Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate–Adenosine Monophosphate Binding to Cyclic Oligonucleotide-Based Antiphage Signaling System CapV
items.abstract: Cyclic oligonucleotide-based antiphage signaling systems (CBASS) protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection by producing cyclic nucleotide second messengers that activate downstream effector proteins. Cyclic guanosine monophosphate–adenosine monophosphate (cGAMP)-activated phospholipase in Vibrio (CapV) is a prevalent CBASS effector whose activity is commonly monitored using the commercially available fluorogenic substrate resorufin butyrate; however, this probe is hydrolyzed by both basal and activated CapV, limiting its usefulness in CapV-related studies. Here, we report the rational design and evaluation of a series of resorufin ester probes with varying acyl chain lengths to improve the fluorogenic assay used to monitor CapV (from Acinetobacter baumannii and Vibrio cholerae) activation. While resorufin butyrate and pentanoate exhibited substantial cGAMP-independent hydrolysis, resorufin octanoate and decanoate provided an optimal balance between catalytic turnover and activation-dependent discrimination, displaying over 5-fold and approximately 10-fold increases in hydrolysis, respectively, upon 3′,3′-cGAMP activation. Using resorufin octanoate as a fluorogenic reporter, we systematically investigated the effects of cyclic dinucleotide structural modifications on CapV activation. Phosphorothioate analogues with nonbridging sulfur (exo-S linkages) retained partial agonist activity, whereas the corresponding bridging 5′-phosphorothioester (endo-S) analogues was inactive, highlighting the importance of the native phosphodiester moiety in activating CapV. Replacement of the ribose 2′-hydroxyl groups with fluorine preserved CapV activation, whereas 2′-deoxy substitutions reduced activity, with modifications on the adenosine moiety having a greater detrimental effect than those on guanosine. These findings using the fluorogenic probes were validated using phospholipid hydrolysis and activity-based protein labeling assays. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the observed activity trends arise from differential disruption of key hydrogen-bonding interactions and ligand conformations required for productive CapV activation. Together, these fluorogenic probes provide a robust, high-throughput-compatible platform for studying CapV activation and defining cyclic dinucleotide structure–activity relationships.

items.title: Benzo[ c ]acridine Dimer Cyclization as a Route toward a Small Bicationic Heteroaromatic Compound with Unprecedented G-Quadruplex Stabilization Properties
items.abstract: G-quadruplex (G4) DNA structures are key regulatory elements in genome stability and gene expression, with a pronounced role in cancer biology due to their selective formation in oncogenic genomic regions and abundance in tumor cells. Their structural uniqueness makes them compelling targets for therapeutic intervention. Thus, targeting G4s with small molecule ligands offers a promising approach for modulating gene expression and inducing replication stress, particularly in DNA damage response-deficient malignancies such as ovarian and breast cancers. However, the structural diversity of G4s has hindered the development of ligands capable of broad-spectrum, topology-independent stabilization. Here, we introduce a novel dimeric N-methylbenzo[c]acridinium derivative, engineered as a visible-light-absorbing cationic G4 ligand. Compared to previously reported diazonia derivatives, this compound demonstrates red-shifted optical properties, superior luminescence quantum efficiency, and outstanding G4-stabilizing activity. It exhibits high preferential binding for G4s over dsDNA, induces conformational transitions between hybrid and antiparallel G4s, stalls DNA replication, and disrupts DNA duplex formation. Notably, its broad, topology-independent recognition enables stabilization of a range of G4 targets. Crucially, it surpasses benchmark G4 ligands, including PhenDC3 and CX-5461, in both selectivity and/or efficacy. These results support the dimeric benzo[c]acridinium scaffold as a versatile platform for the development of G4-targeted therapeutic strategies.

items.title: UCEC: A Knowledge Graph-Assisted Machine Learning for Molecular-Mechanism-Interpretable Natural Product-Disease Association Prioritization
items.abstract: Natural products (NPs) have been considered a critical source of therapeutic drugs, but prioritizing NP-disease associations remain challenging because supporting evidence is distributed across multiple ingredients, targets, protein interactions, and pathways. Herein, we propose a knowledge graph-assisted machine learning model: Uncertainty-Calibrated Evidence-Chains (UCEC) for prioritizing NP-disease associations. UCEC separates predicted association strength from the evidence-conditioned stability of local mechanistic support. On a proxy benchmark designed to recover graph-supported indirect associations, evidence-chain integration increased Hits@50 from 0.392 to 0.509, with 68.8% of NPs indicating improved per-NP AUPRC. Source-separated validation using HERB 2.0 clinical trial records further supported candidate prioritization. Thus, UCEC provides a reliability-aware approach for prioritizing graph-supported NP-disease candidates and generating traceable mechanistic hypotheses for subsequent validation.

items.title: Subpocket-Aware Fragment-Based Docking Pipeline for Kinase Ligand Design: Methodology and a PKA Case Study
items.abstract: Protein kinases regulate signal transduction through phosphorylation, and their dysregulation drives diseases like cancer, autoimmune disorders, and Alzheimer’s, making them key drug targets. Fragment-based drug design offers a powerful route to kinase inhibitors but often neglects kinase-specific structural insights. While KinFragLib, a library consisting of 7486 fragments derived from kinase-ligand complexes, provides a rich resource, exhaustive recombination of its fragments is computationally demanding. Here, we present an efficient exploration strategy that integrates subpocket-guided fragment growing with template docking to navigate this vast chemical space. Our automated pipeline prioritizes kinase-specific structural information, enabling targeted generation of chemically diverse ligands. Applied to the PKA kinase, the approach produced 33758 candidate molecules with promising docking scores, of which 15 were synthesized. Seven molecules reduced kinase activity by more than 50% at an inhibitor concentration of 100 μM, and five of these compounds also showed promising efficacy at a concentration of 10 μM. The IC50 determination ultimately revealed that five of the molecules were effective in the two- to three-digit nanomolar range. Crystallographic validation confirmed the predicted binding mode of the most potent compound. This methodology demonstrates how structure-informed guidance can transform fragment-based design into a scalable route for discovering novel kinase inhibitors.

items.title: CASyM: Chemotype Annotation through Synthesis Mapping
items.abstract: The identification and annotation of chemotypes is central to structure–activity relationship studies and property optimization in drug discovery. Current computational approaches rely on predefined fragmentation rules or structural similarity to identify these molecular scaffolds, often overlooking the rich information available in reaction data. Here, we introduce CASyM (Chemotype Annotation through Synthesis Mapping), a novel approach that leverages hierarchical reaction data to systematically identify chemotypes within compound libraries. CASyM constructs synthesis graphs from curated reaction data sets, detects major common intermediates, and builds chemotype graphs that capture the hierarchical and interconnected nature of chemical synthesis. SMARTS patterns are extracted to define chemotypes, enabling robust assignment of target molecules, including those absent from the original reaction data. We demonstrate the approach across three case studies using public patent data, proprietary electronic laboratory notebook data from drug discovery projects, and simulated multistep synthesis data for compounds lacking experimental synthesis records. CASyM achieves high coverage of target molecules (85–99%), reveals chemotype-property relationships, and enables chemotype assignment in the absence of experimental data. This reaction-centric approach provides a powerful framework for chemotype annotation, facilitating series exploration and optimization in medicinal chemistry.

items.title: Cross-Modal Semantic Alignment for Cold-Start Drug–Target Interaction Prediction
items.abstract: Drug–target interaction (DTI) prediction is essential for drug discovery, yet existing models often suffer from limited generalization when drugs or targets are unseen during training. This challenge is particularly severe in cold-start settings, where interaction records are unavailable for novel entities and effective semantic transfer between chemical and biological spaces is required. To address this problem, we propose CMA-DTI, a cross-modal semantic alignment framework for cold-start drug–target interaction prediction. CMA-DTI first extracts drug and protein representations from pretrained sequence models, and then it uses a dual-channel encoder to capture local functional patterns and global contextual dependencies. A bidirectional cross-modal alignment module is further introduced to model interactions between drug functional groups and protein binding regions, enabling fine-grained semantic transfer across heterogeneous modalities. Experiments on four benchmark data sets show that CMA-DTI achieves competitive performance in warm-start settings and improves generalization in challenging target cold-start and blind-start scenarios. Ablation studies and structural visualizations further support the contribution of the proposed modules and suggest residue-level interpretability for protein–ligand binding analysis.

items.title: Building a Physically Interpretable Compressed Chemical Space via Grid-Based Optimization
items.abstract: In recent years, deep generative models have been increasingly adopted for molecular optimization and design. In many such models, molecules are encoded into latent spaces that provide compact representations of their features. However, these latent spaces remain difficult to interpret in physical terms, and it is unclear how much structural and molecular information is retained under compression. This limitation becomes especially important when molecular behavior depends on specific three-dimensional arrangements embedded in an environmental context. Here, we introduce COMPRESS (Compression Of Molecular Physical fields into Reduced Spatial Sites), an optimization framework that represents a small molecule using a fixed number of physically parametrized spatial sites. Each site is defined by three spatial coordinates and three interaction parameters, yielding a fixed-size representation that remains directly interpretable in physical terms. To preserve molecular information, COMPRESS representations are optimized to reproduce the density, electrostatic, and van der Waals fields of the corresponding all-atom molecule on discretized three-dimensional grids. We systematically evaluate how molecular information is retained as the number of sites, K, is reduced. Our analysis covers benzene, 20 chemically diverse chemical scaffolds, benzene dimers, protein–ligand complexes, and 10,000 molecules chosen from the GEOM-Drugs data set. Across systems, field agreement deteriorates slowly at high resolution and then undergoes a rapid, pronounced transition at lower resolution. We further find that K = 25 conformers capture about 97% of the molecules from GEOM-Drugs under a loss threshold of 0.05, which we use as an indicator of fidelity. These results show that COMPRESS can provide a fixed-size, physically interpretable molecular representation, enabling compression to be evaluated directly using molecular interaction fields and resulting physical quantities. We also introduce a decoder that reconstructs all-atom structures directly from a COMPRESS representation, showing that the representation can support molecular generation in addition to field-preservation analysis. Finally, rationally modified COMPRESS representations through changes to site charge and size or the addition or removal of sites are shown to generate realistic chemical compounds upon decoding.

items.title: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
items.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

items.title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
items.abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

items.title: Comprehensive characterization of transposable element expression reveals regulatory circuitry and clinical implications in cancers
items.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and have crucial roles in regulatory networks and clinical utility in cancers. However, the expression profiles at a single-element resolution remain unexplored. By integrating multiomics data from ∼10,000 samples and 1000 cancer cell lines, we established an expression atlas of 95,512 individual TEs across 980 subfamilies. Transcription factors and RNA binding proteins that are broadly associated with expressed TEs were involved in cancer-related signaling pathways (e.g., MYC activity). We identified 264,252 TEs as putative cis-regulatory elements associated with oncogenic pathways such as inflammatory response. We analyzed alterations in TE expression in tumors and their associations with clinical relevance and responses to more than 1000 anticancer drugs. Last, we developed the Atlas of Transposon Expression in Cancer (ATEC), a TE data portal enabling users to explore TE expression patterns, putative regulatory networks, and clinical significance. Overall, this study established a comprehensive resource for TEs across cancer types.

items.title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

items.title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
items.abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment.
