Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

items.title: Rapid coral bleaching recovery via symbiont transfer from healthy corals
items.abstract: Coral bleaching, the temperature-induced loss of dinoflagellate symbionts, is a major driver of global coral reef decline. Although corals can regain symbionts through repopulation of residual symbionts or via environmental acquisition, these processes are often too slow to prevent coral mortality. Mechanisms that enable rapid and effective symbiont reintroduction leading to full recovery remain largely unknown. Here, we demonstrate coral bleaching recovery through contact-mediated transfer of symbionts from healthy corals using small coral fragments. We show that symbiont transfer is rapid, occurring over days to weeks, and highly efficient, with only brief physical contact with healthy corals required. A single week of contact, and in some cases as few as 3 days, provides sufficient symbionts to initiate sustained and full self-recovery. By 1 week, symbiont population doubling time is approximately 4 days, up to an order of magnitude faster than most recovery times for corals in the field. We identify tissue fusion as the mechanism enabling directional symbiont transfer from healthy to bleached coral tissue. As a result, contact-dependent recovery is restricted to corals of the same genet, whereas heterologous genet pairings trigger antagonistic interactions. However, symbiont transfer via polyp uptake occurs immediately upon contact in both same-genet and mixed-genet pairings, revealing an additional, slower pathway for symbiont transfer that is insufficient on its own to support colony recovery. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized natural process for efficiently reintroducing symbionts to bleached corals, providing a foundation for research into potential recovery interventions.

items.title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus
items.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen’s diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

items.title: A transcriptional cofactor GRIP1 drives PPARγ DNA binding and p300-dependent enhancer activity during homeostatic macrophage polarization
items.abstract: Homeostatic macrophages maintain tissue health and resolve inflammation. Upon sustained exposure to type II cytokine IL4, transcription factors STAT6, KLF4, EGR2 and a ligand-regulated nuclear receptor PPARγ orchestrate the M2 IL4 ‘polarization’, marked by enhancer RNA (eRNA) production near multiple M2 genes. The mechanisms of enhancer activation by unliganded PPARγ are poorly understood. We interrogated cofactor requirements for PPARγ-driven gene expression in M2 IL4 , including those lacking PPARγ or a ligand-dependent nuclear receptor coregulator NCoA2/GRIP1 vs. macrophages treated with the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone. As expected, rosiglitazone activated conventional PPARγ targets; GRIP1 deletion blunted their induction and depleted GRIP1-interacting histone acetyltransferase p300 from PPARγ-bound sites. Surprisingly, GRIP1 colocalized with unliganded PPARγ in M0 and M2 IL4 , and GRIP1 ablation dramatically reduced genome-wide DNA binding of PPARγ itself while promoting broad deposition of CTCF insulator. Functionally, GRIP1 deletion mirrored PPARγ deficiency, establishing GRIP1 as a central regulator of unliganded PPARγ DNA binding, required for both eRNA and mRNA transcription of PPARγ targets in homeostatic macrophages.

items.title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
items.abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

items.title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis
items.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children. K. pneumoniae isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from K. pneumoniae neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative K. pneumoniae vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of K. pneumoniae. Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal K. pneumoniae infection.

items.title: C11-conjugated soft glucocorticoid antibody–drug conjugates for precision immunomodulation
items.abstract: Soft glucocorticoid ADCs undergo lysosomal cleavage and self-immolation to release free GC. Released GC activates the GC receptor, which translocates to the nucleus to induce anti-inflammatory genes and suppress inflammatory cytokines.

items.title: Investigating the Antioxidant Potential of Annona muricata Leaves- An in silico Assisted in vitro Approach
items.abstract: Annona muricata is traditionally used in the treatment of various infectious and chronic non – communicable diseases. The antioxidant activity of the leaves of A.muricata was assessed using DPPH scavenging assay. The DPPH radical scavenging potential was compared with the proven antioxidant, ascorbic acid. The result of the study showed that methanolic leaf extract of Annona muricata exhibited the greatest antioxidant activity than the other three extracting solvents used. Six major phytochemicals present in A. muricata were taken from Dr. Duke’s Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical database and docked with Xanthine oxidase (XO) protein. Campesterol obtained the minimum binding energy value and hence maximum stability. The experimental results were in agreement with the docking results. Fifteen similar molecules of Campesterol were taken from PubChem and docked with XO which revealed that 2-methyltetracycloheptade-7-en-5-ol based scaffolds can act as potent XO inhibitors.

items.title: Old Drugs, New Targets: Multi-parameter computational prioritization of FDA‑approved, brain‑penetrant drugs as isoform‑selective GSK‑3β inhibitors for Alzheimer’s disease
items.abstract: Glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β), a central regulator of tau phosphorylation and amyloid pathology, with its β isoform (GSK-3β) used as a main driver of the Alzheimer’s disease (AD) neurodegeneration. It is a validated therapeutic target in AD, yet no isoform-selective, brain penetrant inhibitors have reached clinical use. This paper screens 1000+ FDA-approved drugs by dual-isoform docking (GSK3α/β) and 8-seed redocking, prioritizing compounds by its α/β selectivity (G_select = G_GSK3A − G_GSK3B), CNS penetration, Hinge H-bonds, and pose plausibility. High selectivity alone provided misleading: filgotinib showed the largest G_select (+1.25 ± 0.03 kcal/mol), yet a reproducibly implausible pose, while abemaciclib (ΔG_select = +0.80 ± 0.09 kcal/mol; plausible‑pose fraction = 0.88) and peficitinib (+0.008 ± 0.02 kcal/mol; 1.00) provided a moderate selectivity with structurally reliable binding. Multi-seed redocking led to a hidden instability (loratinib plausible in only 25% of the seeds). This work provides a ranked, hypothesis-generating shortlist by establishing that isoform-selective GSK3β inhibitor discovery demands joint optimization of selectivity, and multi-seed pose stability, rather than affinity of GSK-3β alone. The following results are computationally prioritized candidates, rather than experimentally verified GSK-3β inhibitors.

items.title: The eventful journey of a ligand in and out of the binding site
items.abstract: The route a ligand follows to reach and leave a protein binding site typically involves complex molecular mechanisms that shape its efficacy as a biologically active compound. These mechanisms are reflected in the binding and unbinding kinetics, which often predict biological activity better than binding affinity alone, yet their calculation remains a bottleneck in ligand characterization. Here, we propose an approach that combines committor-based enhanced sampling with spectral analysis of the infinitesimal generator to characterize in detail how a ligand reaches the binding site of a protein and is eventually expelled. Applied to the paradigmatic benzamidine (BEN)–trypsin complex and the congeneric para-amino benzamidine (PAB), this framework reveals distinct and multifaceted binding pathways for the two ligands, uncovering a previously uncharacterized BEN binding site that competes with the crystallographic site, while identifying a common rotational bottleneck for unbinding. The computed unbinding free energies closely agree with experimental measurements. The spectral decomposition of the infinitesimal generator provides access to the slow dynamical modes of the system. From the slowest mode, we derive residence times and kinetic rate constants that agree with available experimental data and with independent OPES flooding simulations, while requiring substantially less computational effort. This approach offers a privileged perspective to resolve the complexity of protein–ligand binding-unbinding process, with potential applications to ligand screening and the characterization of multiple binding sites.

items.title: Light-driven metal-free thiocarbonyl – olefin metathesis: a general route to sterically hindered alkenes
items.abstract: Highly substituted olefins are attractive scaffolds for molecular machines, optical materials and medicinal chemistry, whilst also serving as valuable intermediates in organic synthesis. However, their efficient and general preparation remains challenging, particularly in light of sustainability requirements. Here, we report a metal-free photochemical thiocarbonyl – olefin metathesis that provides access to a broad range of tri- and tetra-substituted alkenes, where light irradiation promotes both the regioselective formation and subsequent fragmentation of thietane intermediates. The scarcely explored photochemical cycloreversion of isolated thietanes was first thoroughly reinvestigated, leading to the proposal of a thioparabanate-photocatalyzed mechanism supported by Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TD-DFT) calculations. Then, the combination of this cycloreversion with a thia-Paternò_Büchi reaction into a photochemical cascade, enables the in situ generation of the thietane intermediate. Starting from thiocarbonyl substrates, independently prepared or generated in situ via Norrish type II fragmentation of phenacyl sulfide precursors, and diverse alkene partners, this light-mediated thiocarbonyl – olefin coupling offers an innovative and sustainable entry to a library of densely substituted olefins. The synthetic utility of this strategy is also demonstrated through its application to molecular motor templates synthesis.

items.title: Hg(II) Coordination in Human Thioredoxin Reductase 1: Molecular Insights into Mercury Toxicity
items.abstract: Thioredoxin reductase 1 (TrxR1) is an essential selenoprotein oxidoreductase and a sensitive molecular target of mercury, but the coordination chemistry underlying its inhibition by inorganic Hg(II) remains unknown. We use complementary Hg LIII-edge and Se K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), high-energy-resolution fluorescence-detected XAS (HERFDXAS), and density functional theory (DFT) to determine the Hg(II) coordination environment in inhibited human TrxR1. Se K-edge EXAFS provides direct evidence for Hg(II) coordination to catalytic Sec498 in wild-type TrxR1, with a Se–Hg distance of 2.44 Å. Hg LIII-edge EXAFS indicates predominantly two-coordinate, near-digonal Se–Hg–S coordination, with Hg–Se and Hg–S distances of 2.43 and 2.37 Å, respectively. Replacement of Sec498 by cysteine or serine gives bis-thiolate Hg(SR)2 coordination, demonstrating that Sec498 is not essential for Hg(II) binding. Hg Lα1 HERFD-XAS independently supports two-coordinate Hg(II) and distinguishes mixed sulfur/selenium coordination in wild-type TrxR1 from the bis-thiolate U498C variant. DFT calculations show that coordination by the adjacent C-terminal Cys497/Sec498 pair and structures involving the N-terminal redox center are compatible with spectroscopy, but do not unambiguously distinguish their relative energies. In contrast, bis-thiolate coordination in U498S, which retains only Cys497 at the C-terminal redox center, supports recruitment of a cysteine from the N-terminal site. These results directly characterize inorganic Hg(II) binding to TrxR1 and demonstrate how the strong, adaptable chalcogen coordination chemistry of Hg(II) enables it to target the catalytic machinery of this essential cellular redox enzyme.

items.title: DeNoMAP: An Interactive Web Application for Multi-Criteria Prioritization of De Novo Designed Compounds
items.abstract: De novo molecular generation is increasingly used in drug discovery, yet deciding which generated structures merit follow-up remains difficult, because established benchmarking metrics primarily characterize generative models rather than individual compounds. We present DeNoMAP, a general multi-criteria prioritization framework implemented as an interactive, open-access web application, which positions de novo-generated molecules in a normalized three-dimensional space defined by novelty, synthesizability and drug-likeness. A user-defined desirability zone enables transparent and reproducible candidate selection. Novelty is computed against ZINC20 as an external reference collection using the SmallWorld search engine, rather than against the generative model’s training set. Applied to a published library of 8,066 DNMT1 candidates, the web application identified 15 prioritized compounds among 852 successfully evaluated cluster representatives. DeNoMAP is publicly available at https://denomap.streamlit.app/ and its source code at https://github.com/flfeitosa/DeNoMAP.

items.title: Arsenite (Trisenox) Bridges the Redox Centers of Thioredoxin Reductase
items.abstract: Arsenic trioxide (Trisenox) is an effective treatment for acute promyelocytic leukemia and is being explored for broader anticancer applications, yet our understanding of the molecular basis of its anticancer activity remains incomplete. Under physiological conditions arsenic trioxide forms arsenite, As(OH)3, which has been proposed to target the thioredoxin system. Here, we investigate the structural basis of arsenite interaction with mammalian thioredoxin reductase 1 (TrxR1, TXNRD1), a flavoenzyme selenoprotein essential for maintaining cellular redox homeostasis. Arsenic and selenium K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy, including highenergy resolution fluorescence detected (HERFD)-XAS, were combined with site-directed mutagenesis and density functional theory calculations. Wild-type TrxR1 forms a well-defined As(SeR)(SR)2 coordination environment in which arsenite binds the catalytic selenocysteine residue Sec498 and bridges the C-terminal and N-terminal redox centers of the enzyme. Replacement of Sec498 by cysteine yields an As(OH)(SR)2 species, whereas substitution by serine abolishes detectable binding. These results provide the first direct structural characterization of arsenite bound to TrxR1 and reveal a mechanism by which arsenite inhibits catalysis through crosslinking of the enzyme's redox centers. The findings establish a molecular basis for targeting of the thioredoxin system by arsenic trioxide and provide new insight into the chemistry underlying its anticancer activity.

items.title: An Analytical Full-Dimensional Potential Energy Surface for the H + C3H8 Hydrogen Abstraction Reaction: Non-Equivalence of the Primary Hydrogens and Variational Transition State Theory Kinetics
items.abstract: A new analytical full-dimensional potential energy surface, PES-2026, is reported for the gas-phase hydrogen abstraction reaction H + C3H8 → H2 + C3H7. It is built within the valence bond–molecular mechanics, VB-MM, framework and depends on 72 parameters, 65 of which were optimized against a focal-point CBS benchmark and against UMP2/cc-pVTZ geometries, harmonic frequencies and reaction paths. The surface describes the two chemically distinct abstraction channels, primary and secondary, and resolves them into three kinetically distinct channels: the six primary hydrogens are not equivalent, two of them being abstracted through an anti and four through a gauche saddle point whose adiabatic barriers differ by 0.26 kcalmol−1. Classical barrier heights of 12.05, 11.68 and 9.44 kcalmol−1 were obtained for the anti-primary, gauche-primary and secondary channels, reproducing the benchmark to within 0.04 kcalmol−1, and a relaxed two-dimensional torsional scan that did not enter the fit is reproduced with a root-mean-square deviation of 0.11 kcalmol−1. Thermal rate constants were computed between 200 and 1000 K with variational transition state theory and multidimensional tunnelling, CVT/µOMT, treating the three channels separately and summing them. At 300 K the total rate constant, 9.4×10−16 cm3 molecule−1 s−1, is 0.85 times the Tsang evaluation, and the calculated primary contribution, 5.6%, compares with the 4.3–4.7% derived from experiment and improves on the 9.5% of the most recent direct-dynamics study. Kinetic isotope effects are predicted for substrate and for attacking-atom substitution; the latter is inverse below ∼800 K, which is traced to the lowering of the adiabatic barrier upon deuteration of the incoming atom. The muonium analogue is also examined and is found to lie beyond the reach of a harmonic treatment.

items.title: A Highly Stable Cyclic (Amino)(Aryl)Nitrenium Radical Dication Exhibiting Temperature-Dependent Radical Bistability Maruti Suryavansi,a Manas Khatua,b,d Bappaditya Goswami,c Apurba Kumar Pal,a Subhas Samanta,*d and K. Geetharani*
items.abstract: Development of air- and thermally stable organic radicals remains challenging due to the highly transient nature of the free radicals. Herein, we present a strategy for isolating a highly stable N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) stabilized cyclic (amino)(aryl)nitrenium (CAArN) radical. This is the first example of a CAArN radical isolated in the solid state, and its identity has been confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and various spectroscopic studies. These CAArN radical exhibits remarkable stability towards air, water, strong acidic/alkaline conditions, aqueous buffers, and high temperature (~412 °C). The radical residing on two distinct redoxactive motifs exhibits unique temperature-dependent bistability in solution, as evidenced by VT-EPR and VT-UV-vis spectral studies. Polar solvents have played a crucial role in stabilizing the imidazolium motif, thereby facilitating the radical bistability. Further, by employing KC8, selective reduction of the NHC-moiety bonded to the CAArN radical was achieved to yield Thiele’s type hybrid diradicaloid.

items.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Subsequent Drug Release Trajectories using Early Release Information in PLGA Microparticles
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-release behavior from PLGA microparticles may reduce the experimental effort required for formulation characterization, yet conventional prediction approaches rely primarily on static molecular and formulation descriptors and do not incorporate experimentally observed release behavior as it becomes available during an ongoing experiment. Here, we develop a machine-learning framework that integrates molecular and formulation descriptors with early-release measurements to predict subsequent drug-release trajectories from PLGA microparticles. A dataset comprising 4,913 release observations from 321 formulations was analyzed using random forest regression with formulation-grouped cross-validation. Using a common set of 89 formulations, we systematically evaluated the predictive value of increasing amounts of early-release information. Prediction accuracy improved with additional early measurements, but the incremental benefit progressively diminished, with two and three measurements capturing 64.7% and 91.9% of the total predictive gain achieved with four measurements, respectively. The value of early information also varied substantially across formulations, with greater benefits generally observed for formulations that were more difficult to predict from static descriptors alone. Trajectory-level analysis further revealed that early observations constrained subsequent release trajectories to different extents across formulations. These findings demonstrate that experimentally observed early-release behavior provides formulation-specific predictive information beyond static descriptors and establish a data-driven framework for quantifying information sufficiency in drug-release characterization.

items.title: Validation Design Governs the Apparent Predictive Performance of Machine Learning for PLGA Drug Release
items.abstract: Reliable generalization is essential for machine-learning models intended to predict drug-release behavior across heterogeneous experimental settings. However, multi-study experimental data often contain closely related formulations generated under shared materials, processing conditions, release protocols, and laboratory practices, creating hidden dependencies between training and test data. Such dependencies can make model performance appear stronger than its ability to generalize to genuinely new experimental domains. Here, we examine how validation topology governs the apparent predictability of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) microparticle drug release using a public dataset containing 321 formulations and 4,913 release observations collected across 113 studies. Using a common LightGBM prediction framework, we compare validation schemes ranging from random observation splitting to strict study-grouped holdout. Predictive performance decreases markedly as train–test independence becomes more stringent, with 𝑅! declining from 0.939 under random point splitting to 0.616–0.625 under formulation-level holdout and 0.372 when entire studies are withheld. Controlled overlap experiments further show that retaining samestudy sibling formulations in the training set systematically increases apparent performance, while nearest-neighbor analysis reveals lower prediction error for formulations lying closer to the training distribution, particularly when their nearest training counterpart originates from the same study. These results show that formulation-level independence alone does not ensure experimental-domain independence and demonstrate that apparent drug-release predictability is strongly conditioned by validation design. Study-aware validation therefore provides a more rigorous basis for assessing generalization of machine-learning models trained on heterogeneous multi-study experimental data.

items.title: Triple Atom Transfer-Enabled α-C(sp3)-H Aminomethylation of Aliphatic Amines: General and Modular Access to Vicinal Diamines
items.abstract: Vicinal diamines are prevalent structural elements in organic molecules. In particular, those featuring a tertiary alkylamine motif are commonly found in biologically active molecules and therapeutic agents. However, methods for the efficient construction of these architectures from inexpensive and readily available feedstocks remain scarce. Here, we report a mild photocatalytic protocol for the modular synthesis of vicinal alkyl diamines via triple atom transfer-enabled α-C(sp3)–H aminomethylation. This transformation integrates halogen-atom transfer (XAT) and intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) processes to furnish key α-amido alkyl radicals, which subsequently add to in situ-generated iminium ions. Critical to the success of the reaction is the cooperative action of a nickel complex and a zinc salt, which jointly promote the aminomethylation process. Utility of this method is demonstrated through late-stage modification of complex amine molecules, scale-up experiments, and ready access to scaffold-diverse free vicinal diamines. In addition, compatibility with aromatic aldehydes and the ability to functionalize alternative C–H sites further expand the chemical space of diamine architectures, highlighting the robustness and synthetic versatility of this protocol.

items.title: A class A-trained GPCR activation-state classifier transfers to class B1, with attention mass in GLP-1R, GCGR and GIPR spiking at arginine 6.37x37, the TM6 member of the cytoplasmic polar network
items.abstract: Receptor activation state is the structural variable that most GPCR drug discovery is implicitly trying to control. Using class A GPCR structures only, we trained the Receptor Class-Activation-Map Localizer (RCL), a classifier that distinguishes active from inactive GPCR structures, and evaluated it on class B1, a family it never saw. Pooled class B1 performance was AUROC 0.9532 (95% CI 0.9201 to 0.9863, n = 146). On GLP-1R, held out entirely, it reached AUROC 1.0000 across 43 structures (37 active, 6 inactive). Attention in GLP-1R concentrates at the cytoplasmic end of TM6, a region also named in the pre-registered specification. Against a permutation null, the intracellular third of that helix is enriched 6.78 to 11.30-fold, against 2.93 to 4.01-fold for the helix taken in full. Within that third a single position dominates. R348, generic number 6.37x37, carries the attention maximum in 42 of 43 GLP-1R structures, active and inactive alike and apo structures included, holding a median of 53.58 times the attention mass a uniform distribution would place on a single residue. The same position carries the maximum in 17 of 18 GCGR and 6 of 9 GIPR structures, where it is R346 and R338 respectively; it is an arginine in all three receptors. That position was independently mutated in GLP-1R and reported to modulate receptor activation a decade before this model existed. Before the model was trained we specified and committed a single pass criterion, that attention mass would concentrate in the cytoplasmic third. It was met: enrichment 2.07-fold at 6X18 and 1.94-fold at 6XOX, p < 0.0001 in both. This is a result about activation state rather than about pathway preference; no structure in training carried a pathway label. It recovers known activation biology at the level of a single residue: the position carrying the maximum is the TM6 member of the cytoplasmic polar network, a feature independently described as holding the receptor base closed and as breaking when the receptor couples to a G protein. That a model trained without positional supervision places its attention maximum on a characterized activation residue, in a receptor class it never saw, is what makes these maps a usable input into structure-aware biased-ligand discovery.

items.title: Aromatic cis-capping ligands reconfigure a coordination cage system for allosterically controlled BODIPY uptake and release
items.abstract: Biological allostery enables precise molecular recognition and complex function, yet emulating this phenomenon in aqueous synthetic systems remains a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that remote cis-capping ligand (L C ) effects can reconfigure a dynamic metal-organic cage (MOC) system for pronounced allosteric guest uptake and release in water. Incorporation of bipyridine (bpy) as L C into a (Pd-L C ) 6 TImB 4 MOC (TImB = 1,3,5-tri(1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzene) shifts the isomer preference from a tube, favored when L C = tetramethylethylenediamine (tmeda), to a capsule-dominated ensemble, while also inducing axial elongation of the minor tube isomer. DFT calculations reveal two remote effects of bpy: (i) TImB planarization is more readily accommodated – a conformation required for capsule isomer; (ii) a broader range of Pd-imidazole rotations are permittable, enabling the minor tube isomer to elongate. A consequence of these effects is a capsule dominated state that hinders the encapsulation of linear aromatic guests, including a water-insoluble BODIPY fluorophore. We show that SO 4 2‒ acts as an exohedral allosteric effector, triggering upregulation of a BODIPY-binding tube state and a pronounced increase in emission. Removal of the effector anion regenerates the non-binding state, promoting slow release of the BODIPY cargo; a process which operates for other linear guests. This work establishes a general strategy based on remote ligand effects and an allosteric anion effector to control molecular catch-and-release in water.

items.title: High-Resolution MRT-TOF Mass Spectrometry Enables Simultaneous Carbon and Nitrogen Tracing in Stable Isotope Resolved Metabolomics
items.abstract: Stable isotope-resolved metabolomics (SIRM) using dual-isotope tracers, such as [U-13C5,15N2]glutamine, provides complementary insight into carbon and nitrogen metabolism and their integration across interconnected metabolic pathways. However, distinguishing closely spaced 13C- and 15N-containing isotopologues requires resolving power that conventional quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometers (QTOF MS) may not provide. In this study, we evaluated the performance of a multi-reflecting time-of-flight (MRT) mass spectrometer for dual-isotope SIRM using [U-13C5,15N2]glutamine-infused patient-derived tumor xenografts and compared its performance with that of a conventional SYNAPT™ XS QTOF Platform operated at a resolving power of approximately 15,000. A total of 113 metabolites were detected on both platforms, and dual-isotope labeling patterns were evaluated for 29 carbon- and nitrogen-containing metabolites. The Xevo™ MRT Mass Spectrometer, operating at a resolving power of approximately 100,000, resolved closely spaced 13C- and 15N isotopologues that remained unresolved on the SYNAPT™ XS Instrument under the acquisition conditions used. This separation enabled composition-specific isotopologue assignment, independent peak integration, natural-abundance correction, and isotopologue-specific fractional-enrichment analysis. The higher sensitivity of Xevo™ MRT Mass Spectrometer improved detection of low-abundance isotopologues, increasing isotopologue coverage when compared to SYNAPT™ XS MS Instrument. Together, these results demonstrate that MRT-TOF mass spectrometry provides a practical high-resolution platform for dual-isotope SIRM and enables simultaneous assessment of carbon incorporation and nitrogen-transfer reactions within a single experiment.

items.title: Substrate-Controlled Electrophilic Fluorination of Alkenyl Boronates: Direct versus 1,2- H -Migrative Fluorodeboronation
items.abstract: A general fluorodeboronation protocol that converts readily available alkenyl boronates into fluorinated alkenes under mild aqueous biphasic conditions is proposed. The method employs 1-chloromethyl-4-fluoro-1,4-diazoniabicyclo[2.2.2]octane bis-tetrafluoroborate (F-TEDA) as a fluorine source in the presence of KHF 2 , providing broad access to functionalized alkenyl fluorides from β-substituted and β,β-disubstituted alkenyl boronates, including cyclic, heterocyclic, aryl-, heteroaryl-, and alkyl-substituted derivatives, with good functional-group tolerance and preparative scalability. In contrast, αsubstituted alkenyl boronates displayed divergent reactivity, furnishing allylic fluorides through a rearrangement pathway. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support initial electrophilic fluorination of the C=C bond followed by either BF 3 elimination or 1,2-hydride shift, depending on the substitution pattern and stability of the resulting cationic intermediate.

items.title: Radical Cross-Coupling Delivers Complete Sets of Saturated-Heterocyclic Regio- and Stereoprobes for Chemoproteomic Discovery
items.abstract: Three-dimensional molecular shape is a fundamental determinant of protein recognition, yet chemical discovery is often biased toward regio- and stereoisomers that are more readily accessible by synthesis. Here we overcome this constraint using radical cross-coupling (RCC), converting stereoprobe synthesis from selective sampling into exhaustive exploration of three-dimensional chemical space. By combining stereorandomizing and stereopreserving RCC manifolds, we constructed complete piperidine and pyrrolidine matrices (40 and 24 members, respectively) encompassing every theoretically possible regio- and stereoisomer of the corresponding disubstituted scaffolds and expanded these collections to 108 covalent stereoprobes from a small set of readily available precursors. Proteome-wide activity-based protein profiling (ABPP) revealed highly differentiated engagement across regio- and stereoisomers that could further be diversified by changing the covalent reactive group. Selected engagements were structurally characterized by X-ray crystallography, and extension to complementary protein-directed ABPP further expanded the observable ligandability landscape. These findings establish RCC as a practical strategy for removing synthetic bias from stereochemical exploration and identified stereoselective small molecule-protein engagements that could have been missed by conventional non-exhaustive screening.

items.title: Digitalizing Manufacturing Chemistry Targets: A Benchmark for Retrosynthesis Tools
items.abstract: Modern computer-aided synthesis planning (CASP) tools, particularly retrosynthesis planning, are becoming practical aids for the ideation stage of chemical synthesis design. However, the same target molecule can be synthesized via substantially different routes depending on the purpose: a discovery or medicinal chemistry route used to obtain small quantities during early development, or a manufacturing route optimized for industrial-scale production. While CASP tools have been extensively studied and benchmarked for the former, their ability to support manufacturing route design remains largely unexplored. Performance of CASP tools is usually measured by benchmark experiments, which typically report the fraction of target molecules for which a tool can generate a synthesis route, connecting the target molecule through a sequence of intermediates to starting materials. Sometimes, to assess the quality of the generated routes, they are also manually compared with expert-designed routes reported in the literature. Currently, public benchmark datasets focused on process and manufacturing chemistry are lacking. In this study, we take a first step in this direction by analyzing one of the main sources of process chemistry research, the Organic Process Research & Development (OPRD) journal. We reviewed OPRD papers published between 1997 and 2022 and selected 2507 papers reporting multi-step synthesis routes. We then separately collected and digitized the target molecules of corresponding synthesis routes as SMILES strings. This resulted in a collection of 2219 unique target molecules, each paired with the DOI of the original publication reporting their corresponding synthesis route. This benchmark can therefore be used to assess how many process-chemistry targets modern CASP tools can solve and, for solved targets, to compare predicted routes with the expert-designed routes reported in the literature. The dataset is publicly available at: https://github.com/KagakuLab/OPRDbench.

items.title: The Molecular Logic of Platelet-Activating Factor (PAF)
items.abstract: Platelet-activating factor (PAF) is a well-known if enigmatic lipid signal with important roles in inflammatory responses, allergic reactions, autoimmune diseases, and thrombotic cascades. Several lines of evidence suggest that our current model of PAF’s molecular mechanism is inadequate. This report describes a recontextualized model for PAF. The revised model embeds PAF in a plasmalogen-based molecular mechanism in which activation is a spontaneous chemical reaction triggered by environmental conditions that liberates a PAF receptor (PAF-R) agonist from a membrane-bound phospholipid. The active ligand subsequently undergoes a thermodynamically driven spontaneous rearrangement into an inactive isomer, a feature that controls response lifetime. The revised model is a molecule-autonomous set of transformations that create a response with spatial and temporal control. More generally the revised model’s congruence with a similar model for RORγt supports a picture in which plasmalogens form a part of the immune system that is separate from the cell-based innate and adaptive immune systems.

items.title: Catalytic Asymmetric 1,6-Diene Cyclization via Designed Carbocationic 5- and 6- exo Pathways
items.abstract: Catalytic asymmetric electrophilic alkene functionalization provides a powerful strategy for the construction of complex chiral molecules. Despite significant progress in this field, the asymmetric functionalization of alkenes promoted by an electrophilic carbon species via an exo-cyclization mode remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a solution to this challenge: alkenes can undergo designed 5-exo- and 6-exo-carbocationic cyclizations to generate optically pure, complex chiral compounds with high enantio- and diastereoselectivities. In this approach, for 1,6-dienes bearing bulky sulfonamide or quaternary carbon linkers, one double bond of the substrate interacts with an external electrophile, such as a trifluoromethylthio, arylthio, alkylthio, or chlorine species, generating an electrophilic carbon species that promotes the transformation of 1,6-dienes under chiral indane-based chalcogenide catalysis. Notably, the reaction can be terminated by intramolecular nucleophiles via cis-addition or can be captured by various intermolecular nucleophiles. A diverse array of optically pure polycyclic and monocyclic compounds can be obtained, including 5-5-6 tricyclic N-heterocycles and pentasubstituted chiral cyclohexanes. The same strategy can also be efficiently applied to 6-endo cyclizations, leading to the formation of 6-6-6 tricyclic and monocyclic N-heterocycles. The resulting products can be readily converted to various other valuable compounds, further demonstrating the utility of this methodology. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to rationalize the observed selectivities, revealing that the preferential transition-state conformations lower the activation barriers for the desired cyclization pathways. This work offers a versatile platform for the synthesis of enantioenriched chiral scaffolds prevalent in bioactive molecules and pharmaceuticals, significantly expanding the scope of polyene cyclization chemistry.

items.title: Direct Detection of the Calcium–Sodium–Calcium Metal Triad in Thermostable α-Amylases from Bacillus sp. Bacteria in Aqueous Solution by 23Na Quadrupole-Central-Transition NMR Spectroscopy
items.abstract: We report that the Na+ ion within the calcium–sodium–calcium (Ca–Na–Ca) metal triad in two thermostable bacterial α-amylases (ca. 58 kDa) can be directly detected by 23Na (I = 3/2) quadrupole-central-transition (QCT) NMR spectroscopy in aqueous solution. We show that 23Na QCT NMR signals from hyperthermostable Bacillus licheniformis α-amylase (BLA) and its mesophilic homologue, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens α-amylase (BAA), exhibit remarkable subppm spectral resolution, which is unprecedented in NMR studies of quadrupolar nuclei in proteins. Using this new 23Na QCT NMR methodology, we examine the pH-dependent unfolding, melting temperatures (Tm), long-term thermal inactivation profiles, and chemical denaturing of BAA and BLA. We also use 23Na QCT NMR to monitor EDTA titration experiments, which yielded the apparent binding constants of the Na+ ion to BAA and BLA to be (0.3 ± 0.1) × 109 and (0.6 ± 0.1) × 109 M–1, respectively. Because the Ca–Na–Ca metal triad is located in the vicinity of the active cleft, the subppm spectral resolution of 23Na QCT NMR makes it possible to detect subtle changes of the enzyme structure caused by the presence of inhibitors such as acarbose and quercetin. This work represents the first time that Na+ ions tightly bound to an enzyme are directly observed by 23Na QCT NMR in aqueous solution. This new 23Na QCT NMR approach can potentially be extended to detection of other metal ions with quadrupolar nuclei such as K+, Mg2+, and Zn2+ in metalloenzymes in their native aqueous environment.

items.title: A Standalone Flavoprotein Monooxygenase Directs Divergent Tropolone Skeletal Editing through Baeyer–Villiger-Triggered Rearrangement
items.abstract: Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. Complementary well-tempered metadynamics simulations and quantum-chemical calculations support a Baeyer–Villiger branching mechanism, wherein the AO276 active site may preferentially stabilize alternative migration-competent conformations of a putative Criegee intermediate. Each conformation aligns a distinct C–C bond in an antiperiplanar geometry relative to the O–O bond; restricted conformational interconversion within the active site could preserve the initial reactive geometry and bias divergent carbon migration. Collectively, our findings identify conformational preorganization as a plausible contributor to regiodivergent enzymatic Baeyer–Villiger catalysis, offering a rational strategy for steering oxidative skeletal remodeling in complex natural product molecules.

items.title: Photocatalytic Scaffold Hopping of Cyclobutanols to Cyclopentanols via Single-Carbon Insertion into C–C σ-Bonds
items.abstract: A method for skeletal editing of C–C σ-bonds in strained alicycles via single-carbon insertion is reported. This skeletal editing method for cyclobutanols differs from well-established semipinacol rearrangement pathways, offering an efficient route to cyclopentanols by direct scaffold hopping of cyclobutanols. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions in good yields, expanding the toolkit for single-atom insertion into C–C σ-bonds.

items.title: Scaffold Hopping of Pyrimidines into 2-Acylpyrroles
items.abstract: A practical skeletal-editing strategy was developed for the conversion of 4-substituted pyrimidines into 2-acyl-5-arylpyrroles. The transformation directly converts a six-membered, electron-deficient pyrimidine into a five-membered azole while simultaneously installing an acyl group. The reaction sequence involves pyrimidine activation, ring-opening, fragmentation, and ring reconstruction. Central to this strategy is the controlled generation of pyrimidine-derived vinamidinium salts as open-chain A4 synthons, which are then intercepted by α-bromoketones as functionalized annulation reagents. The developed scaffold-hopping method can be applied for late-stage modification of pyrimidine-containing bioactive or pharmaceutical molecules.

items.title: Criegee Intermediate-Enabled Decarboxylative C(sp3)–C(sp3) Cross-Coupling of α,β-Unsaturated Esters with Cyclic Acetals
items.abstract: Ozonolysis and Baeyer–Villiger (BV) rearrangement are among the earliest transformations in which cyclic/acyclic peroxo intermediates, often known as Criegee intermediates, have been detected. Herein, we disclose the merger of a Criegee intermediate with C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling via a rare anti-Giese addition for a new genre of C–C cross-coupling to access complex chemical libraries. Detailed mechanistic investigation reveals the generation of a cyclic tetrahedral peroxo intermediate (CI), and gas-phase analysis establishes the formation of 16O═C═18O under 18O2 conditions and straightforwardly supports the formation of peroxylactones via a Criegee intermediate under our standard conditions. Importantly, many pharmaceutically active drug-like molecules have been screened thoroughly and have been shown to exhibit excellent tolerance and high regioselectivity for this methodology.

items.title: Pd-Catalyzed Freon-Enabled Aminocarbonylation of Aryl Iodides
items.abstract: A palladium-catalyzed Freon-to-carbonyl transfer strategy has been developed for the CO-free aminocarbonylation of aryl and heteroaryl iodides with amines. Using chlorodifluoromethane (Freon-22) as both a difluorocarbene precursor and a carbonyl source, this protocol enables direct access to diverse benzamide derivatives without external CO gas or conventional CO-releasing reagents. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope and good functional-group tolerance, accommodating electronically diverse aryl iodides, polycyclic and heteroaryl iodides, and primary and secondary amines. Its synthetic utility is demonstrated by late-stage benzamidation of bioactive-molecule-derived substrates and concise synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant benzamide scaffolds, including trimethobenzamide and methyl tamibarotene. Mechanistic experiments involving benzimidazole trapping and H218O labeling support a difluorocarbene-derived carbonyl-transfer process in which water contributes to the oxygen atom of the amide carbonyl group. This work establishes Freon-22 as a practical carbonyl surrogate for CO-free amide synthesis.

items.title: [3+2] Cycloadditions of Aldiminoboranes with N -Acylpyrazoles
items.abstract: The [3+2] cycloaddition between aldiminoboranes and N-acylpyrazoles was successfully achieved. Aldiminoboranes, serving as C═N═B building blocks, were generated in situ via direct hydroboration of nitriles with Piers’ borane HB(C6F5)2. The [3+2] cycloaddition furnishes five-membered BN-heterocyclic compounds and notably features an acyl migration. Furthermore, the reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope with respect to both nitriles and N-acylpyrazoles, affording the target products in 56–87% isolated yields.

items.title: Carbene-Catalyzed Enantioselective Formal [4 + 2] Reaction for Rapid Synthesis of 1-Azaspiro[4,5]decane Derivatives
items.abstract: An NHC-promoted formal [4 + 2] cycloaddition reaction is developed for quick access to chiral 1-aza-spirocyclohexane pyrrolidone molecules bearing quaternary chiral carbon centers. A broad scope of β-methylenals and 5-ene pyrrolin-4-one substrates worked well in this reaction. A diversity of chiral 1-aza-spirocyclohexane pyrrolidone molecules can be afforded in generally moderate to good yields and excellent enantioselectivities. The chiral products obtained from this protocol can be transformed into multifunctional chiral spirocyclohexane pyrrolidone derivatives through simple operations.

items.title: Dissecting Binary and Ternary Iminoboronate Assemblies: A Calorimetric Study of Thermodynamics, Kinetics, and Allosteric Effects
items.abstract: Dynamic covalent assemblies derived from ortho-boronoaldehydes, including iminoboronates and boronate esters, are key structural motifs in adaptive materials, chemical sensors, and reversible bioconjugation strategies. Herein, we report a label-free assay based on isothermal titration calorimetry that provides access to observed thermodynamic and model-derived kinetic parameters associated with assembly formation under defined experimental conditions. The assay further reveals cooperative binding between amine-based nucleophiles and diols toward ortho-boronoaldehyde derivatives, providing new insight into multicomponent dynamic covalent systems.

items.title: Umpolung Strain-Release Ring Opening of Carbonyl Bicyclo[1.1.0]butane Aldehydes Enabled by N -Heterocyclic Carbene Catalyzed Redox Esterification
items.abstract: A new type of carbonyl BCB aldehydes was synthesized through oxidation of vinyl-carbonyl BCBs. Under the catalysis of 10 mol % N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC), these BCB aldehydes underwent redox esterification with various primary, secondary alcohols and phenols to afford 1,3-dicarbonyl substituted cyclobutanes in 61%–99% yields. Mechanism study indicates the carbonyl group can activate BCB aldehyde and assist to stabilize the enolate intermediate, which is critical for the success of this reaction.

items.title: FeBr3-Catalyzed Aromatization-C–O Bond Cleavage Process for Construction of Aryl-Substituted Prostaglandin Skeleton
items.abstract: Prostaglandins exhibit therapeutic potential in multiple diseases and the incorporation of aromatic rings into their side chains can often enhance their corresponding biological activities. Although more than 20 kinds of drugs are currently used in clinical practice, there are huge difficulties in the preparation of both active pharmaceutical ingredients and preparations. Prostaglandins directly substituted by aryl groups may overcome these difficulties; however, their preparation remains challenging, and only a few synthetic methods have been reported to date. Herein, we describe a novel FeBr3/ligand-catalyzed aromatization-C−O bond cleavage process that provides access to aryl-substituted prostaglandin skeletons.

items.title: Chemoselective Electrochemical Synthesis of 3-Hydroxyisoindolinones from Phthalimide Imines
items.abstract: We report an electrochemical method for the radical–radical coupling of alkyl iodides with phthalimide imines under mild conditions. This operationally simple electro-reductive procedure enables selective reduction of carbonyl groups, offering an efficient route to access functionalized 3-hydroxyisoindolinones in moderate-to-excellent yields. Notably, the highly functionalized 3-hydroxyisoindolinones have shown promising bioactivity in preliminary assessments, pointing to the significant potential of this chemical scaffold for anticancer cell applications. A comparative analysis has demonstrated that the hydrazone moiety within the product structure plays an indispensable role in conferring bioactivity.

items.title: Dibenzophenazine‐Fused Heterocyclic Luminophores: Decoding High‐Performance Organic Light‐Emitting Diodes Based on Long‐Wavelength Exciplex
items.abstract: Developing highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplexes remains a challenge due to the constraints of the energy gap law and severe non‐radiative loss. In this study, we report a rigid nitrogen‐rich donor, 3N, featuring the first fused framework constructed from two anti‐aromatic phenazine units. This unique architecture ensures 3N has good planarity and an exceptionally shallow highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level of −4.88 eV. Meanwhile, the effective suppression of structural relaxation by its rigid scaffold contributes to a narrow emission at 456 nm. By pairing 3N with planar boron‐containing acceptors through strong intermolecular interactions, highly efficient exciplex emissions ranging from green to orange‐red were successfully achieved. Two representative exciplex systems reached outstanding photoluminescence quantum yields of 92% at 557 nm and 78% at 604 nm, respectively. Correspondingly, organic light‐emitting diodes based on these exciplexes delivered maximum external quantum efficiencies of 25.6% at 556 nm and 24.7% at 586 nm, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, these values rank among the highest performance metrics reported for long‐wavelength exciplexes. These results demonstrate that fusing multiple phenazine units could significantly raise the HOMO level and enhances structural rigidity, thereby enabling highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplex electroluminescence.

items.title: Metal‐Center‐Controlled Fenton‐Like Reactivity of Biomimetic First‐Row Transition Metal Complexes in Aqueous Anticancer Catalysis
items.abstract: Catalytic oxidative cancer therapy exploits elevated hydrogen peroxide levels within tumor microenvironments to induce selective oxidative damage in malignant cells. However, many ROS‐generating therapeutic systems rely on heavy metals or structurally complex inorganic architectures, limiting their biological compatibility and catalytic selectivity. Inspired by nonheme iron‐mediated redox catalysis, we report a series of water‐soluble biomimetic first‐row transition metal complexes supported by a picolylamine‐derived nonheme ligand scaffold bearing a pendant hydroxyl group. Systematic variation of the metal center (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn) generated divergent electrochemical behavior and distinct peroxide‐activation reactivity, yet only the iron complex, [Fe(N 2 Py 3 OH)] 2+ ( 1‐Fe ), promoted hydroxyl radical formation via Fenton‐like hydrogen peroxide activation in water. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and crystallographic analyses revealed a biomimetic coordination environment that stabilizes a quasi‐reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) redox couple suited to catalytic peroxide activation. In gastric cancer cells, 1‐Fe induced intracellular oxidative stress, mitochondrial depolarization, lipid peroxidation, and concomitant apoptosis and ferroptosis, while exhibiting negligible toxicity toward normal fibroblasts. In combination with paclitaxel, 1‐Fe produced synergistic antiproliferative activity in vitro and suppressed peritoneal tumor dissemination in vivo without overt systemic toxicity. Collectively, these results establish biomimetic iron complexes as molecular platforms for Fenton‐like oxidative catalysis in redox‐based cancer therapy.

items.title: Phenolic Metabolites as Therapeutics for Chronic Diseases: One Researcher’s PAINS Is Another’s Translatable Polypharmacology
items.abstract: Phenols, natural and semisynthetic compounds in which a hydroxylated or oxygenated aromatic scaffold is a defining structural feature, occupy a paradoxical position in drug discovery. On the one hand, these compounds are frequently scrutinized for triggering Pan-Assay INterference compoundS (PAINS) structural alerts; on the other, their reported wide-ranging bioactivities support continued evaluation as potential therapeutics, particularly given that several phenolic compounds and mixtures have attained FDA approval for treating diseases ranging from cancers to viral infections. Accordingly, this perspective contrasts concerns raised by PAINS structural alerts with reported broad pharmacological activity and proposes a framework for the rational evaluation as well as the synthetic development of phenolic scaffolds.

items.title: Eudesmane Sesquiterpenoids from Dregea Volubilis Suppress Kidney Stones via Akt Signalling to Inhibit Oxalate Biosynthesis in Drosophila
items.abstract: Dregea volubilis has long been used in traditional medicine for the treatment of urolithiasis, yet its bioactive constituents and molecular mechanisms remain largely undefined. Here, molecular networking-guided UPLC-ESI-MS/MS analysis enabled the isolation of ten sesquiterpenoids, including eight previously undescribed compounds (compounds 1∼4, 6∼9). Among them, dregeaterpene A (1) exhibited potent anti-urolithic activity in Drosophila, surpassing the therapeutic efficacy of potassium citrate. Mechanistically, dregeaterpene A suppressed endogenous oxalate biosynthesis by restoring oxalate-impaired Akt phosphorylation, leading to the downregulation of Daao1 and Daao2, and the upregulation of Agxt. Consequently, oxalate accumulation and calcium oxalate stone formation were markedly reduced. Collectively, these findings identify eudesmane sesquiterpenoids from D. volubilis as bioactive anti-urolithic agents and establish Akt-dependent regulation of oxalate metabolism as their underlying mechanism of action, highlighting dregeaterpene A as a promising lead compound for the development of therapeutics against calcium oxalate urolithiasis.

items.title: Lipid Droplet-Targeted Near-Infrared II Type I AIE Photosensitizer Promotes Ferroptosis by Activating Lipophagy
items.abstract: Lipophagy, a selective autophagic pathway, maintains lipid homeostasis and contributes to ferroptosis by supplying lipid peroxidation substrates. However, organic photosensitizers that activate lipophagy to promote ferroptosis remain scarce. Herein, we developed a NIR-II emissive photosensitizer (MBTTD) targeting lipid droplets (LDs). Compared with its analogue MBTTA, stronger electron-withdrawing groups bathochromically shifted absorption/emission and tuned excited-state decay, enabling efficient type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and high photothermal conversion efficiency. MBTTD nanoparticles (NPs) localized to LDs upon cellular uptake. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, MBTTD NP-mediated phototherapy disrupted LDs and induced Rab7-regulated lipophagy, releasing polyunsaturated fatty acids that underwent ROS-driven peroxidation, triggering extensive lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis. Concurrently, MBTTD-NP-mediated phototherapy triggered endoplasmic reticulum stress and apoptosis. MBTTD NPs showed favorable biocompatibility and potent therapeutic efficacy in multicellular tumor spheroids. In vivo studies revealed that MBTTD NPs enabled NIR-II imaging-guided phototherapy, suppressing 4T1 tumor growth without significant systemic toxicity.

items.title: Discovery of Tricyclic Oxazinoquinolinone-Based BCL6 PROTAC Degraders with Potent Activity Against Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
items.abstract: B-cell lymphoma 6 (BCL6) is a key transcriptional repressor involved in the pathogenesis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). In this study, scaffold hopping of BI-3802 led to compound 1, a new tricyclic BCL6-targeting ligand. Further optimization of linker architecture and CRBN-recruiting motifs led to compound 15, a potent BCL6 PROTAC degrader, which induced rapid and efficient BCL6 degradation in OCI-LY1 cells (DC50 = 5.32 nM) and displayed potent antiproliferative activity in BCL6-dependent DLBCL cells (IC50 = 3.2 nM). BCL6 degradation was CRBN- and proteasome-dependent and was accompanied by G1-phase arrest and increased p21 and p27 expression. Oral administration of 15 inhibited tumor growth in an OCI-LY1 xenograft model (TGI = 84% at 20 mg/kg) and reduced tumor BCL6 and Ki67 levels without appreciable body-weight loss or overt major-organ histopathology. Overall, compound 15 represents a promising BCL6 PROTAC degrader for DLBCL.

items.title: Medicinal Chemistry Strategies for Targeting RNA-Binding Proteins: Design, Optimization, and Therapeutic Potential
items.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are essential regulators of post-transcriptional gene expression whose disruption contributes broadly to tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistance. Through their control of RNA splicing, stability, translation, and epitranscriptomic modification, these proteins orchestrate oncogenic networks that sustain hallmark cancer phenotypes. This central role has stimulated intensive efforts to develop small-molecule RBP inhibitors, yielding mechanistically diverse compounds against m6A pathway components and classical oncogenic RBPs with demonstrated efficacy in preclinical models. However, substantial challenges remain, including achieving high target selectivity, optimizing drug-like properties, and addressing adaptive resistance mechanisms. This article examines recent advances in RBP-targeted therapeutics, highlighting design strategies, structural mechanisms, and key obstacles on the path toward clinical application.

items.title: Discovery of GTA182, a Novel CNS-Active Tricyclic Amide MTA-Cooperative PRMT5 Inhibitor for MTAP -Deleted Cancers
items.abstract: Developing central nervous system (CNS) active, MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors for MTAP-deleted malignancies represents a formidable challenge. Here, we report the discovery of GTA182 via structure-based drug design. Multi-parameter optimization balanced single-digit nanomolar potency and >100-fold MTAP-deletion selectivity with dose-proportional pharmacokinetics. Optimized physicochemical properties, and minimal efflux delivered unbound brain concentrations within the efficacious range. Oral GTA182 demonstrated robust MTAP deletion-dependent efficacy, achieving net regression at 30 mg/kg (102% TGI) in MTAP-deleted HCT116 xenografts (versus 41% TGI in WT) alongside 59% regression and extended median survival (>91 days) in the orthotopic U87MG-luc glioblastoma model. In a Phase I trial (CTR20243795), GTA182 was well tolerated, shrank intracranial tumors, and achieved an overall objective response rate (ORR) approaching 30%. These properties establish GTA182 as a promising therapeutic candidate for MTAP-deleted systemic and CNS malignancies.

items.title: Discovery and Optimization of Anticancer Dibenzothiazepinones That Target the Ribosome Biogenesis Factor NVL
items.abstract: Using inducible forward genetics, we recently discovered a dibenzothiazepinone (1) with activity against cancer cells via inhibition of the ribosome biogenesis factor NVL (nuclear valosin-containing protein-like). Herein, we delineate a comprehensive structure−activity relationship (SAR) study that explores the structural space surrounding the dibenzothiazepinone scaffold. A series of 115 analogs were synthesized and evaluated for activity against the colorectal cancer cell line HCT116 and counter-screened against cells CRISPR engineered to express a compound-resistant mutation in NVL. Our initial medicinal chemistry-driven campaign focused on improving potency, metabolic stability, and in vivo exposure and clearance. A fluorescence polarization assay with recombinant human NVL established a correlation between NVL-binding and antiproliferative activity. Cryo-EM structures of human NVL with select inhibitors revealed a binding mode that is consistent with the SAR data. This study led to the in vivo analog 100 (MM927), which we reported to suppress tumor growth in vivo without detectable toxicity via targeting the NVL.

items.title: Structure-Guided Discovery of Orally Bioavailable Allosteric SLC6A19 Inhibitors that Promote Urinary Amino Acid Excretion In Vivo
items.abstract: SLC6A19 is a sodium-dependent transporter that mediates the absorption of neutral amino acids in the intestine and reabsorption of these amino acids in the kidney. Pharmacological inhibition of SLC6A19 may provide therapeutic benefit by normalizing plasma amino acid levels and potentially reducing renal tubular transport burden. Virtual screening against an allosteric binding pocket observed in the cryo-EM structure of SLC6A19/cinromide (1) identified compound 6 as a promising hit. The cryo-EM structure of SLC6A19/CB3 (2) revealed a second, partially overlapping pocket adjacent to the compound 6 binding site. Analogue design merging these two binding pockets followed by optimization led to compound 20, a potent, selective, and orally bioavailable allosteric SLC6A19 inhibitor. While compound 20 demonstrates an approximately 10-fold rightward potency shift against mouse SLC6A19, it retains good potency against non-human primate SLC6A19. Consistent with the SLC6A19 inhibition mechanism, oral dosing of 20 led to increased urinary amino acid excretion in a dose-dependent manner in human SLC6A19 knock-in mice and wild-type non-human primates.

items.title: Discovery of Indazole-Based Dual-Pharmacophore Inhibitors of Dengue and Zika Proteases as Promising Antivirals
items.abstract: Flavivirus outbreaks caused by dengue virus (DENV) and Zika virus (ZIKV) remain a major global health challenge, with no FDA-approved antivirals available. Herein, we designed, synthesized, and evaluated indazole-based dual pharmacophore motifs targeting NS2B-NS3 serine proteases, essential for viral replication. Enzymatic assays revealed nanomolar to sub-micromolar potency, with strong selectivity over host serine proteases, minimizing off-target risks. Biophysical studies showed ligand-induced thermal stabilization, while kinetic and dialysis analyses confirmed a reversible, competitive, non-covalent inhibition mechanism. In DENV-infected Vero CCL-81 cells, several leads exhibited potent antiviral activity with low cytotoxicity. Notably, compound C8 demonstrated low-nanomolar enzyme inhibition against both viruses, translating to complete viral suppression in cells (EC50 = 0.5 μM) with a good selectivity index, underscoring its therapeutic potential. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported these findings, revealing key active-site interactions consistent with potency and specificity. Collectively, these results highlight indazole-based dual-pharmacophore inhibitors as promising anti-flaviviral leads.

items.title: HER2-Targeting Affibody Equipped with Albumin-Binding Small Molecules for Radiotheranostics
items.abstract: HER2-targeting affibody radioprobes are often limited by rapid systemic clearance and excessive renal accumulation. Herein, we develop a modular chemical strategy to optimize the pharmacokinetic properties of affibodies through conjugation of small-molecule albumin-binding motifs (ABMs). Enabled by our selective S-glycosylation approach, ABMs were introduced via a sugar-based linker, allowing systematic modulation of probe behavior. Evaluation of sugar-modified variants revealed that sugar structure plays a critical role in regulating in vivo distribution, with the GalNAc-modified probe [68Ga]Ga-5c exhibiting favorable tumor-to-background contrast in PET/CT imaging. Further incorporation of ABMs afforded GalNAc-IPBA-functionalized affibody [177Lu]Lu-10a, which achieved an 17-fold extension of circulation half-life, reduced renal accumulation, and maintained efficient tumor targeting. Therapeutically, [177Lu]Lu-10a induced 86.25% tumor growth inhibition with minimal systemic toxicity. This study provides a modular strategy for overcoming pharmacokinetic limitations of affibody-based radiotheranostics.

items.title: FAP-Triggered In Situ Self-Assembly of HPQ in Tumors Empowers 131I Internal Radiotherapy
items.abstract: Fibroblast activating protein (FAP) is specifically overexpressed in malignant tumors. The 2-(2′-hydroxyphenyl)-4(3H)-quinazolinone (HPQ) scaffold exhibits hydrophobicity, aggregation-induced emission (AIE). The responsive probes built on HPQ can undergo in situ activation and self-assembling precipitation, enabling prolonged retention in lesion sites. Herein, a FAP-cleavable Cbz-Gly-Pro-sequence was conjugated to the phenolic hydroxyl of HPQ via a self-immolative linker, with phenol/tyrosine moieties for 131I labeling through aliphatic linkers, affording LWH-1 and LWH-2. LWH-3 further incorporated a tetraphenylethylene moiety, a PEG6-triazole-PEG6 linker, and (D-Tyr)5-NH2. All precursors for radioiodination responded efficiently to FAP, releasing HPQ-OH to generate AIE and illuminating tumors for over 48 h. [131I]LWH-3 showed a 2.76-fold higher molar activity than [131I]LWH-2 and an in vivo half-life of 43.66 min. In PC12-FAP xenografts, [131I]LWH-3 achieved outstanding antitumor efficacy with favorable biosafety. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that internal radiotherapy attenuated tumor metabolic adaptability by modulating fatty acid metabolism-associated networks to impair proliferation.

items.title: FDA Approval of Ensitrelvir: an Oral, Nonpeptidic, Noncovalent SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease Inhibitor for Household Postexposure Prophylaxis
Discovery of Anti-apoptotic BAX Inhibitors
items.abstract: BAX is a critical regulator of the apoptosis cascade and its abnormal activation contributes to the development of disease including cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disorders. Therefore, BAX represents an attractive target for the pharmacological inhibition of pathological cell death. Based on a virtual screen, we identified and modified several EGFR kinase inhibitors with potential activity against BAX. Systematic modifications of the dacomitinib and gefitinib core structure were performed, allowing us to elucidate how structural modifications influence biological activity and leading to a comprehensive structure-activity relationship (SAR) on BAX inhibition. The developed series has favorable drug-like properties and improved BAX inhibitory activity in vitro, in cells, and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain organoids, with significantly reduced EGFR kinase activity. This series therefore represents a promising starting point for the development of improved and potentially therapeutic BAX inhibitors.

items.title: The Phenotypic Hit-to-Probe Challenge
items.abstract: Phenotypic drug discovery (PDD) fuels the clinical pipelines with first-in-class therapeutic modalities. Success rates depend on the quality of the assay models and can be hampered by resource-intensive processes of target and mode-of-action deconvolution. A critical part of this practice is generating focused sets of phenotypic probes to accelerate in vivo validation and to support target/concept tractability and translatability, raising the question of which phenotypic hit analogues to synthesize as high-quality chemical probes for a given campaign. Here, we outline recommendations and discuss criteria tailored to the specific demands of phenotypic probes. With examples of successful PDD programs, some of which have yielded approved first-in-class drugs, we illustrate common design principles. These underscore that phenotypic probes benefit from (a) availability of matched pairs of active/inactive stereoisomers, (b) ligand topology-guided optimization, and (c) exit vectors for ADME- and target deconvolution-driven acceleration of early in vivo proof-of-concept and advancement towards clinical candidates.

items.title: Ligand-Dependent Affinity but State-Dominated Efficacy in Structure-Based GPCR Pharmacology Prediction
items.abstract: High accuracy in structure-based prediction of G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) efficacy may reflect the receptor state rather than ligand-specific information. We addressed these information sources using state rules, ligand-blind baselines, matched receptor-state contrasts, ligand permutation, and out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation, with affinity prediction as a positive control. State rules and ligand-blind geometry achieved binary-efficacy-balanced accuracies of 0.844−0.910 and 0.777−0.870, respectively. Of 75 ligand-aware evaluations, 72 failed at least one prespecified ligand-sensitivity condition, and three lacked required evidence; none met all required criteria. Affinity pretraining gave no detectable efficacy benefit over matched random initialization. In contrast, ligand chemistry supported affinity prediction across 14,740 measured pairs, and all 12 primary affinity permutation comparisons deteriorated, although this advantage did not persist under scaffold, family, or combined OOD splits. Accuracy on endpoint structures therefore cannot alone establish ligand-specific efficacy learning; the findings do not set a general limit on such learning.

items.title: Rethinking log P : Lipophilicity ≠ Hydrophobicity
items.abstract: LogP values have served as cutoffs for hit-, lead-, and drug-likeness as well as thresholds for toxicity and ADME decision-making and are often characterized as lipophilicity. When the properties of octanol and the experimental limitations of logP measurements are considered, it becomes clear that logP > 3 must be due to increased hydrophobicity and not lipophilicity. We propose that the partition coefficient between either octanol or water and “the thermodynamic ideal solution” is a useful reference to separately determine octanol solvation (lipophilicity) and aqueous solvation (hydrophilicity). We further propose that the ideal solubility of solids measures “autophilicity”. Aqueous solvation spans many orders of magnitude, yet octanol solvation is much narrower, and thus lipophilicity is nearly constant. Understanding which molecules are hydrophobic, rather than lipophilic, can be critical in interpreting affinity, PK, ADME, safety, and other behaviors of molecules necessitating these more nuanced definitions.

items.title: Intrinsic physicochemical activity at microplastic–water interfaces
items.abstract: Plastics have become an integral part of our modern society, largely because they are generally regarded as chemically inert under normal circumstances. However, plastics fragmented into microplastics (less than 5 mm in size) have recently raised significant public concerns, and have been detected widely across ecosystems and human tissues with increasing environmental and health risks1–5. Here we show that commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity in water, manifested by the spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species that increases with interfacial hydrophobicity and strongly correlates with interfacial electrostatics. Ab initio calculations support these observations and reveal that hydroxide oxidation becomes energetically more favourable at increasingly hydrophobic microplastic–water interfaces through the combined effects of partial solvation and electrostatics. These interfacial properties and the resulting oxidative chemistry have direct implications for biomolecular adsorption, protein aggregation, and even cellular damage. Together, our findings challenge the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, identify a possibly overlooked mechanism for the detrimental effects of microplastics on health and the environment, and contribute to a fundamental understanding of the structure–activity relationship of interfacial water, which may inform the design of safer and more sustainable plastic materials. Commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity at water interfaces, manifested by spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species, challenging the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, with implications for human health and the environment.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat
items.abstract: Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue (BAT) uses energy to produce heat3. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT.
