Importantly, NAMPT inhibition disrupts the NAD+/NAM ratio and mitigates CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction, ultimately enhancing the efficacy of chemoimmunotherapy when combined with IL-2 across multiple preclinical models of solid tumors. Thus, our findings underscore the NAD+/NAM ratio as a metabolic therapeutic target for enhancing chemotherapy and NK cell-based chemoimmunotherapy efficacy. NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment. However, the effects of chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy regimens on NAD metabolism remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a macrophage-driven IL-1β inflammatory signaling that regulates the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction and show that disruption of the NAD + /NAM ratio sensitises tumors to chemoimmunotherapy across multiple preclinical mouse models.

items.title: CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
items.abstract: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

items.title: High-Throughput Screening Identifies Small-Molecule Inhibitors of the Tau-LRP1 Interaction
items.abstract: The cellular uptake and propagation of tau are central features of tauopathies, including Alzheimer’s disease, and are mediated by the endocytic receptor low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1). While prior studies have implicated LRP1 in tau binding and internalization, the biochemical features of this interaction and its suitability for therapeutic targeting remain incompletely defined. Here, we establish a quantitative and scalable framework to interrogate the tau-LRP1 interaction and identify small-molecule modulators. We engineered and purified the LRP1 ligand-binding domain 4 (BD4), a key region mediating tau interaction, and developed multiple orthogonal assays, including fluorescence polarization, split luciferase complementation, and time-resolved FRET, to measure LRP1-BD4 interactions with tau and a known peptide ligand. Across assay formats, we observe consistent binding affinities in the nanomolar range and demonstrate competitive displacement by tau, receptor-associated protein (RAP), and a peptide ligand, supporting overlapping binding interfaces. Leveraging these platforms, we performed small-molecule high-throughput screening and identified a set of candidate inhibitors of the LRP1-BD4-tau interaction. Selected compounds reduced tau uptake in a cellular assay, phenocopying competitive inhibition by tau and a peptide ligand. Together, these studies define the LRP1-BD4-tau interaction as a biochemically tractable and druggable interface and establish an integrated discovery pipeline linking mechanistic characterization to functional cellular outcomes. This work provides a foundation for the development of therapeutic strategies targeting LRP1-mediated tau uptake.

items.title: Latent Style-Based Quantum Wasserstein GAN for Drug Design
items.abstract: The development of new drugs is a tedious, time-consuming, and expensive process for which the average costs are estimated to be up to around \$2.5 billion. The first step in this long process is the design of the new drug, for which de novo drug design, assisted by artificial intelligence, has blossomed in recent years and has revolutionized the field. In particular, generative artificial intelligence has delivered promising results in drug discovery and development, reducing costs and time to solution. However, classical generative models, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), can be difficult to train and are prone to mode collapse. Quantum computing may be an avenue to overcome some of these issues, providing compact models with far fewer trainable parameters and thereby enhancing the generalizability of GANs. We propose a new latent style-based quantum Wasserstein GAN (QGAN) for drug design, combining a variational autoencoder that maps molecular structures into a latent space with a hybrid quantum GAN. Our pipeline is benchmarked against the classical models of the industry-relevant MOSES suite. Style-based noise reuploading at every rotational gate and a Wasserstein gradient penalty are used to improve trainability and to mitigate mode collapse. Training and large-scale sampling with circuits of up to 15 qubits are performed on noiseless quantum simulators to validate our architecture. We present an inference-only demonstration on a 156-qubit IBM Heron quantum computer using a five-qubit setup, sampling 2,500 new molecules, to investigate the effect of quantum noise. Our default QGAN, using 110 trainable generator parameters, reaches statistically comparable overall performance and statistically significant gains on selected drug-relevant metrics relative to both the MOSES classical latent GAN baseline, which contains about 700,000 trainable parameters for the generator, and a classical latent GAN with matched generator capacity.

items.title: e MolFrag 2 and e Synth 2: Sound Fragment-Based Molecular Decomposition and Reconstruction
items.abstract: We present eMolFrag2 and eSynth2, enhanced successors to eMolFrag and eSynth for fragment-based molecular decomposition and reconstruction. eMolFrag2 is a complete reimplementation of eMolFrag in Python, using RDKit and graph-based molecular representations to preserve connectivity, identify free atoms, combine adjacent linkers, and avoid aromaticity ambiguities that impair downstream reconstruction. eSynth2 generalizes fragment recombination by removing hard-coded molecular-property filters, supporting multiple bonds to a single brick atom, and adding a targeted reconstruction mode for soundness validation. Across 36,534 nonredundant DUD-E active compounds, the eMolFrag2 → eSynth2 workflow reconstructed every input molecule exactly (Tanimoto coefficient, TC = 1.0), whereas the original eMolFrag→ eSynth workflow reconstructed 51 of the 100 molecules in a benchmark subset. The upgraded workflow also produced broader recombinant chemical spaces, including higher entropy in a four-molecule diversity analysis (2.78 versus 2.70). Both tools are open-source, platform-agnostic, and available for academic and commercial use.

items.title: A Molecular Rationale for Tailoring the Growth Mechanisms of Biomimetic Calcium Oxalates: Guides to Simplified Proxies of Renal Stones?
items.abstract: We present a combined molecular simulation and experimental study of the mechanisms of calcium oxalate monohydrate formation within a biomimetic matrix. Using a double‐diffusion approach to feed calcium and oxalate ions into an agarose gel, we show how selective ion association to different crystal faces may guide the morphogenesis and surface charge of the precipitates. Our analyses rationalize two conceptually different growth mechanisms leading to the aggregation of crystallites in terms of negatively charged needles and positively charged platelets, respectively, whereas embedding organic macromolecules are related to the hosting of counterions. We argue that this reflects a key characteristic of renal stone formation, while benefiting from drastic reduction of system complexity. Hence, the biomimetic setup is suggested for both, ex situ formation of (much simplified) proxies to kidney/urinary stones and steps toward the understanding of growth factors for tailoring inner structure, size, and dispersion in water.

items.title: Multitarget Drug Design for Cardiovascular Disease: Bridging Chemistry and Medicine
items.abstract: This review provides an overview of recent advances in the development of multitarget drugs (MTDs) for cardiac diseases, with a particular focus on emerging molecular scaffolds and their pharmacological properties. We discuss the fundamental principles of cardiac polypharmacology and multitarget drug design, highlighting key compound classes, such as 1,4‐benzothiazepines, 1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs), and polyphenol derivatives. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationship between the structural features and the pharmacological activity, efficacy, and therapeutic potential of these compounds.

items.title: Beyond Single‐Target Therapy: Dual‐Acting Cannabinoid Type‐2 Receptor Modulation in Neurological Disorders
items.abstract: Neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and neuroinflammatory conditions involve complex, interconnected mechanisms, including neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, cholinergic dysfunction, and synaptic impairment. The cannabinoid type‐2 receptor (CB2R), primarily expressed in immune and glial cells, has emerged as a promising therapeutic target due to its role in modulating neuroinflammation and providing neuroprotection without the psychoactive effects associated with CB1R activation. Recent research highlights the potential of dual‐acting CB2R ligands that also modulate CB1R, acetylcholinesterase (AChE), and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), offering a multitarget approach to neurological disorders. Although CB1R expression was identified in 1993, significant progress in designing receptor modulators began in the 2000s, with recent focus expanding to autoimmune, metabolic, and cancer‐related applications. This review summarizes advances in the design, synthesis, and structure–activity relationships of CB2R‐targeting ligands, emphasizing dual‐ or multitarget agents with cholinesterase inhibitory activity. Key chemical scaffolds include synthetic cannabinoids, heterocyclic compounds, and hybrid molecules integrating cholinesterase pharmacophores. Molecular docking and in silico studies are discussed to elucidate ligand–receptor interactions, binding modes, and determinants of selectivity. Overall, CB2R‐centric dual‐acting ligands represent a promising strategy for addressing multifactorial neurological disorders.

items.title: Mechanistic basis of μ-opioid receptor allosteric modulation from molecular simulations
items.abstract: The μ-opioid receptor (μOR) is a central mediator of analgesia and opioid-induced adverse effects, yet the molecular basis by which allosteric modulators reshape receptor signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we integrate all-atom molecular dynamics with unbinding kinetics simulations to resolve the mechanistic basis of positive and negative allosteric modulation of μOR. We show that the positive allosteric modulator BMS-986122 enhances signaling not through uniform stabilization of canonical active microswitches, but by selectively remodeling the sodium pocket and, critically, stabilizing the μOR–G protein interface. This stabilization increases interfacial interactions and buried surface area, providing a G protein–dependent mechanism for enhanced efficacy despite increased agonist conformational flexibility and weakened orthosteric contacts. In contrast, the negative allosteric modulator compound 368 broadly enforces inactive-like microswitch conformations while simultaneously stabilizing antagonist binding. Unbinding kinetics simulations reveal that 368 exerts a dominant kinetic effect, restricting naloxone egress pathways and increasing residence time by approximately three orders of magnitude. Together, these results establish a unified framework in which μOR allostery operates through modulation of receptor and ligand conformational dynamics, G protein engagement, and ligand dissociation kinetics. This work provides an atomistic foundation for the rational design of next-generation opioid therapeutics that exploit allosteric mechanisms to enhance efficacy and safety.

items.title: Development landscape of ketohexokinase-C (KHK-C) inhibitors for fructose-driven metabolic disorders: from hit discovery to clinical trials
items.abstract: Excessive dietary fructose intake promotes ketohexokinase (KHK)-mediated fructose-driven metabolic disorders (FDMDs). Targeting KHK with small-molecule inhibitors is emerging as a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of FDMDs.

items.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies naturally derived histidine kinase VbrK inhibitors as potential countermeasures against β-lactam antimicrobial resistance
items.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening identified phlorizin and baicalin as novel histidine kinase VbrK inhibitors that restore β-lactam susceptibility by repressing functional β-lactamase production.

items.title: Defining the Catalytic Boundaries of N -Nitrosourea-Forming StzF/SznF and Related Metalloenzymes through Genome Mining and Mechanistic Analysis
items.abstract: Enzymatic N–N bond formation is a rare and chemically challenging transformation in natural product biosynthesis. The non-heme iron metalloenzyme SznF catalyzes the formation of the N -nitrosourea pharmacophore of streptozotocin via the coordinated action of a diiron heme-oxygenase-like (HDO) domain and a mononuclear iron cupin domain. Although recent computational studies have advanced mechanistic models for this transformation, the determinants governing substrate specificity within this enzyme family remain poorly understood. Here, we employed a multi-pronged approach combining genome mining, substrate scope screening, protein engineering, structural analysis, and biochemical characterization to define the catalytic boundaries of SznF and related homologs. Genome mining identified a previously uncharacterized homolog displaying higher activity toward the native substrate N ω -methyl-L-arginine than SznF, expanding the known repertoire of N-nitrosourea-forming metalloenzymes. Comprehensive substrate screening further revealed the first non-native substrate accepted by this enzyme family, N ω -propyl-L-arginine, whereas all other modifications in carbon chain length, guanidino substitution, alkylation state, or stereochemistry did not result in detectable turnover. Structure-guided engineering that targeted the binding pocket surrounding the terminal alkyl substituent increased the activity of several variants toward N ω -propyl-L-arginine compared to wildtype SznF. Furthermore, cascade experiments, and nitric oxide supplementation further demonstrate that productive catalysis requires a precise combination of steric, electronic, and geometric features that cannot readily be compensated by alternative substrates. Together, these findings show that the substrate specificity of SznF and related homologs is governed by mechanistic constraints arising from the tightly coupled hydroxylation and rearrangement chemistry underlying N–N bond formation. More broadly, this work defines the catalytic boundaries of enzymatic N -nitrosourea formation while identifying new opportunities for the discovery and engineering of N–N bond-forming metalloenzymes for biocatalytic synthesis of structurally diverse N -nitrosourea derivatives.

items.title: Density Functional Theory Bond Dissociation Energies of Model Compounds Relevant to LDL Oxidation: Bis-Allylic C–H, Phenolic O–H and Hydroperoxide O–H Bonds
items.abstract: Background : Oxidative modification of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) contributes to atherogenesis, with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) as its main chemical target. Vitamin E is an effective chainbreaking antioxidant in vitro, yet large clinical trials showed no cardiovascular benefit. We calculated bond dissociation energies (BDEs) of model compounds to quantify the underlying thermodynamics. Methods : Density functional theory calculations (PySCF; B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p)//B3LYP/6-31G*, scaled zero-point energy, 0K) were performed for butane, 1,4-pentadiene, phenol, catechol and methyl hydroperoxide. Vitamin E was not calculated at the relaxed level; published values were used. A truncated tocopherol model (5,7,8-trimethylchroman-6-ol) was run at screening level only (B3LYP/6-31+G*, unrelaxed geometries, no zero-point correction), with phenol at the same level. Results : The bis-allylic C–H bond of 1,4-pentadiene (68.2 kcal/mol) was 28.3 below that of butane (96.5). Catechol O–H (73.4) was 8.4 below phenol (81.8). The hydroperoxide model (79.6) fell 2.2 below phenol, opposite to the approximate literature order; the cause was not investigated. In screening calculations the tocopherol model was 9.0 below phenol. Published values place α-tocopherol O–H at about 77 to 78 kcal/mol, about 10 below phenol, the same direction as our screening gap. Computed values were 1.7 to 8.6 kcal/mol below approximate literature values, so gaps and ordering, not absolute values, are interpreted. Conclusions : The calculations quantify the thermodynamic basis for PUFA vulnerability and for the stronger hydrogen donation of polyphenol-type O–H bonds. They do not by themselves show donation to peroxyl radicals. Bond energies cannot explain the clinical trial results; kinetics, LDL localization and tocopherol-mediated peroxidation must be considered. No clinical outcomes or biomarkers were computed.

items.title: Chromoselective Control for Aminoalkylation of CF3‑Alkenes through Low-Energy Photoredox Catalysis
items.abstract: Recent advances in chromoselective photoredox catalysis have demonstrated that light wavelength can serve as a powerful and orthogonal reaction parameter, enabling divergent reactivity from a single catalytic system. Building on recent advances in the sequential decarboxylative/defluorinative aminoalkylation of trifluoromethyl-substituted alkenes, we report a divergent, wavelength-dependent strategy for the site-selective functionalization of N-arylglycines. High-throughput experimentation (HTE) was used to systematically screen photocatalysts and irradiation wavelengths to identify the most suitable divergent conditions. Interestingly, using [Ru(bpy)3]2+ as photocatalyst, irradiation with blue light promotes efficient difunctionalization of CF3-alkenes with N-arylglycines, affording monofluoroalkenyl-1,5-diamines, while switching the irradiation to red light enables selective monofunctionalization, delivering the corresponding gem-difluoroalkenyl amine intermediates exclusively under otherwise identical conditions, via a spin-forbidden transition pathway. This wavelength-governed switchable reactivity provides a powerful and tunable platform for the controlled radical modification of amino acids, expanding the synthetic utility of visible-light photoredox catalysis in divergent amine synthesis. Mechanistic investigations using photoelectrochemistry and TD-DFT have revealed notably a photo-excitation of intermediates, allowing for the second functionalization to whether happens or not, based on the irradiation wavelength used.

items.title: Solid-phase synthesis and structure-degradation relationships of VHL-recruiting PROTACs for preferential histone deacetylase 6 degradation
items.abstract: This work reports on a series of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL)-recruiting histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) PROTACs based on a vorinostat-inspired HDAC inhibitor. Systematic variations of the VHL ligand, the exit vector, and the linker architecture revealed that longer, semi-rigid linkers promoted efficient HDAC6 degradation. Compounds 12-15 emerged as potent HDAC6 degraders, with 15 exhibiting a half-maximal degradation value of 26 nM with 12 showing particularly rapid degradation kinetics. The lead compounds induced pronounced and preferential HDAC6 degradation in MM.1S and FLT3-ITD-positive MV4-11 cells. Notably, 13-15 displayed submicromolar antiproliferative activity in MV4-11 cells and significantly induced apoptosis. Compound 13 was markedly more active than its non-degrading control nc-13, despite nearly identical HDAC1 and HDAC6 inhibitory activities, which underscores the important contribution of targeted HDAC degradation to the antiproliferative activity. Overall, this study supports VHL-mediated targeted degradation as a promising strategy to translate HDAC6 targeting into pronounced antileukemic activity.

items.title: Drug Molecular and Route Similarity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented LLM Generation with Knowledge Graph for Semantic Reasoning
items.abstract: To address the inherent limitations of large language models (LLMs) in chemical synthesis—hallucinations, and low knowledge dense—this study presents a Knowledge Graph–enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework (KG-RAG-LLM) with a multi-scale calculation of molecular and route similarity. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that KG-RAG-LLM significantly mitigates hallucinations, increasing the proportion of concrete chemical information in generated responses to 39.52%–40.87%, drastically outperforming baseline LLMs and standard literature-based RAG pipelines in response completeness and accuracy. To overcome the inability of traditional 2D linear fingerprints to capture 3D spatial properties and reaction path variations, we further developed a multidimensional molecular and route similarity calculation combining SimHash, core similarity, and FCFP, as an alternative to Route CGR representations coupled with UMAP dimensionality reduction. This formulation accurately distinguishes between subtle and distinct synthetic strategies, demonstrating superior precision over traditional clustering methods for fuzzy retrieval of synthetic routes. Overall, this work provides a reliable, knowledge-dense solution for intelligent retrosynthetic Semantic Reasoning.

items.title: Commit: Automated Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory for model-based pharmaceutical process development: a data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid model case study
items.abstract: In 2025, we introduced the Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory, an automated platform for crystallisation experimentation and Bayesian optimisation. However, the initial case study used a relatively simple three-parameter, single-objective optimisation problem. In this Commit paper, we extend the platform to a five-dimensional, multi-objective cooling-antisolvent crystallisation of lovastatin and benchmark data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid optimisation approaches. Sixteen screening experiments were followed by model-guided experiments targeting yield and particle size (D90). Bayesian optimisation produced continued improvements in hypervolume, while mechanistic and hybrid approaches did not improve experimental performance beyond screening. The results demonstrate the value of experimentally benchmarking optimisation strategies for autonomous process development.

items.title: Cholesteric Liquid Crystals for Ultratrace PFAS Detection
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, mobile water contaminants associated with adverse effects on human health and ecosystems. Current analytical methods require specialized instrumentation, complicating their on-site detection at ultratrace concentrations across distributed water infrastructures. Here we integrate fluorophilic partitioning and proton-responsive recognition within a cholesteric liquid crystal (CLC). The fluorinated component promotes selectivity over non-fluorinated structural analogues, whereas the pyridine receptor transduces protonation into changes in helical organization and reflected color. The formulation was confined within monodisperse spherical droplets and processed as a photocurable photonic ink to produce sensing strips with a strong reflection signal readable by portable fiber-optic spectroscopy. The platform detected five PFAS through concentration-dependent blue-shifts, reaching detection limits of 5.9 parts per trillion (ppt) without sample preconcentration and maintaining comparable performance across three water matrices. Coupling molecular recognition to collective supramolecular reorganization establishes CLCs as promising sensing materials for on-site ultratrace PFAS detection.

items.title: Late-Stage Ligand Prioritization by Combining Rapid-Dissociation Filtering with MM/GBSA
items.abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of binding free energies remains a central challenge in computational chemistry, largely due to the complexity of solvent effects and the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost. Explicit solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed thermodynamic and kinetic insight, now routinely reaching microsecond timescales, while end-point methods such as MM/GBSA offer high efficiency but are sensitive to model parameters. In particular, the accuracy of MM/GBSA strongly depends on the atomic radii used to define the dielectric boundary within the implicit solvent framework. Here, we introduce an explicit–implicit hybrid workflow for late-stage ligand prioritization that integrates the strengths of both approaches. In this framework, microsecond-scale explicit solvent MD simulations act as a rapid-dissociation filter, flagging weak or unstable binders through spontaneous dissociation within the simulation window. MM/GBSA is then used to rank the remaining candidates. To improve the accuracy of the implicit solvent stage, we employ optimized atomic radii sets (OPTBIND), specifically designed for binding free-energy calculations. On the protein–ligand complexes of Curated32-4 set , a new curated benchmark of 32 complexes including 4 congeneric series, the entropy-free MM/GBSA stage with OPT- BIND 6D achieved Pearson r = 0.82 and Spearman ρ = 0.84, with 100% recovery of the experimental rank ordering across all four congeneric series, while a single-replica consistency test of the rapid-dissociation filter yielded an AUC of 0.88 and retained all 15 sub-micromolar binders. Finally, as a real-world drug design application, we apply the workflow to halogen substitutions in SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors, demonstrating its ability to identify favorable chemical modifications. Notably, the approach prospectively identifies F→Cl and F→I as affinity-enhancing substitutions; the predicted enhancement for the chlorine analog is subsequently confirmed experimentally, while the iodine analog remains a testable prediction, highlighting its predictive power in guiding chemical optimization. Together, these results establish a practical framework for detailed studies of receptor–ligand binding and for late-stage ligand prioritization in drug discovery.

items.title: CP-GFM-SGX: Topology-Aware Cyclic Peptide Generation and Design with Receptor-Conditioned Structural Evaluation and Experimental KRAS Affinity Optimization
items.abstract: Cyclic-peptide discovery requires molecular topology, atomic structure, receptor-associated evidence and computational decisions to remain consistent across a multistage workflow. We present CP-GFM-SGX, an all-atom generative AI model for cyclic-peptide design that integrates a topology-aware generative core with a Unified Evidence State Machine (UESM) to track candidate identity, chemical validity, provenance, typed failures and bounded computation. We evaluated three distinct aspects of the system. In Track A, a frozen five-complex known-ligand benchmark with 100 scheduled poses per complex, the native-free FULL route selected a ligand-backbone pose with root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) below 2 Å in four of five systems; retrospective best-of-100 evaluation found a sub-2-Å pose in all five (median selected RMSD, 1.72 Å). In Track B, matched true-pocket versus shuffled-pocket comparisons favored the specified pocket in all seven main targets (median of target medians, +172.6 Rosetta energy units; weakest margin, +3.9 for MCL-1–9CDT). An exploratory post-protocol assessor admitted 42/42, 42/42 and 40/42 selected top-K slots in the full, condition-masked and post hoc head-to-tail arms, respectively. In Track C, FULL UESM produced the specified protective outcomes for six deterministic synthetic fault fixtures and one additional missing-evidence case; targeted ablations isolated the roles of provenance and failure propagation. In a separate KRAS G12D–GDP experimental-feedback series, synthesis and SPR/BLI testing of cyclic-peptide analogues guided position-2 basic-side-chain selection and dual-basic-group placement, advancing the reported SPR affinity from approximately 60 µM for CRO-748 to approximately 6 µM for 748-R1 and approximately 1 µM for 748-RK. Comparisons using the 31-dimension Structured Capability and Evidence Grid (SCEG-31D) demonstrate that CP-GFM-SGX exhibits certain superiority over other design platforms in multiple aspects. Together, we evaluate a topology-aware generative artificial intelligence workflow for receptor-focused cyclic-peptide design and show, in a KRAS feedback series, how binding measurements guide iterative chemical optimization.

items.title: Unleashing AI for preclinical drug development
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping preclinical drug development across target discovery, therapeutic design, synthesis, functional characterization and safety assessment. In this review, we present an integrated view of AI across the preclinical pipeline, beginning with target identification, modality selection and representation learning for molecular, protein, structural, cellular and multimodal data. We then examine major generative modeling paradigms including autoregressive, latent-variable, diffusion, flow-based and guided approaches and their applications across small molecules, peptides, enzymes, antibodies, Tcell receptors and mRNA therapeutics. We discuss how these methods support de novo design, structure- and pocket-conditioned generation, sequence–structure co-design, affinity and activity optimization, developability engineering and synthesis-aware discovery. We further review AI-enabled retrosynthesis, reaction prediction and closed-loop experimental optimization, emphasizing the distinction between computational synthesizability and experimentally executable chemistry. Beyond molecular generation, we organize functional prediction from binding and kinetics through target engagement, pharmacological activity, mechanism of action, pathway response and phenotypic outcome. We also examine singlecell perturbation modeling, organoid-based drug-response prediction, toxicity and off-target assessment, and prospective validation across therapeutic modalities. Across these areas, we highlight the importance of uncertainty estimation, out-of-distribution generalization, reproducibility and experimentally grounded benchmarking. Finally, we discuss how integrating generative AI, mechanistic biology and iterative design–make–test–analyze cycles could transform AI from isolated predictive tools into decision-support systems for preclinical drug development.

items.title: From Vacuum Geometry to Solution-Phase Electronic Properties and Thermodynamics via Equivariant Neural Networks
items.abstract: We introduce a general framework for predicting solution-phase quantum-mechanical (QM) properties of drug-like molecules directly from gas-phase geometries, without solvent-specific structural optimization or property calculations. Using current equivariant neural network (ENN) architectures, such as MACE and Allegro, we demonstrate that they can also predict extensive and intensive QM properties in implicit water at a high level of theory. Direct-and ∆-learning strategies are employed for this prediction task using the Aquamarine dataset, which provides QM properties for the same molecules in both environments. The developed models are systematically evaluated for scalability to larger molecules, transferability across chemical space, and generalization to out-of-equilibrium configurations. Our results show that, despite substantial differences between gas-and solution-phase conformational ensembles, the models can accurately reconstruct ensemble-averaged solution-phase properties from gas-phase molecular dynamics. We further integrate the learned QM properties into the QUEDsol framework (“QUantum Electronic Descriptors in SOLution”) as electronic descriptors for hydration free-energy prediction. A simple and interpretable quadratic regression model trained on the FreeSolv dataset achieves state-of-the-art performance on the challenging and chemically diverse FlexiSol benchmark, outperforming previously reported QM-and ML-based approaches. These results establish ENNs as a versatile approach for inter-phase molecular property prediction and demonstrate that environment-specific QM descriptors generated from gas-phase geometries can provide transferable inputs for complex thermodynamic modeling.

items.title: Application-Specific Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis of Source-Optimized Nanoparticle Textile Formulations: Trade-offs in Washing Durability, Antibacterial Performance, and Laboratory-Scale Raw-Material Cost
items.abstract: Nanoparticle-functionalized textiles offer antibacterial and self-cleaning functions, but their practical suitability is difficult to compare because laundering protocols, reported performance measures, and formulation costs vary across studies. This study develops an application-specific multi-criteria decision-analysis framework using harmonized secondary data from eight source-optimized TiO2-, ZnO-, Ag-, and hybrid-based textile formulations under a school sports-bib scenario. Washing durability and laboratory-scale raw-material cost were evaluated for all eight formulations, while antibacterial performance was included for the six formulations with sufficiently comparable data. Laundering results were converted to a common ten-reference-wash horizon, normalized criterion scores were evaluated across the full feasible weight space, and targeted sensitivity analyses examined uncertainty arising from washing normalization, incomplete Ag laundering conditions, sparse ZnO evidence, and possible cost underestimation. Under baseline conditions, Hybrid ZnO-TiO2 applied by padding-squeezing and Ag deposited through two-step grafting and reduction formed the Pareto frontier in both the two-and three-criterion models. The hybrid formulation was preferred under cost-oriented priorities, whereas the Ag formulation was favored when durability or antibacterial performance received greater weight. This principal decision structure remained stable across the tested uncertainty scenarios. In the Ag-excluded metal-oxide subset, Hybrid Padding-Squeezing remained the budget-sensitive option, while Hybrid In-Situ became more competitive when performance was prioritized. Substantial within-material variation indicated that formulation and deposition route were important sources of practical performance variation within the selected dataset. The framework provides a transparent method for translating heterogeneous published textile data into conditional, application-specific formulation decisions.

items.title: Lipid-Phase Access Does Not Explain P-Glycoprotein Substrate Selection in Matched Pairs
items.abstract: The hydrophobic vacuum cleaner model holds that P-glycoprotein intercepts substrates within the lipid bilayer, which makes lipid-phase access to the transporter a candidate determinant of efflux, but the proposition has never been tested on compounds matched for the properties that otherwise dominate. We simulated nine matched molecular pairs—matched simultaneously on calculated lipophilicity, hydrogen-bond donors, polar surface area and molecular weight, and differing 5.9-to 30.1-fold in measured MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio—in a coarse-grained blood–brain barrier membrane containing human P-glycoprotein, and applied a pre-registered observable: enrichment E of substrate over non-substrate within 3.5 nm of the lateral portal axis. E bears no relation to efflux (ρ = −0.100, p = 0.80, n = 9), and the slope of unity predicted if access governed efflux lies outside the 95% interval [−0.51, +0.79], while five matched replicas put the measurement error at 3.65 times below the pair-to-pair spread, so the null is informative rather than underpowered. Selection is therefore decided after arrival at the transporter rather than during delivery to it.

items.title: Diverse Remote Difunctionalization of Enyne-type Propargylic Carbonates: Regio-, Chemo-, and Stereoselective Access to Highly Functionalized Multisubstituted 1,3-Dienes
items.abstract: Herein, we report the first catalytic heterodifunctionalization and homodifunctionalization of readily available 1-substituted enyne-type propargylic derivatives, proceeding via a multicomponent remote C2,C5-addition/substitution pathway. This palladium-catalyzed protocol enables the modular and straightforward assembly of tri-, tetra-, and penta-substituted 1,3-dienes with diverse functional groups from two heteroatom nucleophiles or one heteroatom nucleophile and one carbon nucleophile. The reaction exhibits high chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity, accommodates a broad spectrum of O-, N-, S-, and C-nucleophiles, and delivers highly substituted (Z, E)-1,3-dienes with precise stereocontrol. Notably, switching from O- to S-nucleophiles triggers a nucleophile-directed stereodivergence. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated through diverse downstream transformations, efficient synthesis of bioactive molecules, and late-stage functionalization of natural products. Mechanistic studies reveal the involvement of heteroatom-containing pentacoordinate π-allyl palladium and π-alkynyl palladium intermediates in this heterodifunctionalization process.

items.title: Transformation product bottleneck: Photo-recalcitrance of rotenolone limits the aquatic degradation of rotenone in a temperature-dependent manner
items.abstract: The environmental fate and toxicity of transformation products (TPs) are frequently overlooked. However, in many cases, TPs are functional analogs that exhibit similar, and often greater, toxicity as the parent compound. In cases where the TP is persistent in the environment, the rate of TP degradation can influence the overall environmental fate. Rotenolone (12𝛼-hydroxy-rotenone, ROH) is the primary TP of rotenone (ROT), a pesticide utilized ubiquitously and highly popular in cold regions. Both ROT and ROH are mitochondrial NADH inhibitors, however ROH is more persistent than ROT and remains unregulated. 2 This work investigated the aquatic photochemical pathways and transformation products of ROH, including simulated Subarctic (low-temperature) conditions. Given that ROT degradation is driven by photolysis, we hypothesized that inhibited photochemical activity of ROH accounts for its persistence. Our results suggest ROH persistence is largely attributed to significantly reduced triplet state lifetimes, absorbance, and apparent quantum yields. Temperature was identified as a significant driver of ROH photolysis, accelerating the direct photochemical transformation rate, with half-lives ranging from approximately 115 h (6 °C) to 66 h (19 °C). This suggests that the cool temperatures of Subarctic surface waters further contribute to ROH persistence. Degradation was accelerated in the presence of chromophoric dissolved organic matter (CDOM); Fenton experiments confirmed ROH reacts with hydroxyl radical at near diffusion-limited rates (2.9×1010 ± 1.1×109 M-1 s-1 at 20 °C). Nontarget analysis of ROH photoproducts revealed novel transformation intermediates not previously identified. These were observed to further transform to smaller products, suggesting that ROH photochemical transformation represents the final step in detoxification. Thus, the photochemical recalcitrance of ROH is involved in limiting the detoxification of ROT following aquatic pesticidal use. These results strongly suggest including ROH monitoring during ROT pesticide applications.

items.title: Spirocyclic Azetidines as Lactam Bioisosteres in Isoindolinones Through Facile C1 Stitching Enabled by Dual Energy- and Electron-Transfer Photocatalysis
items.abstract: Bioisosteric replacement of nitrogen-containing cyclic structures with smaller, more conformationally rigid ring systems such as azetidines and spirocyclic azetidines has emerged as an effective strategy to improve the physicochemical and pharmacokinetic profiles of nitrogen-bearing drug candidates. Despite extensive studies, the use of spirocyclic azetidines as bioisosteres has been limited to simple ring systems and has not been extended to medicinally relevant complex pharmacophores. Herein, we introduce benzo-fused spirocyclic azetidines as three-dimensional bioisosteres of lactam moieties in isoindolinones, significant structural motifs present in >40,000 bioactive compounds. Our synthetic strategy is to “stitch” in one step a broad range of oxadiazoline carbene precursors and substituted 1-azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs), thus accessing structurally diverse spirocyclic azetidines. This reaction is mechanistically novel, merging strain-release activation of ABB with a dual energy-transfer/single-electron-transfer photocatalytic cascade, enabling formal C1-insertion under mild conditions. The physicochemical and metabolic profiling suggests that these spirocyclic azetidine bioisosteres retain key physicochemical properties while improving metabolic stability. Moreover, docking studies indicate conserved recognition with the potential for interaction rewiring at selected targets. Given the ubiquitous presence of lactam and amide-containing motifs in bioactive molecules and drug candidates, this work opens new avenues for drug discovery and clinical development.

items.title: Following Nature’s Lead – Pillar[n]arene Phosphates as Versatile Molecular Hosts
items.abstract: Phosphates are ubiquitous natural recognition motifs. Their charge, hydrogen bonding, variable substitution, and reversible enzymatic installation uniquely enable complex tasks in Biology. However, they are not used extensively in supramolecular systems. Herein, we combine Nature’s modulator with supramolecular rational design, creating rim-functionalised pillar[n]arene phosphates, which act as highaffinity molecular hosts. Using robust phosphoramidite chemistry, we prepared P5Max and P6Max, based on pillar[5]arene and pillar[6]arene cores in four high yielding steps. We developed a high-throughput fluorescence displacement assay enabling us to explore a biologically focused screening panel and so rapidly investigate the recognition properties of our new hosts. P5Max and P6Max bind a series of structurally diverse chemotherapies, neuromuscular blockade agents, anaesthetics and antibiotics, with P6Max proving the more general host. We used functional assays to explore P6Max’s ability to control the biological effect of different drug classes, including highly toxic chemotherapy drugs and antibiotics. The use of high-throughput assays in host-guest systems provides a simple, rapid, and scalable route to translating supramolecular interactions to functional effect.

items.title: FMS2Lib: A Machine Learning-Ready Tandem Mass Spectral Library for Nontargeted Analysis of Non-conventional PFAS
items.abstract: Nontargeted identification of non-conventional per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including fluorinated pharmaceuticals and pesticides, remains challenging. Existing machine learning models for nontargeted analysis, primarily trained on tandem mass spectra of nonfluorinated compounds, may not generalize well to non-conventional PFAS because of their distinct mass spectrometric chemistry. Here, we established FMS2Lib, an experimental tandem mass spectral library containing 34,686 fluorinated drug-like compounds (F 1-4 ), to support machine learning-based nontargeted PFAS analysis. We demonstrated that training with FMS2Lib substantially improved the performance of existing models for both molecular formula prediction and structure annotation. We further applied these models to identify PFAS in passive samplers from wastewater effluents and surface waters and in high-throughput laboratory biotransformation experiments, revealing dozens of non-conventional PFAS and their biotransformation products. Collectively, FMS2Lib addresses a major data bottleneck in machine learning-based nontargeted analysis of non-conventional PFAS.

items.title: A Tumor-Activatable DNA Nanoengager That Orchestrates NK Receptor Clustering and Immune Checkpoint Blockage to Enhance Antitumor Cytotoxicity
items.abstract: Natural killer cell engagers (NKCEs) are promising immunotherapeutic agents for cancer treatment. However, their efficacy against solid tumors is severely limited by immune evasion mechanisms (mediated by the sialic acid–Siglec axis and PD-1/PD-L1 pathway), along with poor pharmacokinetics and off-target effects. Harnessing the precision and addressability of DNA origami, we engineered a tissue-specific, DNA origami-based, dual checkpoint-inhibiting NK synapse engager. This nanoplatform adopts a bilayered barrel architecture: the inner layer is functionalized with aNKp46, aPD-L1, and sialidase, while the outer layer is modified with the serum albumin-binding peptide ABD035 and a pH-sensitive i-motif switch. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the DNA nanoengager undergoes specific dissociation of the outer protective layer, exposing the functional modules. These components concurrently bridge and activate NK cells, block the PD-L1 immune checkpoint, and specifically degrade tumor surface sialic acids, thereby reversing dual immunosuppression. This integrated DNA system enables synergistic integration of targeted activation, dual checkpoint blockade, and tumor microenvironment responsiveness, providing a novel smart nanoscale strategy to overcome multifaceted immune evasion in solid tumors and enhance the safety and efficacy of NK cell-based immunotherapy.

items.title: Leveraging Cubenes to Access Highly Functionalized Fused Cubes
items.abstract: Since 1913, cubane has fascinated chemists owing to its remarkable structure. More recently, however, cubanes have emerged as attractive bioisosteres for aromatic rings. Although substituted derivatives are relatively common, ring-fused cubanes (a.k.a. “fused cubes”) are rare and can be difficult to access. Here, we report a strategy for the synthesis of fused cubes leveraging cubenes, unusual fleeting intermediates possessing hyperpyramidalized alkenes, in strain-promoted trapping reactions. Further, experimental and computational studies for the generation and reactivity of unsubstituted cubene and new substituted cubenes are disclosed. These studies not only push the limits of strained intermediate chemistry but also provide an entryway to highly functionalized fused cubes, including new three-dimensional hybrid structures and other unprecedented chemical space.

items.title: Substrate Length Controls Atropopeptide Complexity and Triggers Excision-Driven Scaffold Hop to Diketopiperazine Alkaloids
items.abstract: Atropopeptides are a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that share conserved cross-link-forming amino acids in their core peptides, yet adopt architectures ranging from simple monocyclic to complex polycyclic structures with intriguing three-dimensional shapes. These complex architectures arise from multiple C–C and C–N cross-links that are installed by a single cytochrome P450 enzyme, but the factors governing these divergent cross-linking patterns and resulting structural complexities have remained elusive. Recent studies on RiPP biosynthesis have revealed a form of substrate-controlled catalysis, in which the precursor sequence, rather than the modifying enzyme, dictates the reaction course. Here, we describe a distinct form of substrate-controlled catalysis in atropopeptide biosynthesis, demonstrating that core peptide length, rather than sequence, determines the cross-linking pattern installed by an atropopeptide-forming cytochrome P450. We further uncover an unusual proteolytic excision of an internal amino acid in mature atropopeptides, generating peptides that spontaneously convert into pyrroloindoline-containing diketopiperazines (DKPs) and thereby effecting a nonenzymatic scaffold-hop from atropopeptides to DKP-derived alkaloids, for which we provide mechanistic insight. Both the atropopeptide and the corresponding DKP exhibit antiviral activity, and their structural diversity can be further expanded through precursor engineering. Our work reveals substrate length as a key determinant of atropopeptide complexity, provides insights into the catalysis of a multicross-link-forming P450, and establishes an unprecedented route connecting atropopeptides to pyrroloindoline DKP alkaloids.

items.title: Modular Access to Tetrasubstituted Allenes via 1,4-Dialkylation of 1,3-Enynes
items.abstract: Herein, a cobalt-catalyzed highly regio- and chemoselective 1,4-dialkylation of 1,3-enynes using readily available fluoroalkyl halides and solid alkylzinc pivalates is disclosed. This ligand-free protocol proceeds under mild conditions and tolerates a wide range of functional groups, including aryl, alkyl, and silyl substituents on the enynes, diverse primary alkylzinc reagents, and various fluoroalkyl halides (monofluoro-, difluoro-, perfluoro-, and bromo-containing derivatives), thus providing a complementary and practical access to structurally diverse fluoroalkylated allenes, expanding the toolbox for allene synthesis and showing potential for drug discovery in medicinal chemistry.

items.title: Synthesis of Diaryl α-Hydroxycarboxylic Acid Derivatives via Three-Component Reactions of o -Quinone Diimides with Alcohols and Diazo Compounds
items.abstract: Highly regioselective three-component reactions of o-quinone diimides with alcohols and diazo compounds have been developed with a rhodium catalyst. This transformation is proposed to proceed through a Michael-type trapping of oxonium ylide intermediates with arylation reagents, giving access to a range of diaryl α-hydroxycarboxylic acid derivatives bearing an oxa-quaternary center in good yields. This reaction featured broad substrate scope, scale-up synthesis, and late-stage functionalization of the complex molecule.

items.title: Iridium-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of Pyridazine Salts under Batch and Flow
items.abstract: Herein, we report an [Ir(COD)Cl]2/(R)-SunPhos-catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation of pyridazine salts to construct chiral hexahydropyridazines. The reaction tolerates a wide range of substituents, delivering products in up to 97% yield with 97% ee under mild reaction conditions. Simultaneously, the gram-scale synthesis, continuous-flow operation, and good catalyst turnover (TON up to 3720 with 94% ee at S/C = 4000; TOF up to 155 h–1) further underscored the practicality of this methodology. Collectively, this operationally simple, scalable, and sustainable protocol provides an efficient platform for valuable N-heterocycles featuring chiral hexahydropyridazine cores.

items.title: MPAThio Ligand-Accelerated Palladium-Catalyzed Nondirected Hydrogen Isotope Exchange of Arenes with D2O
items.abstract: Hydrogen isotope exchange is an atom-economical strategy for accessing deuterium-labeled molecules, but its synthetic utility is often limited by slow exchange kinetics and poor reactivity of π-extended arenes. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed nondirected hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) enabled by a dual-ligand combination of a monoprotected aminoethyl thioether (MPAThio) and an N-heteroarene ligand. This system exhibits faster HIE kinetics, reaching isotopic equilibrium within 30 min at 105 °C (and within 60 min at 90 °C), and enables efficient deuterium incorporation under mild conditions using D2O as the deuterium source. The protocol enables efficient deuteration of a broad range of mono- and multisubstituted arenes. For poorly soluble substrates relevant to organic light-emitting diode materials, a cosolvent strategy addresses solubility limitations, affording high deuterium incorporation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the MPAThio ligand lowers the barrier of accessing the reactive C–H activation manifold, thereby favoring efficient reversible HIE.

items.title: Photochemical Radical Cascade Annulation of 6-Azauracils Enabled by CsPbBr3 Perovskite Nanocrystals
items.abstract: Direct annulation of 6-azauracils has remained challenging due to their strongly electron-deficient and decomposition-prone heterocyclic frameworks. This study presents unique insight into the core modification of the 6-azauracil system enabled by a CsPbBr3 perovskite nanocrystal-promoted photochemical cascade cyclization with an amino acid derivative. N-Phenylglycine, a zwitterion with strong surface binding affinity for the photocatalyst, generated a nucleophilic aminomethyl radical in dimethyl carbonate that added to the C═N bond, triggering a radical cascade to tetrahydroimidazole-fused triazines, structures of emerging relevance in biochemical applications. Dimethyl carbonate ensured radical stability and catalyst integrity, enabling a broad scope and late-stage functionalization. Beyond azauracils, the strategy also supports the late-stage functionalization of a range of biologically important drug molecules, providing a cost-effective, sustainable, and operationally simple platform for light-mediated synthesis empowered by perovskite nanocrystals.

items.title: Synthesis of Pyrido[2,3- d ]pyrimidin-4(3 H )-ones via SNAr/Tandem Cyclization
items.abstract: A new method has been developed for constructing the pyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4(3H)-one scaffold under metal- and ligand-free conditions. In this strategy, 2-bromo-N-phenylnicotinamide is activated by the synergistic electron-withdrawing effects of the pyridine ring and the amide group, enabling tandem nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr)/cyclization with cyanamide or formamide under simple conditions. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support an SNAr/cyclization mechanism. Preliminary photophysical studies show that the products exhibit blue emission, suggesting potential applications in materials science. Additionally, molecular docking studies indicate that the synthesized scaffold may have relevance to medicinal chemistry, providing a foundation for future biological evaluations.

items.title: Solvent Control of Cheletropic Recombination in Benzosultine-Derived ortho -Quinodimethane Diels–Alder Reactions
items.abstract: Thermolysis of benzosultines generates ortho-quinodimethanes (o-QDMs) widely used in Diels–Alder (DA) chemistry, yet productive cycloaddition is often limited by rapid cheletropic SO2 recombination to form benzosulfolenes. Combined computational and experimental studies support a model in which benzosultine thermolysis proceeds through kinetically competent o-QDM/SO2 encounter complexes positioned at the boundary between pericyclic and open-shell reactivity. Although reversible C–S homolysis accounts for efficient TEMPO trapping, stereochemical probe experiments establish that productive cycloaddition proceeds through a concerted DA pathway. The absence of o-QDM dimerization indicates that free o-QDM does not accumulate under the reaction conditions, leading to an apparent mechanistic paradox: how can intermolecular cycloaddition compete with rapid cheletropic SO2 recombination? The combined computational and experimental data are most consistent with a model in which DA reactions occur within the same solvent cage as competing SO2 recombination. As a result, cheletropic SO2 recombination is highly medium sensitive: replacing aromatic solvents such as toluene with nonpolar aliphatic hydrocarbons markedly suppresses benzosulfolene formation and reverses product selectivity in favor of productive DA cycloaddition. These findings establish solvent-controlled encounter-complex partitioning as a general strategy for improving benzosultine-derived o-QDM cycloadditions.

items.title: Gold Single‐Atom Catalysts Enable Selective Shuttle Hydrochlorination of Alkynes
items.abstract: Shuttle catalysis enables the transfer of reactive functional groups without relying on highly corrosive reagents. However, it remains largely confined to homogeneous systems, where catalyst recovery and reuse are often challenging. Here, we report a recyclable gold single‐atom catalyst (SAC) supported on activated carbon (AC) for the selective shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, which are key intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis. Spectroscopic and catalytic studies indicate that the combination of Au(I) single atoms with the AC carrier is essential for the unique chemo‐ and stereoselectivity observed. This heterogeneous system displays broad substrate compatibility, including sterically hindered alkynes, heterocycles, acid‐labile groups, and drug‐derived substrates. Upon reuse, gradual aggregation of gold single atoms into nanoparticles leads to activity losses, but the associated speciation changes are reversible by oxidative redispersion, while quantitative metal retention ensures recoverability. Overall, this study demonstrates how to extend heterogeneous SACs to shuttle catalysis, highlighting the complementary reactivity and distinct catalyst design requirements for developing recoverable, safer, and more sustainable heterogeneous transfer reactions.

items.title: Bioorthogonal Vitamin C Probes Enable Cellular Profiling and Investigation of Lysine Vitcylation
items.abstract: Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C‐derived post‐translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter‐derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time‐resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome‐wide CRISPR‐Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S‐transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C‐derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.

items.title: Discovery of a Potent and Selective First‐In‐Class Antagonist of GPR15 With In Vivo Anti‐Obesity Activity
items.abstract: GPR15 (G Protein‐coupled Receptor 15), an atypical chemokine receptor, is implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple diseases, yet small‐molecule GPR15 antagonists remain undeveloped. Herein, we identify and characterize YL410 , the first‐in‐class potent and selective GPR15 antagonist. In the cAMP‐GloSensor assay, YL410 inhibits GPR15 with an IC 50 of 0.027 ± 0.005 µM, and displays high selectivity against a panel of related GPCRs and kinases. It suppresses GPR15L‐induced Jurkat T‐cell migration, and exhibits favorable pharmacokinetics and acceptable safety. Molecular docking, replicated molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative contact analyses, and mutagenesis experiments support a plausible orthosteric binding model for YL410 , maintained by a reproducible network of polar and hydrophobic contacts, which rationalizes its potent antagonism and observed structure–activity relationships (SAR). Complementary AI‐based structure predictions (AlphaFold3, Chai‐1, and Boltz) recapitulated the energetically accessible orthosteric poses but not the dynamically stable pose selected by the MD simulations, underscoring the importance of kinetic‐stability validation in antagonist pose selection. Notably, in a diet‐induced obesity (DIO) mouse model, YL410 administration induced significant weight loss and exerted blood glucose‐lowering effects. Collectively, this study presents the first potent, selective, and in vivo efficacious GPR15 antagonist, providing new insights into the development of therapeutics for the treatment of obesity.

items.title: One-step skeletal editing of oxetanes to thietanes using thiourea

Chrysanthevelides A−D, the Rearranged 5/5/5 Tricyclic Spiro-Guaianolides and 1, 3-Dioxolane-Containing Nor-Guaianolide Dimers from Chrysanthemum vestitum Target PKM2 to Mediate the Anti-Inflammatory Effect
items.abstract: Four unprecedented dimeric (1−2) and monomeric (3−4) sesquiterpenoids were isolated from the aerial part of Chrysanthemum vestitum. Chrysanthevelides A−B (1−2) represented the first example of the dimers with a special 1,3-dioxolane nor-guaianolide sesquiterpenoid unit, while chrysanthevelides C−D (3−4) were two pairs of unprecedented 1,10-seco rearranged 5/5/5 tricyclic spiro-guaianolide sesquiterpenoids. The undescribed structures of 1−4, including their absolute configurations, were determined through spectroscopic techniques combined with DP4+ NMR analysis and ECD calculations. Compound 1 displayed an NO production inhibitory effect with an IC50 value of 1.62 ± 0.21 μM. Primarily, western blotting and ELISA combined with the RNA-seq results indicated that 1 suppressed downstream-related inflammatory factors (IL-6 and TNF-α) and proteins (COX-2 and iNOS). Mechanistically, the α-methylene-γ-lactone (αMγL) moiety of 1 covalently binds to Cys423 of PKM2, promoting its tetramerization, which in turn regulates the HIF-1α/STAT3 axis and the glycolytic pathway. This ultimately suppressed the expression of inflammatory mediators, thereby achieving its anti-inflammatory function.

items.title: Discovery of a Novel Dual Inhibitor Targeting Tubulin and Histone Deacetylase 8 for Treatment of the Ovarian Cancer
items.abstract: In this work, a series of novel dual inhibitors against both tubulin and histone deacetylase (HDAC) were designed and synthesized by integrating the natural product Millepachine with the key pharmacophore of HDAC inhibitors. Among them, compound 6 exhibited potent antiproliferative activity against 12 cancer cell lines, with IC50 values ranging from 0.020 to 0.244 μM. Mechanistic investigations revealed that compound 6 inhibited both tubulin polymerization (IC50 2.0 μM) and HDAC8 (IC50 0.110 μM), with 54-, 27- and 132-fold selectivity over HDAC1, HDAC4 and HDAC6, respectively. In an ovarian cancer xenograft mouse model, compound 6 exhibited significant inhibitory effect on tumor growth with a favorable safety profile. These findings identify compound 6 as a promising tubulin/HDAC8 dual inhibitor for further investigation.

items.title: Discovery of Thiazolamide-based PI4KIIIβ/HDAC Dual Inhibitors with Potent Activity against Hepatitis C Virus
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a critical global public health burden affecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide. The emergence of antiviral resistance persistently undermines the long-term clinical efficacy of current direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, creating an urgent need for therapeutics with different mechanisms of action. Host-directed multi-target therapy offers a promising avenue to overcome DAA resistance, yet dual inhibitors targeting HCV-essential host kinase phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase IIIβ (PI4KIIIβ) and epigenetic regulator histone deacetylases (HDACs) have not been reported for HCV treatment to date. Herein, we describe the rational design, chemical synthesis, and comprehensive biological evaluation of a series of novel thiazolamide-based dual PI4KIIIβ/HDAC inhibitors. Lead compounds displayed potent dual-target enzymatic inhibition, robust in vitro anti-HCV activity and excellent in vivo tolerability. This work establishes a novel host-directed dual-target therapeutic paradigm for HCV, providing a viable strategy to address the unmet clinical challenge of DAA resistance.

items.title: Developing a Ferric(III) Agent for Targeted Inhibition of Growth and Metastasis of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Based on Human Serum Albumin by Chemodynamic Therapy-Driven Synergistic Therapy
items.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains challenging due to its aggressiveness and the lack of targeted therapies. In this study, we proposed designing a ferric (Fe) agent based on human serum albumin (HSA) for chemodynamic therapy-driven synergistic therapy. To this end, we not only optimized a series of Fe(III) compounds to obtain Fe4, which has remarkable toxicity against TNBC cells, but we also constructed the HSA-Fe4 NPs delivery system. Structural analysis revealed that Fe4 binds within the IB subdomain of HSA, with His-146 coordinating the iron center. Importantly, Fe4/HSA-Fe4 NPs significantly suppressed the metastasis and growth of TNBC in vivo. Moreover, we elucidated the mechanisms by which Fe4/HSA-Fe4 NPs inhibited the growth and metastasis of TNBC: inducing Fenton reaction-mediated chemodynamic therapy, inducing ferroptosis, and tri-activating the immune response through the activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, the induction of immunogenic cell death, and the repolarization of M2 macrophages.

items.title: Rational Design of Near-Infrared Difluoroboron Cyanine Photosensitizers for Lipid Droplet-Targeting Imaging and Tumor Therapy
items.abstract: Specifically disrupting lipid droplets (LDs) is an effective strategy for ablating tumor cells through photodynamic therapy (PDT). However, most reported LD probes possess short excitation/emission wavelengths, limiting tissue penetration, and LD-targeted theranostic probes remain underdeveloped. In this work, we first developed a family of near-infrared (NIR) charge-neutral and lipid droplet-targeting cyanine photosensitizers by systematically introducing heavy atoms (Br/I) at different sites of electrically neutral BF2-bridged cyanine (BCy5). These BCy photosensitizers retain the characteristic near-infrared absorption (>650 nm) and high molar extinction coefficients of classical cyanine dyes while exhibiting good singlet oxygen quantum yields. Notably, BCy5-Br1−BCy5-Br3 nanoparticles with high LD specificity exhibit significant PDT efficacy at submicromolar concentrations and, by inducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation (LPO) accumulation, concurrently trigger apoptosis and ferroptosis, effectively suppressing melanoma growth in vivo. This work provides vital insights into design principles and transformation of LD-targeting NIR cyanine photosensitizers for cancer PDT.

items.title: Antivirulence Benzothiophenes Inhibit Intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis by Targeting the Sensor Histidine Kinase MprB
items.abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis remains one of the most prevalent and threatening infectious diseases. Classical anti-tubercular therapy targets essential enzymes of the pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), thereby suppressing bacterial growth. However, the emergence of drug-resistant strains necessitates alternative therapeutic approaches. Virulence inhibition is a promising strategy that blocks Mtb virulence factors required for survival within host cells. We previously identified a hit compound, BTP15, which protected fibroblasts and THP-1 macrophages from Mtb-induced cell death ex vivo by blocking phagosomal escape through inhibition of the mycobacterial histidine kinase MprB. Due to poor pharmacokinetics, the structure of BTP15 was optimized. New benzothiophene derivatives were screened for MprB inhibition, microsomal stability, toxicity, and ex vivo efficacy in THP-1 and MRC-5 cells. The lead compound, 7a, exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic parameters, showed no toxicity in mice at 250 mg/kg, and prevented Mtb dissemination in an acute mouse model of tuberculosis.

items.title: Development of DCL1191 as a Potent, Selective and Orally Bioavailable Inhibitor for Autophagy-Associated Transcription Factor EB (TFEB)
items.abstract: Transcription factor EB (TFEB) is a promising target for autophagy regulation and cancer therapy, yet it has long been regarded as an undruggable protein. Starting from eltrombopag, an FDA-approved agent that exhibits both thrombopoietin receptor (Tpo-R) agonistic activity and TFEB inhibitory potency, we performed systematic structure−activity relationship optimization and identified DCL1191 as a potent, selective, and orally bioavailable TFEB inhibitor. DCL1191 binds TFEB with a Kd of 80.5 nM and disrupts the TFEB-DNA interaction with an IC50 of 60.5 nM. Computational modeling combined with site-directed mutagenesis elucidated its precise binding mode. DCL1191 exhibits diminished activity toward Tpo-R and MITF. Mechanistically, DCL1191 effectively represses the transcription of TFEB target genes and blocks intracellular autophagic flux. In autophagy-hyperactivated U87 glioblastoma cells, DCL1191 substantially sensitizes tumor cells to temozolomide chemotherapy. Pharmacokinetic evaluation in rats further demonstrated that DCL1191 possesses an i.v. half-life of 16.33 h and satisfactory oral bioavailability of 18.77%.

items.title: Repurposing Approved Chemotherapeutics as Intrinsic Photosensitizers for Single-Molecule Chemophototherapy
items.abstract: Chemophototherapy (CPT), combining chemotherapy and photodynamic therapy (PDT), is a promising strategy to enhance anticancer efficacy while reducing systemic toxicity. Many approved drugs contain chromophoric moieties that absorb visible light, suggesting their potential as intrinsic photosensitizers. Herein, we introduce a single-molecule chemophototherapy (SM-CPT) approach based on computational screening of approved anticancer drugs for repurposing as photosensitizers. A curated library of 238 small-molecule drugs was screened using time-dependent density functional theory to identify compounds with favourable photophysical properties. Fifteen candidates were identified, and mitoxantrone, pixantrone, daunorubicin, and epirubicin were selected for experimental validation. All compounds generated reactive oxygen species upon irradiation and showed enhanced cytotoxicity in breast cancer cell models, with up to an order-of-magnitude reduction in half-maximal inhibitory concentration values. The approach was further validated in ovarian cancer models, including platinum-resistant cells and patient-derived ascites, highlighting SM-CPT as a translationally attractive light-activated cancer therapy.

items.title: Discovery of Novel STING Inhibitors for the Treatment of Severe Acute Pancreatitis
items.abstract: Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) is a promising therapeutic target for severe acute pancreatitis (SAP), but effective small-molecule inhibitors remain limited. Here, structure−activity relationship studies identified compound D4 as a potent STING inhibitor with favorable cellular activity and safety. D4 directly engaged STING, inhibited its oligomerization and downstream TBK1/IRF3 signaling, and restored macrophage phagocytosis, autophagic flux, and mitochondrial function while suppressing NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3(NLRP3)-associated pyroptosis. D4 showed oral exposure with 24.70% bioavailability and no overt toxicity at 1000 mg/kg. In a caerulein/LPS-induced SAP model, D4 markedly reduced pancreatic injury, acinar cell necrosis, inflammatory infiltration, and serum amylase and lipase levels. STING knockdown produced similar protective effects. These findings identify D4 as a promising STING-targeting lead compound for SAP treatment.

items.title: Cinchona Alkaloids-Derived Ammonium Salts for Long-Acting and Sensory-Selective Nerve Blockades
items.abstract: Local anesthetics (LAs), a type of substance with the ability of blocking nerve fiber conduction, are indispensable in clinical practice for pain relief. However, the duration of action and sensory-motor nerve selectivity of conventional LAs require further optimization. Herein, we wish to report the discovery of novel ammonium salts derived from natural cinchona alkaloids for long-acting and sensory-selective nerve blockades. The bicyclic quincoridine skeleton exhibited superior nerve blockade efficacy compared to acyclic and monocyclic analogs. Compound CLA-1-3 produced prolonged nerve blockade (over 50 h) in the rat sciatic nerve block model, possessing an IC50 value of approximately 0.39 μmol/L for voltage-gated sodium channel inhibition. On the other hand, at a concentration range of 0.30% to 0.60%, compound CLA-3-5 achieved sensory-selective nerve blockade lasting up to 3 h. The candidate molecules and underlying mechanistic insights will be valuable assets for drug development and therapeutic innovation.

items.title: Development of N -Hydroxyindole-2-Carboxamides as New Host-Targeted Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Agents Against Human Respiratory Viruses
items.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) oxidoreductases are promising targets for host-targeted antiviral agents (HTAs) because of their essential role in protein folding, including the maturation of viral proteins. Human protein disulfide isomerase family member A3 (PDIA3) is involved in the folding of N-glycosylated client proteins, including viral envelope proteins, making it an attractive but underexplored antiviral target. Here, we describe the discovery of a novel N-hydroxyindole-2-carboxamide class of PDIA3 inhibitors, exemplified by compound AV22 (1o), which effectively inhibits PDIA3 activity and exerts broad-spectrum antiviral activity against major human respiratory viruses. Mechanistic studies indicated that AV22 (1o) increased the release of non-infectious coronavirus particles and reduced disulfide bond formation in the coronavirus spike protein, indicating that its antiviral effect stems from interference with PDIA3 activity. This new class of HTAs provides promising leads for drug discovery targeting viral envelope protein maturation vulnerabilities and is suitable for developing new BSAs.

items.title: Structure-Based Design of HDAC6 Inhibitors Targeting the L2 Pocket: Modulating Autophagy and Liquid−Liquid Phase Separation in Lung Cancer
items.abstract: We herein describe the structure-based design, synthesis and biological evaluation of a new class of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) inhibitors guided by X-ray crystal structures of our previously identified compounds 13-15. X-ray co-crystal structures of second-generation inhibitors 19b (Subseries I) and 20b (Subseries II) within zHDAC6 CD2 confirmed that these compounds behave as highly potent HDAC6 inhibitors with the ability to engage the S531 residue in the L2 loop HDAC6 catalytic domain. Western-blot analysis confirmed the target engagement in cell-based settings, through the increase of acetylated tubulin levels, without significant variation in the histone acetylation status. Compound 20b extensively reduced the viability of A549 cells in both 2- and 3-dimensional cell cultures, through the activation of pro-autophagic pathways. In addition, HDAC6 inhibition impaired the nucleation of stress-granules, confirming the ability of these compounds to modulate liquid−liquid phase separation, an emerging HDAC6-driven hallmark in cancer.

items.title: Ribonuclease H1 Hijacking: Oncotherapeutics through MicroRNA-Triggered Intracellular Construction of Long DNA/RNA Heteroduplexes
items.abstract: Ribonuclease H1 (RNase H1) cleaves the RNA strand of DNA/RNA heteroduplexes and plays essential roles in R-loop resolution, mitochondrial DNA replication, and antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) activity. Because RNase H1 has also been implicated in ASO-induced cytotoxicity, considerable effort has been focused on minimizing its activation. Here we present a reverse strategy that harnesses RNase H1-mediated cytotoxicity for cancer therapy using an oncogenic microRNA (miR-21) as an intracellular trigger. A designed hairpin DNA/hairpin RNA pair undergoes a hybridization chain reaction to assemble long-nicked DNA/RNA heteroduplexes selectively in miR-21-overexpressing cells. The resulting heteroduplexes induce RNase H1-dependent cytotoxicity in cancer cells while exhibiting minimal effects on normal cells. Treatment also caused redistribution of the paraspeckle protein P54nrb from the nucleoplasm to the nucleoli, consistent with RNase-H1-associated nucleolar stress. Furthermore, lipid-nanoparticle-mediated delivery of the DNA/RNA heterohairpin pair significantly suppressed tumor growth in mice. These findings establish a therapeutic strategy that converts RNase H1, traditionally regarded as a source of oligonucleotide toxicity, into a mechanism for selective anticancer activity through the intracellular assembly of long DNA/RNA heteroduplexes.

items.title: Antiviral immunity via telomerase-like reverse transcription in bacteria
Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
items.abstract: Abstract Identifying targets to enhance tumor immunity is an urgent need. Although nucleic acid sensors play critical roles in promoting tumor immune clearance, their exceptionally low mutation rate in cancers suggests potential unexplored roles in tumor progression. Here, we demonstrated that the RNA sensor MDA5 promotes immune evasion, and its high expression was strongly predictive of poor survival and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in patients. Targeting MDA5 reshapes the tumor microenvironment, strengthening immune memory responses and enhancing effector CD8⁺ T cell activity. Mechanistically, MDA5 deficiency triggers UPR-driven immunogenic cell death (ICD) through induction of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), leading to enhanced dendritic cell-mediated antigen engulfment and T cell activation. Additionally, MDA5 loss primes the ASK1-JNK/P38 signaling pathway, sensitizing tumor cells to TNFα/IFNγ, further amplifying this process. Consequently, targeting MDA5 enhances the efficacy of ICB therapy across multiple cancer types, positioning it as a promising therapeutic target.

items.title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis
items.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify two phenotypically distinct neutrophil subsets in PF: a pro-inflammatory subset characterized by CD54 (human) or iNOS (mouse) expression, and an alternative subset marked by Arg1 expression. Notably, CD54+ and iNOS+ neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively.
