Adoptive transfer of iNOS+ neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1+ neutrophils had no significant effect. Further, the expression of PIEZO1, a mechanically activated ion channel, is predominantly upregulated in CD54+ neutrophils from PF patients or iNOS+ neutrophils from PF mice. Piezo1 ablation in neutrophils selectively impairs iNOS+ neutrophil differentiation, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 promotes the differentiation of these pro-inflammatory subsets through the transcription factor IRF4 in a calcium-dependent manner. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54+ neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Importantly, combined inhibition of JAK/STAT and calcium signaling exerts synergistic suppression on the iNOS+ neutrophil expansion and PF progression. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophils. Neutrophils have been shown to be involved in pulmonary fibrosis (PF). Here, the authors identify an expanded pro-inflammatory neutrophil state marked by CD54 in human PF and by iNOS in murine PF, demonstrate that iNOS+ neutrophils promote PF whilst Arg+ neutrophils are less effective, and show that mechanical activation of the PIEZO1 channel contributes to the promotion of PF by CD54 + /iNOS+ neutrophils.

items.title: Precision functional mapping of imagined and experienced pain
items.abstract: Imagination is a principal human capacity, enabling simulation of sensations and situations for planning, learning, and empathy. We examined neural representations of experienced and imagined pain across eight body sites using deep-phenotyping, precision functional MRI with over seven hours of scanning per participant (N = 9). Here we show, using conventional mapping, pattern classification, and representational similarity analyses, that both imagined and experienced pain activated nociceptive regions (e.g., dorsoposterior insula) and non-nociceptive regions (e.g., premotor areas and inferior inter-effector motor cortex). However, imagined pain did not reliably reactivate body site-selective nociceptive patterns in any region. Instead, imagined and experienced pain shared multivariate representations across widespread cortical and subcortical regions, particularly transmodal cortical areas including dorsomedial and lateral prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus. These findings suggest that imagination generates distributed pain-like activity, but with separable neural codes for imagined and experienced pain. This distinction may explain the difficulty of vividly imagining pain and clarify its potential roles in empathy, planning, and pain chronification.

items.title: DHHC12 serves as a critical nutrient-responsive switch that couples amino acid sensing to insulin secretion
items.abstract: Protein palmitoylation covalently attaches the energy metabolite palmitate to target proteins, yet how it is regulated by nutrient status remains elusive. Here, we identify the palmitoyltransferase DHHC12 as a critical nutrient-responsive switch, coupling amino acid availability to insulin secretion. Amino acid deficiency activates the kinase GCN2, which phosphorylates COPA at Thr777, enabling its function as an adaptor for the CRL4 E3 ligase complex and leading to ubiquitination of DHHC12 on two critical cysteine residues (Cys127 and Cys133, with Cys127 within the catalytic DHHC motif) and its subsequent degradation. In male mice, loss of Dhhc12 impairs insulin secretion and causes glucose intolerance. DHHC12 palmitoylates SYT7 to promote glucose-stimulated insulin exocytosis. The physiological relevance of this pathway is underscored by two human DHHC12 variants: the hypoglycemia-associated L196P mutant evades degradation, whereas the hyperglycemia-linked N238I mutant is constitutively degraded. Together, our findings establish the GCN2-COPA-DHHC12 axis as a direct nutrient-sensing mechanism that couples amino acid availability to systemic glucose homeostasis. Men et al. show that amino acid deprivation activates GCN2 to phosphorylate COPA, recruiting CRL4 E3 ligase that ubiquitinates DHHC12 at its catalytic cysteine for degradation. This blocks SYT7 palmitoylation and insulin secretion. Human DHHC12 variants with opposing stability correlate with fasting glucose, validating clinical importance.

items.title: IL-4 exploits TNF signaling to shape its gene expression signature in monocytes and macrophages
items.abstract: Abstract Investigation of crosstalk between antagonistic pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines has focused on mechanisms and functional consequences of cross-inhibition. We investigated cross-regulation between proinflammatory TNF and anti-inflammatory IL-4 in primary human monocytes and in a skin wound-healing model. Surprisingly, TNF functioned mainly as a costimulator of IL-4-induced gene expression, whereas IL-4 selectively inhibited the TNF-induced IFN response, leaving inflammatory gene expression mostly intact. TNF and IL-4 synergistically induced gene sets important for regulating inflammation and tissue repair, which were highly induced during the phase of wound healing when these cytokines are co-expressed. Crosstalk between TNF and IL-4 was mediated by epigenetic chromatin-mediated mechanisms associated with cooperation between NF-κB and STAT6 transcription factors, erasure of negative histone mark H3K27me3, and selective inhibition of IRF1. These results identify a long-sought mechanism for expansion of the IL-4 response, and highlight the complexity of crosstalk between antagonistic cytokines that includes cooperation for select gene responses important in immune response and tissue repair.

items.title: Syndecan-3 couples tumor mechanics to immunosuppressive macrophage identity
items.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages adopt suppressive states, but how tumor stress installs these programs remains unclear. Here, we identify syndecan-3 (SDC3) as a macrophage-intrinsic mechanosensory regulator by integrating in vivo functional screening, single-cell and spatial profiling, and genetic and pharmacological perturbation. SDC3+ macrophages accumulate in hypoxic, stiff tumor niches and suppress antitumor cytotoxic T-cell responses. Matrix stiffness increases mechanical loading on SDC3, reorganizes an SDC3-associated scaffold and opens suppressive chromatin loci. This program engages a CDK7–MAFB relay to induce TREM2, which functions as a required suppressive effector in mice. Human-cell assays support a species-specific TREM2-associated inhibition mechanism. Naldemedine engages TREM2, restores cytotoxic T-cell activity, improves tumor control and enhances immune-checkpoint blockade in vivo. These findings define a targetable SDC3–CDK7–MAFB–TREM2 axis linking hypoxia and tissue mechanics to macrophage-mediated immune evasion. Tumor associated macrophages (TAMs) are a main component of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Here the authors identify syndecan-3 as a macrophage-intrinsic mechano-sensor that drives immunosuppression in the TME.

items.title: Short Wavelength Infrared Diimmonium Nano-Agents for Photoacoustic Imaging
items.abstract: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) as an innovative biomedical imaging modality shows high contrast and superior spatial resolution, yet remains limited by underdeveloped second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) contrast agents, particularly neglecting the NIR-IIb (1500-1700 nm) window. In this work, we designed a new class of diimmonium (DB)-based dicationic nano-agents (DB·2X, X = TFSI - , B(C 2 O 4 ) 2 - , or BF 4 - ) for 1700 nm excitation PAI. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that dicationic DB 2+ exhibits a dramatically reduced excitation energy (1.24 eV) and enhanced oscillator strength (f = 1.11) by molecular engineering, attributed to a symmetry-allowed local excitation mechanism for electronic restructuring. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction further demonstrates the intermolecular spacings >5.0 Å in DB·2X aggregates, facilitating optimized non-radiative transitions for amplified PAI signals. In vivo study using different disease models shows that DB·2TFSI nano-agents under 1700 nm excitation can achieve higher signal-to-background ratio and minimized interference from endogenous chromophores compared to conventional 1064 nm excitation. Biocompatibility assessments confirm low cytotoxicity, underscoring potential for further development of DB·2TFSI nano-agents. This work delivers a robust molecular design paradigm for non-radiative decay optimization, and for the first time establishes 1700 nm-excitable PAI nano-agents, paving the way for tissue high-quality biomedical imaging.

items.title: Ki-67, the chromosome periphery and de-compartmentalisation each contribute to nucleophosmin mislocalisation in acute myeloid leukaemia
items.abstract: The mitotic chromosome periphery (MCP) is an important chromosome compartment but links to disease remains elusive. Here we define the mitosis-specific, Ki-67 interactome, identifying additional MCP components and revealing that MCP genes are commonly mutated in cancer, including nucleophosmin (NPM1). Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML)-specific NPM1 mutations (NPM1c + ), result in protein mislocalisation (nucleolus to cytoplasm). We demonstrate that NPM1c+ fails to adequately bind to the MCP, instead forming aggregates during mitosis. We also report that, de-compartmentalisation at mitotic onset allows formation of NPM1wt/c+ multimers. These mislocalisation mechanisms contribute to a significant hinderance of NPM1 re-entry into daughter cell nucleoli. Enhancing MCP loading capacity via Ki-67 overexpression resulted in increased MCP-bound NPM1c+ during mitosis and greater yield of nucleolar NPM1c + . Ki-67 expression demonstrated a significant interaction with NPM1 mutation status on AML patient overall survival, whereby higher Ki-67 was associated with increased hazard in NPM1wt but reduced hazard in NPM1c+ patients. This work reveals mechanistic insight into AML and evidence that the MCP has untapped therapeutic potential.

items.title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
items.abstract: Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

items.title: From Chlorogermanes to Carbon–Germanium Bonds: Electrochemical Strategies for Modular Germylation
items.abstract: Organogermanium compounds have attracted growing interest in materials science, medicinal chemistry, and catalysis because of their distinctive electronic properties, tunable steric environments, high chemical stability, and emerging utility as bioisosteric motifs. Despite these attractive features, the development of general and modular methods for carbon–germanium (C–Ge) bond formation has lagged that of silicon and tin. Conventional approaches frequently rely on preformed organometallic reagents, hydrogermanes, or stoichiometric chemical reductants, thereby limiting functional-group compatibility and the direct use of readily available organic electrophiles. Electrochemical synthesis offers an alternative strategy in which electron transfer can be regulated through electrode potential, current, catalyst identity, and cell configuration. In this context, chlorogermanes are particularly attractive germylating reagents because they are readily accessible, bench-stable, and structurally tunable. Their combination with electrochemical activation enables the controlled generation of low-valent metal species, carbon-centered radicals, metal-germyl intermediates, or nucleophilic germanium species, depending on the catalyst and electrochemical regime. This mechanistic flexibility provides opportunities to construct C–Ge bonds without the prior preparation of organogermanium nucleophiles. In this Account, we describe our efforts to establish chlorogermane-based electrochemical germylation as a modular platform for C(sp3)–Ge, C(sp2)–Ge, and C(sp)–Ge bond formation, as well as for multicomponent group 14 functionalization. Cobalt electrocatalysis enables the cross-electrophile coupling of chlorogermanes with alkyl, aryl, and alkenyl halides, providing access to alkyl-, aryl-, and alkenylgermanes under mild conditions. Nickel electrocatalysis extends this strategy to regioselective allylic substitution and three-component difunctionalization of 1,3-enynes. Iron electrocatalysis enables the coupling of alkynyl chlorides with chlorogermanes, furnishing structurally diverse alkynylgermanes while suppressing competing homocoupling. We also discuss switchable transformations of nitrile-containing substrates, in which changes in electrochemical conditions and catalyst participation result in either decyanative germylation or anodic C–H germylation. Mechanistic studies involving cyclic voltammetry, radical-probe experiments, electrolysis controls, and density functional theory calculations reveal several recurring design principles. These include catalyst-centered reduction before direct substrate reduction, selective activation of Ge–Cl and C–X bonds, controlled interception of carbon-centered radicals, and electrochemical modulation of radical, organometallic, and radical–polar pathways. Rather than proceeding through a single universal catalytic cycle, these transformations operate through distinct but related mechanistic pathways that can be selected and adjusted through catalyst and potential control. Together, these studies illustrate how electrochemistry can function not only as a redox input but also as a tool for reaction design in organogermanium chemistry. Future opportunities include asymmetric C–Ge bond formation, stereogenic germanium-center construction, the use of nonsacrificial electrode systems, quantitative evaluation of reaction sustainability, and broader applications of organogermanium products in medicinal chemistry and functional materials.

items.title: Design, Synthesis, and Comparative Selection Analysis of a Chemically Diverse Peptide-Like DNA-Encoded Library
items.abstract: DNA-encoded chemical library technology offers a cost-effective method for screening billions of compounds in a single experiment. However, achieving broad coverage of lead-like chemical space remains challenging. Here, we describe the design and synthesis of a three-cycle, peptide-like DEL comprising 403,200 compounds, including an in silico-guided strategy for building block additions. A chemical space model based on 4,774 commercially available amino acid building blocks was used to identify amino acids underrepresented in the original design, in order to expand the library’s physicochemical diversity. Following split-and-pool synthesis, affinity selections against three targets were performed to assess library performance. Selections against carbonic anhydrase II successfully identified a known sulfonamide-containing pharmacophore. These results demonstrate that a computationally optimized, medium-sized DEL can effectively explore lead-like chemical space and identify specific binding motifs for purified protein targets.

items.title: Drug-Likeness, Druggability, and Molecular Developability via Chemometric Evaluation: A Review
items.abstract: High attrition rates constitute a major bottleneck in small-molecule drug discovery, largely arising from poor molecular developability rather than an insufficient pharmacological activity. Drug-likeness, druggability, and molecular developability represent complementary evaluation concepts that address different aspects of small-molecule drug discovery. Nevertheless, inconsistent terminology, fragmented evaluation frameworks, and inherent drawbacks of traditional empirical workflows impair the reliability and applicability of molecular property assessment. As powerful multivariate analytical tools, chemometric methods overcome these limitations and enable quantitative, systematic, and high-throughput molecular property evaluation. This Review clarifies the definitions and relationships among the three concepts and summarizes their classical evaluation approaches. Following the paradigm shift from empirical rules to chemometric modeling, multiobjective optimization, and large-model prediction, advanced computational pipelines are categorized into direct molecular similarity evaluation and predictive modeling of key molecular properties. We discuss the principles, progress, performance, strengths, and limitations of each technical strategy and highlight their synergistic values in lead discovery, structural modification, multiobjective optimization, and focused library design. Finally, challenges for standardized molecular-evaluation systems are analyzed, and future trends of chemometrics-assisted multiobjective optimization and large-model-driven intelligent molecular profiling are prospected.

items.title: Non-Monotonic Glass Transition Behavior as a Molecular Signature of Strong Interactions in Co-Amorphous and Crystalline Celecoxib-Etoricoxib Systems
items.abstract: Co-amorphous API−API systems often exhibit improved physical stability compared to their neat amorphous counterparts. This effect, however, becomes less straightforward when both components possess nearly identical glass transition temperatures (Tg). In this work, we investigate a model celecoxib + etoricoxib (CEL + ETO) system, in which both APIs display comparable Tg and molecular dynamics, yet markedly different physical stability. Using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), broadband dielectric spectroscopy (BDS), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and solid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy (ssNMR), we demonstrate that CEL + ETO mixtures exhibit a rare, non-monotonic dependence of Tg on composition, with a maximum near the equimolar ratio. This behavior is consistently observed across independent techniques and deviates from conventional mixing rules. Despite only moderate changes in molecular mobility, co-amorphization with ETO leads to a pronounced suppression of CEL recrystallization, as confirmed by dielectric studies. Spectroscopic data reveal strong heteromolecular interactions, including hydrogen-bonded heterosynthons, which disrupt CEL self-association and hinder nucleation. Importantly, these interactions may also influence the crystalline phase, where deviations from ideal eutectic behavior and sensitivity to mechanical treatment indicate non-ideal, preparation-dependent crystalline-phase behavior and possible mechanically induced crystalline rearrangements. These findings suggest that non-monotonic Tg − composition dependence can serve as a signature of strong intermolecular interactions and provide a link between amorphous-phase behavior and crystalline-phase organization.

items.title: Prediction of Plasma Concentration−Time Profiles in Mice from Chemical Structure Using a Kinetically Constrained Hybrid Neural ODE
items.abstract: Predicting plasma concentration−time profiles directly from chemical structure remains intrinsically challenging in early drug discovery. Existing approaches typically fall into two paradigms: mechanistic reconstruction via predicted PK parameters, which is constrained by the assumed model structure, and direct data-driven prediction of concentrations, which often suffers from instability and poor temporal coherence under sparse and irregular sampling. Here, we present a kinetically constrained hybrid Neural ordinary differential equation (KCH-NODE) framework for structure-to-PK prediction that bridges these limitations. KCH-NODE anchors predictions to a shared, learnable two-compartment typical trajectory while modeling compound-specific PK behavior as continuous-time deviations governed by a Neural ODE. This hybrid design generates flexible yet pharmacokinetically coherent trajectories, even under sparse observations. Trained on mouse intravenous (IV) and oral (PO) PK data from 1159 compounds across 30 projects, KCH-NODE generally provided more accurate predictions than a purely data-driven Neural ODE in both compound-level and scaffold-based cross-validation (median RMSE 0.374 and 0.388 for IV; 0.564 and 0.570 for PO) and in a temporally held-out evaluation (223 compounds; median RMSE 0.637 for IV and 0.731 for PO), with a smaller loss of accuracy on the temporal split. Predictive accuracy for oral administration nevertheless remained limited on the temporal test set for both methods. Integrated Gradients supported mechanistically consistent feature contributions, and structural similarity to the model-development dataset together with ensemble disagreement provided complementary indicators of prediction reliability. These results indicate that kinetically constrained hybrid Neural ODEs offer an effective and interpretable framework for structure-to-PK profile prediction.

items.title: Injectable Thermosensitive Hydrogel Synergizes Antibacterial Action with Microenvironment Remodeling in Infected Diabetic Wounds
items.abstract: Chronic wounds represent substantial clinical challenges due to their intricate pathophysiology, characterized by persistent infection, sustained inflammation, and compromised tissue regeneration. To overcome these obstacles, we developed an injectable thermosensitive hydrogel system (MR-NPs-Gels), incorporating engineered PLGA nanoparticles (MR-NPs) for the co-delivery of mupirocin, a first-line antibacterial agent, and l-arginine, a nitric oxide (NO) precursor. The MR-NPs-Gels exhibited favorable injectability, tissue adaptability, and ideal rheological properties. MR-NPs penetrated deep into tissues to exert antibacterial effects, while l-arginine released from them generated NO to exert anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects. In diabetic wound models, MR-NPs-Gels achieved a 77.39 ± 1.19% wound closure rate and more than 80% reduction in bacterial colony counts by day 9. Compared with commercial mupirocin ointment, this hydrogel significantly downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-α, while upregulating angiogenic markers VEGF and CD31. Collectively, the co-delivery of mupirocin and l-arginine within MR-NPs-Gels enhances bacterial clearance and remodels the wound microenvironment synergistically, offering a promising topical therapeutic strategy for infected chronic wounds.

items.title: GenMAS: A Machine Learning-Based Modeling and Assessment Strategy for ADMET Profiling and its Application in PBPK Simulation
items.abstract: Evaluation of pharmacokinetic (PK) properties is crucial for the discovery of high-quality drug candidates while minimizing unnecessary biological and clinical trial costs. Compared with in vitro and in vivo studies, in silico methods offer a faster and more cost-efficient alternative. However, despite advances in computational approaches, accurate PK assessment and simulation remain challenging. Current industrial applications are often hindered by a heavy reliance on animal data, limited flexibility, and insufficient project-specific customization. In this study, we present GenMAS, a machine learning (ML)-based strategy designed for comprehensive modeling and evaluation of PK properties. GenMAS was evaluated for its performance in ADMET property prediction and its applicability to physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulation. This strategy synergistically integrated three functional modules: (1) ADMET property prediction module, (2) ML-informed PBPK modeling module, and (3) self-developed high-throughput ADMET-PBPK screening module. The ADMET prediction module was assessed using 10-fold cross-validation, internal test sets, and external validation sets. Cross-validation demonstrated robust performance, with the models yielding an average AUC (area under the curve) of 0.879 and an accuracy of 0.828. For independent test sets, classification accuracy ranged from 70.2% to 88.7%, while average R2 for physicochemical properties exceeded 0.76. The predictive robustness of GenMAS was further confirmed using in-house project datasets, demonstrating its utility in real-world drug discovery. Furthermore, we developed a ML-informed PBPK module and a high-throughput ADMET-PBPK screening module. In the ML-informed module, ML-predicted compound-specific parameters were integrated into a GastroPlus® rat PBPK model. For 9 intravenously administered compounds, the predicted systemic exposures fell within a two-fold error range of observed data, with a 66.7% accuracy for elimination half-life. The high-throughput module couples ADMET predictions with a minimal PBPK model to enable customizable PK screening. Notably, GenMAS can complete ADMET predictions and PK simulations for 100 compounds in approximately 12 s. GenMAS offers a scalable, structure-based workflow to support early-stage drug discovery.

items.title: Synthesis, Moleculer Modeling, and Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitor Effects of Novel 1‐(1‐benzyl‐2‐oxoindolin‐3‐ylidene)‐4‐(3‐sulfamoylphenyl)thiosemicarbazides
items.abstract: In this study, we describe the synthesis of new 1‐(1‐benzyl‐2‐oxoindolin‐3‐ylidene)‐4‐(3‐sulfamoylphenyl)thiosemicarbazides and evaluate their inhibitory activity against hCAs ( 6a–l ). The inhibitory effects of compounds 6a–l were examined in vitro against hCA I, II, IX, and XII isoforms. Acetazolamide (AAZ) was employed as the standard reference compound in this study. The compounds 6a–l inhibited the tumor‐associated hCA IX and XII isoenzymes at nanomolar levels, and showed weak inhibitory effects on the off‐target hCA I and II isoenzymes. Selectivity index (SI) values of compounds 6a–l were determined to be significantly high for hCA IX and XII over hCA I and II compared to AAZ. Compound 6k (R 1 = Cl, R 2 = 3‐Cl) showed the strongest inhibitory effect ( K i = 25.23 nM) and high selectivity (SI = 225, 185) against hCA IX over hCA I and II. Compound 6f (R 1 = CH 3 , R 2 = 4‐Cl) was found to have the highest inhibitory effect ( K i = 36.65 nM) and high selectivity (SI = 377 and 192, respectively) against hCA XII over hCA I and II. Molecular docking and dynamic simulation analyses were conducted to explore how compounds 6f and 6k interact with active sites of hCA XII and IX enzymes.

items.title: Network Pharmacology in Drug Discovery: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions Toward Precision Medicine
items.abstract: Network pharmacology (NP) is an innovative drug discovery method that provides a comprehensive view of drug–body interactions through complex biological networks. Each drug modulates specific network nodes, and understanding these interactions helps predict therapeutic effects and side effects. By integrating diverse data types and advanced computational methods, NP enables more accurate identification of new drug targets, accelerating the development of effective, targeted therapies. It also supports personalized medicine by tailoring treatments to individual biological profiles. This review examines the fundamentals and strategic significance of NP in drug discovery. Network‐based approaches unravel complex molecular interactions and discover drug targets with high accuracy. Holistic NP implementation integrates omics datasets and computational tools to deliver actionable insights. The difficulty of screening all drug pairs due to time and cost constraints has driven the development of computational methods to predict side effects efficiently. NP holds transformative potential for precision medicine, promising improved patient outcomes and innovative treatments across many diseases. Conclusively, NP is transforming drug discovery by providing a whole‐view approach to drug interactions and enabling effective, personalized therapeutic interventions.

items.title: Searching for Novel COVID19 Treatments: Towards Covalent TMPRSS2 Inhibitors
items.abstract: We present the design, synthesis and biophysical and biochemical evaluation of new guanidinium derivatives with potential as covalent inhibitors of Transmembrane Protease Serine 2 (TMPRSS2), aiming to find therapies against COVID‐19. TMPRSS2 is a key protease for SARS‐CoV‐2 entry into host cells, making it a promising drug target since blocking viral entry, viral replication is stopped. We have designed five families of guanidinium derivatives with different scaffolds that would allow establishing covalent interactions with the target. The proposed structures were optimised for better binding and drug‐like properties. Docking studies showed that some of the new compounds had improved binding scores over nafamostat. Physicochemical and ADME properties analysis indicated that most of the compounds exhibit favourable drug‐like properties except for a small number that showed poor solubility or absorption. Different synthetic pathways were designed and optimised for the preparation of the five families, and the 40 compounds obtained were fully characterised. Unfortunately, in cell‐based assays, none of the new compounds prepared effectively blocked SARS‐CoV‐2 entry, suggesting that further optimisation is needed. Overall, the work presented expands the chemical space for targeting TMPRSS2 and provides valuable insights for future antiviral drug development.

items.title: Cascade Remodeling through Late-Stage Electrophilic Fluorination in a Bis-Spiroketal Framework
items.abstract: Cascade reactions efficiently generate molecular complexity but are often incompatible with the late-stage diversification of highly functionalized natural products due to competing degradation pathways. Herein, we demonstrate that electrophilic fluorination can serve as a variable control element, selectively capturing transient nucleophiles to install fragment-deactivating C–F bonds that redirect subsequent reactivity away from default degradation. In a derivative of the antibiotic salinomycin, sequential fluorination events gate a multistep structural cascade, converting a single precursor into diverse, unprecedented scaffolds. Stepwise reagent selection enables divergent cascade routing through enol ether manifolds to achieve controlled scaffold remodeling. These results demonstrate late-stage electrophilic fluorination as a switchable fragment-deactivation strategy for directing complex cascade transformations and unlocking new natural product architectures.

items.title: An IscS Persulfide Donates the Sulfur for Ribosomal Protein uL16 Thioamidation
items.abstract: Posttranslational sulfur incorporation into peptide backbones is increasingly reported. These efforts broaden our understanding of thioamides, which have distinct conformational and hydrogen‐bonding properties compared with amides. YcaO‐catalyzed thioamidation of the ribosomal protein uL16 reportedly occurs across thousands of Pseudomonadota. Here, we identify the cysteine desulfurase IscS, a crucial component of iron–sulfur cluster assembly, as the direct sulfur donor for uL16 thioamidation. Genetic deletion, in vitro reconstitution, kinetic analysis, sulfide scavenging, and mutational studies support this conclusion. Our data support a mechanism in which the IscS persulfide attacks the O ‐phosphorylated uL16 backbone amide to form an IscS–uL16 disulfide intermediate. This labile disulfide is rapidly reduced, and the resulting hemiorthothioamide collapses with phosphate release to give the thioamide. IscS binds uL16 with mid‐nanomolar affinity and can be displaced by other IscS‐dependent sulfur acceptors. IscS promotes formation of the 2:2 YcaO–uL16 complex from the otherwise predominant 1:1 complex. Structural and mutational studies identify uL16 residues important for catalytically competent enzyme–substrate interactions. These findings define the sulfur delivery pathway for uL16 thioamidation and reveal an additional role of the IscS persulfide beyond iron–sulfur cluster assembly, suggesting it serves as another nucleophile for YcaO‐catalyzed backbone modification.

items.title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
items.abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

items.title: CHARMM-GUI Covalent Ligand Docker as a Web-Based Molecular Docking Platform for Covalent Ligands
items.abstract: Covalent inhibitor research is an emerging topic in drug discovery because of its superior performance in specificity and inhibition effects. While molecular docking is a popular strategy in predicting and assessing ligand conformations or poses in receptor proteins, covalent ligand docking requires nontrivial preparation efforts as the ligand structure changes during the covalent complex formation. In order to facilitate molecular docking for covalent ligands, we have developed CHARMM-GUI Covalent Ligand Docker (CGUI-CLD), a new module for covalent ligand docking supported by AutoDock4. CGUI-CLD automates ligand preparation, supports ligand modification, implements docking simulations, and presents results through an intuitive user interface. A knowledge-based library built in CGUI-CLD currently supports 66 warheads and 8 amino acids, which can be used to automate the covalent ligand transformation from a prereaction to a postreaction adduct form seamlessly. Moreover, CHARMM-GUI High-Throughput Simulator is integrated for rapid generation of multiple molecular dynamics simulation systems. CGUI-CLD is expected to significantly reduce the unnecessary workload of covalent ligand docking and advance covalent ligand research.

items.title: Nanozymes in Action: Inbuilt Asymmetric Local Electric Field for Enhanced Ferroptosis‐Pyroptosis Therapy
items.abstract: Conventional nanozymes are generally reported to have a symmetric coordination environment near the active centers that can hinder electron transfer and result in limited catalytic efficiency. In a recent article by Na Na and colleagues, an axial sulfur‐bridged Mo–S–Cu (A‐CuN 3 S 1 @MoS 2− x ) nanozyme is developed that functions by utilizing an expanded asymmetric local electric field (LEF). The innovative structure significantly ramps up multienzymatic activities, which include catalase‐, peroxidase‐, and oxidase‐like functions, while concomitantly depleting glutathione. As this nanozyme specifically targets mitochondria in tumors, it initiates a cascade of reactive oxygen species (ROS), activating combined ferroptosis and gasdermin E (GSDME)‐mediated pyroptosis. We highlight these findings on how the axial‐bridging strategy offers a sophisticated design for nonapoptotic tumor therapy through the modalities of coordination chemistry and electronic structure modulation.

items.title: Limiting Trial‐and‐Error: Linker‐Based 2D Descriptor Analysis to Support Very Early Proteolysis‐Targeting Chimeras Design
items.abstract: Targeted protein degradation has emerged as a clinically validated therapeutic strategy, culminating in the recent FDA approval of the first proteolysis‐targeting chimeras (PROTAC) drug (VEPPANU). Within PROTACs, the linker plays a central role in modulating degradation efficiency as well as physicochemical and in vitro absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion properties, yet linker optimization still largely relies on empirical “linkerology” approaches. Here, we investigated whether simple 2D linker descriptors could provide informative insights for very early‐stage PROTAC design. Four matched PROTAC series, including both cereblon‐ and von Hippel–Lindau‐recruiting degraders, were retrospectively analyzed using a workflow combining the in‐house Bellerophon‐based linker extraction with principal component analysis. Selected descriptors captured linker hydrophobicity, polarity, flexibility, and topology and were correlated with experimental degradation, permeability, solubility, lipophilicity, protein binding, and metabolic stability data. In several datasets, linker‐dependent trends associated with the molecular properties of degraders and their degradation efficiency were identified, particularly for von Hippel–Lindau‐based PROTACs. Although the limited size of currently available datasets prevents broad generalization, this work highlights the potential of simple descriptor‐based analyses to support early candidate prioritization and reduce unnecessary synthetic efforts.

items.title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel aminopyrimidine derivatives as potent EGFRC797S inhibitors for overcoming osimertinib resistance
Beyond global drug-likeness: The FamDLike framework as a target family-specific drug-likeness score
items.abstract: Drug-likeness is a central metric which is used to evaluate the physicochemical profile of small molecules either as a filter for virtual screening or, more recently, as a reward function in generative design tasks. Established scores such as QED are widely adopted for these purposes, although the ligands of different therapeutic target families occupy different regions of physicochemical space. Applying a single global drug-likeness criterion can therefore systematically reward some target classes while penalising others, narrowing the chemical space considered druglike in a way that may not reflect the actual requirements for a given project. In this work, we propose a target family specific drug-likeness approach, the FamDLike framework, designed to distinguish target families more accurately than existing metrics and to explore family specific druglike regions of chemical space. This framework combines three complementary modelling paradigms: desirability functions, generalized additive models and tree-based machine learning models that span the interpretability-flexibility spectrum. The three components can also be used independently, depending on whether interpretability or predictive flexibility is prioritized. The abilities of the proposed method have been tested on real-world use cases in computational medicinal chemistry: an independent set from DrugBank, library screening of Enamine and KLIFS compounds, and de novo molecule generation via REINVENT4. The proposed approach therefore provides a more discriminative, interpretable and target-aware complement to existing drug-likeness scores, suitable for ranking in early discovery pipelines and as a reward function for generative chemistry. Furthermore, a user-friendly web portal (https://huggingface.co/spaces/kochgroup/FamDLike) is available to obtain drug-likeness profiles of molecules.

items.title: Synthesis and evaluation of novel meso-coumarin-substituted dithieno[3,2-b]thiophene BODIPY derivatives for photodynamic therapy
Dual inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 Nsp13 helicase functions with broad anti-hCoV activity and combination effects with approved antivirals
items.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 non-structural protein 13 (nsp13) is a highly conserved helicase essential for viral replication and immune evasion. Its conservation across coronaviruses makes it an attractive target for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents. Hence, we rationally designed and synthesised 42 novel 2-iminothiazolidin-4-one derivatives as potential inhibitors. Several compounds displayed low-micromolar IC 50 values against both nsp13 NTPase and unwinding activities. Among these, 3i emerged as the lead compound, combining enzymatic inhibition (IC 50 unwinding 2.65 ± 0.51 μM and IC 50 NTPase 8.52 ± 0.68 μM) with a favourable antiviral activity/cytotoxicity profile in two complementary cell models of SARS-CoV-2 infection (EC 50 23.80 ± 1.80 μM in VeroE6-GFP, SI 18.15; EC 50 6.7 ± 0.86 μM in Calu-3 cells, a human lung epithelial model). 3i also showed antiviral activity against hCoV-229E and MERS-CoV, with EC 50 values of 5.7 ± 0.1 and 4.6 ± 1.1 μM, respectively, supporting activity across human coronaviruses. The compound further demonstrated no marked hepatocellular cytotoxicity under the tested conditions in HepG2 cells, negligible inhibition of human helicases DDX3X and DDX5. Experimental biomimetic HPLC analyses provided an initial assessment of its physicochemical and distribution properties. Binding affinity evaluation by SPR revealed a K D value of 6.20 μM, while enzyme kinetic studies indicated mixed-type NTPase inhibition. Exploratory docking and molecular dynamics analyses predicted possible binding regions that may account for the simultaneous modulation of the two nsp13 enzymatic functions. Finally, 3i showed a favourable antiviral combination profile with Remdesivir or Nirmatrelvir , mirroring established combination strategies in antiviral therapy.

items.title: Engineering a Reconfigurable Transmembrane Receptor Enables Logic-Controlled Signal Translocation
items.abstract: Transmembrane receptors relay extracellular cues into intracellular responses through reconfigurable conformational changes, yet engineering synthetic systems that emulate receptor-like signal translocation with programmable control remains challenging. Here, we engineer a reconfigurable transmembrane receptor that enables logic-controlled signal translocation across lipid membranes. The receptor is constructed from an oriented Y-shaped triplex DNA architecture that inserts directionally into the plasma membrane via dual cholesterol anchors and integrates two environmental inputs─H+ and ATP─through an i-motif and an aptamer module. Under dual-input conditions, cooperative duplex-to-triplex switching triggers reconfigurable structural rearrangement and drives transmembrane relocation of a signaling strand from the outer to the inner membrane leaflet. This receptor-mediated signal translocation converts extracellular chemical cues into spatially defined intracellular activation. The repositioned strand serves as a modular intracellular effector that can be functionalized to implement programmable reactions, including bioorthogonal catalysis and light-triggered photocatalysis at the membrane interface. Importantly, endogenous tumor-microenvironmental cues trigger receptor reconfiguration and signal translocation in 3D tumor spheroids and in vivo, enabling logic-gated intracellular photocatalysis and >85% tumor growth inhibition in xenograft models. By coupling logic-gated reconfigurable switching with directional transmembrane signal propagation, this work establishes an engineered transmembrane receptor for programmable intracellular activation and provides a general strategy for synthetic signal translocation in living systems.

items.title: Enantioconvergent Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling for the Synthesis of α-Aryl Ketones via Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
items.abstract: Photochemical enantioselective nickel catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing stereogenic C(sp3)–C(sp2) bonds in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel-catalyzed enantioconvergent decarboxylative cross-coupling of α-aryl carboxylic acid derivatives with aliphatic carboxylic acids, providing efficient access to enantioenriched α-aryl ketones. The reaction selectively engages two structurally distinct carboxylic acid-derived coupling partners while suppressing competing protodecarboxylation and homocoupling pathways. This protocol features broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and excellent enantioselectivity (up to 98% ee), providing a modular and practical approach to chiral α-aryl ketones from readily accessible carboxylic acid feedstocks.

items.title: Chiral 1,2-Benzothiazine Synthesis via Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Activation/Cyclization with Chiral Carboxylic Amides
items.abstract: Chiral sulfur-containing fused heterocycles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry. Expanding the catalytic repertoire for the asymmetric synthesis of bioactive sulfur heterocycles via C–H activation remains a persistent pursuit. We report herein an efficient annulation of sulfoximines with diarylacetylenes catalyzed by an achiral Cp*Rh(III) complex, where stereocontrol is governed by a chiral carboxylic amide additive. This protocol provides access to a diverse array of enantioenriched 1,2-benzothiazines in excellent yields (up to 99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee).

items.title: 1,4-Dioxane as a Sacrificial Radical Buffer Enables Pd-Catalyzed Regioselective C2 Acylation of Indolyl Ketoximes: Access to 2,3-Diacylindoles and Indole-Fused Heterocycles
items.abstract: Pd-catalyzed regioselective C2 acylation of indoles has been achieved using a C3-ketoxime directing group and glyoxal/aldehydes. The protocol provides C2 acylated indoles with high selectivity and enables one-pot access to indole-fused pyridazines and 2,3-diacylindoles. Mechanistic studies revealed that 1,4-dioxane acts not only as solvent but also as a sacrificial radical buffer that modulates TBHP derived tBuO• and tBuOO• species. Thereby suppressing undesired side reactions while facilitating the desired acylation pathway.

items.title: Divergent Assembly of Functionalized Medium-Sized N , O -Heterocycles from N -(2-Hydroxyethyl)sulfonylamide
items.abstract: The divergent base-mediated formal [4+3] and [4+4] annulation of N-(2-hydroxyethyl)sulfonylamides was described for the preparation of seven- and eight-membered oxazaheterocycles. This strategy exhibited mild conditions, moderate to excellent yields, broad substrate scope, and functional group tolerance. The viability of this synthetic method was confirmed by scale-up reactions and additional transformations. In vitro toxicity experiments revealed that the three kinds of N,O-heterocycles exhibited significant antibacterial activity.

items.title: Topological Engineering of NIR‐II Emissive Conjugated Oligomers With Unexpected Excited‐State Manifolds for Efficient Phototheranostics and Cancer Immunotherapy
items.abstract: Phototheranostic agents operating in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window hold great potential for precision cancer therapy, yet the rational regulation of excited‐state processes to simultaneously optimize fluorescence and phototherapeutic performances remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report a topology‐driven excited‐state engineering strategy for constructing conjugated oligomers with tailored excited‐state manifolds and multi‐channel excitation dynamics. By precisely manipulating molecular topology, conjugated topological oligomers achieve enhanced light‐harvesting capability and optimized exciton utilization, thereby enabling synergistic regulation of excitation dynamics. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, nanoparticles (NPs) derived from TBT‐3 exhibit 2.8‐fold enhanced NIR‐II fluorescence brightness, 2.7‐fold improved photothermal performance, and 7.5‐fold increased total reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation compared with TBT‐1. In vivo studies demonstrate that TBT‐3 NPs enable high‐resolution NIR‐II fluorescence imaging and efficient tumor elimination. Moreover, TBT‐3‐mediated phototherapy induces immunogenic cell death and enhances antitumor immunity, leading to improved therapeutic efficacy when combined with anti‐PD‐1 immune checkpoint blockade. This work provides a molecular topology‐based strategy for manipulating excited‐state landscapes and establishes conjugated oligomers as versatile candidates for NIR‐II phototheranostics and cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Biomarker and Bioorthogonality Dual‐Locked Chemiluminescent Probes for Cancer Urine Test
items.abstract: Bioorthogonality‐activatable optical imaging activates caged or quenched probes via bioorthogonal reactions for disease diagnosis. Although chemiluminescence enables low‐background detection, it has rarely been applied to bioorthogonality‐activatable imaging. Here, we synthesize chemiluminescent tetrazine probes (CLTZs) by coupling a tetrazine acceptor to a phenoxy‐1,2‐dioxetane donor through π‐conjugated vinylene linkers, enabling biomarker and bioorthogonality dual‐locked activation for cancer urine testing. Unlike conventional chemiluminophores, tetrazine in CLTZs mediates an internal‐conversion‐to‐a‐dark‐state quenching mechanism, suppressing chemiluminescence even after phenolate formation. Strong chemiluminescence is restored only when the phenolate form undergoes bioorthogonal reaction with bicyclononyne (BCN), generating pyridazine‐containing donor–π–acceptor chemiluminophores. This unique dark state enables development of an H 2 O 2 and bioorthogonality dual‐locked probe ( H BCP), emitting only when both H 2 O 2 and BCN are present. By engineering BCN into a cancer‐activatable bioorthogonal urinary reporter ( C BUR) that releases renal‐clearable BCN in tumors, a chemiluminescent bioorthogonal pair ( H BCP & C BUR) is created. This pair achieves in vivo tumor imaging with a signal‐to‐background ratio of 438 and detects lung metastasis in early urinary assays with up to 23.9‐fold signal enhancement over healthy mice. This work provides a molecular design for bioorthogonality‐activatable chemiluminescence toward noninvasive, sensitive disease diagnosis.

items.title: Modular Construction of Cyclic and Linear Quaternary Carbon Centers through Visible‐Light‐Induced Triplet Nitrene Transfer Reaction
items.abstract: All‐carbon quaternary centers represent a fundamental structural unit found in a wide range of functional molecules. Within the versatile synthetic toolbox, the semipinacol rearrangement (SPR) stands as one of the most powerful tools for assembling this sterically congested motif. In this context, ‌radical‐mediated SPR pathways‌, especially those entailing alkyl migrations, remain underexplored from a strategic standpoint. Herein, we report a visible light‐promoted formal SPR of tertiary allyl alcohols using in situ‐generated triplet nitrene species as the initiator under redox‐neutral conditions. This method demonstrates broad substrate scope, enabling efficient construction of all‐carbon quaternary centers across various steric environments, including rigid cyclic/spiro frameworks and flexible acyclic systems. Mechanistic investigations reveal substrate‐dependent pathways: alkenyl cyclobutanols undergo triplet nitrene addition followed by concurrent ring‐expansion and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to form cyclic ketones, while nonactivated allyl alcohols proceed through aziridination/ring‐opening/SPR sequences to produce linear β‐amino ketones. Preliminary biological assessments of these α‐quaternary β‐aminoketone derivatives revealed that compound 4a exhibited potent anti‐DENV‐2 activity, with an EC 50 value of 0.95 ± 0.02 µM against viral replication.

items.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Trap‐Mimetic DNA Nets Enable Concurrent Bacteria‐Targeted Eradication and Toxin Neutralization
items.abstract: Current antibacterial therapies often suffer from limited bacterial selectivity, host‐cell toxicity, and inflammation triggered by toxin release during bacterial killing. Here, we report a neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)‐mimetic, dopamine‐incorporated DNA net, termed D A Net‐DA, enabling targeted bacterial eradication and concurrent toxin neutralization. Inspired by the trap‐kill‐neutralize function of NETs, D A Net‐DA selectively captures and traps bacteria, followed by in situ catalytic formation of polydopamine nanoshells on the trapped bacteria. This process enables efficient photothermal bacterial eradication while minimizing damage to host cells. Meanwhile, the nanoshells act as molecular sponges to sequester and neutralize bacterial toxins, thereby mitigating toxin‐associated inflammation. These integrated functions endow D A Net‐DA with potent therapeutic efficacy in vivo, as demonstrated by markedly reduced bacterial burdens, toxin levels, tissue inflammation in both conventional and burn wound infection models. Moreover, the simultaneous clearance of bacteria and residual toxins alleviates pro‐inflammatory macrophage polarization, thereby accelerating wound tissue regeneration. This work presents a NETs‐mimetic antibacterial strategy that integrates pathogen clearance with toxin neutralization, offering a promising method for treating bacterial infection‐associated diseases.

items.title: A Selective Bis-Catecholate Siderophore-Ampicillin Conjugate Expands Activity against Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a global public health crisis, with multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa among the most critical threats. The high cost and slow pace of novel antibiotic development, coupled with rapid resistance evolution, demand innovative strategies. Here, we present a Trojan horse approach using siderophore-antibiotic conjugates (SACs) to hijack bacterial iron uptake systems and deliver β-lactam payloads across the Gram-negative outer membrane. We designed a series of ampicillin conjugates with mono-catecholate, bis-catecholate, and catecholate-hydroxamate siderophores. These conjugates demonstrate potent antimicrobial activity. Notably, the lead compound, BC-2-Amp, shows broad-spectrum and highly selective activity against a panel of 105 clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that BC-2-Amp utilizes PiuA as a critical receptor for targeted delivery. Complementary in vivo experiments further confirmed its promising therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, these findings establish SACs as a potent strategy for broadening the spectrum of β-lactam antibiotics and provide a robust platform for high-potency drug delivery.

items.title: A Peripheral Sulfonium Moiety Engineering Strategy to Enhance AIEgen-Based Antitumor Photodynamic Therapy
items.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of photosensitizers (PSs) strongly depends on their capacity to efficiently generate reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a peripheral sulfonium moiety engineering strategy and identify a lead aggregation-induced emission (AIE)-based PS, S12. The sulfonium moiety enhances the photosensitization of S12 primarily by increasing spin−orbit coupling (SOC) and reducing ΔEST, thus boosting ROS generation. Moreover, the sulfonium unit enables S12 to simultaneously produce both Type I and Type II ROS, rendering its photosensitization weakly dependent on O2 concentration. Owing to its cationic character and the inherent amphiphilicity of the AIE core, S12 exhibits dynamic organelle-targeting behavior, initially anchoring to membranes and subsequently accumulating in lipid droplets. Such localization facilitates ROS-triggered ferroptosis, leading to potent in vitro antitumor photodynamic therapy activity and effective tumor suppression in a 4T1 mouse model. Overall, this work provides a rational design strategy to advance AIE-based PSs with enhanced therapeutic potential.

items.title: Maleimide−Thiol Conjugation Enables the Optimization of 68Ga-Labeled CAIX Targeting PET Probes
items.abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a well-established biomarker of tumor hypoxia and an attractive target for molecular imaging. Despite the development of small-molecule CAIX-targeting positron emission tomography (PET) probes, most exhibit high normal-organ uptake and suboptimal tumor-to-background contrast. Moreover, their application in hypoxic tumors remains insufficiently explored. Herein, we reported four 68Ga-labeled CAIX-targeting probes based on the acetazolamide (AAZ) scaffold, employing distinct conjugation strategies, including amide coupling and maleimide−thiol ligation. All probes demonstrated detectable tumor uptake in vivo. Among them, [68Ga]Ga-SMIC-2607 displayed the highest tumor uptake (14.67 ± 3.06 %ID/g) and tumor-to-kidney ratio (1.69 ± 0.41) at 1 h in subcutaneous OS-RC-2-bearing mice, along with high tumor uptake in HT-29-bearing mice (2.98 ± 0.28 %ID/g at 1 h). Overall, [68Ga]Ga-SMIC-2607 demonstrates favorable imaging characteristics, with high tumor uptake and high tumor-to-normal organ ratios, representing a promising candidate for imaging CAIX-overexpressing tumors and supporting clinical translation.

items.title: Enzyme−Targeted Therapeutics for Neurological Disorders
items.abstract: Neurological disorders represent one of the leading causes of disability and mortality worldwide, and their prevalence is expected to increase substantially with population aging. Despite major advances in neuroscience, effective disease-modifying therapies remain unavailable for most chronic disorders of the central nervous system (CNS), highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies. Enzymes are attractive drug targets because they regulate fundamental processes including neurotransmission, signal transduction, energy metabolism, protein homeostasis, epigenetic regulation, lipid metabolism, and cellular detoxification. This review summarizes the major classes of druggable CNS enzymes, discuss clinically approved drugs and emerging investigational agents, and evaluate therapeutic opportunities across neurodegenerative, neurodevelopmental, neuropsychiatric, cerebrovascular, and neuro-oncologic diseases. Key challenges including blood−brain barrier penetration, target selectivity, off-target pharmacology, and clinical translation are also examined. By integrating diverse enzyme-targeting modalities across multiple neurological disorders, this review highlights both the progress achieved to date and the substantial opportunities that remain for future CNS drug discovery.

items.title: Design, Synthesis and Evaluation Donepezil-Based Dual BuChE/FAAH Inhibitors for Alzheimer’s Disease Therapy
items.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is multifactorial, prompting multi-target therapy. A series of donepezil-based derivatives were designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual inhibitors of human butyrylcholinesterase (hBuChE) and fatty acid amide hydrolase (hFAAH). Among them, lead G15 displayed potent and balanced inhibition with IC50 values of 2.44 μM and 0.17 μM, respectively, and favorable selectivity over carboxylesterases CES1/2 (SI 14.4 and 8.4). G15 not only acted as a time-dependent, mixed-type hFAAH inhibitor and a pseudo-irreversible hBuChE inhibitor, but also exhibited good drug-like properties, including high BBB permeability and oral bioavailability (108%). Moreover, G15 chelated Zn2+, protected PC12 cells from oxidative stress, and promoted microglial M1 → M2 polarization. In an Aβ1−42-induced mouse model, G15 significantly reversed cognitive deficits, outperforming donepezil. Therefore, G15 is poised for further development as a promising multi-target candidate for AD therapy.

items.title: Evaluation of 68Ga Labeling Strategies and Thermostability of HER2-Targeted Nanobody NB46
items.abstract: The HER2-targeted nanobody NB46 was evaluated for labeling strategy flexibility and thermostability. Random and site-specific 68Ga labeling strategies were compared. Both conjugates exhibited high HER2 affinity, comparable to unmodified NB46. Cellular uptake, pharmacokinetics, micro-PET/CT imaging, and biodistribution in HER2-positive and HER2-negative tumor-bearing mice revealed no significant differences between the two strategies. NB46 retained HER2 affinity at temperatures up to 90 °C, demonstrating exceptional thermostability. Both conjugates achieved >95% radiochemical yields at all tested temperatures. Micro-PET/CT imaging showed sustained high tumor uptake with renal clearance as the primary elimination pathway. Blocking studies confirmed that NB46 and trastuzumab competitively bind to HER2. Elevated labeling temperatures did not compromise tumor targeting but resulted in a mild increase in renal uptake, notably for the random conjugate at 90 °C. These findings suggest that random labeling may represent a simpler, equally effective alternative for 68Ga-NB46 preparation, and confirm the excellent thermostability of this nanobody scaffold.

items.title: PRPF19 drives hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis via PKM2-mediated glycolytic reprogramming
items.abstract: Activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) is a pivotal event driving fibrogenic remodeling of the injured liver. However, the upstream regulators that integrate post-translational signaling with metabolic reprogramming during HSC activation remain poorly defined. Here, we identify pre-mRNA processing factor 19 (PRPF19) as a ubiquitination-linked metabolic regulator that promotes HSC activation. PRPF19 expression was elevated in human and murine fibrotic livers, enriched in activated HSCs, and positively correlated with fibrosis severity. Conditional deletion of Prpf19 in HSCs (Prpf19flox/flox;Lrat-CreERT2), but not in hepatocytes (Prpf19flox/flox;Alb-CreERT2), attenuated HSC activation and liver fibrosis in vivo. Integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses indicated that PRPF19 sustains glycolytic flux and transcriptional programs associated with HSC activation. Mechanistically, PRPF19 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2), facilitating its nuclear translocation and hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α)-dependent transcription of glycolytic and fibrogenic genes. These findings support a role for the PRPF19-PKM2 pathway in metabolic regulation during HSC activation and liver fibrosis. Zhang et al. show that PRPF19 promotes hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis by driving PKM2-dependent glycolytic reprogramming, identifying a potential metabolic target in chronic liver disease.

items.title: A self-limiting mechanotransduction feedback loop ensures robust organ formation
items.abstract: Abstract Organ morphogenesis uses mechanotransduction feedback loops to convert forces into gene expression changes that regulate cell mechanics. How these loops integrate with developmental programs to ensure robust outcomes remains unclear. We show Yap mechanotransduction establishes a self-limiting positive feedback loop for semicircular canal formation in zebrafish. Canal development proceeds through bud initiation, extension, and fusion within the otic epithelium. Local swelling of hyaluronan-rich extracellular matrix (ECM) in the bud activates Yap in a spatial pattern. Yap induces its target ccn1l1 , promoting further ECM expansion to sustain bud extension. This feedback loop confers developmental robustness: graded knockdown of ccn1l1 reduces extension rate, yet canal formation persists and fails only with strong disruption. Critically, the loop contains its own termination mechanism. During bud fusion, PKA-CREB signaling, activated by an adhesion GPCR, gpr126, suppresses ccn1l1 , ending the loop. These findings reveal how mechanotransduction loops with built-in termination provide developmental control by integrating mechanical forces, transcriptional responses, and morphogenetic outcomes.

items.title: CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons
items.abstract: Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Using mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation, we show that CREST is essential for motor neuron maturation by activating mature neuronal genes and repressing progenitor genes. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.

items.title: Enhancing Natural Product Therapy with PROTACs: Targeted Degradation of TLR4 Confers Potent Endothelial Protection
items.abstract: TLR4-MyD88-mediated endothelial dysfunction drives cardiovascular disease. To overcome the weak efficacy of ferulic acid, we synthesized six ferulic acid-based PROTAC derivatives. Migration and TLR4 expression assays in HUVECs identified FP-4 as lead. FP-4 induced the targeted degradation of TLR4, suppressing the TLR4/MyD88-NF-κB pathway and downstream TNF-α, ICAM-1, and VCAM-1. Protection was validated in zebrafish. This expands PROTAC beyond oncology and offers a framework for natural product-derived cardiovascular therapy.

items.title: Discovery of G2019S Mutant Selective LRRK2 Inhibitors Based on an Indazole Octahydrocyclopenta[ c ]pyrrole-Based Hybrid Chemotype
items.abstract: LRRK2 is an important kinase target for Parkinson’s disease with disease-modifying potential. In this article, we report our efforts to identify indazole octahydrocyclopenta[c]pyrrole-based hybrid chemotypes as LRRK2 inhibitors utilizing a structure-guided hybridization approach. The initial set of compounds with a piperidine motif showed favorable potencies, but had a rather narrow selectivity window between wild-type and G2019S mutant LRRK2. In contrast, the replacement of the piperidine motif with an octahydrocyclopenta[c]pyrrole enhanced the selectivity window while maintaining good potencies. In short, the presented hybrid chemotype represented by 34 can serve as an alternative starting point and may enable the discovery of next-generation LRRK2 inhibitors through subsequent optimization campaigns.

items.title: Targeting Piezo1 in Peripheral Nerves: Mechanotransduction and Electrostimulation for Pain Control
items.abstract: Piezo1-mediated mechanotransduction (PMT) is a fundamental mechanism in peripheral sensory physiology, converting mechanical stimuli into electrochemical signals that influence neuronal excitability, inflammation, and pain perception. Mechanosensitive (MS) ion channels have been identified as the major contributors to membrane tension sensing and mechanobiological signaling in neuronal and non-neuronal cells. Piezo1 has been implicated in peripheral pain development and maintenance including inflammatory and neuropathic pain through its modulation of Ca2+-dependent signaling pathways, reactive oxygen species production, inflammasome activation, cytoskeleton reorganization, and neuroimmune interactions. Piezo1 is widely expressed in DRG neurons, Schwann cells, keratinocytes, immune cells, and endothelial cells, suggesting a complex role of Piezo1 in peripheral nociceptive processing and mechanical hypersensitivity. Recent advances in pharmacological modulation, genetic targeting, and neuromodulation technologies have brought new insight into the therapeutic potential of Piezo1 in peripheral pain. Preclinical models have demonstrated the modulatory effects of small-molecule agonists and antagonists (e.g., Yoda-series compounds and Dooku1) and gene-silencing techniques on Piezo1 mechanotransduction and inflammatory responses. Meanwhile, the application of peripheral nerve stimulation, transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation, ultrasound neuromodulation, and bioelectronics interfaces are increasingly recognized as important electrostimulation and neuromodulation strategies for pain control and indirect regulators of Piezo1-mediated mechanotransduction by modulating the membrane biophysics, cytoskeletal dynamics, and intracellular calcium signaling. This Review aims to critically evaluate the mechanistic and therapeutic significance of Piezo1 in peripheral pain, with particular emphasis on its potential as a therapeutic target for pain management. It further covers the novel intersection of mechanotransduction and electrostimulation therapies and potential effects of electrical stimulation and neuromodulation on Piezo1-associated signaling and peripheral pain pathways. The review also examines current limitations and translational barriers to Piezo1-targeted therapies, while highlighting emerging strategies such as precision medicine, sonogenetics, nanotechnology-enabled delivery systems, and adaptive neuromodulator platforms for the development of targeted and personalized pain therapeutics.

items.title: A neuronal GPCR modifies neuropeptide signaling to suppress proteostasis in distal tissues
items.abstract: The proteostasis network (PN) safeguards the integrity of proteins by promoting various cellular activities. However, with aging, the PN’s competence declines and aggregated proteins accrue within cells. This process underlies the development of neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s and Huntington’s diseases. While the PN functions within cells, proteostasis is regulated across the organism by intertissue communication, which is partially governed by neurons. We previously found that reducing the expression of gtr-1 , which encodes a neuronal heterotrimeric guanine nucleotide–binding protein–coupled receptor, mitigates the toxicity of the Alzheimer’s disease cause, Aβ peptide. Here, we investigated the mechanism that is acted upon the knockdown of gtr-1 and found that it differentially modulates gene expression profiles, including of neuropeptide-coding genes, and dissimilarly modifies protein aggregation in worms that express distinct proteotoxic proteins. The knockdown of gtr-1 also enhances protein degradation. These findings highlight the roles of neuropeptides as organismal coordinators of proteostasis in the face of distinct proteotoxic challenges.

items.title: Canonical Wnt induction by OTULIN prevents keratinocyte death and skin inflammation
items.abstract: Loss-of-function mutations in the human OTULIN gene, encoding a deubiquitinase with exclusive specificity for linear ubiquitin chains, cause a severe multiorgan autoinflammatory condition involving the skin. Mice lacking OTULIN selectively in keratinocytes develop inflamed skin lesions that progress into squamous tumors, a phenotype driven by excessive tumor necrosis factor (TNF)–induced cell death. Previous studies suggest a role for OTULIN in mediating Wnt signaling during development, but the physiological relevance of this association is unknown. Here, we show that OTULIN promotes Wnt signaling in keratinocytes by regulating the linear ubiquitination status of β-catenin. Stabilization of β-catenin in OTULIN-deficient keratinocytes prevents progressive skin inflammation in prophylactic and therapeutic settings by blocking keratinocyte death. We demonstrate that OTULIN prevents proteasomal degradation of β-catenin in cultured keratinocytes. Reduced Wnt signaling in OTULIN-deficient keratinocytes leads to degradation of TCF3/4, an essential survival factor for keratinocytes. Collectively, our data identify OTULIN’s linear deubiquitination activity as a key regulator of epithelial cell viability, not only by preventing cell death downstream of TNF, but also by promoting canonical Wnt signaling.

items.title: Targeting SUV39H2 exon skipping reverses resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors via transcriptional activation of p21
items.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) are standard therapies for estrogen receptor–positive breast cancer, but their efficacy is limited by drug resistance. While dysregulation of alternative splicing has been implicated in cancer progression, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we uncover a splicing-mediated mechanism whereby exon 2 inclusion in SUV39H2 drives its overexpression in CDK4/6i-resistant breast cancer cells. Clinically, elevated exon 2 inclusion in SUV39H2 correlates with poor prognosis in patients with breast cancer. Targeting SUV39H2 with gapmer antisense oligonucleotides or a methyltransferase inhibitor overcomes CDK4/6i resistance and reinstates therapy-induced senescence in breast cancer cells by reducing SUV39H2 expression or activity. Mechanistically, targeting SUV39H2 promotes transcriptional activation of senescence-associated secretory phenotype genes, including p21 , through H3K9me3 removal at enhancer regions and subsequent chromatin opening at promoters. Our work unveils a splicing-mediated resistance mechanism and presents a potential synergistic drug target for CDK4/6i therapy.

items.title: Cell heterogeneity contributes to the variable response of HIV-1 to latency-reversing agents
items.abstract: Transcriptional noise contributes to gene expression variability, but its origin and impact in HIV-1 latency remain incompletely characterized. Here, we combine a dual-copy MS2-tagging system with dedicated mathematical analysis to investigate the variability of HIV-1 transcription in live cells. In the basal state, the transcriptional activity of proviruses located in the same cell was uncorrelated, indicating that expression variability primarily comes from the intrinsic stochasticity of promoter dynamics. Upon stimulation with diverse latency-reversing agents, transcription of viral copies became more correlated within cells than across them, revealing a shift from promoter-driven to cell state–driven variability. Analysis of the molecular drug targets confirmed variable effects across cells. Our findings indicate that cellular heterogeneity can shape the response to latency-reversing agents and demonstrate how quantitative tools can dissect noise sources. This work offers mechanistic insights into HIV-1 latency and informs strategies to target the latent viral reservoir.

items.title: A bifunctional actuator to correct loss-of-function deficits in cardiac voltage-gated sodium channels
items.abstract: Despite their emerging prominence, ion channelopathies have remained challenging to correct, as ion channel dysfunction linked to disease is multifaceted, involving changes in activity and/or localization. Yet, current corrective strategies typically focus on restoring only one aspect leading to incomplete efficacy. Here, focusing on the voltage-gated sodium channel, Na V 1.5, whose dysfunction is linked to life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias, we develop a genetically encoded bifunctional actuator as a proof-of-concept molecular strategy to reverse pathophysiological changes in channel function. Specifically, we engineer a high affinity nanobody targeting Na V 1.5 with two moieties: (i) a peptide that restores proper inactivation and (ii) a linkage-specific deubiquitinase that promotes surface-membrane localization. Functional validation in heterologous systems and in human and mouse cardiomyocytes demonstrated restoration of Na V 1.5 trafficking and/or gating. In all, this approach shows promise for reversing molecular deficits observed with Na V channelopathies and provides a framework to engineer multifunctional modulators targeting ion channelopathies.

items.title: Phage-ICE tandems facilitate bacterial adaptation and antimicrobial resistance spread
items.abstract: Phages and integrative and conjugative elements (ICEs) drive bacterial evolution, but how their interplay shapes bacterial adaptation and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dissemination remains unclear. Here, we characterize phage-ICE tandems formed by site-specific accretion of phages and ICEs into cotransferable units. In Streptococcus , phage-encoded integrases (IntIE Phage ) drive stress-inducible excision and circularization, after which ICE machinery mediates conduction of the tandem. When excision is impaired, phage and phage-ICE fragments disseminate by transformation and integrate via RecA-dependent homologous recombination (HR), providing a fail-safe route. This pathway enables cotransfer of flanking chromosomal DNA, generating length-variable integrations that remodel transcriptional programs and increase oxidative stress tolerance. A global screen identified 612 phage-ICE tandems across seven phyla and 135 species, including multidrug-resistant pathogens, with lineage-specific repertoires of AMR, virulence, and metabolic genes. Rather than a hybrid element, these structures represent functional interplay where prophages exploit ICE conjugation while facilitating mobilization of the composite region. By coupling excision, transfer, and recombination, phage-ICEs shape adaptation and accelerate AMR spread.

items.title: Citron kinase activity controls alternative splicing events that drive prostate cancer growth
items.abstract: Prostate cancer (CaP) remains a major cause of cancer death in men, underscoring the need for mechanistically novel therapies. We previously identified the action of the mitotic kinase citron (CIT) kinase as a key driver of CaP progression and promising therapeutic target, but selective CIT inhibitors are not available. We therefore asked whether a better understanding of the action of CIT substrates, which execute CIT kinase action in CaP cells, can lead to novel approaches and/or alternative targets to indirectly interfere with CIT’s activity during CaP progression.
